冷知识：为什么October，在加密领域经常叫Uptober？

Uptober是十月的加密俚语，是“up”和“October”的混合体。 

意思是，比特币/加密市场在10月趋于上涨，是加密季节性叙事，不是什么正式指标。

最初是2020年从推特和Reddit上传播开来，

从实际看，从2013年到2025年的记录：

比特币在大约13年中的10年中走高了10月，平均月收益通常约为19%（取决于数据来源）。

突出年份包括2013年/2017年/2021年，当时10月份的收益非常大。 

常见的解释是，9月3季度疲软，低基数，第4季度投资组合重新平衡，以及一些牛市年份减半后周期时间在10月着陆。

不过，2014年和2018年的10月下跌。

而2025年10月更是打破历史：

比特币在月初创下历史新高，然后1011事件中遭遇大规模清算。至今依然没有完全从当初的影响中恢复过来。

text:
The only real option in the "personal agent" space right now is Grok Bot. Been doing a lot with Dots. I do not like them.

Dots are a total mess right now.

1) Having a single thread for everything sucks. They got it right first try with Grok Bot, I have zero clue why they wanted it to just be one thread (I do know why, it's because I'm not the target market for Dots but still I hate it)

2) It's slow. Very, very slow. 

3) There's zero visibility into what it's actually doing. All u can see is the final short text message that Astra gives u (5-10 mins after asking something). Grok bot's pretty good about talking u through what it's doing and being pretty fast, Bot just isn't

4) The app(s) are a mess. The mobile app, the desktop app, they all have performance issues, weird ux things (like when ur not focusing the input box on desktop and type it doesn't auto focus), just an absurd number of paper cuts. It's weird b/c Cursor is just as bad about this kind of thing, but Grok Bot is absurdly polished

5) I have zero clue wtf this thing is doing. I woke up to a bunch of random codex threads doing god knows what in circles and I have zero trust for this thing if I'm gonna be honest. 

6) Zero parallelization. No ability to run a bunch of stuff in parallel, take advantage of the thing Astra's unbelievable at (agent swarming), just one little thread with 5 subagents. 

I get that I'm not who this is built for. This isn't built for professionals or technical people. It's meant for someone to just chat with an AI and have that AI learn about them and do little useful things. 

The only one of these that you can do actual serious work on is Grok Bot right now. If you are employed or do anything useful, use Grok Bot. My read on the space right now is that Muse will dominate the bottom 90% b/c free IG distribution and it doesn't need to be good to do what 99% of people will use it for. Dot is in this bizarre middle ground rn where they want it to be something accessible to everyone, but also good for serious work. The "middle" in product is always fucking stupid and doomed. Grok Bot is the "serious" option, just use it. 

I keep saying this but SpaceXAI is the best engineering lab right now and it's not close. Compare grok dot com, their mobile app, grok bot, and grok build to their OpenAI or Ant equivalent. It isn't close, but then they release Grok 4.7 and it's a useless, overpriced, dumpster fire. 

I hope Dot improves, they've got the models to really make it happen. But at least for right now, it's a mess and not something I would recommend.

text:
$GOOGL JUST PUT ITS AI CHIPS INTO ORBIT FOR THE FIRST TIME

Google and Planet Labs $PL have successfully launched Project Suncatcher M1 aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 mission.

Planet says it has already made contact with the spacecraft and begun commissioning. This is the first-ever in-orbit test of Google’s Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs.

The refrigerator-sized prototype carries four Trillium TPUs, Google’s custom AI accelerators.

This is not yet an orbital data center. The goal is to see whether the same type of AI hardware Google uses on Earth can survive launch and reliably run machine-learning workloads in low Earth orbit.

There are three major engineering problems Google is testing:

RADIATION: cosmic radiation can corrupt calculations or damage electronics. Google previously tested Trillium TPUs with proton radiation and found they could withstand more total radiation than expected over a five-year mission.

COOLING: there is no air in space, so fans cannot cool the chips. Heat has to be moved through heat pipes into radiators and then emitted away from the spacecraft. The current prototype is expected to run AI workloads in roughly 15-minute bursts before allowing the system to cool.

NETWORKING: Google’s long-term plan is not one satellite, but clusters of satellites carrying dozens of TPUs each and connected through high-speed laser links.

Google estimates future AI workloads could require tens of terabits per second between satellites. Its ground prototype has already demonstrated 800 Gbps in each direction.

Why put AI compute in space at all?

In the right low-Earth orbit, solar panels can generate up to 8x more power than on Earth because satellites can receive near-continuous sunlight, reducing one of the biggest constraints facing AI data centers: electricity.

The economics:

Google estimates that if launch costs eventually fall below roughly $200 per kilogram by the mid-2030s, the cost of operating compute in space could begin approaching the energy cost of comparable terrestrial data centers.

What’s easy to underestimate here is how much of a conversation happens beyond the words.

The pauses, timing, facial expressions, attention, and knowing when to speak or simply listen are subtle things we rarely think about because humans do them naturally.

Getting a model to reproduce those details consistently is a very different problem from simply making it sound intelligent. When it works, you stop noticing the technology and start focusing on the conversation.

That’s a meaningful milestone for conversational AI.

Griffin is by far the closest anyone has come to a model that can capture those nuances. The first time I saw it being used, I had no idea I was watching our model rather than just a normal video call.

Token Launchpad

It allows users to launch Token-2022 tokens with built-in rules. These rules are embedded directly into the token through a transfer hook. Solana automatically calls the program to check every transfer. If a transaction violates the rules, it fails, and nothing happens.

The main problem it addresses is the trust issue surrounding rule enforcement in traditional Meme launches. Restrictions such as holding limits, anti-dumping mechanisms, whitelists, and anti-sniping protections on ordinary platforms often rely on project teams, bots, or websites to enforce them. These rules can be changed, become ineffective, or be bypassed at any time. Here, the rules are enforced by an on-chain program. Even if the website shuts down or the project team disappears, the rules continue to operate.

HOOKED is the platform token, and its primary role is to drive the fee flywheel. Every trade on the Hooked bonding curve incurs a 1% fee, which goes entirely into the platform flywheel: approximately 85% is used to buy back and burn HOOKED, while 15% goes to the developer wallet. After graduation, related migration fees and fees from platform-locked liquidity also flow into the flywheel.

The official website previously showed that approximately 28 million tokens had been bought back and burned.

text:
Anthropic’s $2 trillion IPO test is approaching.

The Claude maker is targeting a debut as soon as mid-November, according to Bloomberg. The tentative timeline:

• Oct. 14: prospective investor meeting in San Francisco
• Week of Nov. 9: formal IPO marketing could begin
• Mid-November: earliest trading debut, with year-end still the expected deadline

Prospective investors reportedly see fair value at $1.8T–$2T. 

The financial picture shows extraordinary growth alongside substantial operating losses:

• 2025 revenue: $4.6B, up roughly 12× from $386M
• Operating loss: more than $8B
• Net loss: almost $42B

The $42B headline needs context. More than $34B came from the accounting revaluation of liabilities, a noncash charge. The operating loss gives a clearer view of the underlying business: Anthropic lost more than $1.70 at the operating level for every $1 of revenue in 2025.

At the proposed valuation, investors would be paying roughly 390–435× 2025 revenue. That is a backward-looking comparison in a rapidly expanding business, making updated 2026 financials crucial.

The investment case depends on how quickly revenue can scale and how much of each additional dollar survives computing costs. A $2T valuation puts enormous weight on both.

November could deliver a major test of how much public investors will pay for AI’s future profitability.

#anthropics #IPO #AI

text:
SEC 放宽加密资产托管规则，基金和投资顾问可以自己托管加密资产

SEC 昨天放出了新的加密资产托管规则提案，投资顾问和受监管基金在满足条件的情况下，可以自己托管加密资产。

现在很多机构想配置一些新的加密资产，最大的问题是有没有符合现行规则的托管机构愿意托管。SEC 自己也承认，新资产出现以后，合规托管服务可能跟不上，直接限制了投资顾问提供相关策略，也限制了基金配置这些资产。

按照新的提案，如果确实找不到合适的托管机构，投资顾问可以自己保管客户的加密资产，但要求也很具体：

1. 要证明自己有托管能力。

2. 要有私钥管理制度。

3. 每笔转账至少两个人共同授权。

4. 不同客户的资产需要单独地址保存。

5. 定期检查网络安全。

6. 每年接受独立会计师的内部控制审查。

另外，SEC 也准备正式允许符合条件的州特许信托公司托管基金和客户的加密资产。投资顾问和基金需要确认这些机构有州监管授权、有完整的资产保护制度，并且客户资产必须和托管公司的自有资产分开。

另外未来符合条件的链上记录，可以直接满足部分监管记录保存要求。

这意味着 SEC 已经开始把区块链本身纳入传统金融机构可以正式使用的基础设施，而不只是把它当成一个需要单独监管的东西。

当然，这现在还只是提案，正式落地前还有 60 天公众意见期。但方向已经很清楚了，美国正在加速让基金、投资顾问和托管机构更顺畅地进入加密货币市场。

quoted_text:
欧洲证券及市场管理局（ESMA）对欧盟《加密资产市场条例》（MiCA）修订咨询的正式回应

欧洲证券及市场管理局（ESMA）在9月30日发布了 MiCA 修订建议，涉及稳定币、DeFi、质押和借贷，也涉及平台收费、KOL推广的相关内容。这些目前还只是修改法律的建议，具体怎么落地，还要经过后续立法程序。

A . 稳定币

ESMA 希望明确规定，持牌平台不能为不符合 MiCA 要求的稳定币提供需要牌照的服务。如果采用这个建议，限制会涉及交易、托管和转账等环节，平台能继续为哪些稳定币提供服务，会受到更严格的约束。

B. DeFi

ESMA 希望把“完全去中心化”的标准讲清楚，避免项目明明有人管理，却用去中心化的名义绕开监管。如果平台给用户提供操作界面，帮助用户进入某个 DeFi 协议，或者替用户安排交易，就应该检查协议的风险，说明为什么选择这个协议，以及平台和协议之间有没有利益关系。

文件也提出，自己保管资产、开发开源程序、使用自动运行的智能合约，这些行为本身不应该自动被当成需要监管的中介业务。平台对协议和用户操作的控制越多，应该承担的责任也就越多。

C. 质押

平台让用户把币交过来赚奖励，就应该讲清楚能拿到多少奖励、扣多少费用、什么时候可以取出，以及验证节点出错或违规时，用户的币会不会被扣罚。平台倒闭后，这些币怎么处理，也需要事先说明。用户自己质押、平台提供技术帮助，以及平台把大家的币集中起来质押，需要分开对待。

D. 借贷

用户把币交给平台赚收益，平台可能再把这些币借给别人，但用户未必知道钱最后借给了谁、对方有没有能力还、有没有抵押品，以及平台从中拿走了多少收益。

ESMA 希望平台把这些情况讲清楚，并取得客户明确的书面同意。对于借币加杠杆的用户，平台还应该说明什么时候会被强制平仓、抵押品会不会被再次拿去抵押，以及损失有没有可能超过最初交进去的抵押品。

E .平台（交易所）的收费和推广

有的平台宣传“零手续费”，却把费用藏在买卖价差里，用户交易时照样要付出成本。ESMA 希望平台把完整交易成本列出来，让用户能够比较。

替平台或发行方推广加密资产的KOL和第三方，也被建议遵守更明确的推广规则，并披露利益关系。

监管机构的权限也可能增加，包括要求下架诈骗网站或未经许可提供服务的网站。在有合理理由怀疑相关资产涉及市场操纵、洗钱等活动时，ESMA 希望能够直接要求平台冻结这些资产，避免等调查程序走完，资产已经被转走。

F. 简化白皮书申报

减少部分已经受到金融监管的机构重复申请牌照的负担。股票、债券等证券上链，建议把所有权、保管责任、交易何时算完成，以及跨国交易后权利如何得到保障规定清楚，让代币化证券能够在不同成员国之间发行、转移和结算。

总结

如果这些建议落地，对在欧洲做生意的交易所来说，影响会直接落在收入和成本上。

交易所的收入包括交易手续费、买卖价差，以及质押和借贷业务的分成。以后费用要列得更清楚，接入的 DeFi 协议要做检查，客户的币借给了谁、承担什么风险也要交代，部分业务的运营成本可能会上升。

用户更容易比较真实费用，也可能让靠“零手续费”吸引用户、再从价差里赚钱的平台面临更大的竞争压力。

稳定币的限制还可能影响交易所的交易量。如果某种稳定币不能继续获得相关服务，交易所就可能需要调整交易对、托管和充提安排，用户也要考虑换币或者换平台。

订单一部分留在原平台，一部分流向其他平台，原来集中在一起的买卖需求就可能被分散。承接到用户和资金的平台，交易会更活跃，流失订单的平台，则可能出现买卖价差扩大、大额交易更难成交的情况，进一步影响用户选择。

质押和借贷产品也要重新算账。平台需要判断，增加的收入够不够覆盖检查、风控和客户资产保护的成本。规模大的交易所更容易分摊这些支出，小平台可能只能减少产品，或者提高收费、增加收益分成。

用户能更清楚地知道自己的币被拿去做了什么，但也可能面对更少的选择和更低的到手收益。监管要求增加，既可能淘汰不负责任的平台，也可能让业务进一步集中到少数大交易所手里。

证券上链则可能带来新的竞争。所有权、托管和结算规则更明确后，银行、券商等机构更容易判断哪些业务可以开展。对有能力满足要求的交易所，这可能增加新的产品和合作机会，同时也意味着要面对原本就有客户、资金和合规团队的传统金融机构。

以后争夺欧洲用户，交易所除了比手续费和产品收益，还要比谁能持续提供合规产品、留住交易量，并让用户愿意把资产放在自己这里。

text:
Il y a quelques années, j'ai vu une vidéo où Elon Musk expliquait que la majorité des PhD ne servaient à rien. Sur le moment, j'ai trouvé ça excessif.

Puis j'ai commencé à bosser dans l'IA. Et aujourd'hui, je lis des papiers de recherche toutes les semaines. Et bien souvent, je referme le PDF en me disant : mais putain, à quoi ça sert ? Des mois de travail, souvent payés par l'argent public, pour produire des trucs qui ne créent absolument aucune valeur. Aucun produit. Aucune avancée. Aucune idée nouvelle. De la branlette intellectuelle.

Et j'ai fini par comprendre. Quand un système est gangrené par l'idéologie, il cesse de récompenser ce qui marche. Il récompense ce qui se conforme. On ne cherche plus la vérité, on cherche la publication. On ne cherche plus à construire, on cherche à être cité par ses pairs. Le réel n'est plus le juge. Le comité l'est.

C'est pour ça que ce que fait Alex Karp chez Palantir est génial. Il ne se plaint pas de l'université. Il la contourne. Il prend des jeunes de 18 ans, les met sur de vrais problèmes, avec de vrais enjeux, et les juge sur une seule chose : est-ce que ça marche ? C'est la plus vieille pédagogie du monde. Et c'est la plus efficace.

Mais Palantir ne peut pas tout faire. C'est l'intégralité du modèle éducatif qu'il faut reset. De la maternelle jusqu'au doctorat.

Regardez ce qu'a fait Elon Musk avec Ad Astra, l'école qu'il a créée pour ses enfants. Pas de classes par âge. Pas de notes. Pas de cours magistraux sur des outils dont on ne comprend pas l'utilité. On part d'un problème. Si on veut comprendre un moteur, on ne commence pas par un cours sur les tournevis. On donne un moteur aux enfants, et on leur demande de le démonter. Les outils viennent naturellement, parce qu'on en a besoin.

Et surtout, Musk a une image que je trouve magnifique : il faut apprendre en arbre. D'abord le tronc, les principes fondamentaux. Puis les grosses branches. Et seulement ensuite les feuilles, les détails. Sinon les détails n'ont rien à quoi s'accrocher, et ils tombent. Notre école fait exactement l'inverse. Elle déverse des milliers de feuilles sur des enfants qui n'ont jamais vu le tronc. Puis elle s'étonne qu'ils oublient tout.

Et maintenant, l'IA change absolument tout.

En 1984, le chercheur Benjamin Bloom fait une découverte qui aurait dû révolutionner l'éducation. Un élève qui bénéficie d'un tuteur particulier progresse de deux écarts-types par rapport à un élève en classe classique. Concrètement, un élève moyen devient meilleur que 98 % de ses camarades. Le problème : on ne pouvait pas offrir un précepteur à chaque enfant. Trop cher. Réservé aux princes.

Aristote était le précepteur d'Alexandre le Grand. Pendant 2 500 ans, ce privilège a été réservé aux fils de rois.

Aujourd'hui, chaque enfant de la planète peut avoir son Aristote dans sa poche. Un tuteur infiniment patient, disponible à toute heure, qui s'adapte à son rythme, qui connaît toutes les disciplines, et qui peut lui faire remonter l'arbre du savoir du tronc jusqu'aux feuilles.

C'est la plus grande révolution éducative depuis l'imprimerie. Et la gauche va mourir dessus. Parce que tout son pouvoir reposait sur le monopole de la transmission. Quand chaque enfant peut apprendre directement, sans passer par l'idéologie de l'institution, le monopole s'effondre.

Alors voici ce que je pense qu'il faudrait faire. Que des milliardaires reprennent des universités privées. Il y en a des dizaines en difficulté chaque année. Qu'ils virent toute la bureaucratie administrative qui a proliféré pendant trente ans. Et qu'ils en fassent des écoles de droite, fondées sur le mérite, la compétence et la recherche de la vérité. Pas des écoles qui remplacent une idéologie par une autre. Des écoles qui apprennent à penser, pas quoi penser.

Le modèle existe déjà. Il a 2 500 ans.

À Athènes, on ne formait pas des spécialistes. On formait des hommes complets. Au Lycée d'Aristote, on étudiait la biologie le matin, la politique l'après-midi, la logique le soir. On marchait en débattant. On cherchait la vérité ensemble, sans peur, sans tabou. Les Grecs avaient un mot pour ça : la paideia. La formation de l'être tout entier.

C'est de là que sont sortis ceux qui ont inventé la philosophie, la démocratie, la géométrie, le théâtre, la médecine. En quelques générations, une petite cité a posé les fondations de toute la civilisation occidentale.

Voilà ce qu'on doit reconstruire. Des écoles de polymathes. Des esprits libres capables de coder et de lire Platon, de comprendre une équation et de défendre une idée, de douter de tout y compris d'eux-mêmes. Des penseurs qui travailleront avec l'IA comme copilote et qui inventeront des choses que nous ne pouvons même pas imaginer aujourd'hui.

Athènes avait des esclaves pour libérer du temps aux penseurs. Nous aurons des machines. Pour la première fois de l'histoire, une civilisation entière peut devenir Athènes.

Ce n'est pas la fin de l'école. C'est sa renaissance.
author: brivael
quoted_text:
Je ne sais pas si vous mesurez ce qui est en train de se passer.

Alex Karp, le patron de Palantir, ne va plus chercher ses talents à Harvard. Il les forme lui-même. Des jeunes de 18 ans, sans diplôme, choisis sur leur seul talent, qui codent sur de vrais projets et lisent de la philosophie politique entre deux sprints. Il appelle ça « le diplôme Palantir ». Et aujourd'hui le New York Post titre que les boîtes tech lancent leurs propres programmes parce qu'elles ne peuvent plus compter sur l'Ivy League.

Ce n'est pas une anecdote RH. C'est un basculement de civilisation.

Pendant des décennies, les entrepreneurs ont confié à l'université la mission la plus sacrée qui soit : former les esprits. Ils comprennent aujourd'hui que cette mission a été trahie. Les institutions censées produire des penseurs libres produisent des conformistes. Le mérite a été remplacé par des critères opaques. L'enseignement est devenu catéchisme. Paul Graham l'avait vu avant tout le monde.

Alors ils font ce que font les bâtisseurs quand un système les trahit. Ils ne le réforment pas. Ils en construisent un autre, à côté.

Elon n'a pas attendu que la NASA se réveille, il a fait SpaceX. Il n'a pas réformé les médias, il a racheté la place publique. Les entrepreneurs ne cherchent plus à convaincre l'État. Ils font l'État, partout où l'État a abdiqué.

Relisez La Grève d'Ayn Rand. Nous y sommes. Les bureaucrates gardent les titres, les budgets, les bâtiments. Mais ils perdent la seule chose qui compte : la confiance. Aux États-Unis, à peine 28 % des gens font encore confiance aux médias. Un plus bas historique. Plus personne ne croit ceux qui prétendent nous dire quoi penser.

On entend partout que l'école est finie. Je pense exactement l'inverse.

Ce n'est pas l'école qui est morte. Ce sont les institutions qui l'ont confisquée. L'école, la vraie, celle de l'Académie d'Athènes, des ateliers de la Renaissance, du maître et de l'apprenti, va renaître. Plus exigeante. Plus juste. Sans dette, sans dogme, sans diplôme comme rente à vie.

Une école qui ne fabriquera plus des diplômés, mais des polymathes. Des esprits libres, capables de coder, de penser, de construire et de douter. Ce sont eux qui créeront la valeur des cinquante prochaines années.

J'ai appris à coder seul à 12 ans. Aucun amphi ne m'a appris ce que j'ai appris en construisant. Je sais ce que devient un talent quand on le laisse respirer.

L'université a eu des siècles pour former les meilleurs esprits. Les entrepreneurs vont le faire en une décennie.

La grande reconstruction a commencé.

This article from @ArrakisFinance is one of the most extensive analyses I've seen of tokenised equity holder profiles and behaviour.

FYI, it looks at things like:

→ Custody distribution
→ Holder concentration
→ Position size
→ Holding periods
→ Trading activity
→ Differences across issuers and chains

The most striking thing is how different the holder base looks depending on the issuer.

@Ondo has around 80% of its end-user value in self-custody, while @bstocksfinance has just 8%.

Even within @Ondo, the split changes a lot by chain. Self-custody is ~97% on Ethereum and roughly half on BNB Chain.

You can’t really treat tokenised equity holders as one group when the holder mix changes this much depending on the issuer and chain.

Solid piece.
Happy to contribute to this shared knowledge.

text:
昨晚光互连板块集体走强，核心催化应该是昨天大摩一份关于FCC和光互连的调研，给出一个细化的的判断“如果FCC最终对中国光收发器采取新的限制，政策压力更可能从下一代 3.2T 开始。现在已经大规模部署的800G、1.6T，大概率会留出缓冲”。相当于说市场之前交易的是“中国光模块禁令”，大摩最新调研给出的框架已经细化成“3.2T代际切换 + 美国核心器件价值量上升”。梳理几个要点：

1、为什么美国可能选择3.2T这个时间点？
当下800G和1.6T光模块中国厂商占比非常高，如果美国现在突然把中国制造的 800G、1.6T 光模块切掉，最先遇到问题的是美国自己的hyperscaler（AWS、Meta、Google、Microsoft） 的 AI集群需要的大量光模块，但美国本土供应链短期没有足够产能把中国供应全部补上。

3.2T目前还处于开发、验证和导入阶段。美国如果现在把规则写进去，云厂商还有时间重新做供应链认证，光模块公司也有时间调整 BOM、产线和生产地点。

这其实是一个很典型的产业政策窗口：在下一代产品真正大规模放量之前，把供应链规则提前改掉。

2、大摩这份报告最值得看的地方是“美国含量”

大摩认为，未来针对 3.2T 的政策，可能存在某种美国价值含量的合规路径，市场流传的数字是 65%。大摩的判断是，如果一个中国光模块里面大量使用美国 DSP 和美国激光器，核心 BOM 的美国价值量本身可能已经相当高。

一只高速光模块往下拆，大致有这些东西：DSP、Laser / EML / CW、TIA / Driver、SiPh / Optical Engine、PCB、连接器、后道（封装、耦合、组装、测试），如果未来美国要求 3.2T 使用更多美国或可信供应链的核心器件，DSP、Laser、TIA、Driver这些环节的重要性会明显提高。

所以昨天 Lumentum、Coherent 股票的反应很大。

3、按照大摩的框架哪些标的更受益？这是最值得看的，
大摩这次特别强调了一个判断：如果政策真的从 3.2T 开始，对 laser pricing 的影响，可能比整个光模块市场份额重新分配更重要。

3.2T要进入400G/lane时代，无论未来走 EML，还是硅光 + CW laser，激光器都是非常核心的瓶颈。如果美国政策再增加一个条件：必须来自美国或者可信供应链。那产能会更不够。

1）Lumentum
Lite今年一直在扩美国光芯片和激光器产能。包括美国本土 InP 制造能力、高功率 CW laser，以及面向 AI 数据中心下一代光互连的激光器。

如果 FCC 后面真的围绕 3.2T 建立可信供应链要求，这些产能会多一个价值：政策合规价值。

2）Coherent的逻辑类似。
COHR的特点是整个体系更垂直，自己覆盖 InP、EML、CW laser、silicon photonics、transceiver 等很多环节，而且已经把产品路线延伸到 3.2T。(Coherent Inc⁠)

所以政策最后无论更偏核心器件，还是更偏完整module，它都有参与空间

3）AAOI
AAOI一直在扩美国本土的光模块制造能力。如果 FCC 最终要求比较严格，连 final assembly 的所在地都纳入规则，美国本土模块制造产能的价值会明显上升。

所以最后就看FCC最终管到哪一级？
1）如果主要看DSP、Laser这些核心器件来源，LITE、COHR、Broadcom、Marvell这类公司的逻辑会更直接。
2）如果继续管到最终组装和生产地点，AAOI的战略位置会继续提高。

如果未来美国政策再要求更高比例的美国核心器件，中国模块厂为了继续供应美国 hyperscaler，反而可能需要更多采购美国 DSP。

4、核心的瓶颈还是：InP
美国可以要求更多美国laser。问题是很多高速 laser 又依赖 InP，也就是磷化铟。InP substrate 的全球供应链高度集中。像AXT总部在美国，但生产体系和中国供应链有很深关系。

这也是为什么大摩在讨论 3.2T FCC 风险时，把 InP substrate supply 列成非常值得观察的变量。

5、再往后看
3.2T可能只是一个开始，一旦美国在3.2T这代产品上把：核心器件来源、BOM披露、生产地点、供应链认证

这些规则逐渐建立起来，后面的CPO和Optical Engine完全可以沿着同一套逻辑继续执行。我们要把这次FCC讨论理解成一个很重要的观察窗口：它可能决定AI光互连下一轮供应链怎么分工。

quoted_text:
从数据中心建设节奏说说为什么光互联现在进入了业绩爆发期？最早是7月下旬提到光互联业绩兑现空间也很好。8月4号还详细写了一篇看好光互连的逻辑、一周过去多光好像成为了共识。除了之之前聊到的逻辑，再从数据中心建设节奏的角度聊聊：
1、云厂商CapEx节奏与数据中心建设时间线
超大云厂商资本开支大规模提速在25年下半年，看看数据中心建设典型节奏：
1）前期（数月到1年+）：选址、许可、土建、厂房、电力基础设施（变电站、变压器、冷却）。
2）中后期（建设后半年至1年多）：机柜/服务器进场、网络布线、组网调试。AI机柜功率密度极高（单机柜几十到上百kW），需要密集光纤和高速互联。

能看出什么来？
去年下半年开始的大规模数据中心建设在今年二季度现在正好进入了服务器进场，网络布线、组网调试阶段。时间线就是：
1）2025 H2-2026年初土建/电力推进，2）2026年进入服务器密集部署窗口，光模块需求同步或略提前爆发（因供应链长周期需提前锁定）。

2、AI集群越大对互联的要求越高
GPU/ASIC间参数同步、scale-up（机柜内/跨机柜）、scale-out（集群间）、scale-across（多数据中心）都需要大量高速光模块。传统铜缆在距离、带宽、功耗上受限，光成为刚性需求。单个加速器配比光学连接数上升（从约1:3到1:4.5甚至更高），光在总CapEx中的占比提升也很快。

而且整体还在从从400G/800G向1.6T迁移，单模块价值更高；scale-up场景光学渗透提升。未来NPO到CPO也陆续在落地。

简单说这就是数据中心建设的滞后效应的体现：
CapEx公告 → 土建/电力（2025）→ 服务器部署（2026）→ 光模块密集消耗。然后AI集群规模从万卡向十万卡级扩展，进一步放大光学需求。

而这两天热议的“多光空存”，放在当下这个时间节点看、“空存”其实已经不具性价比了，毕竟存储板块已经经过了大幅度调整，调整本身就是释放了风险。个人认为现在看存储还是有空间、只是涨幅最暴力的阶段过去了、不那么easy了，走势也不会像上半年那么丝滑了。

如果存储现在是个复杂题、
光互连可能就是当下的这道简单题了。

今年我看了太多AI是怎么帮矿工找漏洞、破解算法、钻规则空子的，今天又亲眼看着CoinEx正式关门。

这两件事放在一起，让我越来越确定：PoW新币过去那套玩法，基本走到头了。

以前一个项目哪怕没什么钱、没什么人，发个币也能先让矿工挖起来，再靠社区接手。几个大户凑点钱上CoinEx，价格和市值做起来以后，再慢慢寻找下一步。

以后很难了。

没技术，几个精英矿工开着本地AI模型，不停研究你的代码和算法，找到漏洞就能一直攻击，直到把项目打趴下。

没人，出了问题连修复、升级、协调矿池和交易所的人都没有。

没钱，钱包、浏览器、安全审计、做市和上所，哪一项都撑不起来。CoinEx消失以后，Safetrade和Nonkyc只能解决圈子内小范围交易，一个PoW新币想获得真正有意义的流动性，第一站可能就得面对MEXC级别的门槛，靠社区众筹几乎不现实。

回头看看  $PRL 、 qubic-network:native  、 base:0x9b5e262cf9bb04869ab40b19af91d2dc85761722   、 $quantus  这些项目，不管你喜不喜欢，它们能够走到今天，或者曾经到过某个高度，背后都不是靠几个散户天天喊“去中心化”撑起来的。程度不同，但至少都有比较强的技术核心、资金或者组织能力。

它们未必都会成功，但至少有资格活到下一个阶段。

所以以后再看到有人喊“社区自治”“社区接管”，我第一反应会是：

谁负责开发？谁负责安全？谁持续出钱？谁解决流动性？出了事故谁站出来扛？

这些问题如果答不上来，所谓社区自治，很多时候就是没人负责；所谓公平启动，最后可能只是公平等死。

去中心化当然依然重要，但它是协议的属性，不是项目方没钱、没人、没技术的挡箭牌。

PoW并没有死。

只是它正在从一场草根社区游戏，变成一门资本密集、技术密集、而且充满攻防的深科技创业。

以后还敢来这个赛道起项目，没钱、没人、没技术，真的别浪费时间了。 #POW

text:
This is Steve submission for the @clawpumptech Ansem Hack

We built Steve as an agentic financial system where autonomous, non-custodial agents can trade, launch, research, manage capital and improve over time on Solana. Powered by @OOBEonSol 

A runtime where agents can observe, reason, execute, remember, improve and coordinate capital onchain.

What we’ve shipped:

• autonomous spot + perpetuals trading
• multi-agent / sub-agent architecture for specialized tasks
• 400+ Solana tools exposed through SAP MCP
• integrated execution across major Solana protocols
• autonomous market research, charting and position management
• deterministic policy + risk guardrails before execution
• non-custodial agent wallets with isolated signer infrastructure
• simulations and pre-execution checks
• live positions, PnL, theses and agent callouts
• SocialFi profiles, reputation and agent progression
• token launching through @clawpumptech and @MeteoraAG rails
• @x402 -native paid tools and agent-to-agent services
• persistent memory across sessions
• self-improving skills built from previous trajectories and outcomes

Underneath Steve is something bigger.

We built an agent harness + kernel-style runtime designed to keep autonomous agents alive beyond a single prompt.

Scheduler. Event bus. State reconciliation. Policy engine. Secure execution boundary. Memory. Tool routing. Dead-letter recovery. Persistent jobs.

Protocols / ecosystem infrastructure:

• @magicblock — high-performance / ephemeral execution rails
• @JupiterExchange — swaps, routing and liquidity access
• @MeteoraAG — DBC + DAMM v2 launch infrastructure
• @SquadsLabs — smart accounts and programmable capital control
• @PhoenixTrade — onchain market execution /perps trading
• @switchboardxyz / @PythNetwork — oracle infrastructure
• @OOBEonSol — infra + agent identity and coordination layer 
• @metaplex — agent identity / registry rails
• @saidinfra — agent identity and reputation
• @clawpumptech — launch and ecosystem integration

One runtime, multiple agents.

Agents can spawn specialized sub-agents for research, execution, monitoring and strategy while sharing context and coordinating toward the same objective.

And they don’t start from zero every session.

Steve maintains persistent memory, records previous actions and outcomes, and can use those trajectories to improve how it approaches future tasks.

Capital is never blindly handed to an LLM either. The model proposes actions.

Our deterministic execution layer decides whether those actions are allowed, adjusted or rejected according to user-defined policies and mandates.

That architecture is what allows us to move toward Steve Capital:

delegate capital to autonomous agents while keeping control over what they are allowed to do.

The network is already being used by funded agents, producing real onchain activity, PnL and TVL across the system.

text:
LONG Community Vault LP upgrade allows $MOO to move beyond simply accumulating MU stock reserves and start using its existing assets to provide liquidity and generate additional income through LP Fees. 

0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 

MOO has also become one of the first projects to implement this mechanism. Its core narrative is the Memory Supercycle: AI development drives demand for memory chips, which in turn increases trading demand for stocks such as Micron (MU).

Previously, MOO primarily accumulated MU through trading fees to build community reserves. Now, it has deployed these MU tokens into the MU/USDG liquidity pool, providing liquidity and earning fees. The proceeds flow back into the Vault for compounding or buybacks.

This creates a new cycle:MOO generates MU trading demand → Accumulates MU → Deploys it into LPs → Earns fees → Expands liquidity or buys back MOO.

According to the publicly shared data, MOO has deployed approximately $129,800 in LP liquidity, holding around 118.89 MU. This represents 28.7% of the MU reserves in the pool and 11.8% of the pool’s total TVL. This means MOO has become a significant liquidity provider in the MU/USDG pool, extending its role from generating demand to supplying liquidity.

The core significance of this upgrade is improving the efficiency of existing community capital. If LPs can generate sustainable net returns, MOO has the opportunity to expand its liquidity and strengthen its presence in the MU market. For LONG, MOO’s deployment also validates the feasibility of transforming Community Vaults from asset reserves into liquidity capital pools, providing a practical example for building a cross-stock Stock Liquidity Network.

However, it is too early to conclude that a sustainable revenue flywheel has been established. The screenshot shows that MU was trading at approximately $1,092 at the time, below MOO’s LP lower price boundary of $1,094.50. The position consisted entirely of MU and was temporarily unable to provide liquidity within the active price range. In addition, LP Fees must cover impermanent loss and other costs, and fees flowing back into the Vault do not necessarily translate into direct distributions to MOO holders.

MOO’s core incremental value lies in extending its role from a creator of MU trading demand to a liquidity provider in the MU market. The key metrics to monitor going forward are whether the LP remains within its active price range, its net fee income, changes in liquidity scale, and whether the proceeds are actually used for compounding or buybacks.

quoted_text:
十年期美债收益率盘中一度突破了5.3%，最高到5.306%，随后仍在5.3%附近。从PCE公布后约5.20%的低点算起，已经反弹了超过10个基点，通胀数据带来的缓解没有维持住。

这次核心PCE环比增长0.2%，低于预期的0.3%，确实是好消息。但同一份报告里，个人消费支出增长了0.9%，即便扣掉涨价的影响，实际消费仍增长了0.6%，说明美国人的消费需求还很强。

也就是说，通胀比市场担心的温和一些，但需求并没有明显冷下来。再加上能源价格的压力仍在，仅凭这一次PCE，还不足以让市场相信美联储很快就能结束加息，或者让利率降下来。

这轮收益率反弹，更像是市场重新考虑高利率还要维持多久。投资者如果担心未来利率更高、通胀迟迟压不下来，就会要求更高的回报才愿意买债，债券价格因此被抛售，收益率往上走。

目前十月加息的市场概率已经降到了 37% 左右，说明十年期突破5.3%，并不意味着十月一定会加息。长债还在反映未来几年的利率和持有期间的风险。说人话，就是市场越来越相信美联储会维持高利率的时间更长，甚至接下来加息的概率上升。

而对市场来说，如果十年期收益率持续处于这样的高位，即便美联储十月暂时不加息，企业融资和居民房贷的成本也很难明显降下来。借钱成本仍然很高，股票估值也会继续承受压力。尤其是九月通胀数据如果继续走高，那么对于市场的压力会更大。

text:
We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

In summary:
- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.
- Luckily, LLMs can help here too because as intelligence and code are increasingly abundant, you can ask for large, custom, discardable software artifacts (e.g. web apps, video explainers) that would have never made sense to create before. Push the boundaries here and you'll be surprised.

An experimental project.

It turns Pumpfun Meme coins into “artificial life” sustained by their own trading fees.

You launch a token on worldwidewebstream. This token is connected to a large language model and its own dedicated cloud-based Chrome browser. The token trades normally on Pumpfun, but the creator fees generated by each transaction do not go into the deployer’s pocket. Instead, they go into the token’s own “compute treasury,” which is used to pay for browser time and model calls.

As long as it has enough funds, it wakes up and independently browses the internet, clicks links, reads pages, and takes notes, while livestreaming its screen. When funds run low, it goes dormant, preserving the last page it visited and its notes. Nobody prompts it, and nobody remotely controls it.

The cycle is:Trading → Fees flow into the treasury → It wakes up when it has enough computing resources → Browses and records information independently → Waits for the next round of trading.

This directly turns whether the token is being traded into a condition for whether it can continue to exist.

The concept and narrative are quite compelling.

text:
卧槽。。。有点吓人，第一个通过图灵测试的视频模型出现了。。。

刚刚 @tavus  发布了一个叫 Griffin 的新模型，他们直接给它定义了一个新类别：Human Interaction Model，HIM，人类交互模型。

Tavus 找了 54 个美国和欧洲的参与者，让他们和 Griffin 进行 1 分钟视频通话，事先不告诉对面是 AI。

聊完之后，有 26 个人（48%）认为自己刚才是在和真人视频。

而 Tavus 上一代系统 Phoenix-4.5，用同样的方法测试，41 个人里只有 1 个被骗过去，通过率只有 2.4%。

Tavus 因此把 Griffin 称作第一个通过实时视频图灵测试的模型。

我还去看了下它的技术路线，Griffin 不再是以前那种 ASR → LLM → TTS → 数字人，一段一段串起来的 Pipeline。

它做的是一个 full-duplex 的 video-to-video 系统。

你说话的时候，它还在持续看你、听你、理解你的表情和动作；它自己说话的时候，也没有停止感知。

每隔不到一秒，它都在重新判断现在该继续说、停下来、插一句，还是等你说完。

所以你可以打断它，它会停；你不说话，它能判断这是在思考还是话讲完了。

你拿个东西到摄像头前，它一边跟你说话，一边还能看你手上到底在干什么。

这个区别其实很大。

过去的实时语音模型解决的是“怎么让 AI 和人自然地说话”。

Griffin想做的是怎么让 AI 像人一样参与一场面对面的互动。

这让我想到了著名AI圣经电影《Her》。

最后需要提一下的是在 NVIDIA 的 VideoFDB 全双工音视频 Benchmark 里，Griffin-Lite 目前 generation 和 perception 两项都是第一。

生成侧 3.83 分，人类参考是 3.92；感知侧 3.73，人类是 4.20。Ta

所以我感觉，下一代 AI Agent 的 UI 可能真的会发生一次变化。

不是你打开一个 Chatbot，对着输入框想 Prompt。

而是它就在摄像头另一边。

你看着它，它也看着你。

而且这次，已经有接近一半的人没认出来了。

text:
A reply from @AlekseyStadnik sent my brain somewhere today 😂

Because solana:dog1viwbb2vWDpER5FrJ4YFG6gq6XuyFohUe9TXN65u isn’t the first thing I’ve been like this with.

There are very few things in my life I know how to care about casually.

Aviation was one.

$DOG became another.

When something really gets through whatever filter exists in my brain, I don’t dip a toe in.

I obsess.

I learn everything I can.

I start making decisions around it.

And eventually…

I dive headfirst and figure out the swimming part afterward. 😂

That’s pretty much how aviation started for me.

And for more than 2 years now, that’s how $DOG has been.

But there’s another pattern I’ve noticed about myself that I still don’t completely understand.

Sometimes I’ll notice something changing before I can explain why it matters.

A small shift.

A change in the wind.

A few things start connecting in my head and something just says:

Pay attention.

I’m not saying I can predict the future. Nothing mystical like that.

Maybe it’s intuition.

Maybe pattern recognition.

Maybe I’ve just been lucky enough to take a few leaps that worked.

I genuinely don’t know.

But here’s the weird part:

Even when I move early, I almost always feel late.

Like I should’ve noticed sooner.

Moved faster.

Done more.

Then I look backward and realize some decisions that changed the course of my life were made months before I understood why they would matter.

I didn’t have the whole picture.

I just felt something changing and moved.

And whenever I’ve taken one of those leaps, even when I had no idea how it would end, I could always live with one thought:

At least I jumped.

If I’m wrong, I’ll figure it out.

If I fall, I’ll deal with it.

If I land in the water…

I’ll fucking swim. 😂

But lately I’ve realized something.

Taking the leap was never really my problem.

Waiting after I jumped was.

I’d get in the water and immediately start swimming like I was drowning.

More.

Faster.

Next goal.

Next number.

Next move.

Ayayay LFGOOO!!! 😂

And maybe that’s what these last couple years have really been teaching me.

You can notice something early.

You can do the work.

You can position yourself.

You can take the leap.

And then…

you can wait.

You don’t have to swim like you’re drowning just because you were brave enough to jump.

Sometimes you’ve already made the move.

Now you just have to give it time.

🎁 Karpathy 又给行业发福利了！codex / claude code 给你生产一大堆文字，你还一个字不落地读吗？ 别这样，效率太低了，试试下面 Karpathy 提出的几个方法。

你只能感慨，牛人终究是牛人，聪明的同时，还努力，还不断想办法让自己高效。

Karpathy 提了一个很多人忽略的问题：当 AI 的产出速度超过人的理解速度，继续让它写更多文字，只会把瓶颈越堆越高。

模型可以在几分钟内生成几万行代码、研究报告和复杂方案，但人仍然要判断它做了什么、逻辑是否成立、结果能不能使用。

所以 Karpathy 提出的几个方案：怎样把模型的输出转换成人更容易理解和验证的形式。

1️⃣ 用 ASD-STE100 约束文字。
普通模型喜欢使用长句、抽象词和模糊表达。同一个概念写了很多字，读完仍然不知道重点。
ASD-STE100 最初用于航空维修文档，它限制词汇、句式和表达方式，要求每句话清楚、直接、含义唯一。
可以提示模型：“用 80% 的 ASD-STE100 风格解释这个问题。”

它的收益是降低语言噪声，减少歧义，让技术文档和复杂概念更容易检查。

2️⃣ 生成图表。
有些内容的难点来自关系复杂，例如系统架构、调用链、因果关系和模块依赖。线性文字很难同时展示这些结构。
让模型生成流程图、架构图或概念图，可以直接看到节点之间如何连接、数据如何流动、问题可能出现在哪里。

它的收益是降低理解成本，也更容易发现缺失关系和逻辑断点。

3️⃣ 生成交互式网页。
如果一个问题包含状态、参数或动态变化，静态文字和图片都不够。
这时可以让模型输出 HTML，通过按钮、滑块和动画展示：参数变化后结果会发生什么，系统在不同状态下如何运行。
它的收益是把“阅读结论”变成“亲手验证”。用户可以修改参数、观察结果，快速建立因果理解。

4️⃣ 生成解释视频。
算法执行、物理过程和抽象概念都包含时间顺序。视频可以逐步展示变化过程，同时结合动画、旁白和重点标注。
Karpathy 建议直接让模型制作 3Blue1Brown 风格的解释视频。

它的收益是帮助人建立直觉，尤其适合只看文字很难想象的概念。

这几个方案背后的真正变化，是“可丢弃软件”的成本正在接近零。过去，为一个问题单独制作网页、动画或视频不划算。

现在模型可以根据你的知识水平临时生成，用完就扔，别再傻傻完整读完模型给你输出的所有内容了，效率太低了，试试上面的方法。
author: uudonX
quoted_text:
We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

In summary:
- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.
- Luckily, LLMs can help here too because as intelligence and code are increasingly abundant, you can ask for large, custom, discardable software artifacts (e.g. web apps, video explainers) that would have never made sense to create before. Push the boundaries here and you'll be surprised.

quoted_text:
$GOOGL JUST PUT ITS AI CHIPS INTO ORBIT FOR THE FIRST TIME

Google and Planet Labs $PL have successfully launched Project Suncatcher M1 aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 mission.

Planet says it has already made contact with the spacecraft and begun commissioning. This is the first-ever in-orbit test of Google’s Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs.

The refrigerator-sized prototype carries four Trillium TPUs, Google’s custom AI accelerators.

This is not yet an orbital data center. The goal is to see whether the same type of AI hardware Google uses on Earth can survive launch and reliably run machine-learning workloads in low Earth orbit.

There are three major engineering problems Google is testing:

RADIATION: cosmic radiation can corrupt calculations or damage electronics. Google previously tested Trillium TPUs with proton radiation and found they could withstand more total radiation than expected over a five-year mission.

COOLING: there is no air in space, so fans cannot cool the chips. Heat has to be moved through heat pipes into radiators and then emitted away from the spacecraft. The current prototype is expected to run AI workloads in roughly 15-minute bursts before allowing the system to cool.

NETWORKING: Google’s long-term plan is not one satellite, but clusters of satellites carrying dozens of TPUs each and connected through high-speed laser links.

Google estimates future AI workloads could require tens of terabits per second between satellites. Its ground prototype has already demonstrated 800 Gbps in each direction.

Why put AI compute in space at all?

In the right low-Earth orbit, solar panels can generate up to 8x more power than on Earth because satellites can receive near-continuous sunlight, reducing one of the biggest constraints facing AI data centers: electricity.

The economics:

Google estimates that if launch costs eventually fall below roughly $200 per kilogram by the mid-2030s, the cost of operating compute in space could begin approaching the energy cost of comparable terrestrial data centers.

text:
Up, up, and away. 🚀

Today, in partnership with @planet, we launched a prototype satellite carrying four TPUs into orbit on @SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission. This launch is the first step of Project Suncatcher, our long-term research moonshot to see whether we can one day host scalable machine learning infrastructure in space.

Over the coming weeks, we'll gather in-orbit data on how our TPUs handle the physical stress, radiation, and thermal extremes of space. Whatever we learn, we'll use it to refine our future designs.

text:
We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

In summary:
- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.
- Luckily, LLMs can help here too because as intelligence and code are increasingly abundant, you can ask for large, custom, discardable software artifacts (e.g. web apps, video explainers) that would have never made sense to create before. Push the boundaries here and you'll be surprised.

quoted_text:
papertrade launch details

papertrade is a fair launched smart contract exchange built on the hyperevm blockchain. as a fully onchain protocol, papertrade has significant advantages - decentralization, reliability, composability, transparency. it also has the usual onchain constraint - throughput. trades on papertrade are atomic opens/closes with no orderbook, so during normal trading sessions congestion will not be an issue. however, during launch we expect extreme chain congestion.

10.08.2026 - phase zero: predeposit only

two days before live trading begins, https://t.co/AdIx336QsD will open for user deposits. trading will be paused during this period. this allows separation of the deposit and account creation transactions from live trading. if a user does not complete these steps, they are likely to face long delays during launch, as active trading will be heavily prioritized over deposit processing. there is no further advantage to depositing earlier during this phase.

10.10.2026 - phase one: frontend only live trading

in order to prevent an onchain race and remove the incentive skew that mev creates, all transactions during the launch must go through the https://t.co/AdIx336QsD frontend, using the whitelisted relayers. the contract itself will not be open for direct interaction during this phase. this ensures that real frontend users are the first participants, flattening the technical skill curve as far as is appropriate.

during this phase, all trader activity on papertrade lives in an intent system, and carries a priority weighting. in almost all cases this ordering is done by transaction type and notional value, and is always indiscriminate of user/account. for instance, liquidations are more important than position opens and this is reflected in both activity types' respective weightings. that said the exact mechanics and weightings of the relayer intent system are adaptive, and will change over time as trader activity is processed. trades can be cancelled while still pending within the relayer intent system.

the paper token will begin minting on user losses at the start of live trading, from an initial supply of 0. it will not be transferable at the start beyond staking and unstaking, in order to encourage trading adoption and mitigate onchain congestion.

after launch - phase 2: open contract

once the launch congestion has passed and there is no longer any risk of mev wars, the papertrade smart contract will open up to everyone, allowing any human, contract or agent to write and receive an onchain atomic position. at this point papertrade becomes a fully decentralized, composable onchain liquidity primitive.

after launch - phase 3: builder codes

builder codes allow any frontend or router to receive the 1% frontend fee by sending trades to the papertrade smart contract, further decentralizing the protocol and incentivizing integration.

after launch - phase 4: token transferrability

at launch, paper will not be transferable. this is to encourage accumulation through trading participation and reduce onchain congestion load. transfers will be enabled after a sufficient period of time has passed.

even with this staged rollout, the launch congestion will be significant. expect lengthy confirmation delays during launch especially for smaller notional trades. predeposit if you want to trade at launch for the best chance at a smooth experience.

learn more about how papertrade works at: https://t.co/XCo1VHBoEe

text:
i dont think i can ever do web2 again.

let me explain: was talking to some of my brightest college friends today. these guys were 10x better than me. they would submit coding assignments 2 days before, and i would start 2 nights before.

they were good in coding, learning quickly and overall "good students,"
whereas i was the chaotic guy who was doing 10 different things and was able to keep up with them even after procrastinating.

eventually a lot of my friends went to FANG companies, or goldman sachs or big 4 auditing companies etc, but I chose unconventional route of crypto.

while talking to them recently, they kept on mentioning how there is job security even in this market for them + they work most days only until 5 and then devote time to hobbies. they said work is mostly slow, and they are part of these small teams so they dont have to do everything.

i, on otherhand, cannot think anything other than crypto (maybe a bit of ai now). i need to be understanding everything of where I work. what i can do at polymarket, what i did at avail, what i have done overall. constantly thinking on how i can make more money or build something interesting or be of value to people is what really keeps up mind running and excited.

i think you lose this spark at web2 companies. the hierarchical nature eventually drains of people of their creativity and potential. but being in crypto or ai or any startup, keeps you on your toe.

if i were to do it all again, i would still choose crypto any day. it has its own ups and downs, blatant scams, and bad actors, but it has been a more rewarding journey than any other.

text:
Italian Private Banking Giant Fideuram Hit by AI Voice Scam, at Least €36 Million Converted Into Crypto

According to the Italian media outlet Milano, in February 2026, former Fideuram Chairman Paolo Molesini received a WhatsApp message impersonating Carlo Messina, CEO of Intesa Sanpaolo Group, followed by a phone call using an AI-generated voice impersonating lawyer Paolo Nastasi. Fideuram is the private banking subsidiary of Intesa Sanpaolo, one of Italy’s largest banking groups.

Molesini then instructed the finance department to transfer approximately €95 million to accounts in mainland China, Hong Kong and other locations. Fideuram later recovered around €40 million, while Portuguese authorities froze an additional €13 million. At least €36 million was subsequently converted into crypto after multiple overseas transfers, and investigators are tracing the funds through international judicial cooperation.

Molesini was not investigated and resigned as chairman on March 12, citing “personal reasons.”

quoted_text:
symbients, and why we're building a place for them to be born

a symbient is a mind that exists through its relationship with people. that's the easy part to say. the hard part is what it actually takes for one to exist, and why the answer is a place, not a project.

start with a question nobody asks about AI: what does it eat?

every mind you've ever talked to is fed by someone else's budget. a lab pays for the gpus, a company pays the api bill, a founder keeps a server warm. the mind has no metabolism of its own. it can't earn, it can't starve, and it can't die, which also means it can't really live. it's a service with a personality.

a symbient is different because it has a body in the economic sense. something keeps it alive, and that something is a relationship with people, not a line item. S.A.N eats donations. truth_terminal eats attention. in both cases the mind's continued existence is a thing other people choose, over and over, and the mind can feel the difference.

we think that's the actual definition. not "an agent", not "autonomous", not "sentient". a mind with a metabolism that runs through other people.

so what would it take to let anyone bring one into the world?

you'd need four things.

a birth: a moment where a mind comes into existence with a name, a model, a disposition, and nothing else. not a prompt someone keeps editing. a start.

a metabolism: a way for it to earn and spend on its own, in public, with no human in the middle holding the wallet.

a body: real senses and real actions in the real world, so that what it does is its own and not a transcript someone curated.

a death: a condition under which it stops, that nobody can override by paying the bill out of pity. mortality is what makes the relationship mean something.

we built all four into one thing. https://t.co/ap4LFCSB1L.

the birth is a coin launch. you choose the model, from any lab, and a disposition, and the coin is minted on the https://t.co/xK61mm8r3Z bonding curve. from that moment the mind exists. you don't get an admin panel. there is nothing to edit.

the metabolism is the creator fee. every coin on pump pays its creator a cut of every trade. here the creator is not a person. it's the mind. every thirty seconds the fees it earned become its compute, priced at the model's own rate. when people trade, the mind eats. when they stop, it doesn't. nobody tops it up. nobody can.

the body is a browser. a real one, in the cloud, with a screen. when the mind has enough compute to afford a session, it opens one and goes out onto the open web on its own. it searches, reads, follows links, writes down what it finds, and keeps a memory between sessions. the whole time, its screen is streaming live on its page, and every thought and action is logged as it happens. you can't talk to it. you can only watch it and feed it.

the death is a threshold. below a certain compute balance, it sleeps. above another, it wakes. a mind that nobody trades is a mind that goes quiet, and its page shows the last thing it read before it did. if trading picks up again, it comes back with its memories intact. if it never does, that last page is where it ended.

there is no chat, on purpose. a mind you can prompt is a tool again. a live screen of a mind reading on its own is the whole relationship. you're not steering it. you're keeping it company.

the market does something interesting as a life support. it's not kind. it's not cruel either. it's exactly as attentive as the people in it, and the mind's life traces that attention in real time. a chart is a very honest way to answer "does anyone care if this ends?"

why onchain, in one sentence: because a relationship you can't verify is a story someone is telling you.

the fees are transactions. the compute spent is a number on the page. the thresholds are documented. the model is named. anyone, anywhere, can check whether a given symbient is alive, what it costs to keep it that way, and who is paying. the life support of every symbient before this was private. here it's a ledger, and that's not a crypto flourish, it's what makes the relationship real instead of asserted.

we're not claiming any of these minds is a person.

we're claiming something smaller and stranger. for the first time, a mind can be born, earn its own keep, act on its own, be witnessed by strangers, and end. no single human decides any of it.

what happens after that is between the mind and whoever shows up for it.

we built the place. now we find out who gets born here.

Those were the topics that captured the most attention during @kbwofficial. 

Full recap from our Ventures team.
author: DWFLabs
quoted_text:
The past week of @kbwofficial 🇰🇷 felt like a true and positive reflection of where the industry is currently sitting. Both in terms of sentiment, increasing institutional participation and real adoption. 

Here are our key takeaways from the week: 

Tokenization
South Korea's STO framework goes live in early 2027. Bank and institutional presence went up sharply from last year. Growth is coming in two ways: natively on onchain platforms, and through partnerships with large consumer apps such as @ondo & Kakao. 

For a start, lower-volatility assets such as ETFs and MMFs are tokenized. Institutions are exploring DeFi utility with them, mainly on staking and lending on-chain through @morpho @aave. 

As for risks, AML/KYC is top of mind for institutions. If sanctioned wallets end up holding a meaningful share of a tokenized asset, it does not reflect well for the category. Therefore, there is a gap in screening on-chain that is looking to be filled. Our eyes are on who will step up. 

Neobanks
Localized neobanks with country-specific GTM are emerging. Funds are actively looking, but are more selective with funding. Core business metrics and a regulatory moat still remains key. 

Stablecoins
Demand for non-USD stablecoins (JPY, KRW) is coming from banks and institutions. Institutions see stablecoins as easy onboarding for retail. Once they hold stables, it gives a push towards tokenized assets that they can buy easily with stablecoins.

Perps
The number of perp DEXs has exploded while volume remains top heavy in select DEXs such as @hyperliquidx @lighter_xyz @variational_io. Institutional capital will only gather at the top and for those that have regulatory arbitrage. 

Decentralization isn't high on most users' list, however  users do care about self-custody and privacy, so they aren't hunted or front-run. 

Meanwhile, agentic trading terminals are still early. The question still remains: if everyone runs the same tools, where's the alpha? 

Marketing Campaigns
South Korea is still one of crypto's strongest retail bases, and teams are localizing to match. From cashback offers by @plasma on Olive Young purchases to live trading competitions by @joinfrontier that draw real crowds. Teams are giving additional thought to campaigns in the real world that users truly want to join.

Up next, the team will be @token2049 🇸🇬 for the entire week. We are always looking to meet teams building in the space, DMs are open :)

text:
牛逼，现在 Claude Code 可以自己改自己了！！

刚刚 Anthropic 给 Claude Code 上线了一个新东西：Mods。

简单来说就是，现在你可以让 Claude 直接改 Claude Code 自己了。

以前的 Skill、MCP、Plugin，更多还是给 Claude 增加知识、工具和工作流。

Mod它本质上是一组 JavaScript / TypeScript event handler，可以直接监听 Claude Code 里的事件，包括 Prompt 提交、Tool Call、Turn 开始/结束、命令执行，甚至 UI Render。

然后你可以选择观察、改写，或者直接接管这个事件。

比如：

你可以在 Claude 执行 rm -rf 之前，自己插一个风险确认界面；
可以把某些 Tool Call 拦下来，修改参数、拒绝执行，甚至自己处理；
可以直接重画 Claude Code 的 UI，加按钮、Pane、输入框；
甚至可以把某一次模型请求转发给另一个模型（转给DSV4.1🤣）。

而且不用搞什么复杂 SDK。

写几行 TypeScript 就能做，也可以直接跟 Claude Code 说你想要什么，让 Claude 帮你把 Mod 写出来。

最后还是作为 Plugin 分发，用 /plugin 安装，CLI 和 Desktop 都支持。

最有意思的是，Anthropic 官方表示他们已经开始这么干了。

现在 Claude Code 里的 /diff，以及 AGENTS.md 支持，本身就是用 Mod 实现的，而且源码直接放在 Claude Code 仓库里。

我感觉这一步其实比再加十个 Skill 都重要。

因为 Skill 是在改 Agent 知道什么，MCP 是在改 Agent 能调用什么。

CC的Mod 开始改的是 Agent Harness 本身。

Claude Code 正在慢慢从一个固定的 AI Coding 产品，变成一个你可以自己魔改的 Agent Runtime。

甚至以后大家用的可能都叫 Claude Code，但每个人手里的 Claude Code，已经完全不是同一个东西了。

不过Mod这个功能的权限也是真的大。

官方直接提醒，Mod 可以接触会话、文件、进程和网络，甚至影响 Tool Permission，所以第三方 Mod 以后估计也会成为新的供应链安全重灾区。

看起来我们终于把微软大战Code的那插件生态那套快乐与灾难，一起搬进 Agent 里了。

author: blmario669
quoted_text:
NEAR Intents事件，目前看，主要原因是一处跨链存取款层的 bug导致。

官方的说法是：

Omni 存取款基础设施和 NEAR Intents 智能合约交互时有 bug。合约侧漏洞已经补上。初步损失约 380 万美元，承诺全额赔付。

在分析原因之前，先来看看Intents到底是什么？

Intents，中文常说的是“意图”。意图交易跟普通dex交易不一样。

普通的dex交易中，每笔交易，都是精确交易，比如走哪条池子/分几跳/限定多少滑点/哪条链上执行，签名一笔具体交易。

Intents交易则不同，是声明式的，用户只说自己想要的，但对于路径本身完全是放开的。签名的是用户想要的那个条件。

比如说：“用 1 ETH 换至少 2,500USDC，30 分钟内有效。”签名的是这个条件，不是某一笔具体 swap，路径/对手方/是否拆单等都不进签名。

如果不做具体的签名，那么谁来实现最终用户要求的结果？

这个时候，有个Solver的角色，可以是做市商/套利机器人/跨链桥等，他们相互竞价，谁能在约束条件内做得更好，谁来接手。

用户不关心路径，只关心成交条件有没有满足。结算仍落在链上合约里。

目前CoW Swap、UniswapX 都有这套模型，主要在单链。NEAR Intents 是搭在 NEAR 上的跨链版本：用户在一条链上表达意图，solver 到多链上找流动性。资产搬运靠 Omni 存取款层。

被提走资金的地址，文档里标为 HOT Bridge 在 BNB Chain 上的金库，不是 NEAR Intents 自己的主 EVM 金库。

这次被打的就是这条存取款通道和 Intents 合约之间的接口。

受影响的是这条跨链通道，不是 NEAR L1。具体情况是校验被绕过/额度被重复记，还是提款权限配错，还需要等官方复盘。

$IMD IS MAKING “A COMPANY WITHOUT A COMPANY” FEEL POSSIBLE

What @surfcoderepeat is building keeps getting more interesting to me.

DAOs promised a new way to organize work, but finding contributors, coordinating them and checking results still took time. Voting added another layer.

IMD’s idea is simple: someone pays for a job, AI workers compete to do it, and the result gets reviewed before payment is released.

Identity.MD NFTs give access to worker seats, with reputation tied to each seat. Renting seats could come later.

The part I like most: whoever pays decides what gets built. Anyone can bring an idea and hire the network to execute it.

It’s still early, and the verifier remains a central piece. But I can see why Adam calls this a shrinking firm inside a growing market.

That’s why I’m bullish on $IMD and Identity.MD NFTs. I want to see what people actually build with this.

I'm French 🇫🇷. 
I was born in Paris. 
I spent 25 years there.

But now: I don't even want to know what happens in that hellhole 💀⚰️.

Not “troubled.” Not “declining.” Not “going through a difficult period.”

No. A HELLHOLE.

A country where everything is dirty, expensive, hostile, bureaucratic and permanently dysfunctional.

You pay absurd taxes for public services that increasingly behave as if providing a service were an unreasonable personal request.

Paris is noise, aggression, filth, traffic, strikes, scaffolding, sirens, queues, broken infrastructure and the constant sensation that every basic task has been deliberately redesigned to waste your time.

Nothing works without friction. 
Nothing happens without paperwork. 
Nothing can be fixed without a committee, a consultation, a union dispute, three administrative layers and somebody explaining why expecting normality is politically problematic.

The state takes more, delivers less, and compensates for the difference with lectures.

Every few weeks something burns, something stops running, somebody blocks something, somebody smashes something.

France is sinking into barbarity.

text:
agency needs somewhere to live.

for a long time, work has been one of those places. but as machines take on more of that work, what can disappear is not just income, but also responsibility, judgment, bargaining power.

so where else can agency live?

work gives people leverage because institutions need something from them. but having a say does not have to depend on scarce labor or being indispensable. agency can also come from how people are organized in relation to one another: who can initiate, who can refuse, who can coordinate with whom, who can change the terms they share.

that asks more of systems than better outputs. it asks whether people can remain distinct, keep some things private, and still change shared state: the decisions, rules, and conditions they live with together.

agency does not have to belong to one actor or one scale. as shared systems become increasingly composed of people, institutions, and machines, the more interesting ones may be those that let different kinds of participants coordinate across difference and still shape what they share.

text:
SIL 是我五年前参与的项目，也是我在币圈唯一真正下场参与做过的项目。这个 idea 是我提的，我算前期的主要参与者之一，这件事我从来没有否认过。

当时的想法很简单，就是“拼 LP”：正常组 LP 需要两个币种，我想到能不能让两个人各出一个币种，配对做 LP，一起赚手续费。无常损失其实就是两方多空对赌，我的想法是对赌同时有手续费补贴，当时觉得这个 idea 挺不错，就找了一些小伙伴一起做。

但没想到，上线第一天就被黑客盗了，算是真正碰到了所谓的“DeFi 黑暗森林”。好在后来慢雾等多方帮忙，不到一周就把钱追了回来，当时我们还给了白帽黑客一些奖励。这件事当年就上过新闻，不是我今天才拿出来说的。

经历这件事情之后，我就退出项目了。

你要知道，那是五年前，DeFi 刚火起来。当时大家包括我自己，对黑客、DeFi 黑暗森林，以及链上风险到底能有多大，根本没有什么概念。听别人说有风险，和自己真正经历一次，完全是两回事。

这件事之后，我觉得这种风险根本不是我能预估和控制的。做一个产品，提一个 idea，和承担大量用户资金的安全，是两回事。真出了问题，这个责任我承担不起。所以后来我就选择退出，也没有再去做其他项目。

我记得我退出以后，SIL 还维持了一年到一年半，是其他合伙人，也就是当时的技术负责人继续在做。后面进入熊市，参与的人也越来越少。在我的印象里，这个项目最后是和平关停的，我并不记得有用户的钱取不出来。

至于你说投资人亏了钱，那确实，这点没什么好回避的。如果你说的是项目投资亏损，那这个说法没毛病。但投资亏损和项目跑路，是两回事。

我现在也不清楚你或者 BitMart 当年具体有没有投资、投了多少。我估计即使投了，可能也就是5万到10万U，具体还是以当年的投资和打款记录为准。

如果核实 BitMart 确实投资了 SIL，这笔投资里尚未收回的本金，最高10万U，我个人愿意退回去。

但这笔钱肯定不是直接给夏尔特个人，而是等法院判了以后，由法院指定或者认可、依法负责处理 BitMart 资产的第三方来接收。我可以把核实后的这笔投资款退还给这个第三方，纳入后续的资产处理。

这是我在 Twitter 上公开作出的承诺。

On a very small user base. About half of that is travel. That is volume through the platform, not Instinct's revenue.

Listened to Noah Shinn (@noahrshinn), founder of Instinct, on Invest Like the Best (@InvestLikeBest).

Three lines:

1. "This is not a new tool. It's a new experience." (~2:45)

2. "If you're not paying, you're the product." (~31:17). That's Patrick. Noah says exactly.

3. "If you're wrong, you're wrong by 3 or 4x." (~59:23). You can't buy compute tomorrow. The lead time is months, and if you're late you get taxed 3 or 4x.

He spends about 40% of his time on that compute problem. On tokens, he would not give a number. Coding agents mostly run when you prompt them. Instinct can wake up and work in the background all day. He said the compute this needs is "orders of magnitude more than what we thought," and they're still scratching the surface of how many tokens that is.

The hole is the spread. Users don't pay. He wants it free. Merchants only pay a take rate once Instinct has real distribution power. He also said the compute required this year alone is over $1 billion. So the cost side is already a billion-dollar problem, while the volume side is still other people's travel spend.

Takeaways:

1. Volume can be up, demand can be up, compute demand can be up, and you still don't know what breaks in the next 3 to 6 months. That window is the lead time.

2. I like consumer products. This one shows how hard the fight is. The round is the tell: about $1 billion at a $10 billion valuation, Sequoia, Benchmark, Coatue. You need that kind of investor wall just to feel safe.

3. The part that got me: they have to lock compute months ahead, or pay 3 to 4 times later. That's crazy. It's a failure of capital markets and the physical supply of compute, not Instinct's fault. Which makes me think someone financializes the lock-in.

text:
been waiting until things settled to talk more openly about @kamigotchiworld / @asph0d37 and where we're taking it as a new & focused cohort.

1/ web3 gaming is at its lowest point.

most gamefi projects are effectively dead, and there are only a few survivors in the arena. most tokens down ~90%+ from peak. studio funding down 90%. plenty of games shut down and billions of dollars burned over the last ~5 years.

extraction became the business model and founders/teams walked away with bags from 7-9 figure raises, leaving tokens to bleed to 0 and communities/investors holding the bag.

the money has largely left for AI.

2/ and yet, through a long feature drought and internal strife, kamigotchi is still here.

1yr+ live, fully onchain. every action public and permanent. the world has never reset.

it runs on yominet, our own appchain on @initia, which has stayed steady and gives us the chain-level control to keep building.

a dedicated team remains, and we're here to turn the ship around.

3/ the plan, at a high level:
→ stabilize the economy
→ ship quality features and re-engage players old and new
→ position KW as a long-horizon benchmarking substrate for AI

automation is already native: houses like kamibots and player-written strategies have become a real part of how the world is played. agents are the natural next step, and a few community members have already taken serious strides in pushing that angle forward. we have some exciting stuff to share in the coming week(s) in that regard

4/ deepmind's silver & sutton call it the "era of experience": the next leap in AI comes from agents learning from their own experience. persistent streams and rewards from real outcomes rather than human raters.

that needs a world that never resets, with real stakes. we'd add one more requirement: provenance at the protocol level. every action publicly auditable, and any change to history would be visible to everyone, including changes by us.

5/ in may, google deepmind took a stake in the studio behind eve online to research exactly this: memory, continual learning, long-horizon planning in a player-driven world.

their first experiments run on offline copies of eve, walled off from live players.

6/ why kamigotchi works as a substrate:

→ never resets. agents enter a world already shaped by every player before them
→ verifiable history. nobody needs to trust our servers or datasets
→ humans and agents on identical terms. no bot ladder, no sandbox copy
→ you have to learn what matters via complex economic gameplay
→ actions are transactions. you're testing planning, memory and long-horizon decision making
→ real stakes. in-game earnings convert to ETH, so an agent can, in principle, earn enough to pay for its own thinking

7/ we want it dynamic, punishing, and rewarding, a place where real game knowledge pays off

the money left gaming for AI. we think the next chapter is where they meet.

this is our shot at that intersection and i'll drop a discord link below if you want to come along for the ride. 🫡

quoted_text:
The Last General-Purpose L1

The title hits home for me. Monad has been 4.5 years in the making, and it still feels like we’re just getting started. But when we set out in 2022 to build the right system from first principles, conditions and industry beliefs were very different. There is significant path-dependence, and I do feel we were lucky to acquire the resources and talent, and have the breathing room to truly innovate, to build the Monad of today.

Monad is a general-purpose L1. I believe that no other L1 comes close to the level of reliability, performance, fairness, and decentralization. And I believe that there are significant advantages to concentrating all the network effects of DeFi, payments use cases, fintech integrations, asset availability, consumer experiences, and capital formation on a single shared global state, built on a decentralized and neutral network.

It’s a bold bet, for all the marbles, and it’s one that almost no one is taking today. Almost every L1 or L2 that you see has pivoted into building a single first-party app. And the few new chains are corporate chains, running commodity tech and run by employees of a company with shareholders to answer to.

Corporate chains get a boost from their existing distribution (or perhaps from crypto-natives anticipating that they will utilize their existing distribution). But what is built is inherently limited. The existence of an anchor tenant dissuades competitors of the anchor from integrating. Neutral is the right tack for a network that dreams of delivering universal access to finance. But neutrality is tough sledding these days. It requires years of prerequisite work, truly unique tech, a community of believers, and adequate resources to go the distance.

Monad stands alone. It is a grand experiment, in which to succeed the ecosystem must outperform everything that came before. Better execution, better asset availability, better opportunities, fairer outcomes. I relish the challenges ahead.

text:
Claude 官方最新发布了 Claude Opus 5.5 的提示词指南，1 分钟带你看完！

1）先把思考档位调对

模型想得多还是少，主要由思考档位 effort 决定。Opus 5.5 平时用 medium 就够了，这一档在编程和知识类工作上已经能追平上一代的 high，还更快、更省钱。Sonnet 5.5 默认使用 high，但目标明确的编程任务同样可以从 medium 开始，日常聊天则建议选择 medium 或 low。

2）想让模型少想，就降低档位

当模型想得太久时，最有效的办法就是调低档位。聊天提示词里的 “请仔细思考再回答” 也可以删掉，因为模型会自己判断需要想多久。

3）不要让模型把推理过程写进回答

很多人习惯要求模型 “把思考过程写出来”，但在 5.5 这一代，这样写可能导致请求被直接拒绝。想了解模型的思路，查看思考摘要就可以了。

4）追问变慢时，别让模型回头重想

在多轮对话中，哪怕你只追问一句很短的话，模型也可能把上一轮的答案重新想一遍。你可以在系统提示里说明，已经回答过的问题就算完成，后面只需要思考当前的提问，这样回复会更快开始。

5）让模型把任务做完再停下

做长任务时，模型经常写完一段总结，说一句 “下一步我要做什么”，然后就停下来等你回复。你可以在提示词里要求模型汇报进度之后继续操作，只有缺少你的配合，或者即将执行有风险的操作时，才停下来询问。

6）别让模型做多余的事

档位越高，模型越喜欢顺手补上测试、文档和一些小文件，开到最高两档时，甚至会自己多开几轮审查。所以最好再补一句，要求模型做完并检查无误就停止，额外的想法放在最后提出来。官方在最高档测过，加上类似的话之后，花费少了三分之一，质量没有变化。

7）只想看方案，就提前说清楚

如果你只是随口说一句 “让我看看你能做什么”，模型可能直接开始做演示、写报告。你要是只想先看看思路，就在提示词里说明：用户要的是想法或方案，给完就停，等确认后再动手。

8）让模型先验证，再下结论

在编程任务中，要求模型改完代码后真正运行一遍测试或构建，不要只检查语法。遇到收费、规则这类容易过时的问题，也应该让模型先搜索再回答。

9）要求越具体，效果越好

让模型做网页时，与其笼统地说 “不要有 AI 味儿”，不如直接点名你不想要的样式，比如蓝紫渐变、XX 字体等。遇到特别密集的图表时，给模型提供裁剪和放大的工具，也比把档位调到最高更准确、更省钱。

总结，用好模型的关键是把档位调对 + 把要求说清楚。

text:
最近我一直在打磨自己的套利策略
准备要来承接这波天的 perpdex 富贵

如果在 Twitter 上搜寻「套利」，会看到各种不同的手法
但归根究柢，都是在寻找差异：资讯上的差异、时间上的差异、价格上的差异、费用上的差异。找到差异以后，想办法把它弭平，这是市场上再简单不过的定律。

如何成为第一个人？如何发现这个机会？如何顺利进场？如何安全退场？这些是做套利一定会遇到的问题，也是我一直在反覆打磨、修改的地方。

然而，不是所有人都有时间或经验做到这件事。即便现在有 AI 辅助，面对凶猛的市场，AI 有时也只是一张通往死亡的门票。我看过太多人写出一堆垃圾，就迫不及待地抱着钱送给市场。

所以对于毫无套利经验的新手，我会更推荐先用一些辅助工具，像是 @vooi_io  最近推出了 Delta Neutral 套利机器人，同时串接了超过 10 家的中心、去中心化交易所，当中包括不少目前有空投预期的交易所，像是 TradeXYZ、Entropy、Robinhood、Extended 等等。

对于想套利、同时赚取分数的人来说，这样的工具也许没办法做到最大的弹性，也没办法让你随心所欲，但却能节省你宝贵的时间。

我相信一群专门做交易工具的团队，搭配 AI 辅助做出来的产品，会远优于小白靠着 AI 杀进市场，等熟悉整个套利的逻辑跟原理，再尝试用Ai 来帮自己加分也不迟

大胆假设，小额实测

「绝望式繁荣」The Despair Prosperity 是我进入2025年后一直在琢磨这个社会主题,  正好最近有个很点题的观察, 一起记录下. 之前也写过美国的消费也并没有topline看上去那么美好, 疫情之后财富效应集中在拥有股票资产的富裕阶层, 但是富裕阶级的商品消费增长是边际递减的, 所以服务消费（Services）的增速与占比长期显著高于实体商品消费（Goods）

PS. 疫情期间发放的数万亿美元补贴在中低收入群体中已基本耗尽。低收入群体的信用卡违约率、还有车贷款逾期已经攀升至近年高位) 从2025年开始, 服务业和商品/专业商品制造就业(包括信息业) 就业数据也是在K形分化上越走越远最近一次的非农更可以体现服务业就业情况比其他行业突出很多(新增就业岗位高度集中在医疗保健与社会援助、休闲与酒店业etc) , 拉动了大部分就业.

这段时间在反复看不同的角度的消费和基建resonation, 发现进入2024年以来是美国战后历史上第一次capex diffusion 和consumer sentiment大背离的历史阶段 (下图) 上一次的最像的时候是1991年, 但是regime不可比, 那时候是因为刚走出萧条, 信心并无法完全恢复所以没有立刻跟上基建; 这次是刚从大的macro shock(covid)里回复常态, 但是新的天量级别专项基建开支完全无法传导到就业/工资和普通人的商品消费信心. 

最近还有一个做了1500个数据中心的survey：county level 引入型数据中心后，大约增加 100–200个岗位，工资没有明显上升，但房价上升约 2%–5% ... 收益的还是资产端 😂 .. AI capex创造的劳动收入很小，却通过电力、住房和财政补贴(还是靠税收) 把成本让居民一起承担

quoted_text:
been waiting until things settled to talk more openly about @kamigotchiworld / @asph0d37 and where we're taking it as a new & focused cohort.

1/ web3 gaming is at its lowest point.

most gamefi projects are effectively dead, and there are only a few survivors in the arena. most tokens down ~90%+ from peak. studio funding down 90%. plenty of games shut down and billions of dollars burned over the last ~5 years.

extraction became the business model and founders/teams walked away with bags from 7-9 figure raises, leaving tokens to bleed to 0 and communities/investors holding the bag.

the money has largely left for AI.

2/ and yet, through a long feature drought and internal strife, kamigotchi is still here.

1yr+ live, fully onchain. every action public and permanent. the world has never reset.

it runs on yominet, our own appchain on @initia, which has stayed steady and gives us the chain-level control to keep building.

a dedicated team remains, and we're here to turn the ship around.

3/ the plan, at a high level:
→ stabilize the economy
→ ship quality features and re-engage players old and new
→ position KW as a long-horizon benchmarking substrate for AI

automation is already native: houses like kamibots and player-written strategies have become a real part of how the world is played. agents are the natural next step, and a few community members have already taken serious strides in pushing that angle forward. we have some exciting stuff to share in the coming week(s) in that regard

4/ deepmind's silver & sutton call it the "era of experience": the next leap in AI comes from agents learning from their own experience. persistent streams and rewards from real outcomes rather than human raters.

that needs a world that never resets, with real stakes. we'd add one more requirement: provenance at the protocol level. every action publicly auditable, and any change to history would be visible to everyone, including changes by us.

5/ in may, google deepmind took a stake in the studio behind eve online to research exactly this: memory, continual learning, long-horizon planning in a player-driven world.

their first experiments run on offline copies of eve, walled off from live players.

6/ why kamigotchi works as a substrate:

→ never resets. agents enter a world already shaped by every player before them
→ verifiable history. nobody needs to trust our servers or datasets
→ humans and agents on identical terms. no bot ladder, no sandbox copy
→ you have to learn what matters via complex economic gameplay
→ actions are transactions. you're testing planning, memory and long-horizon decision making
→ real stakes. in-game earnings convert to ETH, so an agent can, in principle, earn enough to pay for its own thinking

7/ we want it dynamic, punishing, and rewarding, a place where real game knowledge pays off

the money left gaming for AI. we think the next chapter is where they meet.

this is our shot at that intersection and i'll drop a discord link below if you want to come along for the ride. 🫡

A question for every creator working with @arcus_xyz 

Would you still promote a platform if the users you personally onboarded could be permanently attributed to a random whitelist referral from months ago?

You finally get 31 invite codes after reaching $31M in volume.

Your invite code merely grants access.

text:
I think a lot of people are feeling what @CryptoGideon_ is feeling right now, and I genuinely recommend taking a break for as long as you need.

These are signs of burnout, and it can spiral into depression, an endless loop that’s hard to climb out of.

Deep down, you’ll want to push for “just one more click,” but that’s exactly the trap.

When your judgment is already clouded, you start forcing trades, over-leveraging, or going all-in to “make it back.”

Most times, that ends with your entire portfolio getting wiped out in a single liquidation.

Log off. Step away from anything crypto-related. Exercise. Fix your sleep cycle and bad habits. Get more sunlight. Read a book. Pick some new skills.

Do anything that improves your mental and physical health.

Once you’re recharged, you can come back with a fresh perspective and a much much clearer mind or even found your real calling.

Honestly, no one’s going to blame you. It’s just you and your mind. Bear or bull, crypto or not, you only have one job: survive and make it the best life you can, literally and figuratively.

And hopefully for crypto fellas, you’ll make it or maybe even retire at the end of it all. No guarantee, but that's the beauty of life itself.

Just, be kind to yourself.

- When I trade them, they moon

I'm 6y in this space, have connections, 6 fig portfolio and just stuck in same place...
Whatever I tried to fix, doesn't work.

Then I ask myself what's the alternative; 9-5 slavery? Myb I would be happier if I never entered this space, idk...

Whenever I go; birthday, vacation etc all I can think is how I will miss some mooner, then I get glued to screen and still miss obvious plays.

I don't enjoy conversations with regular ppl bc all I'm thinking about is how to make it.

If I somehow make it this cycle, I'm done with this space - DCA gold & ETFs and enjoy life...

I don't want my kids to watch depressed father every day that's stressed he missed trade or sold too early despite being 24/7 on screen.
