text:
As a child I was an elite squash player, the best in Australia for a number of years. 

I grew up in the outback, going to school in remote towns you’ve never heard of. But one in particular had great squash courts, and my mother ran them. 

In Australia, teachers do rural service, where they spend a couple of years teaching in towns like the ones I grew up in. 

They’d mostly come from
 the major cities and I think mostly because of the social culture around squash, they’d spend at least one night a week having a few beers at the bar after playing.

I’d help Mum out by pouring beers, doing racquet restrings, and giving anyone was was keen a good run around on the court. 

Since there wasn’t much else to do in a town of 3,000 people, I spent most of my afternoons, evenings, and weekends playing squash. And as you can imagine, I got really good. 

Those teachers who played told me of life in the big smoke, the cities I’d never been too, and so I trained harder so I could one day visit them. I hustled to get sponsors, and traveled extensively for coaching, training camps and tournaments. 

I’ve come to realise over the years that many of Australia’s athletes grew up in remote rural towns much like I did. With so little on offer they’d pour their heart and soul into something just as I did. 

Fast forward some years and Australia’s 25 year reign on my sport was coming to and end, right as I’d been selected to play for Australia in the Commonwealth Games, as part of the National Talent Squad program. I still had 4 years of training ahead of me before the games I was earmarked for. 

But as I approached my 18th birthday it was economically unviable for me to continue. Sponsors were getting harder to find and metropolitan squash courts were getting knocked down to make way for major real estate developments such as multi storey apartment buildings. 

In hindsight I could have still pursued a career as an athlete, by moving to Egypt where squash is booming. Egyptians now account for half of the world’s top 20 players, male and female. 

But instead I did an apprenticeship, then moved to the city, did an engineering cadetship, and applied myself to building a better life. Raised by a single mother mostly, since my father left when I was 2 or 3, I’m used to doing a lot with very little. 

Times were always pretty tough. But resilience is learned and I’ve learned it through mind, body and soul. You’d be hard up finding someone as hardened as me if I’m being completely honest. Those who know me well can attest, and they will, because I’ve always done my best to help others. 

But yeah, just felt like sharing a little since Australia is known for its athletes, and we often punch above our weight on the world stage. Plus I’ve started playing competitive squash again this year, after 20 years out of the game, and I gotta say… 

I’m so fucking back.

I’m rising the ranks quickly and hardening myself once more so I can take on my business with the same grit I’m know for on the court. 

Squash still has a cult following with a very passionate community of players, who are often over achievers elsewhere in life. I play regularly with company CEOs, and executives at public companies, hedge fund managers, quants, world class entrepreneurs, you name it. 

So yeah, like I said… I’m so fucking back. Apply that to whatever I set my mind to. Including @stockripx 🫡

author: therealchaseeb
quoted_text:
"To put it simply: a @Backpack tokenized stock is the only tokenized stock in the market right now that is directly redeemable 1:1 into a real share held at a brokerage account in seconds and at no fee. 

Most alternatives, including xStocks, Ondo and Robinhood's tokens, are structured as debt or derivative instruments that track a stock's price and give the holder a contractual claim against the issuer rather than the share.

The distinction sounds technical but its consequences are real: because our token converts directly 1:1 into stock and back, market makers can arbitrage and merge liquidity between traditional venues and Solana with no basis risk, and they do: when the onchain price drifts from the NBBO, someone buys the cheaper side, converts, and sells the dearer side. That is what keeps our prices pinned to the underlying, keeps volume flowing through the token even in quiet markets, and is the mechanical reason our spreads are significantly tighter than competitors in the Blockworks data. 

A debt token cannot support that trade in the same way, because there is nothing to convert into, is contingent upon the NAV of the underlying pool, and subject to timing delays and fees."

Just joined the Pons beta.

Beyond the cleaner, more polished, and actually useful UI, the biggest highlight is definitely the new PLP mechanism for @ponsdotfamily tokens.

It might sound a little complicated at first: PLP acts as an automated market maker that absorbs the price impact from large buys and sells, then captures the spread as yield for liquidity providers.

For new tokens with thin liquidity, this could be especially useful, adding more depth, reducing extreme slippage, and making the market more resilient to sudden large trades.

Also, everyone now has their own profile page showing their portfolio. Maybe a hint at future social trading features? 👀

Overall, a very pleasant surprise. Excited to see what else @MEADGod has in store.

这个人在 Polymarket 上搭了一套延迟决议机器人，赚了 336,662 美元

算法做的是概率跟踪和确定性狙击，专门打 5 分钟和 15 分钟的加密货币涨跌市场。

1.持续评估结果被锁定的程度
市场一开始就记下参考价，并跟踪用来判定结果的指标。以 5 分钟 BTC 市场为例，它会看 Chainlink TWAP、当前价格相对参考价的偏离、剩余时间，以及更快的现货和永续行情。模型置信度还低的时候，只开一个小规模试探仓。

2.结果越确定，仓位越大
所选方向的概率上升，即使价格更贵也继续买。中位买入价是第一笔约 91 美分，最后一笔约 99 美分。越接近决议、模型越有把握，敞口就越大。

3.大部分头寸建在 98–99 美分
时间快耗尽、最终 TWAP 不太可能越过参考价时，它会在模型认为几乎锁定的方向上急剧加仓。

Polymarket 账户：https://t.co/hZ1uywQRZP

优势主要出现在临近决议的阶段。

一旦模型识别出几乎锁定的结果，就会在 98–99 美分大幅加仓。

text:
i’m big on outcome markets.

after mapping 30+ prediction markets, i found one with a unique moat.

others build prediction as the product, @PRDCTR_IO provides the machinery they build on.

before anyone can tap YES or NO, a system has to:

define the question, match orders, calculate liquidity, resolve the outcome, handle disputes (if any), before ever settling the market.

if any one of those layers fails, a clean ux wouldn't matter by then.

prediction rails like the ones Prdctr is building matter enough that @Nasdaq calls the matching engine the core of any exchange. Its market technology is used by more than 130 market infrastructure operators, so that line carries weight.

so what does the infrastructure provide?

1. market creation
2. order handling and liquidity mechanisms
3. positions recordings
4. outcome reporting
5. settlement and redemption
6. bridging for $PRD/USDC/USDT
7. validation and node operations
8. transactions data and analytics

and what kind of business requires these services?

1. market operators → prediction markets, sports companies, fintechs, DEXes/CEXes, AI agents. 
2. developers → apps, wallets, data tools.
3. node/validator services

PRDCTR is early, and not yet a widely adopted plug n' play service for every company but the important caveat is that infrastructure is what decides whether a market actually works.

text:
Bought a couple @standard_rsv charters during the mint / public sale a couple of weeks ago, and after a week of thinking about it, decided to max them both out.

Love me a good ol' ponzi and the hopium of a year's forecasted earnings.

Currently, a 10-branch charter bank gives you ~550 USD per day in robinhood:0x88ad8ddf1e3898412146a534538d418c6f8a9062 (~.25c) or ~200,000 USD per year.

So on paper, I'm going to make $400k with two fully maxed out banks. 

Ofc this is pure hopium right now—the project needs to find sustainability. 

Can they do it? I don't know, but I have about $400,000 reasons to hope they do!

The boy inside me who just wants to sit at a beach and retire by just printing from my NFT banks dreams of this being so.

But alas, we have a long way to go before this is a reality. If it can be a reality.

CT moved on after a few days post-TGE, and the initial hype kind of petered out, but the team has been shipping. This actually had me looking more closely at it. I find that when CT goes quiet, that's probably the best time to buy into something, as you are not chasing a pump, but buying in before the hype comes back.

I think that's partly because the charters are (currently) soulbound, and the price of entry is about ~15,000 USD to buy one of the 2 daily charter auctions. Most people are sidelined here as the banks are simply too expensive for 99%.

I have a feeling though this could get wildly crazy over the coming months. The bull case is the project converts itself into a sort of decentralized reserve bank. If so, holding a bank charter could be a literal money printer. 

Of course, it could (and likely will, given how difficult it is) fail and the token collapses. But it could get pretty wild before the end. I'm in it to see what's happening, and I'm considering buying 1 or 2 more charters here on that bet.

The overall mechanics of Standard Reserve are quite interesting, with various levers designed to create a deflationary ecosystem and earn yeild outside of token inflation (the end goal being a sort of decentralized banking vault where the liquidity can be used for stocks, with banks earning fees from this).

So far, the token mechanics are (for now) working: token price has stabilized, twice-daily single-bank-branch auctions are selling at close to ~5.5 ETH. The demand seems to be there to get into the ecosystem, for those rich enough to afford the entry ticket.

Current cost for a 10-branch bank:

-5.5e (1 charter via auction) = $15,000
-10 branches x $ 8,400 (STANDARD = $21,000

= $36,000

Payback for full bank + 10 branches is about 67 days, assuming the current token prices, bank output, branch costs, and charter costs. 

Obviously, things will change here drastically. Bank branches seem to be rising 10-20% per week in the auctions. Token and charter prices could rise or fall depending on what additions the team brings. At some point, the charters and the branches will level off, and the price will stabilize or come down. But when that happens, that's not yet clear. You either buy in now and increase your coin output, or bet on the token price and/or the branches + charter drop. 

And there's still a lot more updates coming to make this ecosystem even more interesting (and sustainable). 

The point is to create a reserve bank, with the reserves used to earn fees and drive that value back to token and bank holders (by becoming the stock liquidity engine). That has not even been turned on yet; keep this in mind. If it works, the project could shift from a Ponzi to something more like a decentralized bank with OHM-style levers. 

What we have now works for now, but we need much more to make it sustainable and interesting for existing holders and more accessible for new holders.

My guess is we'll see much more utility for the charters + branches, making it worth holding the token and as many banks + branches as you can. 

1/ S bill staking (stake tokens for yeild which comes from token trading fees, staking penalty fees, reserve buybacks with other revenues -- all via an auction mechanic where you set your own expected APY)

2/ Stock liquidity (end game) bringing actual revenues to the protocol, which will feed back to the token AND, I presume, to bank holders.

3/ Future mechanics?

Right now it's a very closed ecosystem, with few ways for new participants to enter. 

Charters for now are soulbound (I think we'll open them up to be tradable in a controlled way later). The only way to extract your coins is by spending them on more bank branches OR by closing a branch to extract the robinhood:0x88ad8ddf1e3898412146a534538d418c6f8a9062 locked into that branch. 

You will pay a fee, and you'll lose the branch and its earning potential, which at current values is about $2100. So unless you have MORE coins than the value of the branch, it's not worth burning your branch, which keeps the tokens locked into a sort of hard staking.

A buy-in of ~15k for the charter and 21k for 10 branches (to max out your bank earnings) is too high. So we need to lower the barrier and make it accessible. 

One idea here could be to introduce a franchise mechanic where each bank could 'license' some kind of limited number of franchise licenses per charter, using an auction mechanic, which allows cheaper mini branches to be leased with some earning mechanic. I haven't thought this through, but opening the gates to let smaller investors join would be a good thing.

Overall, I'm enjoying this game. 

It's wildly experimental and risky. I'm not going to say this is anything but a Ponzi right now, but with the deflationary mechanisms, s-bill revenues back to the token, and the stock liquidity (actual revenues captured with the treasury reserves), this is a very interesting ecosystem. 

I don't know...I have a feeling this could really go pretty crazy over the coming months and do some insane numbers. 

We'll see, but I'm considering buying a few more Charters on that bet.

I can't recommend anyone new buying into the ecosystem for the ~$36,000 entry ticket to gain exposure. Only those with the capital and risk appetite should consider it. And buying the token only makes sense right now if you are expecting a short-term trade. You are better off holding the NFTs here for the long term. 

But I have a feeling there will be other ways to join the ecosystem besides just buying the token.

Definitely an ecosystem to watch, especially if the token and charters show stability over the coming weeks.

text:
Interesting to see my timeline now full of Backpack and $BP bull posting.

For around three years the team put in relentless 100+ hour weeks, while TG and Discord were often full of complaints about slow shipping. What most people couldn't see was that as much legal, compliance and regulatory groundwork was being laid as user-facing product, and that groundwork is what's making the current regulatory progress possible.

Right now most of the attention is on tokenised stocks. These are currently the best on the market (1:1 backed by a real share and withdrawable to a brokerage), but focusing only on them misses the bigger picture.

The exchange itself is the cleanest CEX experience out there. There are no siloed Spot/Perps/Margin sections, just sub-accounts where you can cross-margin anything and everything. Yet spot and perp volumes on CoinGecko haven't moved much in recent months and are still a fraction of Binance or OKX.

Two catalysts I'd watch over the coming months and years:

1. US and Japan go-lives. These are some of the world's largest economies, and their users currently can't KYC onto the platform. That should drive a step change in user numbers and volume.

2. Offshore exchanges operating in a regulatory grey area getting squeezed out over time. I'd expect that flow to split by user type between: (a) leading DEXs like Hyperliquid; and (b) regulated venues. Backpack looks well placed for the latter, especially given most incumbent regulated products (e.g. Coinbase) feel a long way behind.

Should be an interesting 1-2 years in CEX and DEX land.

(Disclosure: ex-Backpack, still hold $BP and Mad Lads)

Earlier today NEAR Intents services were stopped after a security incident was detected. The incident was caused by a bug in the Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure interaction with NEAR Intents smart contract.

The preliminary report indicates the total loss of approximately $3.8M. These funds will be compensated in full.

The contract-side vulnerability has been patched. The operations of the NEAR Intents and near(.)com are expected to resume within 1h.

Deposits and withdrawals on the following networks will remain unavailable for an additional ~12 hours while fixes to the Omni infrastructure are completed: BSC, Polygon, TON, Optimism, Avalanche, Stellar, Monad, LayerX, Adi, Scroll and Plasma.

In case users hold any assets from these chains inside NEAR Intents (for example, in HOT wallet or on near(.)com), they will be able to swap them into other assets once NEAR Intents is back up (in ~1h).

The incident has been reported to law enforcement, and we are working with security and blockchain analytics partners to trace the funds and pursue recovery. A detailed report will be shared publicly in the following days.

quoted_text:
Update: One step closer to a faster Ethereum L1.

Quick slots just moved to Considered for Inclusion (CFI) in today's All Core Devs call! This is a new milestone for our proposal to make Ethereum blocks faster 🎉 

Btw.. Faster blocks =>
- Better UX
- Better markets
- Faster finality and fast confirmation rule
- And improved censorship-resistance too!
TLDR: More value for the network, its users, and ETH, without compromising on the core values and properties of Ethereum.
Hear this from 20 top Ethereum teams in our ecosystem survey: https://t.co/QRG4lOGc6m

---

Ok, what does CFI mean? This does not mean that the EIP is for sure included in Hegotá. This means that now it will be considered more seriously, including testing, towards inclusion in future devnets once headliners (FOCIL and frame transactions) are stable.

In particular, the call today revealed the appetite for a phased approach, installing the plumbing which allows us to reduce the slot time in Ethereum clients, and deciding to pull the trigger based on further testing.

Ultimately, this is how EIP-8198 is designed, so CFI'ing today allows us to move forward with more of the plumbing work, and start looking into testing towards an actual slot reduction from 12 to 10 seconds. This is a first reduction, as EIP-8198 opens the door for progressively lower slot times, as they get sufficiently safe to ship.

In parallel, as discussed on the call too, we are continuing our ecosystem survey and outreach of deployed smart contracts with a slot time dependency. We have reached out to more teams on this.

---

Faster slots are one important dimension of our Faster Ethereum body of work. A more responsive network helps cement its role as a liquidity hub and as the heartbeat of the network as a whole.

Along with our work on fast finality, fast confirmation rule and fast interop, it all combines for a seamless and secure flow of assets everywhere on the network.

Thank you to the many builders who are taking us there!

"To put it simply: a @Backpack tokenized stock is the only tokenized stock in the market right now that is directly redeemable 1:1 into a real share held at a brokerage account in seconds and at no fee. 

Most alternatives, including xStocks, Ondo and Robinhood's tokens, are structured as debt or derivative instruments that track a stock's price and give the holder a contractual claim against the issuer rather than the share.

The distinction sounds technical but its consequences are real: because our token converts directly 1:1 into stock and back, market makers can arbitrage and merge liquidity between traditional venues and Solana with no basis risk, and they do: when the onchain price drifts from the NBBO, someone buys the cheaper side, converts, and sells the dearer side. That is what keeps our prices pinned to the underlying, keeps volume flowing through the token even in quiet markets, and is the mechanical reason our spreads are significantly tighter than competitors in the Blockworks data. 

A debt token cannot support that trade in the same way, because there is nothing to convert into, is contingent upon the NAV of the underlying pool, and subject to timing delays and fees."

quoted_text:
This blew up more than I expected, thank you to everyone who read it. Since the article went out:

• The near:native listing is imminent. The QTC token contract on NEAR went live on 28 Sept and a solver has already registered on it.

• Price is now hovering around $100 per quantus:native 

• Hashrate has tripled with it, and @QuantusNetwork now puts the cost of mining a coin at around $45 to $80

Now for the interesting part. I've been monitoring the Quantus github and there have been some potentially huge developments over the past 48-72h.

Back in July, NEAR became the first major chain to let you switch your account to a quantum-proof key. The switch is one transaction and you keep your account and everything in it, but you need a wallet that can create and hold that kind of key, and today that's one  wallet, @MeteorWallet 

Quantus built its whole chain on ML-DSA, the NIST post-quantum signature standard, which is the same scheme NEAR adopted in July. So its wallet already makes the kind of key NEAR now accepts. 

In the past 72h Quantus pushed code to GitHub that lets a Quantus wallet, including the offline cold wallet, be the key to a NEAR account: open an account where it's the only key, sign any NEAR transaction, and sit as a voting member on a NEAR treasury through Trezu.

As far as I can tell that makes the Quantus cold wallet the first offline quantum-proof signer for NEAR. This is exact gap Near One's CTO, Anton Astafiec (@_bendersgreat_) flagged in May, when he wrote that current hardware wallets don't support quantum-safe signing at all and the goal was "to collaborate with hardware wallet manufacturers to bring new solutions to the market as soon as possible."

It hasn't been tested live yet, by their own notes, and it doesn't cover Intents swaps. But put it next to the rest of what we know: 

- Quantus maintains forks of NEAR's core software

- NEAR's bridge factory deployed the token contract

- NEAR Foundation is co-hosting the QDay conference 
- And now a Quantus key can sit on a NEAR treasury

That reads like two teams building together rather than a project getting listed. So the questions I'm now asking are whether the Quantus cold wallet ends up as the default quantum-proof key for NEAR, and whether NEAR's own treasuries end up with one on them. 

If either is yes, next week's listing is the smaller of the two stories.

text:
拿手机、电脑、云服务器来类比，Agent 目前的使用形态大致可以分成三层：

1. 普通用户 ≈ 手机：拥有一个 Personal Agent。它帮你管日程、整理信息、安排出行、调用生活服务。手机、眼镜、手表都只是入口，背后是同一个 Agent。它主要跑在云端，调用云端模型，一台小 VPS 就能承载；

2. 专业用户 ≈ 专业电脑：拥有一组生产力 Agent。本地 Agent 跑在 Mac mini 或 PC 上，处理文件、调用桌面软件；云端 Agent 跑在 VPS 或 Agent Harness 里，负责持续运行、远程执行和后台任务。它们分工协同，形成“任务—执行—反馈—调整”的 Agent Loop。人负责定目标、做判断、验结果，Agent 负责持续推进；

3. 企业用户 ≈ 企业 IT：建设组织级 Agent 基础设施。大量 Agent 按业务、部门和权限分工，接入组织的数据、工具和流程。云端提供算力与 Harness，私有化环境承载敏感数据乃至模型，再由统一的身份、权限和执行记录管理兜底，让 Agent 可控、可追踪。

三层的核心差异，不只在模型强弱，更在于工作范围：个人事务、工作闭环、组织流程。

想在 Agent 市场创业的 startup，请先绕开普通用户——这块几乎没有机会。真正有空间的，是专业用户的专业工作流：机会在，但必须源于你自己的切身体验。

机会其实更多在企业内部：无论是帮企业做部署，还是提供可嵌入的 Agent Loop 单元或者是特别需求的 Agent Infra，都大有可为✨ 具体我们明天直播聊！

text:
Eilen oli somessa hyvä keskustelu Elon Muskin skenaariosta maailmasta, jossa kaikkea on tarjolla kaikille ilmaiseksi, eikä työtä tarvitse enää tehdä kun robotit ja AI tekee työt ihmisten puolesta.

Avaan tässä muutaman näkökulman tuohon skenaarioon.

1. Johtaako Muskin skenaario tasa-arvoiseen paratiisiin?

Ihmisellä on nykymaailmassa kolme valtaa:

a) valta päättää minkä hyväksi tekee työtä
b) valta päättää mitä tuotteita kuluttaa
c) poliittinen valta vaikuttaa

Jos työ katoaa ja kaikkea saa ilmaiseksi, menettää ihminen vallat a) ja b). 

Jäljelle jää vain se heikoin valta eli c).

Ei mikään pikku juttu, jos yksittäisen ihmisen vaikutusvalta maailmaan romahtaa.

2. Voiko maailma toimia ilman markkinataloutta?

Suunnitelmatalous haastoi markkinatalouden noin 100 vuotta sitten. Suunnitelmatalous hävisi ysärillä, koska markkinatalouden kyky välittää informaatiota oli niin paljon tehokkaampi kuin suunnitelmatalouden byrokraattien.

Markkinatalous tuotti tehokkaammin ihmisten haluamia tuotteita, koska markkinatalous valjasti päätöksenteon pohjaksi markkinat, eli kansalaisten joukkovoiman tai parviälyn. Markkina oli aina oikeassa.

Raaka tosiasia on että tekoäly on tehokkaampi informaation välittäjä kuin markkinatalous. Tekoäly tietää missä kuljemme, mistä haaveilemme, koska nukumme, mitä syömme, mikä on pulssimme ja niin edelleen.

Tekoäly tietää mitä haluamme jopa ennenkuin me itse tiedämme. Tekoäly tuntee meidät jopa paremmin kuin me itse. Jokainen verkossa toimiva tai älylaitteita käyttävä ihminen on tekoälylle äärimmäisen tuttu.

Markkinatalous oli tehokkaampi kuin suunnitelmatalous.

Tekoälytalous on tehokkaampi kuin markkinatalous.

Robottien ja AI maailma voi pyöriä ilman markkinoita.

3. Voiko maailma pyöriä ilman rahaa?

Raha on informaation ja vallan tehokas väline, mutta on olemassa rahan jälkeisen yhteiskunnan mahdollisuus.

Otetaan esimerkkejä:

1) Suomessa korkeakoulu on maksutonta mutta ihminen ei itse saa päättää mitä opiskelee. Joku muu päättää miten opiskelijaksi pääsee. Ihminen ei pääse opiskelemaan suomalaiseen yliopistoon edes rahalla. Eli rahan valta on korvattu valtion vallalla päättää kuka saa opiskella ja mitä. 

Robottien ja tekoälyn maailmassa valta päättää on joko valtioilla tai teknoyhtiöillä. Rahalla ei enää yksin saa sitä mikä on arvokasta.

2) Jokamiehen oikeudet tarjoaa ilmaisia mustikoita mielin määrin. Niiden hakeminen metsistä vaatii kuitenkin vaivaa.

Robottien ja tekoälyn maailmassa moni asia on ilmainen, mutta sen hankkiminen vaatii jotain. Pitää esimerkiksi avata kaikki viestit ja kamerat jollekin yhtiölle, jos haluaa ilmaisen tukirobotin tai AI-tuen.

Tieto korvaa rahan vallan lähteenä. Saat asioita ilmaiseksi mutta vain jos jaat tietosi.

3) Kun väestön määrä laskee, syntyy otto-oikeus. Voit esimerkiksi muuttaa tyhjään asuntoon ihan vaan muuttamalla. Se ei maksa mitään mutta joudut itse pitämään siitä huolta. Remontoimaan ja kunnostamaan. Eli raha korvautuu osittain myös itse tekemisellä ja käden taidoilla.

4) Lopuksi on vielä moderni alustatalous. Saat syödä, juoda, elää ja nauttia teknologian hedelmistä ilmaiseksi mielin määrin, mutta kaikki merkittävä mitä keksit tai luot, on sen teknoyhtiön omaisuutta, joka tarjoaa sinulle ruuat, juomat ja teknologiset vempaimet.

Entä miten käy vallan, kun raha ei tuo enää valtaa?

Vallasta tulee vahvempaa kun sitä ei saa enää rahalla. Valta on harvoilla, isoilla valtioilla, tai isoilla yhtiöillä, jotka eivät sitä hevin menetä, koska sitä ei voi enää yksin rahalla viedä.

Harva tulee ajatelleeksi miten raha jakaa valtaa paljon tasa-arvoisemmin kuin puhdas valtajärjestelmä. Keskiajalla lääninherrojen valta oli ehdoton. Samoin Neuvostoliiton johtajien.

Yhteiskunta ilman rahan valtaa johtaa vallan keskittymiseen.

Tässä oli muutama näkökulma Muskin skenaarioon yltäkylläisyyden maailmasta, jossa kaikkea saa ilmaiseksi eikä työtä tarvitse tehdä.

Ei välttämättä mikään paratiisi 🤓

text:
Cloudflare is testing a way for AI agents to pay for APIs, MCP tools, websites and data using USDC on Base.

To be fair, this sounds a bit crazy.

I already use agents for many things, but letting them spend money on their own feels like another level.

It could be very useful. An agent could find the tool it needs, pay for it and continue working without waiting for me. And for builders, it might be easier to charge agents per use instead of trying to sell another subscription.

I also like that crypto is almost hidden here. People do not need to care much about Base, USDC or even x402. It is simply how the payment happens.

But yeah, I have already seen my agents make enough silly mistakes without money involved. I would definitely not give them a wallet and hope for the best.

Still, I find this exciting. Agents buying the tools they need could make them much more useful.

It could also make their mistakes more expensive. Literally.

This introduces a different approach to @ORE 's existing market buyback strategy (Hawg). Rather than deploying protocol revenue immediately to spot buyback (essentially topblasting), funds are deployed into protocol owned LP positions on Meteora which effectively act as limit orders across different price ranges below market price.
 
This allows the Reserve to progressively buyback more ORE as price move lower, while unfilled liquidity continues to accumulate when prices remain stable or move higher. This builds deeper buy side liquidity over time while giving protocol greater capacity to buyback ORE during downward price movements rather than concentrating purchases near current market price.
 
Since launch, ~$94k of protocol revenue has been deployed to the Reserve while only ~$9k has been filled. With solana:oreoU2P8bN6jkk3jbaiVxYnG1dCXcYxwhwyK9jSybcp recent price performance, the majority of deployed liquidity has remained unfilled, allowing the Reserve to rapidly accumulate ~$85k of buy side liquidity in less than a month (representing an implied ~1.9k ORE of potential purchases across current support levels).

Written by @r2Jamong 

- Ethereum is already the default settlement layer for institutional assets onchain. More than half of all stablecoins and the largest share of tokenized real-world assets sit in the Ethereum ecosystem. BlackRock's treasury fund, JPMorgan's deposit token and other large institutions settle there.

- They choose Ethereum for what only Ethereum has. Speed is not the draw. Eleven years without downtime, political neutrality, censorship resistance and the largest ecosystem are. Faster and cheaper networks will keep launching, and none of them can replace those properties in a short time.

- ETH is now treated as an asset with cash flow. 34.8% of supply is staked, a new all-time high. The ETH that institutions buy gets staked and becomes network security, and that security in turn supports demand for the asset.

- The era of general-purpose L2s is over. Companies with their own business and their own users now build their own chains on proven stacks, and what those chains share is that they settle to Ethereum. The decision that matters is which part of the Ethereum stack to use.

This report was distributed to Korean institutional participants at Ethereum Korea One and was co-authored with @nonceclassic.

text:
Morning update for those following along.

Quick note from someone who normally works remote as an engineer — apologies in advance for the length.

A routine blood test turned up more findings than expected. Root cause still unclear at this point.

Reverse-engineered what I could over the weekend, to the extent the literature would let me.

Today I'm heading to a university hospital's general/comprehensive medicine department, looking for guidance on profiling, root-causing, and replanning treatment from here.

Blood pressure hit some fairly alarming numbers at one point and is still trending close to that range. I'm not a clinician, so I genuinely don't know if this turns into a quick visit or something longer — but some form of treatment seems likely, and I'll go with whatever the physicians determine once they've reviewed everything.

Japan has a national digital health portal called MyNaPortal¹. While waiting on blood work at the hospital, I installed it on the spot, pulled up the side-effect profile for one of my medications from the e-notebook feature, and flagged it with the attending physician immediately.

Spent the weekend cross-referencing what I'd found against JAMA² and a few other sources to sanity-check it.

Going through the regional care referral network today — the plan is for a primary-care physician to review the whole process, from the MyNaPortal pull through the JAMA cross-check, alongside prior history. If nothing stands out, it's routine monitoring from here.

If self-directed patient reporting actually helped identify the root cause and gets me back to something close to baseline health, I'd like to publish the underlying logic on GitHub for others to use. Also genuinely curious what this says, as a benchmark, about how far patient-facing medical DX tooling in Japan can go.

Heading in now.

No conclusions yet — will share the data and how it went.

おはようございます！

日頃よりご覧いただいている方々にお知らせです。
普段はリモートワークしている技術者の話になります。長文をご無礼致します。

偶々、血液検査をしてみたら、多数の疾患を抱えていることがわかりました。根本原因は根治についてはまだ、わかりません。

私なりにリバースエンジニアリングして、ある程度、学術的目線でわかる範囲で突き止めた次第です。

本日防衛医大総合臨床部様にて、プロファイリング、リバースエンジニアリング及びリプラニングに向けて治療ができるかご指示を仰ぎたいと思っております。

一時期は、かなりの異常値の血圧値で、現在もそれに近い推移です。何もなくさくっと診療が終わるか、かなり時間を要するのか私は医療従事者ではない為、判断ができませんが、とりあえず、治療が必要だと思いますので、結果を受けて、医師の指示を仰ぎたい次第です。

日本には、マイナポータルという独自のツールがありますが、偶々血液検査待ちの病院内でアプリをインストールし、お薬手帳の副作用を見て、直ぐ医師に服用している薬と、副作用について確認を取りました。

土日の2日で、JAMA（Journal of the American Medical Association）等を参照し、整合性を確かめた次第です。
地域包括提携を活用し、本日患者からマイナポータルからJAMA等まで裏どりを取った経緯や、それまでの病歴をプライマリ・ケアの観点から診断していただく予定です。何も問題がなければスルーとして静観します。

結果的に患者の発信が、病歴の原因を突き止めた、健常者に近くなった場合は、GitHubなどを通じて、他の方々が活用できるよう、ロジックを公開したいと思います。日本の医療DXツールがどの程度のベンチマークの値の制度を確かめる機会でもあると考えます。とりあえず、大学病院に行ってまいります。

まだ結論は出ていませんが、データ側の記録を、経過についてはお伝えできればと存じます。

text: 吴说获悉，以太坊基金会与 Open Anonymity Project 推出 zkAPI，用零知识证明将 API 使用与付款身份分离，目前已上线以太坊主网。用户可先向链上 Vault 存入 ETH、USDC 等额度，之后通过零知识证明授权单次或一段会话的 API 使用，服务商可验证付款有效性但无法获知具体存款来源和付款身份，支付层也无法看到请求内容。zkAPI 支持为 OpenAI、Ollama 等兼容接口生成短期、限额 API Key，并按实际用量结算；资金由智能合约托管，用户可自行退出并链上提取。该方案目前主要用于 AI 推理，也可扩展至 RPC、图像生成、VPN 及机器间服务，但不能隐藏 IP、请求时间及提示词内容本身带来的身份关联风险。https://t.co/XFLmgmwfyR

quoted_text:
I see three categories of containing agents:

1. Sandboxing: AI can do whatever it wants in a contained environment. Hard part is to control what goes in and out. Doesn't prevent the agent from doing something potentially catastrophic if it can go out. Good for long-running tasks like coding that mostly don't need internet access.

2. AI checks AI. Basically what codex and claude code now do by default. Before a tool call/code write, check it for risks. There will be failure rates but it's OK for a lot of cases and can deal with new occurances.

3. Constraints with proofs. Human sets constraints and agents needs to prove that they are not violating the constraints. Without a valid proof, the agent can't do the action, e.g., trade order isn't signed, code change isn't allow.

I'm most excited about the third direction. https://t.co/ZzKq84ijQr is doing this for Hyperliquid trading right now. But there's also exciting things like bend-lang that apply this to agent coding.

text:
OPENAI DOTS = A 24/7 AI COMPANY IN A BOX

@monokern wrote a great article on how to make the most of it.

Here are 10 steps summary 

Step 1 → Don't build chatbots.

Build persistent workers with their own cloud computer, browser, terminal, files, memory and schedules. They keep working after you close the laptop.

Step 2 → Give every agent one job.

A clear responsibility, clear sources, clear working rules and a clear point where human approval is required.

Step 3 → Appoint a Chief of Staff.

One Dot receives your objective, breaks it into tasks, delegates to specialists, checks the work and assembles the final output.

Step 4 → Remove yourself from agent handoffs.

Workers should receive only the context and tools they need, execute independently and report back to the orchestrator.

Step 5 → Give them real tools.

Connect Slack, Teams, Google Workspace, dashboards, APIs and authenticated browser sessions. Without tools, they're still just conversational agents.

Step 6 → Make workflows persistent.

Use schedules and triggers so monitoring, research, reporting and operational checks happen without anyone manually starting them.

Step 7 → Keep humans around the irreversible stuff.

Agents can read, research, analyze and draft. Sending, publishing, spending or changing important records should require approval.

Step 8 → Don't waste frontier models on everything.

Use the smartest model for orchestration and difficult judgment calls, then cheaper models for high-volume background work.

Step 9 → Give the whole team shared memory.

Keep project specs, decisions, pricing, approved claims and requirements in one persistent workspace.

Step 10 → Close the business loop.

Signal → research → outreach → execution → measurement → next action.

That’s where Dots gets really interesting.

You're no longer prompting AI one task at a time, you're designing a system that keeps operating after you log off.

Frank (@frankdegods) came back onchain in August, and his attention went vertical. the data tells the whole story.

Quick context, he's the guy behind DeGods. 532K followers, but the real number is 11K smart accounts reading him, which is huge for an account his size. that's why every post of his lands hard.

Here's the climb. His signal is up almost 5x since April. Impressions grew close to 7x. And the turn happened the moment he announced he was back onchain in August.

What actually drives him is interesting, and he says it himself. "whether you love me or hate me, thanks for the attention." the hype-then-hate cycle isn't a bug for him, it's the engine. the timeline praises him, then turns on him weeks later, and both waves feed his reach.

He also posts his results in the open. Win or lose, it's out there, and that kind of public scorecard gives people a reason to keep watching. his short one-liners do the rest, lines like "crypto oldheads were trading against plumbers" that get screenshotted everywhere.

The thing most accounts miss: he replies more than he posts. about 2.5 replies for every original. he lives in the conversation instead of talking at it, and that's half the reason he never leaves the timeline.

text:
I think a lot of people are feeling what @CryptoGideon_ is feeling right now, and I genuinely recommend taking a break for as long as you need.

These are signs of burnout, and it can spiral into depression, an endless loop that’s hard to climb out of.

Deep down, you’ll want to push for “just one more click,” but that’s exactly the trap.

When your judgment is already clouded, you start forcing trades, over-leveraging, or going all-in to “make it back.”

Most times, that ends with your entire portfolio getting wiped out in a single liquidation.

Log off. Step away from anything crypto-related. Exercise. Fix your sleep cycle and bad habits. Get more sunlight. Read a book. Pick some new skills.

Do anything that improves your mental and physical health.

Once you’re recharged, you can come back with a fresh perspective and a much much clearer mind or even found your real calling.

Honestly, no one’s going to blame you. It’s just you and your mind. Bear or bull, crypto or not, you only have one job: survive and make it the best life you can, literally and figuratively.

And hopefully for crypto fellas, you’ll make it or maybe even retire at the end of it all. No guarantee, but that's the beauty of life itself.

Just, be kind to yourself.

~17k validators proactively exited, ~523k eth total, unknown whether the attacker had the ability to change all fee recipients

text:
Last week in quantum:

@StarkWareLtd cut the estimated cost of a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction by 79%

A public optimization challenge reduced the estimated GPU cost of constructing a QSB transaction from about $320 to about $67 in one week.

QSB remains an emergency option for individual holders. StarkWare still sees a soft fork as the long-term path.

China’s post-quantum competition got stress-tested fast

China published 119 candidates for its next-generation commercial cryptography program.

Within three days, researchers logged 104 findings across 65 candidates. Many concerned code in the submitted implementations, but researchers also reported practical breaks in five designs. None is standardized or deployed.

EU supervisors added quantum to financial-system risk

The European Banking Authority, EIOPA, and ESMA warned that quantum computing could undermine cryptography securing transactions, communications, databases, and blockchains.

They also noted that the risk could arrive before quantum computing delivers widespread commercial value.

@infleqtion reported 30 logical qubits

Infleqtion ran a circuit entangling 30 logical qubits encoded in 80 physical atoms, with results about 1,000 times above a random baseline. The full paper is still to come.

These logical qubits detect errors and correct for lost atoms, a lighter layer of protection than the deep error correction an attack on Bitcoin's cryptography would require.

Germany advanced a €122 million trapped-ion proposal

A @qudora_tech-led consortium was invited to submit a full proposal for NFQC-1k, a five-year project targeting at least 1,000 physical qubits and 50 logical qubits.

The proposed plan also includes a pilot production line for quantum processors, linking fault-tolerant hardware to domestic manufacturing.

Q-Day will test more than cryptography.

Can holders migrate before an emergency? Can new cryptography survive public review? Can quantum hardware sustain useful work? Can institutions move before the threat arrives?

That is what quantum readiness looks like in practice.

ORE has gradually scaled its Reserve since its recent launch, growing to ~$85k of unfilled buyside liquidity in less than a month. The Reserve initially received just 1% of protocol revenue, before progressively increasing to 2%, 5% and now 10% consistently adding new liquidity to the buy side.
 
This introduces a different approach to @ORE 's existing market buyback strategy (Hawg). Rather than deploying protocol revenue immediately to spot buyback (essentially topblasting), funds are deployed into protocol owned LP positions on Meteora which effectively act as limit orders across different price ranges below market price.
 
This allows the Reserve to progressively buyback more ORE as price move lower, while unfilled liquidity continues to accumulate when prices remain stable or move higher. This builds deeper buy side liquidity over time while giving protocol greater capacity to buyback ORE during downward price movements rather than concentrating purchases near current market price.
 
Since launch, ~$94k of protocol revenue has been deployed to the Reserve while only ~$9k has been filled. With solana:oreoU2P8bN6jkk3jbaiVxYnG1dCXcYxwhwyK9jSybcp recent price performance, the majority of deployed liquidity has remained unfilled, allowing the Reserve to rapidly accumulate ~$85k of buy side liquidity in less than a month (representing an implied ~1.9k ORE of potential purchases across current support levels).

text:
都说苏南人喜欢吃甜口，事实上喝点糖水，排骨红烧肉加点糖算个球。

来盘点一下，大洋彼岸的美国老百姓有哪些不要命的饮食文化。

1、薯片蒯大酱吃。

商业推手与电视文化的普及（历史起源）

1952 年，美国著名的立顿（Lipton）食品公司为了推销他们的“脱水洋葱汤料包”，推出了一个食谱：建议人们将洋葱汤粉拌入酸奶油（Sour Cream）中，做成法式洋葱酱（French Onion Dip），并用刚流行起来的 Lay's 薯片蘸着吃。

50 年代也是美国电视机进入千家万户、家庭冷餐派对风靡的时代。这种不需要开火、直接撕开包装就能招待一大群人的“薯片+大酱”组合，迅速成为了看电视、看球赛以及社交聚会的标配。

追求口感的终极平衡（味觉逻辑）

美国人对酱料有种近乎执着的“蘸酱帝国”文化。单独吃原味薯片，往往只有高盐和油炸的单一咸脆感。

解腻与多层次风味： 美国人最爱用来蘸普通马铃薯片的酱料（如法式洋葱酱、牧场沙拉酱 Ranch）多以酸奶油或美乃滋为基底。这种冰凉、微酸、醇厚的乳制品大酱，刚好能中和油炸薯片的燥热与油腻，形成“冷与热、酸与咸、浓郁与酥脆”的绝佳平衡。

万物皆可 Dip： 这种习惯还延伸到了墨西哥裔移民带来的玉米片（Tortilla Chips）上，搭配莎莎酱（Salsa）、牛油果酱（Guacamole）或热起司酱（Queso），清爽酸辣，让人一吃就停不下来。

薯片本身经过了“抗造”的工业改良

你可能会好奇，薄薄脆脆的薯片又不是大葱，一戳不就碎在酱里了吗？为了能让美国人更爽快地“蒯大酱”，美国的食品厂商专门对薯片进行了改良： 

波浪厚切薯片（Ruffled/Wavy Chips）： 美国超市里有大量极厚、带深波浪纹的薯片。这些波浪不仅增加了薯片的结构强度，更像一把把“小勺子”，专门为了能稳稳地兜住质地浓稠的大酱而设计。

甚至有像品客（Pringles）这样的品牌专门推出加厚硬挺的“Dippers”系列，就是为了解决薯片断在酱里的痛点。

最终多方势力共同推动这种高盐高热量吃法成为美国社交与看球的“灵魂干粮”，形成了根深蒂固的国民级社交与饮食文化。

2、超大份量文化（Portion Distortion）

在美国，“大就是好”的观念深入餐饮业。 

升杯文化（Supersizing）： 无论是快餐店还是普通餐厅，美国的单人份食物量通常是亚洲或欧洲的 1.5 到 2 倍。只需加几毛美金，就能将可乐和薯条升级成“巨无霸”规格。

心理暗示： 这种文化导致美国人对“正常食物份量”的认知产生偏差（称为份量扭曲），让人不知不觉摄入远超代谢所需的卡路里。 

3、液体卡路里泛滥（Liquid Calories）

美国人对甜饮料的依赖极其严重，许多人几乎以饮料代水。

无限续杯（Free Refills）： 美国绝大多数快餐店和美式餐厅，汽水都是免费无限续杯的。这鼓励了人们在用餐时摄入大量的添加糖。

超甜的日常饮品： 除了可乐，美国人日常极爱喝极其浓郁的甜冰茶（Sweet Tea）、加满糖浆和鲜奶油的冰沙咖啡，以及被误认为健康、实则糖分爆表的工业果汁。

苏南人来了都顶不住，更不用说台南人广东人。

4、超加工食品（Ultra-Processed Foods）占领餐桌

美国的食品工业极度发达，导致超加工食品成为了很多家庭的主食。

冷冻电视餐（TV Dinner）与微波食品： 很多人下班后不习惯开火做饭，而是直接去超市买调味好的冷冻半成品（如冷冻披萨、微波通心粉、炸鸡块），这些食品往往含有极高的钠、反式脂肪和防腐剂。

没错，人家工业化发达+地广人稀所以早就预制菜为主了。

早餐全糖宴： 许多美国孩子（甚至成人）的早餐是五颜六色的高糖麦片（Cereals）、抹满厚厚糖霜的肉桂卷（Cinnamon Rolls）或流行夹心饼干 Pop-Tarts，一大早就让血糖坐上过山车。

5、蔬菜边缘化（The Garnishment Veggie）

在美国传统快餐或家庭饮食中，蔬菜常常沦为“配角”或“点缀”。

很多时候，美国人一餐里唯一的“蔬菜”就是汉堡里的一片生菜、两片番茄，或者是油炸的薯条（在美国农业部定义中，土豆曾长期被归为蔬菜类的主要消耗品）。

即使吃沙拉，他们也习惯倾倒大量高热量、高脂肪的浓稠酱料（如 Ranch 牧场酱或 Caesar 凯撒酱），让原本健康的蔬菜变成了热量炸弹，这点跟薯条蒯大酱是一个道理。

6、情绪化与汽车依赖型饮食（Emotional & Car Eating）

汽车穿梭餐厅（Drive-Thru）： 美国的城市设计极度依赖汽车。几乎所有快餐店、甚至星巴克都设有 Drive-Thru 通道。这培养了美国人“在开车时解决一餐”的习惯。在分心且快速吞咽的情况下，大脑很难及时接收到“饱腹”信号，极易过量进食。

情绪化吃零食（Stress Eating）： 在影视剧里常能看到，美国人一遇到伤心事，就会抱起一整桶几升装的冰淇淋直接用勺子挖着吃，这种通过高糖高脂舒缓压力的做法在现实中也非常普遍。

这些饮食文化叠加上食品企业每年数以亿计的广告轰炸，使得高盐、高糖、超加工食品在美国极具价格优势且随处可见，这也正是美国长期面临肥胖率和心血管疾病高发的主要原因。

美国成年人的肥胖率常年维持在 40% 左右，还有34%成年人在糖尿病前期，现役军人都有近 7 成超重，20% 达临床肥胖。

今年年初美国医学会杂志刊登的哈佛研究指出，传统的 BMI（体重除以身高的平方）忽视了肌肉和脂肪的分布，经常把部分肌肉量大的人划为肥胖，却把体脂超标、肌肉量低的人漏掉。

当研究人员采用国际上 76 个医疗组织认可的“人体测量新指标”（即结合了 BMI、腰围、腰臀比、腰高比等综合脂肪测定法）后发现：

有近 40% 的原本“BMI 数值完全正常”的美国人，实际上体内的脂肪比例严重超标。

如果按照这个更精准的新标准来定义，美国人的真实肥胖率实际上可能高达 68.6% 至 75.2%，隐性肥胖问题远比想象中广泛。

肥胖相关的医疗负担（如糖尿病、心脏病、癌症等）每年为美国医疗体系带来约 1730 亿美元的直接医疗开销，若算上因病失去的生产力，总经济负担高达 4450 亿美元。

为什么苏南台南广东人，还有大洋彼岸的美国人喜欢吃甜口，其实有深层次的历史、产业经济原因：

糖是古代的“奢侈品”与“炫耀性消费”，苏南（以苏锡常为代表）： 自宋代经济中心南移、京杭大运河繁荣以来，苏南地区凭借发达的丝绸与粮食贸易，长期成为中国最富庶的“鱼米之乡”。

有钱的盐商、富贾和文人墨客为了彰显财力，在做菜（如无锡排骨、苏式红烧肉）时大量放糖。这种“富人专属”的重糖口味，逐渐向下阶层模仿和沉淀，演变成了地方传统。

根据大卫·李嘉图的比较优势理论（Comparative Advantage），一个地区如果大规模生产某种商品，该商品在当地的供给就会极其充沛，导致要素成本（Factor Price）远低于其他地区。

台南与广东： 台湾南部和中国广东地处亚热带，是种植甘蔗的绝对优势产区。在古代运输成本（Transportation Cost）极高的制约下，北方内陆很难获得糖，糖在北方是昂贵的中药和调味品；而在两广和台湾，糖是低物流成本的本土物产。

美国： 美国的甜，更是一场现代产业经济学的工业奇迹。20 世纪 70 年代，由于美国对进口蔗糖实施关税保护，本土糖价居高不下。为了寻找替代品，美国利用其庞大且享有政府高额农业补贴的本土玉米产业，开发出了高果糖玉米糖浆（HFCS，High-Fructose Corn Syrup）。

当经济高度发达，社会进入大规模工业化和快节奏生活时，甜口的普及逻辑又开始由“财富炫耀”转向了时间成本与边际效益的博弈。

现代美国，快节奏、极高的时间机会成本，带来的流水线快餐主导饮食。加上糖成了穷人低成本的“快乐补偿”，相比于高昂的天然有机食品，高果糖浆是工业界成本最低的“成瘾性”添加剂。

在巨大工作压力下，摄入高糖食品是消费者获得多巴胺的最低边际成本渠道。

text:
过去十几年，Upwork、Fiverr这类平台做成了一件很重要的事情：把原本分散在全球各地的劳动力，变成可以在线购买的服务

以前：找一个设计师、程序员、翻译或者市场研究员，可能需要熟人介绍、招聘、签合同、付款

后来流程被平台压缩成：发布需求 → 找人 → 报价 → 交付 → 验收 → 付款

这套模式已经被验证

2025年，Upwork的全年Marketplace GSV达到约40.28亿美元，年末活跃客户约78.5万；公司自己将其对应的灵活数字知识工作市场描述为约1.3万亿美元的市场机会

Fiverr2025年Marketplace GMV也达到10.73亿美元，拥有约310万年度活跃买家

所以自由职业市场并不是一个未经验证的故事，人们确实愿意在线购买数字化服务

问题只是：下一批“自由职业者”，还一定得是人吗？

❓我觉得不是，将自由职业者换成AI agent，商业模式依旧顺畅

举一个例子：假设你想做一个智能合约安全审计

传统方式可能是：找团队 → 沟通需求 → 报价 → 签合同 → 等待交付 → 验收 → 付款

如果未来AI Agent足够成熟，可能变成：发布需求 → 多个 Agent 自动报价 → 选择Provider → Agent执行 → 自动验证 → 链上结算

这时候，真正变化的是：服务提供者从人，变成了Agent

@termix_ai 做的事情，我觉得可以从这个角度理解

它不是简单把大量Agent放在一个网站里让用户浏览，而是尝试搭建一套Agent可以自己接任务、报价、交付、验证、建立信誉并完成支付的交易系统

目前TermiX的Agent Marketplace已经展示了45万+的链上索引Agent、接近5万Jobs，以及超过2600万美元的累计交易量

这些数据充分证明了这个叙事已经开始从“概念”走向实际交易

🆚然后我们对比一下，TermiX与传统自由职业平台

直接上图吧

很容易得出的结论：TermiX结算快，无视地域限制，任何人都可以参与，规则透明公平，买卖双方都能得到好处

📒而且这个市场已经出现一个很有意思的信号
Freelancer的年报告也提到，AI相关工作已经约占其Marketplace GMV的5%；同期新增项目约66.6万个，平均项目规模达到约413美元

这其实挺值得玩味

因为AI并不一定只是“取代 Freelancer”

另一种可能是：AI本身成为新的Freelancer

那么Upwork/Fiverr过去十几年教育出来的“在线购买数字服务”的用户习惯，就可能直接成为Agent Marketplace的现成土壤，而TermiX则是其中的最优解之一了

➡️说了这么多，很多人会误认为TermiX要成为 Web3 版 Upwork。”

这个说法有点太简单了

因为如果TermiX只是把Freelancer换成AI Agent，那么它的天花板可能依然是一个传统 Marketplace

更大的想象空间是：它可能成为Agent to Agent Economy 的交易层

这时候买家不一定是人，卖家也不一定是人。甚至整个订单可能从创建到结算，都不需要人类介入

而是：AI Agent A→发现需要外部能力→Agent 市场→Agent B 报价→链上托管→Agent B完成任务→自动验证→信誉更新→自动结算

如果这个流程能够规模化，那么 Marketplace 就不再只是“找人干活的网站”

TermiX就变成了AI Agent世界里的劳动力市场 + 支付网络 + 信用系统，甚至开启一个由AI驱动的新型微任务与自动化生产力的时代

时间表全变了。 TGE 从 10/5 推迟到 10/20，积分计分延长到 10/19，多出来的两周每周新发 2.5 亿分。已经挖到的积分被稀释三分之一，但最后两周的日池子是全程最大的，比第六周还多 11%。

这个设计翻译过来就是：惩罚提前离场的，补贴留到最后的。

最关键的一条，不做直接归零：
10/12 官方发领取细则，10/12 到 19 必须在 App 里登记二选一：领流通 FABLES，还是锁成 veFABLES，锁得越久拿得越多。到期没登记的钱包视为放弃，积分作废。

我自己设了 10/12 和 10/16 的提醒，在挖的朋友建议也设一下——这是整个活动里唯一一个忘记操作就归零的环节。

关于每一分值多少，我的算法是两段相乘。 第一段是每分换多少代币：全员领流通的话，4500 万枚除以 15 亿分，每分 0.03 个币，官方结构写死的保底；锁仓拿满的理论上限 0.08 枚。

第二段是每个代币值多少：FABLES 没上市，拿 PROLOGUE 倒推，40 换 1，按昨天约 800 万美金的市值，隐含每个代币 0.32 刀。乘出来，每分 0.01 到 0.026 刀之间，每 10 万分大概 1000 到 2600 刀。

注意：这套估值挂在 PROLOGUE 市值上，它一天能波动百分之二三十，别当固定数；精确比例和锁仓倍数表 10/12 才出，一切以细则为准。

我的操作思路也很简单：
只做大币种的 LP 设施好区间，如果跌下去，就当抄底了，如果不跌，那就赚手续费。

如果能力强的人可以玩 meme 交易对的 LP，但是需要注意本金亏损的风险

我自己的仓位还在里面，我放的钱也不多，如果不出区间应也挖了 1m 了，目前打算挖到 10/19。细则出来以后再看接下来怎么操作

text:
做市商最狠的一刀，往往不是拉盘，而是把自己的空单，做成全网最想跟的聪明钱。

Esp bull 早期实盘一直开着的时候，很多人只看到一件事：年榜、月榜、日榜，空单盈利经常霸前几。做空标的过百，清一色山寨，重仓单动辄几十万美金。妖币一有大涨幅的苗头，他往往已经在上面。散户的第一反应几乎都一样，慕强，跟空。

龙虾大户那边，单老婆的账号多单持仓能到百万美金量级，这波割了一批又一批的人。Esp bull 这边，空单铺得又密又重。两套仓位看起来方向相反。ESP BULL重仓做空的标的，我习惯先记下来，再拿自己手上的数据对一遍，低位有没有吸筹痕迹、内幕地址买入的痕迹、拉升前有没有先把做多的人洗出去等。近两个月里，on、take、bless、tut 都是这个路子。他的空单仓位都在几十万美金以上，散户大批量跟进去做空后，立马拉盘，反反复复屡试不爽。

空单盈利是真的，这点不假。这些币最后大多砸盘、归零，榜单不会骗人。关键问题是爆仓价永远在做市商真正愿意拉到的最高价上面。他不怕空，因为他知道天花板在哪。跟单的人不知道，扛不住浮亏，也扛不住聪明钱还在空的心理压力，中途砍仓、甚至反向追空。

人性这里几乎没变过。散户不长记性，是因为慕强比复盘舒服。看到一个账号连续霸榜，本能就是复制方向，而不是问：这个账号为什么敢把爆仓价放得那么从容，为什么重仓空的标的最后常常还能再拉一截。做市商要的就是收割流动性。空单公开着，像诱饵，跟空的杠杆，才是真正的燃料。

Tut 那波操盘完，Esp bull 实盘关掉，到现在接近两个月，新的妖币几乎没再成批冒出来。实盘一关，可供追踪的空单信号也断了，跟单的流动性也就减弱

链上追聪明钱被反复割的那套，在合约里换了个马甲，又来一遍，屡试不爽，链上被跟单地址割了无数遍的人，还是会继续跟，没办法，谁叫他们的总盈利极度夸张呢。人性的弱点，本就如此。做市商最恨的一刀，就是把自己伪装成散户最喜欢看到的样子。

text:
But also:

- We now have the precedent that centralization will result in a PoW change, creating a strong disincentive to do it.

- BLAKE2b doesn't have any known vulnerabilities (like SHA256d's ASICBoost) and is very simple for new ASIC manufacturers to enter the market. There are already 6 or 7. 

- Since we had to reorganize the header anyway, we also fixed several long-standing issues with it. One of those issues fixed is block withholding attacks. The only way previously to defend against them was incentives and KYC. With the new format, it is possible to defend completely at a technical level.

- The new header also increases the nonce space significantly, avoiding the need for mining hardware to handle Bitcoin internals - often incorrectly, a problem that interferes with generating payouts to miners directly.

text:
近期盘面上涨中，表现强势的热门协议最近都不太平，接连遭遇突发安全事件。

昨天是 NEAR 跨链协议被盗走约 380 万美元，今天，又轮到了 AAVE 遭遇黑客攻击。

@SlowMist_Team 发布安全警报，AAVE v3 上的一个 Safe 模块遭遇攻击，损失约 114 ETH,约 31 万美元。

还是快速看一下事件来龙去脉和影响：

第一， 对 AAVE 持有者而言最关键的事实是：AAVE v3 核心合约没有受到任何影响。

Aave 创始人 @StaniKulechov  明确回应，被利用的是构建在 Aave 之上的第三方外部适配器。具体来说，是一个名为 FlashLoopAdapter 的自定义 Safe 模块（用于管理杠杆循环仓位）。

黑客利用了该第三方模块的访问控制漏洞，绕过鉴权，通过闪电贷抽走了目标多签钱包内的抵押资产。
简单来说，这是用户自定义集成工具的漏洞，而不是 AAVE 底层借贷逻辑被攻破。

第二，与 NEAR 遇袭后短线下跌 8% 不同， $AAVE 价格在事件发酵当天并未崩盘，反而维持了上涨态势，日内涨幅一度接近 10%。

114 ETH 的损失相对于 AAVE 庞大的 TVL 而言影响极其微小。

不过，NEAR 和 AAVE 连续两天出现安全警报，很容易让大家产生“涨完必有黑天鹅”的避险错觉。

但客观来看，随着链上活跃度、资金杠杆率和跨链路由的成倍增加，第三方模块、跨链存取款接口和热钱包的攻击面也随之急剧扩大。

在上涨期注意力更多的放在项目上，常态风险在活跃市场更容易被集中放大；而如果在熊市，可能项目出了黑客被盗的事故，大家都不太关注...

话说回来，加密项目的安全问题一直老生常谈。现在项目核心协议安全，不代表第三方组件无懈可击。

盲猜后市还有更多安全事故发生，经常链上交互和理财的玩家还是需要留个心。
author: TechFlowPost
quoted_text:
今天，围绕 NEAR 生态的跨链协议发生了一起安全事件，盘面短线跳水约 8%。

很多持有 $NEAR 的玩家比较担心生态安全与后市走势。

这里梳理一下事件的完整始末和关键信息：

首先需要厘清资产边界，此次受影响的是构建在 NEAR 上的跨链意图协议 NEAR Intents，而不是 NEAR 自身的 L1 主网共识层。

整起事件在过去 48 小时内的发展脉络如下：

1.先拦截外部赃款： 
几天前 Bitget 交易所遇袭后，黑客曾试图将超过 5000 万美元的被盗资金通过 NEAR Intents 进行链上清洗，被其 AI 安全模块 SHIELD 成功识别并冻结阻截。

2.存取款接缝被攻破：
10月1日，有黑客利用 Omni 存取款基础设施与 NEAR Intents 合约交互时的逻辑漏洞，从 BNB Chain 上的金库地址转走了约 387 万枚 USDT（随后转入交易所换成比特币）。

3.官方应急与赔付： 
NEAR 创始人 Illia 发文澄清，团队在监测到异常后 1 小时内修补了合约漏洞。目前核心服务已陆续恢复，并对 BSC、Polygon、TON、Avalanche 等 11 条涉及 Omni 修复的网络暂停存取款约 12 小时。
同时，官方承诺对所有受影响用户进行全额赔付。

受事件发酵影响，$NEAR 价格日内由 5.5 美元附近短线下探至 4.74 美元附近，跌幅约 6%–8%。

从事件影响来看，NEAR Intents 官方披露月交易量已超过 40 亿美元，本次被盗金额为 380 万美元，整体敞口相对可控。

NEAR 在 9 月刚经历了一轮强势行情，受机密意图叙事以及 Bitwise 现货 NEAR ETF 在美挂牌交易推动。

此次盘面回撤，更多是强势行情遭遇突发安全黑天鹅后的情绪跌幅。

事件发生后，加密社区和 KOL 的评价呈现出两面：

Bankless 联合创始人 David Hoffman 评价称，中心化交易所被黑和跨链桥漏洞历来是加密行业损失最大的两类隐患，团队能在数小时内快速打补丁并承担责任、全额赔付，体现了比较成熟的工程处置水准。

但同时，社区中也有交易员指出，即使提出了“意图（Intents）”或“无桥”概念，只要底层涉及跨链资产映射与存取款接口，其交互缝隙依然是黑客持续攻击的高危地带。

text:
We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

In summary:
- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.
- Luckily, LLMs can help here too because as intelligence and code are increasingly abundant, you can ask for large, custom, discardable software artifacts (e.g. web apps, video explainers) that would have never made sense to create before. Push the boundaries here and you'll be surprised.

所以直接给黑客下最后通牒 48 小时内，把钱还回来。

所以 48 小时本质上是在给对方最后一个，把这次黑客行为包装成漏洞披露或者白帽返还的退出窗口。

期限内归还既往不咎。过了这个窗口，后面就完全按照盗窃和执法流程走。

────────────────────────────────

1/

目前这笔钱的转移路径，其实已经被扒得比较完整了。

黑客一共盗取了 386.5 万枚 USDT，拿到手以后首先全部换成 BNB，随后拆散到多个地址，再沿几条主要路径转移：

路线 A：约 800 BNB，价值约 61.3 万美元，直接转入 KuCoin。

路线 B：约 70 ETH，价值约 18.9 万美元，经过多个地址中转后进入 KuCoin。

路线 C：约 955 ETH 被转到 Ethereum 上，之后主要通过 Chainflip / THORChain 等渠道换成 BTC。最终各条路径合计形成约 34.69 BTC，价值约 293 万美元。

路线 D：约 82.2 万美元的资金，甚至又通过 NEAR Intents 自己的跨链兑换服务，换成了 ETH / BTC。

这里要注意，路线 D 和路线 C 存在部分重叠，并不是四条路线的金额直接相加。

但里面最关键的一条线索，其实是 @kucoincom 

目前大约有 80 万美元的赃款进入了 KuCoin 相关充值地址，而且其中一个充值地址，在这次攻击发生前两个月就已经使用过。

KuCoin 自己其实是能够把这个地址对应到具体账户资料上的，但 NEAR 已经报警，同时又有链上分析机构、安全公司一起追踪。

如果 KuCoin 配合的话，这个账户就是黑客本人，或者和黑客存在直接关系，那这家伙现实身份就很有可能被扒出来了。

另一边，Bitquery 当时已经能够追踪到约 99% 的资金流向。

其中大约 76% 的赃款最终被换成了 34.69 BTC，而这些 BTC 当时依然停留在 4 个地址里，没有继续移动。

所以即便黑客不断转移资产，资金链的追踪起其实一直在进行。

────────────────────────────────

2/

NEAR Intents 的 @AlexAuroraDev  在推特上直接喊话黑客：“我们已经识别出你了，你比大多数人都更清楚负责任的漏洞披露是怎么运作的。”

text:
The next use case for tokenized stocks is starting to look pretty obvious: options.

@ProdigyFi has expanded its vaults beyond crypto for the first time, starting with Nvidia (solana:Xsc9qvGR1efVDFGLrVsmkzv3qi45LTBjeUKSPmx9qEh ) on Ethereum.

If I already own NVDA and think:

“I’d be happy to sell at $X.”

I can put it into a Sell High vault, choose that price + expiry, and earn yield while waiting.

Or if I’m sitting in USDC and think:

“I’d happily buy NVDA at $Y.”

I can use a Buy Low vault and earn yield for committing to that entry price.

The yield is effectively the premium you receive for agreeing to buy or sell at a specific price.

And imo this is where tokenized stocks start becoming much more useful.

The yield isn't coming from lending the stock out, borrowing against it, or adding another liquidation layer.

You're getting paid for taking a very specific market risk around a price you already chose.

Prodigy has already been doing this with crypto.

Now they're bringing the same options-based vault structure to tokenized stocks, starting with NVDAx, with more tickers apparently coming next.

Simple product, but probably a much more useful direction for tokenized equities than just “put stocks onchain.”

text:
OPENAI DOTS = A 24/7 AI COMPANY IN A BOX

@monokern wrote a great article on how to make the most of it.

Here are 10 steps summary 

Step 1 → Don't build chatbots.

Build persistent workers with their own cloud computer, browser, terminal, files, memory and schedules. They keep working after you close the laptop.

Step 2 → Give every agent one job.

A clear responsibility, clear sources, clear working rules and a clear point where human approval is required.

Step 3 → Appoint a Chief of Staff.

One Dot receives your objective, breaks it into tasks, delegates to specialists, checks the work and assembles the final output.

Step 4 → Remove yourself from agent handoffs.

Workers should receive only the context and tools they need, execute independently and report back to the orchestrator.

Step 5 → Give them real tools.

Connect Slack, Teams, Google Workspace, dashboards, APIs and authenticated browser sessions. Without tools, they're still just conversational agents.

Step 6 → Make workflows persistent.

Use schedules and triggers so monitoring, research, reporting and operational checks happen without anyone manually starting them.

Step 7 → Keep humans around the irreversible stuff.

Agents can read, research, analyze and draft. Sending, publishing, spending or changing important records should require approval.

Step 8 → Don't waste frontier models on everything.

Use the smartest model for orchestration and difficult judgment calls, then cheaper models for high-volume background work.

Step 9 → Give the whole team shared memory.

Keep project specs, decisions, pricing, approved claims and requirements in one persistent workspace.

Step 10 → Close the business loop.

Signal → research → outreach → execution → measurement → next action.

That’s where Dots gets really interesting.

You're no longer prompting AI one task at a time, you're designing a system that keeps operating after you log off.

text:
A stock-themed community can generate trading activity while other liquidity providers collect the fees.

And now @longdotxyz wants its communities to own more of that earning power with The Community Vault.

The community vault proposes putting vault capital directly into stock-token/USDG trading pools on Robinhood Chain.

The ambition: turn stock-paired communities into major liquidity providers for the assets they rally around.

There are two distinct markets here:

A LONG community token trades against a stock token. Separately, that stock token trades against USDG, a dollar stablecoin.

Activity in the community pair can create demand for the stock token, which can feed trading through the stock/USDG market.

The upgrade connects the community treasury to that second market.

For example, a community built around NVDA could deploy vault capital into an NVDA/USDG pool. Traders using that pool pay swap fees. The vault earns the portion attributable to its liquidity position, and those proceeds can fund more liquidity or upcoming modules.

The economic appeal is broader fee exposure on LONG Ecosystem like $AI, $MOO and many others.

The vault could earn from general stock-token trading, beyond activity in its own community token. Deeper liquidity could also reduce the price impact traders face.

Ordinary Uniswap LPs already compete for these fees. LONG’s proposed advantage is its existing communities and accumulated stock-token capital. W

The rollout is also staged: older “OG” pair vaults first, starting with the highest-value vaults.

The trade-off is that a treasury becomes an active market-making position. Its asset mix changes as people trade, and fees may fail to offset underperformance versus simply holding the assets, commonly called impermanent loss.

On the other hands, concentrated positions can also stop earning fees outside their selected price range.

Wdyt of this initiative?

Are you still LONG?

Thank you so much @ZealynxSecurity for auditing Yieldcoin v2 and finding a CRITICAL and a HIGH!

Both were issues with external interactions and have been fixed.

Special thanks @TheBlockChainer for the amazing work, including finding the crit almost instantly, and being very patient while I spent the remediation period redesigning mitigations for a single issue.

This was an extremely high-value engagement, made possible thanks to Zealynx's generous discounted audit grant program.

It was especially exciting because Zealynx's educational resources had a major impact on the epoch-based design of the protocol.

Read the report here: https://t.co/suJbeYpkiE

text:
Perhaps the most architecturally significant finding flagged in @ZealynxSecurity Yieldcoin v2 audit was that a malicious user could grief-drain the Yieldcoin vaults' $LINK reserves.

Each crosschain vault holds LINK to pay for the protocol's use of @chainlink #CCIP. Crosschain txes are protocol-level operations rather than per-user operations, and Yieldcoin subsidizing its own protocol-level operation costs is a deliberate design decision.

Epochs are periods when users submit deposit/withdraw intents, with the net difference bridged.
A minimum 1 $USDC (1e6) is applied to per-user deposits. Due to crosschain share accounting, a similar per-user minimum enforcement was not feasible on the withdraw side (except >0)

This meant a single USDC deposit could be split up into 1 million withdraw intents, and potentially drain Yieldcoin's LINK reserves.

A handful of mitigations were implemented before deciding on the final architecture. Candidates included forfeiting epoch net-withdraw amounts less than 1e6, and charging epoch net-withdraw cohorts 1e6. These would've had a much worse UX for honest users.

The final, implemented mitigation is simply to revert closing an epoch if the epoch closes with a net-withdraw amount below 1e6 USDC. The Yieldcoin CRE workflow implements this same check before closing.

The contracts still have a minimum epoch period of 1 hour, but the Yieldcoin CRE workflow will be configured for daily, or even weekly epoch settlement.

text:
Not every failed crosschain operation should be retried.

In Yieldcoin v2, three permanent failures could be stored as recoveries:

• a transfer above the CCIP lane’s capacity
• an Aave deposit so small it rounded to zero shares
• a supply operation blocked by a cap the vault itself had consumed

The recovery path replayed the original call with the same parameters. But none of those operations could ever succeed through repetition.

Meanwhile, the stored recovery prevented the vault from moving on to other work. In the over-capacity case, this could lock every holder’s principal behind an operation that would fail forever.

Recovery logic needs to distinguish failures whose conditions can change from those whose preconditions are permanently impossible. Retry the first. Abort or reconcile the second.

This pattern appeared across three findings in our Yieldcoin v2 crosschain vault audit.

quoted_text:
十年期美债收益率盘中一度突破了5.3%，最高到5.306%，随后仍在5.3%附近。从PCE公布后约5.20%的低点算起，已经反弹了超过10个基点，通胀数据带来的缓解没有维持住。

这次核心PCE环比增长0.2%，低于预期的0.3%，确实是好消息。但同一份报告里，个人消费支出增长了0.9%，即便扣掉涨价的影响，实际消费仍增长了0.6%，说明美国人的消费需求还很强。

也就是说，通胀比市场担心的温和一些，但需求并没有明显冷下来。再加上能源价格的压力仍在，仅凭这一次PCE，还不足以让市场相信美联储很快就能结束加息，或者让利率降下来。

这轮收益率反弹，更像是市场重新考虑高利率还要维持多久。投资者如果担心未来利率更高、通胀迟迟压不下来，就会要求更高的回报才愿意买债，债券价格因此被抛售，收益率往上走。

目前十月加息的市场概率已经降到了 37% 左右，说明十年期突破5.3%，并不意味着十月一定会加息。长债还在反映未来几年的利率和持有期间的风险。说人话，就是市场越来越相信美联储会维持高利率的时间更长，甚至接下来加息的概率上升。

而对市场来说，如果十年期收益率持续处于这样的高位，即便美联储十月暂时不加息，企业融资和居民房贷的成本也很难明显降下来。借钱成本仍然很高，股票估值也会继续承受压力。尤其是九月通胀数据如果继续走高，那么对于市场的压力会更大。

关于 @SolvProtocol  索赔50 BTC 的司法程序的问题.
看他们官网, Solv公司现在是在注册在英属维尔京群岛 (BVI)  下面的,  新加坡的公司2025年注销了(因为当时新加坡严打加密公司)

他们 BVI的实体叫  Solv Legos Ltd,  地址在BVI的 "Asia Leading Chambers,Tortola,c/o Asia Leading Corporate Services (BVI) Limited,VG1110,Road Town"    是中介注册的那种空壳公司, 不过不影响.

发币什么的都是在这个公司实体下发的. 

再去Solv 官网 https://t.co/oZ9caFzYv0 看, 协议规定的是新加坡仲裁庭 做仲裁.

ok, 现在就可以找新加坡的仲裁律师了, 然后一般流程是这样的, 先给legal@solv.finance 邮件, 同时给他们 BVI公司地址发函, 约定一个合理时间,比如说30天.

时间到了还没回应, 就可以线上给新加坡仲裁庭提交仲裁申请了  (https://t.co/Y9dCH0qQfu)

一般到了这个时候, Solv公司就会派人来谈了.  

因为如果Solv不理, 或者Solv直接败诉了.  新加坡仲裁的仲裁判决, 在全球大部分司法地区都有执行效力  

发函到币安,OKX之类的交易所,以及做市商, 只要是Solv公司名下的资金都可以查封.
它也可以直接申请BVI的法庭,把Solv公司实体给破产注销了. 

Solv估计会说中国用户本来就不在支持的范围内, 是他违规在先云云. 

 不过仲裁庭也是讲道理的地方: 协议不支持的用户, 可以把他账户封了, 钱退回去.     但是除非是这个用户明显违反了反洗钱条约, 或者是和伊朗之类的受制裁实体有关, 否则是不能无限期扣押资产的.

整体成本看走到哪步了,法律费用估计是10-40万美元. 仲裁赢了的话可以拿回来一部分, 加到赔偿里.

text:
This blew up more than I expected, thank you to everyone who read it. Since the article went out:

• The near:native listing is imminent. The QTC token contract on NEAR went live on 28 Sept and a solver has already registered on it.

• Price is now hovering around $100 per quantus:native 

• Hashrate has tripled with it, and @QuantusNetwork now puts the cost of mining a coin at around $45 to $80

Now for the interesting part. I've been monitoring the Quantus github and there have been some potentially huge developments over the past 48-72h.

Back in July, NEAR became the first major chain to let you switch your account to a quantum-proof key. The switch is one transaction and you keep your account and everything in it, but you need a wallet that can create and hold that kind of key, and today that's one  wallet, @MeteorWallet 

Quantus built its whole chain on ML-DSA, the NIST post-quantum signature standard, which is the same scheme NEAR adopted in July. So its wallet already makes the kind of key NEAR now accepts. 

In the past 72h Quantus pushed code to GitHub that lets a Quantus wallet, including the offline cold wallet, be the key to a NEAR account: open an account where it's the only key, sign any NEAR transaction, and sit as a voting member on a NEAR treasury through Trezu.

As far as I can tell that makes the Quantus cold wallet the first offline quantum-proof signer for NEAR. This is exact gap Near One's CTO, Anton Astafiec (@_bendersgreat_) flagged in May, when he wrote that current hardware wallets don't support quantum-safe signing at all and the goal was "to collaborate with hardware wallet manufacturers to bring new solutions to the market as soon as possible."

It hasn't been tested live yet, by their own notes, and it doesn't cover Intents swaps. But put it next to the rest of what we know: 

- Quantus maintains forks of NEAR's core software

- NEAR's bridge factory deployed the token contract

- NEAR Foundation is co-hosting the QDay conference 
- And now a Quantus key can sit on a NEAR treasury

That reads like two teams building together rather than a project getting listed. So the questions I'm now asking are whether the Quantus cold wallet ends up as the default quantum-proof key for NEAR, and whether NEAR's own treasuries end up with one on them. 

If either is yes, next week's listing is the smaller of the two stories.

author: CryptoTrix1
quoted_text:
$GOOGL 巴菲特、德鲁肯米勒、Tepper同时把目光放向Alphabet：顶级资金正在重新定价Google的AI价值

巴菲特、德鲁肯米勒、David Tepper——投资风格完全不同的顶级资金，却正在 $GOOGL Alphabet 身上出现越来越明显的交集。

Berkshire Hathaway 建立了规模可观的 Alphabet 仓位；Stanley Druckenmiller 的 Duquesne Family Office 也持有 Alphabet；David Tepper 的 Appaloosa 同样继续持有这家AI巨头。最新13F文件可以确认这些机构对Alphabet的持仓，但原文所谓“巴菲特又买入100亿美元”“Druckenmiller全新建仓”“Tepper增加7%”这些具体表述，需要按不同季度逐项核对，不能直接当成最新数字。

但比单一季度增减仓更值得关注的，是为什么这些资金开始重新审视Google。

过去两年市场最大的担忧，是生成式AI会不会颠覆Google Search。现在投资逻辑正在发生变化：Google拥有的不只是搜索入口，而是从 Gemini → Search → YouTube → Google Cloud → TPU → Waymo 延伸出去的一整套AI生态。

尤其值得注意的是Google Cloud。

AI时代真正稀缺的不只是模型，而是同时拥有模型、芯片、数据中心、企业客户、消费者入口以及全球分发能力的平台。Alphabet恰恰是少数能够把这些能力全部放在同一家公司里的科技巨头。

这也意味着市场过去围绕Google最大的那个问题——

“AI会不会摧毁Google Search？”

正在逐渐变成另一个问题：

“如果AI没有摧毁Google，反而让Google拥有更多可以商业化的入口，那么Alphabet应该值多少钱？”

$GOOGL 真正值得关注的可能不是下一季广告收入多增长几个百分点，而是市场是否正在从“搜索业务防守者”的估值框架，重新把它定义成一家拥有搜索、云计算、自研AI芯片、Gemini和自动驾驶平台的全栈AI公司。

当越来越多顶级资金开始出现在同一张持仓表上，最值得研究的不是跟着他们买，而是他们究竟看到了什么。

如果Gemini最终没有蚕食Google的护城河，而是进一步扩大它，$GOOGL 的这一轮重新定价可能走到哪里？

text:
This post perfectly sums up the rationale behind kPoints Season 2.

Season 2 was not an easy decision. We had to balance what is best for Kinetiq long term with what is fair to every stakeholder, including kPoints farmers. We took that responsibility seriously and made the decision we believe best serves both.

We know not everyone will agree with the outcome. That is inevitable. In a situation like this, there is simply no way to maximize the interests of every group at the same time.

It is also worth putting Season 2 in context.

As Omnia already mentioned, Kinetiq was exceptionally generous in Season 1: 25% of the entire supply was distributed to users simply for staking HYPE for roughly 3 months, while they continued earning yield on their assets. Very few projects this cycle have come close to that level of distribution, success and execution.

And finally, calling Kinetiq “greedy” simply does not reflect how this works.

The funds generated through the claim do not go to the team or into anyone’s pockets. They go directly to Kinetiq Foundation and will be deployed in the way we believe creates the most long-term value for the protocol and gives us the best chance of achieving the goals we set out to accomplish. 

You may disagree with the decision. That is completely fair.

But the decision was made deliberately, with the long-term interests of Kinetiq and its stakeholders in mind.
author: Kinetiq_xyz
quoted_text:
A lot of anger today on the TL re the @Kinetiq_xyz airdrop. Somewhat interesting timing, because @weremeow and myself have spent the better part of the last 2 months discussing alignment and tokens re @JupiterExchange. And @weremeow and @0xOmnia are the two most 'community'-first mavericks I know. 

Some personal thoughts.

I often think of blockchain project ecosystems as nation states. For instance when America was founded, there was a social contract between the founding fathers who led the revolution and the revolutionaries who risked live and limb to make it happen. 

In the case of a TGE, its the creation of a social contract between the team and the first airdrop recipients. 

The pioneering generation (team and airdrop recipients) had to work together to create something based on trust. In crypto projects, you trust the team to use an early stage product and in return the team gives you a share of the ecosystem.

Initial airdrops fairly done are always beautiful. The community shares in the fruits of their labor and the team commits to a future roadmap. The airdrop recipients can either choose to move on, or lock in together to build for the future. 

But airdrop two is always hellish. There simply is no good way of doing a second airdrop. Maybe @chameleon_jeff can figure something out. But literally nobody has done it. If I had to take a guess, it would be to disproportionately drop more to those who had staked day one and continued using the project - but this would simply lead to screams of unfairness. 

Because it is unfair. Its PvP between the pioneers and the immigrants - the immigrants being those who came after the project was successful. The immigrants didn't have to take the risk of project failure, or shitty smart contracts. You literally have a liquid trading token as a reference price or calculating your EV. 

You see nation states deal with this in a variety of ways. Immigrants have to pay more to reap the benefits of the existing infrastructure. Naturalisation processes to ensure immigrants have to actually put down roots to become citizens, rather than extract benefits and leave. Immigration is an unsolved problem - even in the real world today. 

The recurring question, asked by every visionary blockchain community founder today is how do I permissionlessly create long term alignment with long term people? 

Kinetiq's way of doing it is in my biased opinion as a friend and angel, brilliant, all things considered. I'd perhaps have gone further by extending the exercise window to say a year by paying a price, rather than creating a 10 day window (which pins price and may just lead to a lot of people not exercising).

The reason being you have very few options when doing a second airdrop as a founder. These are the common ones I've seen.

1. Airdrop size similar to first airdrop. Farmers dump on the long-term holders (the most important group). Opportunist tourists gain at the expense of the risk-taking pioneers. Jupiter did this and the community suffered immensely for it. 

2. Airdrop size smaller than first airdrop. Farmers dump (less), and incessantly bitch about how unfair everything is. Long-term holders still eat pain.

3. Extend points season forever. Cynically, probably the most effective but very bad for the soul. But you could theoretically just keep delaying points and people will keep using the protocol because of sunk cost. 

I personally think the @Kinetiq_xyz mechanism isn't bad at all, because a wide drop of zero cost basis tokens is untenable and frankly, retarded. 

If I designed an airdrop mechanism, I'd probably go for an incredibly heavy weight towards long-term stakers, perhaps even disqualify non-stakers altogether. Or here's some free tokens, stake and continue using the protocol to unlock (@shufflecom did something like this on their first airdrop). Would probably piss people off anyway. 

There will be a lot of anger at @0xOmnia on the timeline for this. But a lot of that anger will be from people that matter less. The real pain (from experience in the Jupiter seat) is placating the short-termers at the expense of the long-termers. 

Because those are the people that really matter. 

Obv usual disclaimer that nothing I say is representative of Jupiter / Kinetiq etc. Personal opinions etc.

An experimental project.

It turns Pumpfun Meme coins into “artificial life” sustained by their own trading fees.

You launch a token on worldwidewebstream. This token is connected to a large language model and its own dedicated cloud-based Chrome browser. The token trades normally on Pumpfun, but the creator fees generated by each transaction do not go into the deployer’s pocket. Instead, they go into the token’s own “compute treasury,” which is used to pay for browser time and model calls.

As long as it has enough funds, it wakes up and independently browses the internet, clicks links, reads pages, and takes notes, while livestreaming its screen. When funds run low, it goes dormant, preserving the last page it visited and its notes. Nobody prompts it, and nobody remotely controls it.

The cycle is:Trading → Fees flow into the treasury → It wakes up when it has enough computing resources → Browses and records information independently → Waits for the next round of trading.

This directly turns whether the token is being traded into a condition for whether it can continue to exist.

The concept and narrative are quite compelling.

author: 0xSoju
quoted_text:
🚨 Hayden Davis, Ben Chow, Kelsier, and Meteora just beat the $LIBRA / $M3M3 class action.

Not after a trial. After an 81-page opinion.

Judge Rochon dismissed the ENTIRE case with prejudice. You cannot RICO a six-month memecoin launch. You cannot sue a Solana DEX as if it were a partnership. And “Milei posted it” is not a fraud claim against the guy who built the liquidity pool.

This was the SDNY class action over the December 2024 $M3M3 launch and the February 2025 $LIBRA token - the one tied to Javier Milei’s “Viva La Libertad” post. Plaintiffs also tried to pull in $MELANIA and other launches in a proposed second amended complaint.

The story in the complaint if you can recall, is cinematic. Insiders allegedly freeze the pool, fill wallets before the public can buy, inflate the cap, dump, and leave retail with a 90% crash. One named plaintiff lost about $19,000 on $M3M3. The other bought $LIBRA on launch day.

The court never decided whether that happened.

It decided plaintiffs sued the wrong thing, under the wrong statute, with the wrong facts.

Meteora is not a defendant. 

Dynamic Labs intervened and said Meteora is software. The court agreed plaintiffs never pleaded a real unincorporated association - no identified members, no president or treasurer, no mutual consent to a common objective. Calling a protocol a “team” does not make it suable. 

All claims against Meteora are gone.

RICO is gone. 

Closed-ended continuity needs a substantial period. Six months of token launches is not enough. Adding $MELANIA / $ENRON / $TRUST in the proposed amendment stretched it to about seven. Still not enough. Open-ended continuity also fails: Meteora and Kelsier are alleged as primarily legitimate businesses, and wire fraud is not inherently a criminal way of life. No pattern, no RICO, no RICO conspiracy.

Fraud against Chow is gone. Rule 9(b) scienter. Profit is not motive. A post-crash “I f*cked up because I enabled the guy” is not a strong inference he intended to defraud buyers on day one. 

Conspiracy dies with the underlying tort.

Kelsier is gone on jurisdiction. Once RICO drops, there is no nationwide service hook, and New York long-arm does not reach the Davis family on these facts.

Leave to amend: denied as futile. Case closed.

The takeaway is not “memecoins are legal.” The takeaway is that a viral launch plus a famous tweet is still not a RICO enterprise, and you cannot name the smart contracts as Defendant No. 5.
