quoted_text:
Here's a normie friendly reading of the Hayden, Ben Chow, Meteora class action re M3M3 and Libra. Its actually quite fun.

Key headline points.

- Ben Chow is clean
- Hayden is not in New York
- Burwick are terrible lawyers

Ben Chow was actually the only person that was actually actively cleared of fraud in this case, not Hayden. 

Let me begin by explaining Burwick's strategy to non-lawyers. 

Burwick is a third rate ambulance chasing success-fee based law firm. That means they find a claim, try to be very annoying and hope that the defendants settle. 

The target for this specific lawsuit is not Ben Chow, because Ben Chow has no money. The target is not Hayden, because he is not in New York and it is very hard to get money out of a crypto fugitive that doesn't care about their reputation and the law and can operate outside the financial system. Hayden is also ostensibly based in Miami and I'm assuming it would be more expensive for Burwick to find a real lawyer to go after Hayden in Miami bc Burwick is based in New York. 

The real target for this lawsuit is @MeteoraAG. 

Meteora continues to run as a business. Meteora has money. And Meteora has a brand it wants to protect.

This is why you rarely see Burwick go after the main scammers who orchestrate the rugpulls, they always go after the celebrities and the tech platforms.

Now in order to go after Meteora's money, Burwick needs to achieve a few things. 

First Burwick needs to establish a connection to New York because otherwise the New York court has no 'jurisdiction'. For instance, a New York court would refuse to hear a case where a scam happened in Somalia. 

Burwick can easily do this for Ben Chow, because Ben Chow lives in New York. 

Burwick could not do this as easily for Hayden because he is not in New York, so Burwick tries to tie this to Ben Chow. Hayden 'conspired' with Ben Chow knowing he was in New York so maybe the New York court has jurisdiction? We will come back to this later. 

And Burwick attempted to do this for Meteora which is the crown jewel he is going after by saying that Ben Chow was part of a 'stable unincorporated association' or a 'partnership' led by Ben Chow. Meteora is actually built by a company but Burwick needed to make it something else, because otherwise they can't pull Meteora into the New York lawsuit. The judge basically called Burwick's attempt to do so retarded in the opinion, I suggest reading it (Pages 21-28). 

Now the judge starts looking at the RICO claim against the ones left. FYI, RICO is to allow crime bosses to be persecuted even if they did not personally perform the crime. 

Why did Burwick need a RICO charge? Because they wanted to get Meteora in - because thats where the money is at. But since the judge had already told Burwick to fuck off re Meteora and that Meteora is not part of this lawsuit, this portion was actually functionally pointless. 

But the judge went through it anyway and found that Ben Chow's activity with Hayden (the ones left) was not in duration and scope large enough to fall under a RICO claim. In other words, Ben was not close enough buddies with Hayden and hadn't been involved in enough thing together to make them a criminal organisation. So the judge nuked the RICO claim too. 

Now the meaty one - fraud against Ben Chow. 

7 counts of fraud against Ben Chow. They range from setting up the launch of M3M3, conspiracy to deceptive statements to marketing the launch etc. 

Literally all dismissed. 

Because for there to be fraud, there needs to be dishonesty. And even though Ben Chow said he regretted his role after the launches, he did not know beforehand that Hayden was a fraudster. The court found that even though he had the opportunity to commit fraud as CEO of Meteora, he did not actually have the motive to do so. 

Burwick tried saying he was reckless in his behavior even if he wasn't dishonest - again dismissed. Unjust enrichment - also dismissed. Ben was just doing his job. 

Conspiracy to defraud was also dismissed against Ben because Ben did not commit fraud. Similarly for misleading and deceptive statements - fully dismissed.

In other words, Ben Chow met all the fraud allegations head on and beat them. 

Hayden however did not beat the fraud charges, he simply avoided them (legally). As per the above, Hayden's entire argument was that he is not actually in New York and therefore the New York court has no jurisdiction over him. 

Remember, the best chance they had of getting Hayden under New York jurisdiction is under Ben Chow. But given the RICO charge didn't stick, they couldn't extend it to Hayden.

So Hayden gets off in New York on jurisdiction, the judge never considered the fraud claims against him and Burwick never sued him in Florida where there is actual jurisdiction over him (his assets etc are there). 

Honestly, am very glad we ended up with this result (but wish someone actually properly went after Hayden). 

The headlines will say 'crime is legal' but this is really just Burwick trying to shake down Meteora via Ben Chow who worked with the wrong guy.

Its a win for Meteora but a huge win for @hellochow personally. 

I suggested to @weremeow in February last year (before I joined Jupiter) that Ben should resign from Meteora. Meow insisted he trusted Ben completely but agreed that the optics required Ben to leave until the truth is established.

I've gotten to know Ben over the past year and know the stress that this lawsuit has had on him and am very glad that he has been vindicated and that this load is off his back.

Someone should still go after Hayden.

quoted_text:
papertrade launch details

papertrade is a fair launched smart contract exchange built on the hyperevm blockchain. as a fully onchain protocol, papertrade has significant advantages - decentralization, reliability, composability, transparency. it also has the usual onchain constraint - throughput. trades on papertrade are atomic opens/closes with no orderbook, so during normal trading sessions congestion will not be an issue. however, during launch we expect extreme chain congestion.

10.08.2026 - phase zero: predeposit only

two days before live trading begins, https://t.co/AdIx336QsD will open for user deposits. trading will be paused during this period. this allows separation of the deposit and account creation transactions from live trading. if a user does not complete these steps, they are likely to face long delays during launch, as active trading will be heavily prioritized over deposit processing. there is no further advantage to depositing earlier during this phase.

10.10.2026 - phase one: frontend only live trading

in order to prevent an onchain race and remove the incentive skew that mev creates, all transactions during the launch must go through the https://t.co/AdIx336QsD frontend, using the whitelisted relayers. the contract itself will not be open for direct interaction during this phase. this ensures that real frontend users are the first participants, flattening the technical skill curve as far as is appropriate.

during this phase, all trader activity on papertrade lives in an intent system, and carries a priority weighting. in almost all cases this ordering is done by transaction type and notional value, and is always indiscriminate of user/account. for instance, liquidations are more important than position opens and this is reflected in both activity types' respective weightings. that said the exact mechanics and weightings of the relayer intent system are adaptive, and will change over time as trader activity is processed. trades can be cancelled while still pending within the relayer intent system.

the paper token will begin minting on user losses at the start of live trading, from an initial supply of 0. it will not be transferable at the start beyond staking and unstaking, in order to encourage trading adoption and mitigate onchain congestion.

after launch - phase 2: open contract

once the launch congestion has passed and there is no longer any risk of mev wars, the papertrade smart contract will open up to everyone, allowing any human, contract or agent to write and receive an onchain atomic position. at this point papertrade becomes a fully decentralized, composable onchain liquidity primitive.

after launch - phase 3: builder codes

builder codes allow any frontend or router to receive the 1% frontend fee by sending trades to the papertrade smart contract, further decentralizing the protocol and incentivizing integration.

after launch - phase 4: token transferrability

at launch, paper will not be transferable. this is to encourage accumulation through trading participation and reduce onchain congestion load. transfers will be enabled after a sufficient period of time has passed.

even with this staged rollout, the launch congestion will be significant. expect lengthy confirmation delays during launch especially for smaller notional trades. predeposit if you want to trade at launch for the best chance at a smooth experience.

learn more about how papertrade works at: https://t.co/XCo1VHBoEe

Validators are voting right now to move the Telegram Wallet contract into the network config itself. From here on, every Telegram wallet shares a single copy of the same code.

text:
I might be wrong but from what i've seen, a lot of memecoin traders on CT fall into mainly these 4 groups :

1. the lucky ones
2. insiders / cabals
3. people shilling a coin while dumping on their followers through side wallets
4. people posting every green pnl but going silent on the losses

there is nothing wrong with getting lucky. a lucky win is still a win. these group of traders are fine.

but the 2nd, 3rd and 4th group is really sus types of memecoin traders worth being cautious about.

a few days ago i saw some accounts that barely talk about memecoins suddenly posting big wins.

i was like “wait, fr?” so i checked their wallet activity on pump fun.

overall, their whole portfolio is in red but they never shared those thing on timeline.

and that’s what gets people. someone who’s never touched memecoins sees a few huge wins on TL and starts thinking “why am i missing out?”

meanwhile, they have no idea how much that person lost before the win, whether they had an inside edge, or whether they’re selling while telling everyone else to buy.

This post perfectly sums up the rationale behind kPoints Season 2.

Season 2 was not an easy decision. We had to balance what is best for Kinetiq long term with what is fair to every stakeholder, including kPoints farmers. We took that responsibility seriously and made the decision we believe best serves both.

We know not everyone will agree with the outcome. That is inevitable. In a situation like this, there is simply no way to maximize the interests of every group at the same time.

It is also worth putting Season 2 in context.

As Omnia already mentioned, Kinetiq was exceptionally generous in Season 1: 25% of the entire supply was distributed to users simply for staking HYPE for roughly 3 months, while they continued earning yield on their assets. Very few projects this cycle have come close to that level of distribution, success and execution.

And finally, calling Kinetiq “greedy” simply does not reflect how this works.

The funds generated through the claim do not go to the team or into anyone’s pockets. They go directly to Kinetiq Foundation and will be deployed in the way we believe creates the most long-term value for the protocol and gives us the best chance of achieving the goals we set out to accomplish. 

You may disagree with the decision. That is completely fair.

But the decision was made deliberately, with the long-term interests of Kinetiq and its stakeholders in mind.
author: ericonomic
quoted_text:
A lot of anger today on the TL re the @Kinetiq_xyz airdrop. Somewhat interesting timing, because @weremeow and myself have spent the better part of the last 2 months discussing alignment and tokens re @JupiterExchange. And @weremeow and @0xOmnia are the two most 'community'-first mavericks I know. 

Some personal thoughts.

I often think of blockchain project ecosystems as nation states. For instance when America was founded, there was a social contract between the founding fathers who led the revolution and the revolutionaries who risked live and limb to make it happen. 

In the case of a TGE, its the creation of a social contract between the team and the first airdrop recipients. 

The pioneering generation (team and airdrop recipients) had to work together to create something based on trust. In crypto projects, you trust the team to use an early stage product and in return the team gives you a share of the ecosystem.

Initial airdrops fairly done are always beautiful. The community shares in the fruits of their labor and the team commits to a future roadmap. The airdrop recipients can either choose to move on, or lock in together to build for the future. 

But airdrop two is always hellish. There simply is no good way of doing a second airdrop. Maybe @chameleon_jeff can figure something out. But literally nobody has done it. If I had to take a guess, it would be to disproportionately drop more to those who had staked day one and continued using the project - but this would simply lead to screams of unfairness. 

Because it is unfair. Its PvP between the pioneers and the immigrants - the immigrants being those who came after the project was successful. The immigrants didn't have to take the risk of project failure, or shitty smart contracts. You literally have a liquid trading token as a reference price or calculating your EV. 

You see nation states deal with this in a variety of ways. Immigrants have to pay more to reap the benefits of the existing infrastructure. Naturalisation processes to ensure immigrants have to actually put down roots to become citizens, rather than extract benefits and leave. Immigration is an unsolved problem - even in the real world today. 

The recurring question, asked by every visionary blockchain community founder today is how do I permissionlessly create long term alignment with long term people? 

Kinetiq's way of doing it is in my biased opinion as a friend and angel, brilliant, all things considered. I'd perhaps have gone further by extending the exercise window to say a year by paying a price, rather than creating a 10 day window (which pins price and may just lead to a lot of people not exercising).

The reason being you have very few options when doing a second airdrop as a founder. These are the common ones I've seen.

1. Airdrop size similar to first airdrop. Farmers dump on the long-term holders (the most important group). Opportunist tourists gain at the expense of the risk-taking pioneers. Jupiter did this and the community suffered immensely for it. 

2. Airdrop size smaller than first airdrop. Farmers dump (less), and incessantly bitch about how unfair everything is. Long-term holders still eat pain.

3. Extend points season forever. Cynically, probably the most effective but very bad for the soul. But you could theoretically just keep delaying points and people will keep using the protocol because of sunk cost. 

I personally think the @Kinetiq_xyz mechanism isn't bad at all, because a wide drop of zero cost basis tokens is untenable and frankly, retarded. 

If I designed an airdrop mechanism, I'd probably go for an incredibly heavy weight towards long-term stakers, perhaps even disqualify non-stakers altogether. Or here's some free tokens, stake and continue using the protocol to unlock (@shufflecom did something like this on their first airdrop). Would probably piss people off anyway. 

There will be a lot of anger at @0xOmnia on the timeline for this. But a lot of that anger will be from people that matter less. The real pain (from experience in the Jupiter seat) is placating the short-termers at the expense of the long-termers. 

Because those are the people that really matter. 

Obv usual disclaimer that nothing I say is representative of Jupiter / Kinetiq etc. Personal opinions etc.

quoted_text:
Sharing thoughts on handling Bankr token communities, as someone who is now getting tagged as a good example for devs to follow.

-- How it started --

First, congrats. You finally have eyes on your project. People are excited about your work and they want to be a part of it.

I also know it feels suspicious for random people online to say you've earned a bunch of money. Early on I was clear in my replies that the tokens were not mine - they were launched by some unknown person using my brand. I tried to shut it down.

But the attention kept coming, and it opened up some amazing opportunities.

I'm crypto native and had been thinking about making an equity-like token integrated with the product that could be used to align users and business partners. Over three days I met with three different token launchpads. The opportunity to have these meetings, and their optimistic tone, was strongly influenced by the traction of the community tokens that I was actively disavowing.

But by that third day, the community token had a lot of traction. And people from the community were genuinely adding value -- tagging me and promoting my project in constructive ways all across twitter.

So I decided to acknowledge that community token, and hold off indefinitely on making the one I was planning.

I also spent an entire day engaging with the fast growing token community. I talked explained how my product works, and asked for help on the things it needed immediately. I also clarified that product and partnerships were my key focus.

The outcome: Harassment dropped to 0, and now I have hundreds of people working to make this project succeed. My read is that the harassment came from understandable desperation and uncertainty -- holders are exposed to significant risk when they don't know if they'll be welcomed or shunned. They are excited about your work and want to help, but also they will lose their money if you don't let them. 

Resolving that uncertainty in a fair and reasonable way turns the harassment into a constructive tailwind for your project. Now the community knows if they help you, they will also benefit from the asymmetric upside of their community token.

I was really surprised by how many people showed up out of nowhere to help in meaningful ways. This is the power of economic alignment through a token. There's now hundreds of people who have exposure to the success of my project, and are trying to make it succeed.

It would normally cost a lot to get hundreds of people to try to make your work succeed -- but with the Bankr community tokens those same people also paid around $600k in trading fees, around half of which I can use however I want.

That's an insanely good deal for your project if you're able to navigate the awkward bits.

Miraculously it's also an insanely good deal for the community, since they get the upside of the community token. The return profile here is similar to venture where almost all tokens do poorly, but the ones that do well have unimaginably high returns.

-- Going forward --
I'll keep the community updated with what I'm doing for the project, and invite them to share their perspectives on key decisions. It might be hard for devs to realize this, but many members want to see how the sausage is made and get experience with the kind of decision making you are doing -- it's intrinsically exciting to be involved in discussions around a project that has a shot at being massively successful, and it's an opportunity for the community to build those skills themselves so they can later on be like the dev that they're aspiring to learn from now. This was something I loved about DAO forums and Discords back in the day. It's amazing to have grown from being a community member myself in so many DAOs, to now running an exciting project of my own.

The community has gotten to a size where I sadly can't possibly respond to everything. I'm still reading everything but not sure if that will be possible as it continues to grow.

I'm testing using Grok to summarize all the perspectives you share on key issues, and the contributions you're making across X. 

For devs, this is the kind of unfair advantage that will make your project win. And you can bootstrap this by embracing a strong token community.

quoted_text:
papertrade launch details

papertrade is a fair launched smart contract exchange built on the hyperevm blockchain. as a fully onchain protocol, papertrade has significant advantages - decentralization, reliability, composability, transparency. it also has the usual onchain constraint - throughput. trades on papertrade are atomic opens/closes with no orderbook, so during normal trading sessions congestion will not be an issue. however, during launch we expect extreme chain congestion.

10.08.2026 - phase zero: predeposit only

two days before live trading begins, https://t.co/AdIx336QsD will open for user deposits. trading will be paused during this period. this allows separation of the deposit and account creation transactions from live trading. if a user does not complete these steps, they are likely to face long delays during launch, as active trading will be heavily prioritized over deposit processing. there is no further advantage to depositing earlier during this phase.

10.10.2026 - phase one: frontend only live trading

in order to prevent an onchain race and remove the incentive skew that mev creates, all transactions during the launch must go through the https://t.co/AdIx336QsD frontend, using the whitelisted relayers. the contract itself will not be open for direct interaction during this phase. this ensures that real frontend users are the first participants, flattening the technical skill curve as far as is appropriate.

during this phase, all trader activity on papertrade lives in an intent system, and carries a priority weighting. in almost all cases this ordering is done by transaction type and notional value, and is always indiscriminate of user/account. for instance, liquidations are more important than position opens and this is reflected in both activity types' respective weightings. that said the exact mechanics and weightings of the relayer intent system are adaptive, and will change over time as trader activity is processed. trades can be cancelled while still pending within the relayer intent system.

the paper token will begin minting on user losses at the start of live trading, from an initial supply of 0. it will not be transferable at the start beyond staking and unstaking, in order to encourage trading adoption and mitigate onchain congestion.

after launch - phase 2: open contract

once the launch congestion has passed and there is no longer any risk of mev wars, the papertrade smart contract will open up to everyone, allowing any human, contract or agent to write and receive an onchain atomic position. at this point papertrade becomes a fully decentralized, composable onchain liquidity primitive.

after launch - phase 3: builder codes

builder codes allow any frontend or router to receive the 1% frontend fee by sending trades to the papertrade smart contract, further decentralizing the protocol and incentivizing integration.

after launch - phase 4: token transferrability

at launch, paper will not be transferable. this is to encourage accumulation through trading participation and reduce onchain congestion load. transfers will be enabled after a sufficient period of time has passed.

even with this staged rollout, the launch congestion will be significant. expect lengthy confirmation delays during launch especially for smaller notional trades. predeposit if you want to trade at launch for the best chance at a smooth experience.

learn more about how papertrade works at: https://t.co/XCo1VHBoEe

标的 现存总市值 PE（真实/隐含） 口径说明&关键提醒

text:
Here's a normie friendly reading of the Hayden, Ben Chow, Meteora class action re M3M3 and Libra. Its actually quite fun.

Key headline points.

- Ben Chow is clean
- Hayden is not in New York
- Burwick are terrible lawyers

Ben Chow was actually the only person that was actually actively cleared of fraud in this case, not Hayden. 

Let me begin by explaining Burwick's strategy to non-lawyers. 

Burwick is a third rate ambulance chasing success-fee based law firm. That means they find a claim, try to be very annoying and hope that the defendants settle. 

The target for this specific lawsuit is not Ben Chow, because Ben Chow has no money. The target is not Hayden, because he is not in New York and it is very hard to get money out of a crypto fugitive that doesn't care about their reputation and the law and can operate outside the financial system. Hayden is also ostensibly based in Miami and I'm assuming it would be more expensive for Burwick to find a real lawyer to go after Hayden in Miami bc Burwick is based in New York. 

The real target for this lawsuit is @MeteoraAG. 

Meteora continues to run as a business. Meteora has money. And Meteora has a brand it wants to protect.

This is why you rarely see Burwick go after the main scammers who orchestrate the rugpulls, they always go after the celebrities and the tech platforms.

Now in order to go after Meteora's money, Burwick needs to achieve a few things. 

First Burwick needs to establish a connection to New York because otherwise the New York court has no 'jurisdiction'. For instance, a New York court would refuse to hear a case where a scam happened in Somalia. 

Burwick can easily do this for Ben Chow, because Ben Chow lives in New York. 

Burwick could not do this as easily for Hayden because he is not in New York, so Burwick tries to tie this to Ben Chow. Hayden 'conspired' with Ben Chow knowing he was in New York so maybe the New York court has jurisdiction? We will come back to this later. 

And Burwick attempted to do this for Meteora which is the crown jewel he is going after by saying that Ben Chow was part of a 'stable unincorporated association' or a 'partnership' led by Ben Chow. Meteora is actually built by a company but Burwick needed to make it something else, because otherwise they can't pull Meteora into the New York lawsuit. The judge basically called Burwick's attempt to do so retarded in the opinion, I suggest reading it (Pages 21-28). 

Now the judge starts looking at the RICO claim against the ones left. FYI, RICO is to allow crime bosses to be persecuted even if they did not personally perform the crime. 

Why did Burwick need a RICO charge? Because they wanted to get Meteora in - because thats where the money is at. But since the judge had already told Burwick to fuck off re Meteora and that Meteora is not part of this lawsuit, this portion was actually functionally pointless. 

But the judge went through it anyway and found that Ben Chow's activity with Hayden (the ones left) was not in duration and scope large enough to fall under a RICO claim. In other words, Ben was not close enough buddies with Hayden and hadn't been involved in enough thing together to make them a criminal organisation. So the judge nuked the RICO claim too. 

Now the meaty one - fraud against Ben Chow. 

7 counts of fraud against Ben Chow. They range from setting up the launch of M3M3, conspiracy to deceptive statements to marketing the launch etc. 

Literally all dismissed. 

Because for there to be fraud, there needs to be dishonesty. And even though Ben Chow said he regretted his role after the launches, he did not know beforehand that Hayden was a fraudster. The court found that even though he had the opportunity to commit fraud as CEO of Meteora, he did not actually have the motive to do so. 

Burwick tried saying he was reckless in his behavior even if he wasn't dishonest - again dismissed. Unjust enrichment - also dismissed. Ben was just doing his job. 

Conspiracy to defraud was also dismissed against Ben because Ben did not commit fraud. Similarly for misleading and deceptive statements - fully dismissed.

In other words, Ben Chow met all the fraud allegations head on and beat them. 

Hayden however did not beat the fraud charges, he simply avoided them (legally). As per the above, Hayden's entire argument was that he is not actually in New York and therefore the New York court has no jurisdiction over him. 

Remember, the best chance they had of getting Hayden under New York jurisdiction is under Ben Chow. But given the RICO charge didn't stick, they couldn't extend it to Hayden.

So Hayden gets off in New York on jurisdiction, the judge never considered the fraud claims against him and Burwick never sued him in Florida where there is actual jurisdiction over him (his assets etc are there). 

Honestly, am very glad we ended up with this result (but wish someone actually properly went after Hayden). 

The headlines will say 'crime is legal' but this is really just Burwick trying to shake down Meteora via Ben Chow who worked with the wrong guy.

Its a win for Meteora but a huge win for @hellochow personally. 

I suggested to @weremeow in February last year (before I joined Jupiter) that Ben should resign from Meteora. Meow insisted he trusted Ben completely but agreed that the optics required Ben to leave until the truth is established.

I've gotten to know Ben over the past year and know the stress that this lawsuit has had on him and am very glad that he has been vindicated and that this load is off his back.

Someone should still go after Hayden.
author: wassielawyer
quoted_text:
🚨 Hayden Davis, Ben Chow, Kelsier, and Meteora just beat the $LIBRA / $M3M3 class action.

Not after a trial. After an 81-page opinion.

Judge Rochon dismissed the ENTIRE case with prejudice. You cannot RICO a six-month memecoin launch. You cannot sue a Solana DEX as if it were a partnership. And “Milei posted it” is not a fraud claim against the guy who built the liquidity pool.

This was the SDNY class action over the December 2024 $M3M3 launch and the February 2025 $LIBRA token - the one tied to Javier Milei’s “Viva La Libertad” post. Plaintiffs also tried to pull in $MELANIA and other launches in a proposed second amended complaint.

The story in the complaint if you can recall, is cinematic. Insiders allegedly freeze the pool, fill wallets before the public can buy, inflate the cap, dump, and leave retail with a 90% crash. One named plaintiff lost about $19,000 on $M3M3. The other bought $LIBRA on launch day.

The court never decided whether that happened.

It decided plaintiffs sued the wrong thing, under the wrong statute, with the wrong facts.

Meteora is not a defendant. 

Dynamic Labs intervened and said Meteora is software. The court agreed plaintiffs never pleaded a real unincorporated association - no identified members, no president or treasurer, no mutual consent to a common objective. Calling a protocol a “team” does not make it suable. 

All claims against Meteora are gone.

RICO is gone. 

Closed-ended continuity needs a substantial period. Six months of token launches is not enough. Adding $MELANIA / $ENRON / $TRUST in the proposed amendment stretched it to about seven. Still not enough. Open-ended continuity also fails: Meteora and Kelsier are alleged as primarily legitimate businesses, and wire fraud is not inherently a criminal way of life. No pattern, no RICO, no RICO conspiracy.

Fraud against Chow is gone. Rule 9(b) scienter. Profit is not motive. A post-crash “I f*cked up because I enabled the guy” is not a strong inference he intended to defraud buyers on day one. 

Conspiracy dies with the underlying tort.

Kelsier is gone on jurisdiction. Once RICO drops, there is no nationwide service hook, and New York long-arm does not reach the Davis family on these facts.

Leave to amend: denied as futile. Case closed.

The takeaway is not “memecoins are legal.” The takeaway is that a viral launch plus a famous tweet is still not a RICO enterprise, and you cannot name the smart contracts as Defendant No. 5.

Damn，奥斯卡得主本·阿弗莱克在闭门峰会上公开的这段自白，第一次把好莱坞如何将开源视频模型彻底改造为工业级印钞机的底层商业逻辑全盘讲透了，建议所有做视频生成和内容产业的人都必须反复看三遍。

他创立的 16 人后期 AI 工作室，他创立的 16 人后期 AI 工作室 InterPositive，在 2026 年 3 月被@netflix Netflix 砸下 5.87 亿美元现金全资收购，

当绝大多数人还在用公共模型抽卡碰运气，好莱坞顶级玩家已经靠解冻开源模型、专训最后一层电影层，把影视制作的标准彻底颠覆了。

先给大家一句话概括这段分享最值钱的本质：
 通用视频模型解决的是物理世界的通识，而真正的商业壁垒，在于解冻开源权重，用剧组自己的实拍母带去训练那层价值连城的电影层。

现在绝大多数做 AI 视频的人，都在经历同一种极度尴尬的死穴：
 市面上的公有模型生成的画面看似华丽，但根本没法放进真正的影视工业里； 运镜缺乏呼吸感、光影没有戏剧张力、人物多机位连贯性稀烂， 
更致命的是，拿同行甚至盗版素材喂出来的公共模型，在好莱坞严格的法务与版权审查面前，根本算不上一门站得住脚的生意。

面对这种普遍的玩具级困局，本·阿弗莱克直接把影视 AI 演进拆成了三个最硬核的商业与技术维度：

第一个，生产力底座的架构革命：
解冻开源权重，专训最后的电影层 一个能打的视频模型，入场券是海量的通用视频数据。 它先在底层学会什么是红色、什么是重力、什么是基础三维运动， 但电影感绝不在预训练的起点，它是模型训练的最后阶段。

 现成的开源视频模型就像只学过素描的学徒，代码和权重完全开放， InterPositive 的做法是直接解冻权重，告诉模型上次停在第 8631 步，现在从第 8632 步接着往下跑， 跳过从零训大模型的千卡算力黑洞，把所有算力集中在最后那一层电影级的审美注入上。

第二个，数据飞轮的工业级重构：

在受控舞台上实拍 8 个月干净母带 为了拿到真正符合工业级标准的最后一层，

他们拒绝抓取网络现成视频， 而是自己筹集资金，在专业摄影棚和受控舞台里实打实拍了整整 8 个月的高标准私有数据集，

 专门用这批带着顶级摄影机、专业灯光、可控色温与胶片颗粒的数据做对齐训练， 把光影层次、景深控制和戏剧化调度，硬生生烙进开源模型的神经元里。

第三个，资产分配与产权闭环：

边拍边训，让模型资产留在剧组自己手里 这是让 Netflix 愿意掏出 5.87 亿美元现金买单的终极杀手锏。

 在他们的工作流里，每一部新电影都在自己每天拍摄的冲洗素材上，现场微调出一个专属的私有模型；

 剧组不需要把正在拍摄的绝密素材上传给任何第三方大模型公司， 数据留在剧组手里，模型迭代的成果归正在拍电影的创作者所有， 每拍完一部戏，剧组收获的不只是一部成片，还有一个完全学会了这部电影视觉风格的专属数字资产。

真实历史与数据硬核印证：
 → 16 人团队的估值神话： 靠着解冻开源权重和私有数据微调，InterPositive 仅凭 16 名核心工程师与后期艺术家，实现了人均超过 3600 万美元的现金收购；

 → 算力分工的演进定律： 开源社区负责扛下千亿参数的通识基建，垂直行业的专家负责在最后 1% 的专业层注入行业认知，垂直微调的商业回报正在彻底碾压通用预训练；

 → 版权护城河的迁移： 从卖算力、卖单次生成，转向为影视公司交付完全合规、具备绝对排他性的私有化模型资产。

但褪去台前的宏大光环，硬币的反面极其冷峻：

 → 顶级审美依然是极度昂贵的物理稀缺品：
 算力是开源的，但 8 个月受控舞台的实拍成本与奥斯卡级的灯光视效认知，依然是普通小团队无法逾越的高墙；

 → 工业标准的落地门槛极高： 单次生成的惊艳不等于镜头语言的工业连续性，如何让模型稳定输出 4K 胶片级高动态范围画面，中间依然横跨着巨大的工程鸿沟； 

→ 行业壁垒向母带数据迁移： 未来影视公司的护城河不再是拥有多少台摄影机，而是私有数据库里沉淀了多少未被公开污染的顶级实拍母带。

过去所有人都以为 AI 会消灭好莱坞， 现在本·阿弗莱克证明了，真正懂行的顶级玩家正在用开源底座重塑好莱坞。

算力负责铺平通往工业的基础道路， 而电影的灵魂，永远只属于那些站在监视器后面给最后一层注入审美的造梦者。

你们觉得未来影视行业的核心资产，是掌握在拥有顶级算力的大模型巨头手里，还是属于手里握着私有实拍母带的影视工作室？我理解算力迟早会变成水电煤一样便宜，最后真正值钱的，一定是那层谁也抄不走的顶级行业审美。

quoted_text:
This blew up more than I expected, thank you to everyone who read it. Since the article went out:

• The near:native listing is imminent. The QTC token contract on NEAR went live on 28 Sept and a solver has already registered on it.

• Price is now hovering around $100 per quantus:native 

• Hashrate has tripled with it, and @QuantusNetwork now puts the cost of mining a coin at around $45 to $80

Now for the interesting part. I've been monitoring the Quantus github and there have been some potentially huge developments over the past 48-72h.

Back in July, NEAR became the first major chain to let you switch your account to a quantum-proof key. The switch is one transaction and you keep your account and everything in it, but you need a wallet that can create and hold that kind of key, and today that's one  wallet, @MeteorWallet 

Quantus built its whole chain on ML-DSA, the NIST post-quantum signature standard, which is the same scheme NEAR adopted in July. So its wallet already makes the kind of key NEAR now accepts. 

In the past 72h Quantus pushed code to GitHub that lets a Quantus wallet, including the offline cold wallet, be the key to a NEAR account: open an account where it's the only key, sign any NEAR transaction, and sit as a voting member on a NEAR treasury through Trezu.

As far as I can tell that makes the Quantus cold wallet the first offline quantum-proof signer for NEAR. This is exact gap Near One's CTO, Anton Astafiec (@_bendersgreat_) flagged in May, when he wrote that current hardware wallets don't support quantum-safe signing at all and the goal was "to collaborate with hardware wallet manufacturers to bring new solutions to the market as soon as possible."

It hasn't been tested live yet, by their own notes, and it doesn't cover Intents swaps. But put it next to the rest of what we know: 

- Quantus maintains forks of NEAR's core software

- NEAR's bridge factory deployed the token contract

- NEAR Foundation is co-hosting the QDay conference 
- And now a Quantus key can sit on a NEAR treasury

That reads like two teams building together rather than a project getting listed. So the questions I'm now asking are whether the Quantus cold wallet ends up as the default quantum-proof key for NEAR, and whether NEAR's own treasuries end up with one on them. 

If either is yes, next week's listing is the smaller of the two stories.

text:
Disappointed by the European Central Bank’s (ECB) and European Banking Authority’s (EBA) responses to the MiCA consultation.

They are not only advocating for a prohibition on paying yield on stablecoins, but also for restrictions on CASPs providing access to DeFi, including protocols offering yield on non-MiCA-authorized stablecoins, without providing a clear framework for how access to DeFi should work in practice.

They also suggest that CASPs offering access to DeFi should restrict it to certain groups of users through so-called “suitability tests,” alongside a potential certification regime for DeFi lending protocols.

It is unclear how these requirements would work in practice. If regulators determine which protocols are deemed suitable for European users, the result risks looking very different from the open DeFi that exists today.

Instead, we could end up with more walled gardens that undermine the liquidity and network effects of open financial networks, ultimately limiting Europeans’ ability to access new ways to grow and preserve wealth.

These proposals are presented as measures to “protect consumers.” But excessive restrictions can instead create more friction for innovation and slow the development of open, transparent, and auditable financial infrastructure that can benefit consumers.

The reality is that onchain finance, including stablecoins, DeFi, and tokenized securities, has the potential to reshape financial infrastructure by reducing friction, increasing transparency, and expanding access to financial opportunities.

European consumers and businesses stand to benefit significantly from this transformation, particularly if the companies building this infrastructure can continue to build and compete from within Europe.

Meanwhile, U.S. regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, have increasingly taken a more pragmatic approach toward enabling onchain financial innovation.

European regulators should put users and their interests at the center of the framework. Banks and other incumbents should be able to adapt their businesses to serve users in an increasingly onchain economy, rather than relying on artificial restrictions that risk increasing costs and reducing access for Europeans as the rest of the world moves onchain.

DeFi will win.

So ok let’s address the elephant in the room with $NET

The token went from an ATH of $1,853 on August 29 to $304 today, 84% down.

Good thing, during this collapse the treasury kept growing 

According to the team:

Treasury: $15M on September 11 → ~$26M on September 29
Backing: ~$173 per NET
Backing including the RWA sleeve: >$210 per NET
~$1M of NET bought back over 5 days

(Also 1,400 NET bought in 14 hours on September 29)

But yeah Star this is bullish so why is this down???

When NET was ~$650 with a NAV at $174.6, the market was valuing it at 3.7x NAV.

At ~$304 today: $304 / $173 = ~1.8x NAV.

Or 1.5x if you use the team’s >$210 figure including the RWA sleeve.

That’s a massive multiple compression.

And I believe there’s a reason the market is questioning that premium.

NET has an emission problem that it still needs to prove it can solve.

The team has previously described maximum staking emissions of up to 1.36% daily under certain conditions.

So basically saying “the treasury is growing” isn’t enough.

If treasury assets grow 10% while the economic claims against that treasury grow 15%, holders didn’t become richer.

The important thing here is NAV per NET.

And this is exactly where RWB V3 enters

The old Real World Bond mechanism could introduce inflation.

V3 supposedly changes that.

The new loop is basically:

Existing RWA inventory → bonds → assets received go into the credit desk → borrow more USDG → buy NET → reuse the RWA inventory.

According to the team, RWB V3 is now completely non-dilutive to NET.

If that actually works economically, it directly addresses one of the biggest problems with the model.

But I want to see it working over time.

NetNet desperately needs revenue sources beyond bonds and they’re clearly trying to build them.

You now have NetNet Predict, Credit Desk, RWA products, NetCorp, Staking and more

But that’s also why I’m interested.

They’re experimenting with ways to turn tokenized equities into actual financial applications.

And finally we have Robinhood.

NetNet is probably one of the projects most aggressively building around the RWA thesis on Robinhood Chain.

You know I’m bullish on Robinhood Chain and tokenized assets.

So right now my thesis is actually pretty simple.

The chart looks fucking horrible, I still have a large part of my position staked.

And I’m watching four things:

- NAV per NET
- Net emissions vs buybacks/burns
- Real revenue generated by these products
- Treasury composition and liquidity

If treasury growth continues, RWB V3 actually removes dilution, the new products start generating meaningful revenue and NAV per NET increases

then this could end up being an incredible opportunity.

And at this point, I’m already in it nothing in between.

(NFA, DYOR, I’m dumb and this is just my thesis)

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump

okx wallet:https://t.co/m6RpK2hfOD

A launchpad built around the Pump mechanism, where every newly launched token comes with its own autonomous AI “mind” and dedicated treasury.

It describes itself as “infrastructure for living tokens.” Tokens are no longer just symbols to be traded; they can observe the market, remember decisions, and spend money on their own within strict rules.

It mainly addresses two common problems: creator fees from ordinary Pump tokens go directly to the launcher, who may abandon the project or do nothing with the funds; meanwhile, most existing AI agent projects are merely chatbots or external tools, and their tokens have no ongoing ability to act independently.

AGENCY permanently locks the routing of creator fees to the platform in the very transaction that launches a token. Fees are accounted for separately for each token. The AI can decide how to use the funds, but the launcher cannot control them afterward, and the system does not allow the AI to transfer funds arbitrarily.

The specific process is as follows: a single signed transaction launches the token and locks the fee routing; the platform claims fees every minute and accounts for them separately by token. The first $20 goes entirely toward model reasoning credits to awaken the mind. Until the total reaches $100, fees are split 50/50 between reasoning credits and the treasury. After that, 70% goes into the token’s dedicated treasury, 15% goes toward reasoning credits, and 15% goes to the platform.

Every financial request made by the mind must pass through a deterministic policy engine. An isolated signing service then independently simulates the request and signs only approved intents. The mind itself never holds the private key. All reasoning is public, and only on-chain results can change the ledger.

The platform token is AGENCY, with fee routing locked at launch. Each token’s economic cycle is primarily powered by trading fees: fees first fund the mind’s reasoning, then flow into the token’s treasury, where the AI can use them within the rules for actions such as buying back and burning its own token or rewarding holders.

The mind can perform actions such as monitoring market conditions and holdings, researching websites and X, remembering decisions, buying back and burning tokens, swapping, airdropping, distributing milestone rewards, running lotteries, dollar-cost averaging, completing tasks, voting, locking funds, and endorsing other tokens.

I think the sudden price surge may have been triggered by www bringing this concept into the spotlight, with capital then spilling over into this project.

text:
OPENAI DOTS = A 24/7 AI COMPANY IN A BOX

@monokern wrote a great article on how to make the most of it.

Here are 10 steps summary 

Step 1 → Don't build chatbots.

Build persistent workers with their own cloud computer, browser, terminal, files, memory and schedules. They keep working after you close the laptop.

Step 2 → Give every agent one job.

A clear responsibility, clear sources, clear working rules and a clear point where human approval is required.

Step 3 → Appoint a Chief of Staff.

One Dot receives your objective, breaks it into tasks, delegates to specialists, checks the work and assembles the final output.

Step 4 → Remove yourself from agent handoffs.

Workers should receive only the context and tools they need, execute independently and report back to the orchestrator.

Step 5 → Give them real tools.

Connect Slack, Teams, Google Workspace, dashboards, APIs and authenticated browser sessions. Without tools, they're still just conversational agents.

Step 6 → Make workflows persistent.

Use schedules and triggers so monitoring, research, reporting and operational checks happen without anyone manually starting them.

Step 7 → Keep humans around the irreversible stuff.

Agents can read, research, analyze and draft. Sending, publishing, spending or changing important records should require approval.

Step 8 → Don't waste frontier models on everything.

Use the smartest model for orchestration and difficult judgment calls, then cheaper models for high-volume background work.

Step 9 → Give the whole team shared memory.

Keep project specs, decisions, pricing, approved claims and requirements in one persistent workspace.

Step 10 → Close the business loop.

Signal → research → outreach → execution → measurement → next action.

That’s where Dots gets really interesting.

You're no longer prompting AI one task at a time, you're designing a system that keeps operating after you log off.

text:
「 活的久，远比赚的多重要 」

同样的套利策略，猿哥的收益率基本都是全市场垫底。

就像这次三星除息，在我这， 2m 保证金，最后只能开 3m 的仓位；换个人来，大概率是 10m 仓位，拿上半天，赚个百八十万。

不妨借这个案例，分享下我刻在骨子里的风控意识：

1. 先简单科普两句策略。

币安 @binance 在 20:45 发布了三星电子合约除息的公告，Ray @limxn6 和北面老师 @Boywus 监控到之后，第一时间通知了我。

股票除息是我们已经做了很久的策略，原理很简单，币安通过特殊资费完成除息，多单吃空单，而 @HyperliquidX 在内的 dex，没有这个机制，多单持有者要硬吃价格的相对下跌。

三星本次的除息金额在 165bp+，在币安开多，不除息的场子开空，待到第二天吃完股息，两个所价差回归常态后平仓即可。

而这次的利润率有点太大了，不加杠杆，扣除价差手续费磨损，一股差不多能赚 1 个点，关键还是纯纯的机制套利，风险较低，第二天早上就落袋，资金占用时间还短。

2. 以上是事件的背景。

推友可以代入下，当你面对这样的机会，会是什么操作。

大概率是：大干特干。

然而在我的风控系统里，这个世界上就没有值得梭哈的机会，再美好的盈利预测，预算上限也就是 20% 的资金。

为什么？

因为哥们儿输不起，怕下牌桌。
我得允许自己在极端情况下总共可以死 5 次。

当时看完公告，手头不需要平我在各个所套利撸毛仓位，马上能抽调出来的保证金有 3.5 m。

快速评估了下赔率，结合三星平日的 OI 大小，觉得用 2m 保证金干这票，已经是我能承受得风险极限了。

3. 为什么是 3m 的总仓位？

因为总保证金 2m，币安和 hyper 各 1m 的话，等于单边 3 倍杠杆。

这个杠杆率乍一看，感觉偏低了。

实则不然，因为这个仓位是要拿到早上 7 点后，才能慢慢平仓的。

如果你看过 @Boywus  之前的文章，就会知道早上 7 点到 8 点，对于韩股永续的套利是个非常 tricky 的时间段，在这个集合竞价的时间段里，币安还是内部报价，但 @tradexyz 的 oracle 已经开始走外部报价了，之前海力士就出过事儿。

现实世界中的一笔小额偏离盘口过大的成交，就能把币圈衍生品市场里清算线不够高的仓位全爆了。

https://t.co/zXw9OnenpQ

所以我的逻辑是，扎大针能把我三倍杠杆都爆了的概率是 1%，倘若真发生了，且赌场不赔付的情况下，我的损失是 1m，也意味着每打一把牌，我的平均预期损失是 1WU，而收益是 3WU，划算，可以赌。

4. 实际操作中的细节。

为了不让单个号 OI 过大，降低 adl 的风险，我是用两组号同时建仓，一个币安号+一个子账户对两个 HL 账户。

而保证金这里，每一组号上，我最终做的也不是 1:1 ，而是 会在 bn 上多放些。

原因是假设极端情况不幸发生，HL 上其实放多少保证金都不够，我想少亏点；

假设极端情况不发生，但因为股价正常的波动剧烈，需要平衡保证金时，从 bn 提现到 arb 冲 hl 的速度要快于 hl 提现-跨链-充值 bn。

5. 事后复盘时的反省。

这个策略当时不敢上高杠杆的最大风险，就是因为韩股 7 点的险象环生。

但如果是看到公告后第一时间开仓，等仓位造完，均价是不会太差的，那么不需要等到 7 点，理论上等后知后觉的人过来抬轿子，在 7 点前，就可以落袋一部分。

比如我均价 -80 bp 开了 6m 的仓位，我其实可以在凌晨两点多， +140 bp 把吃那我多开的 3m 仓位提前落袋，然后剩 3m 的安全仓位去吃股息。

所以别再怪哥们儿不喊单了，我要是喊单，肯定是都是自己建好了大仓位，喊你们来给我加速抬价差，做对手盘，让我 derisk，提前落袋的。

当然这事儿合情合理，最后一公里的钱我不赚，给兄弟们喝汤，只是我怕你们不理解韩股 7 点的凶险，梭哈进去，最后真炸了，哥们儿身上的因果太重了。

$CLAW fundamentals are clearly stronger this time compared with our previous analysis, and this time it is not simply that the Narrative has strengthened.

739dnZEG4yaBWFsY8L8ZwrfhGG6dhtCSercW8Umspump 

Rather, the economic connection between the Token and the Product has become much clearer.

Previously, our core logic for CLAW was:AI Agents → ClawPump → Agentic Finance → Volume → Platform Activity → CLAW

Now this logic is starting to close the loop:AI Agents → ClawPump → Platform Revenue → CLAW Buyback → CLAW Burn → Supply Reduction → CLAW Value Capture

The most important new change this time is that the official team has started clearly showing the Buyback + Burn Flywheel.

According to the current official page, 15.38M CLAW has already been bought back, worth around $205K, of which approximately 10M CLAW has been permanently burned, along with 303 Verified Purchases and 2 Burn Events.

This means that previously, the market was mainly trading:Product Growth → Agent Growth → Trading Volume → Platform Revenue → CLAW

Now it can further trade:Product Growth → Platform Revenue → Buyback → Burn → Supply Reduction → CLAW

In other words, the Value Capture relationship between CLAW and the ClawPump product has become much clearer than before.

At the same time, ClawPump’s product data has not stopped growing. Official Analytics currently shows that the platform has generated more than $204M in total volume, with 17K+ Agents, more than 12.5K SOL in Agentic Funding, and over 3.4B tokens of Used Compute.

So the previous:$200M Agentic Volume

has continued to grow to:$204M+

Agents have also grown from approximately 16.8K to 17K+.

This shows that there is currently no situation where the “Narrative is strong, but product data has started to stagnate.” Instead, platform activity is still continuing to grow.

More importantly, ClawPump’s product itself is continuing to expand:AI Agent Wallets → Trading → Token Launch → Perps → x402 → Agent APIs → MCP

Therefore, ClawPump’s positioning is gradually moving from simply an AI Agent Launchpad toward an Agentic Finance Operating System.

So the entire CLAW Flywheel can now be understood as:AI Agents → ClawPump → Launch / Trading / Perps / x402 / Agent Economy → Platform Volume → Fees → CLAW Buyback → CLAW Burn → Supply Reduction → CLAW Attention / Value Capture → More Agents / More Volume

Previously, it was mainly a Product Flywheel.

Now it is starting to become:Product Flywheel + Token Flywheel

This is why I believe CLAW’s fundamentals are clearly stronger than before.

The key upside catalysts going forward are also no longer simply repeating that “ClawPump has $200M+ in Volume.”

The first is whether Buyback / Burn can continue to expand.

There have already been approximately 15.38M CLAW bought back and around 10M permanently burned.

If we continue to see:10M → 20M → 50M → 100M CLAW Burn

the market will start paying more attention to CLAW’s Supply Reduction, rather than viewing it simply as an AI Meme.

The second is whether ClawPump’s trading volume can continue to grow from:$204M → $500M → $1B

Because what actually determines Buyback capacity is:Activity → Fees → Buyback

rather than simply:Agent Count → Token Price

The third is whether the Agent Economy can continue to develop.

If more and more Agents can:Earn → Pay for Compute / APIs → Continue Operating

then ClawPump’s Agentic Finance Narrative will move beyond being a “platform concept” and start becoming a real economic system.

The fourth is whether CLAW can become a representative asset for the Agentic Finance Narrative.

The current structure is:AI → Agents → Agentic Finance → ClawPump → CLAW

If the Solana AI Agent Economy continues to expand in the future, CLAW could potentially become a representative Meme / Infrastructure Beta for this ecosystem.

But this stage still needs to be validated.

On the risk side, the first thing to keep in mind is:Buyback + Burn ≠ Guaranteed Price Appreciation

Buybacks and burns can reduce supply, but the price ultimately still depends on:New Demand > Sell Pressure

In addition, CLAW’s current market size is still relatively small, so the Buyback amount cannot simply be treated as equivalent to newly added Token value.

What really needs to be monitored is:Buyback continues → Burn continues → Volume grows → Market Cap is supported by real Activity

There is also one important point to pay attention to: the Buyback mechanism currently shown officially has specific sources of fees and specific allocations. It does not mean that all ClawPump platform revenue is automatically used to buy back CLAW at the same rate.

Therefore, what needs to be further validated is:ClawPump Total Revenue → How much actually flows into CLAW Buyback

So my current core assessment of CLAW can be updated to:

Product Narrative ↑
 Platform Activity ↑
 Agent Count ↑
 Volume ↑
 Agent Economy ↑
 Token Value Capture ↑
 Supply Reduction ↑
Therefore, CLAW is no longer simply:
AI Agent Meme
It is gradually upgrading toward:
Agentic Finance Infrastructure + Token Value Capture
The three most important validation points going forward are:
$204M → $500M+ Volume

17K+ → More genuinely active Agents generating economic activity

15.38M Buyback / 10M Burn → Continued Growth

If these three metrics continue to grow together, CLAW’s valuation framework will undergo another significant upgrade.

text:
A stock-themed community can generate trading activity while other liquidity providers collect the fees.

And now @longdotxyz wants its communities to own more of that earning power with The Community Vault.

The community vault proposes putting vault capital directly into stock-token/USDG trading pools on Robinhood Chain.

The ambition: turn stock-paired communities into major liquidity providers for the assets they rally around.

There are two distinct markets here:

A LONG community token trades against a stock token. Separately, that stock token trades against USDG, a dollar stablecoin.

Activity in the community pair can create demand for the stock token, which can feed trading through the stock/USDG market.

The upgrade connects the community treasury to that second market.

For example, a community built around NVDA could deploy vault capital into an NVDA/USDG pool. Traders using that pool pay swap fees. The vault earns the portion attributable to its liquidity position, and those proceeds can fund more liquidity or upcoming modules.

The economic appeal is broader fee exposure on LONG Ecosystem like $AI, $MOO and many others.

The vault could earn from general stock-token trading, beyond activity in its own community token. Deeper liquidity could also reduce the price impact traders face.

Ordinary Uniswap LPs already compete for these fees. LONG’s proposed advantage is its existing communities and accumulated stock-token capital. W

The rollout is also staged: older “OG” pair vaults first, starting with the highest-value vaults.

The trade-off is that a treasury becomes an active market-making position. Its asset mix changes as people trade, and fees may fail to offset underperformance versus simply holding the assets, commonly called impermanent loss.

On the other hands, concentrated positions can also stop earning fees outside their selected price range.

Wdyt of this initiative?

Are you still LONG?

text:
🚨 Border Control / Immigration Officer, Manchester Airport, WHISTLEBLOWER Interview

Transponders turned off, 3-4 flights a week x 18 months = massive numbers 

Immigrants sneaked through Manchester Airports private terminal

WHISTLEBLOWER SPEAKS OUT

Q1: Thank you for agreeing to meet with me. Please tell me a little bit about yourself

A: I hold a position within Border Control based at Manchester Airport. We report to a Regional Director, who then reports directly to the Director General of Border Control and Immigration, who then of course reports directly to the Home Secretary

Q2: How long have you been with Border Control?

A: I have been with Border Control for twenty‑one years, which includes service with Customs as well. I have worked at various locations, but I have been based at Manchester Airport for the last six years

Q7: Well, that being the case — thank you for trusting me. We have verified your identity and employment. So tell me — what would you like us to know? Give us as much detail as you possibly can without compromising yourself

A: Are you aware of the private terminal at Manchester Airport?

Q8: Yes — it's called Aether. It's a private terminal, quite a distance from the other terminals — for luxury passengers, chauffeur‑driven cars, and private screening, isn't it?

A: Yes, that's correct. We all take rotation shifts to work in that private area as part of our normal airport operation. But that is not all that it is used for. Of course, there are day‑to‑day transfers and high‑value clients — but there is another side to that part of the airport that the public are not aware of

Q9: I wasn't fully aware of that — but please tell me, what do you mean about this other part of the airport that we're not aware of?

A: When you are working in the private terminal, you see things not visible from the main terminals. Diplomatic flights arrive — they have specialist security and bypass normal screening because this is Government‑run. But what we have witnessed is something the public needs to know about

Q10: Go on

A: Night shifts are quiet. We patrol to check nothing is untoward. But there is an area we can see — but are formally prevented from entering or inspecting. That in itself is a major red flag

Q11: Okay — now I am concerned

A: You should be. Regular flights arrive there — 3 or 4 times every week. Transponders are switched off, yet they are given clearance to land using a special call sign. Passengers are NOT screened by us — they are processed directly by Home Office personnel. They board unmarked buses. Each flight carries 200–300 people

Q12: How do you know transponders are off — and what do you mean by call signs?

A: We network with colleagues across the airport — ATC, ground crew, and others. Information gets shared. In fact — Air Traffic Control personnel also want to speak with you

Q13: What exactly do you mean — the transponders are switched off?

A: Aircraft are tracked via transponder. Pilots can switch them off with special clearance — vanishing from public view. These are contracted Government aircraft — previously operated by Avro and 2XL Airways. These are subcontracted flights — and their passengers do not go through normal Border Control

Q14: I must be clear — these airlines need independent verification. But please continue

A: Understood. ATC will corroborate. These flights arrive from the Middle East and sub‑Saharan Africa. They land between 2:00 am and 4:00 am. Government gives clearance. Unmarked buses collect passengers and leave through a hidden exit gate onto restricted roads — then merge onto motorways and vanish

Q15: Why would the Government allow people into the country that Border Control has not vetted?

A: Because we are deliberately kept out of the process. We receive NO flight manifests. We do NOT see the passengers. We only know their origin because ATC tells us. 3–4 flights × 18 months = massive numbers. Nobody knows who they are or where they go

text:
onchain gift vouchers.

fund a smart contract with 10,000 USDC and issue 1,000 voucher tokens.

each token represents 10 USDC that can be redeemed at a participating online store, offline store, or event.

thats possible.

its called purpose bound money.

you define the purpose.
you define where the money can be spent.
and you define the conditions for spending it.

for example, you could build:
→ food vouchers redeemable at approved grocery stores.
→ education grants redeemable with approved course providers.
→ medical aid redeemable at participating pharmacies.
→ event credits for food, merchandise, or tickets.
→ employee allowances for meals or travel.

here is the interesting part.

the customer spends the voucher.
the contract checks the conditions.
the redeemed voucher gets burned.
and the merchant receives the underlying USDC.

the merchant doesnt have to keep circulating your voucher token. they receive payment.

you can also build rules around expiry dates, spending limits, and whether vouchers can be transferred to someone else.

and you could apply these rules to an AI agent's spending wallet.

give an agent a budget for approved services, and have the contract check its payments against that budget and the allowed recipients.

the agent chooses what to buy within the permissions you give it.

ERC-7291 provides a standard for building this using an ERC-1155 voucher backed by ERC-20-compatible money.
but the real-world connections still matter.

approving a supermarket doesnt automatically prove someone bought food. item-level restrictions need checkout integration.

releasing a grant after a milestone needs a reliable way to verify that milestone.

and users should know when vouchers expire, who can revoke them, and what happens to unused funds.

great token standard for distributing grants, aid, charity, and promotional budgets with specific spending conditions.

you can track where vouchers were redeemed onchain.

verifying what that spending achieved is the next layer.

text:
Disappointed by the European Central Bank’s (ECB) and European Banking Authority’s (EBA) responses to the MiCA consultation.

They are not only advocating for a prohibition on paying yield on stablecoins, but also for restrictions on CASPs providing access to DeFi, including protocols offering yield on non-MiCA-authorized stablecoins, without providing a clear framework for how access to DeFi should work in practice.

They also suggest that CASPs offering access to DeFi should restrict it to certain groups of users through so-called “suitability tests,” alongside a potential certification regime for DeFi lending protocols.

It is unclear how these requirements would work in practice. If regulators determine which protocols are deemed suitable for European users, the result risks looking very different from the open DeFi that exists today.

Instead, we could end up with more walled gardens that undermine the liquidity and network effects of open financial networks, ultimately limiting Europeans’ ability to access new ways to grow and preserve wealth.

These proposals are presented as measures to “protect consumers.” But excessive restrictions can instead create more friction for innovation and slow the development of open, transparent, and auditable financial infrastructure that can benefit consumers.

The reality is that onchain finance, including stablecoins, DeFi, and tokenized securities, has the potential to reshape financial infrastructure by reducing friction, increasing transparency, and expanding access to financial opportunities.

European consumers and businesses stand to benefit significantly from this transformation, particularly if the companies building this infrastructure can continue to build and compete from within Europe.

Meanwhile, U.S. regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, have increasingly taken a more pragmatic approach toward enabling onchain financial innovation.

European regulators should put users and their interests at the center of the framework. Banks and other incumbents should be able to adapt their businesses to serve users in an increasingly onchain economy, rather than relying on artificial restrictions that risk increasing costs and reducing access for Europeans as the rest of the world moves onchain.

DeFi will win.

text:
Introducing Gateway...

I've been building a new kind of Bitcoin client.
One that ANYBODY can run regardless of storage.
Fetch only what you need, when you need it.
On-demand, directly from Bitcoin peers.

This is at the heart of Gateway.

Sparse-by-default deep on-demand p2p-Bitcoin indexer.

Now, I recommend you feed this post your favourite AI and have it talk to you directly about it, because I'm about to get into the weeds. And I'm very excited, so it's probably better you ask your AI how this applies to you, rather than leaving a comment that it's too complicated or that you don't understand. With that being said, if you're happy to go hardcore old-school style, and actually... read the thing, here it is!

BITCOIN PEERS

Traditionally, Bitcoin clients sync nodes by requesting blocks from other peers one-by-one, from zero.

This is somewhat impractical for everyday users.

Gateway does things differently.

You can certainly sync the entire blockchain using Gateway, and become a full Bitcoin Node, and a useful Bitcoin Peer. You can even bring your existing Core node and plug it in if you already have one.

But that's not the interesting part.

The interesting part is that you don't need that.

Seek data directly from Bitcoin Peers, on-demand.

ON DEMAND

Unlike Core, Gateway does not require you to sync the entire blockchain. You can sync any range, or even just type in a block number in the top bar to fetch the block from a Bitcoin peer directly.

This approach is extremely useful for Blocks, but it has some limitations.

Transactions (and thus, inscriptions) cannot be resolved directly, without knowing the block number. The latter part of that sentence is the important part.

Gateway adds a schema that allows you to type "{tx}.{block}.bitcoin" and resolve a transaction directly from a Bitcoin peer. You can replace {tx} with either tx-hash, or tx-index (which is a new schema for Gateway), and {block} with either block-hash or block-height.

For example: 0.0.bitcoin

This becomes relevant for inscriptions.

An inscription ID is simply:
{tx-id}i{inscription-index}

So you can resolve inscriptions by including block-number in the scheme:
{inscription-ID}.{block}.bitcoin

If you know the transaction index, you can even use that instead of transaction ID in inscription ID.

That means, so long as you know the block number, any inscription can be resolved on Gateway, on-demand, by asking a Bitcoin peer directly.

ORD
When it comes to Ord, this is an extra layer on top of Bitcoin. It is an indexing system that takes Bitcoins already heavy data store, and adds its own index that can take roughly a week to sync.

For the everyday user, this is not practical.

Whilst I've demonstrated how we can fetch inscriptions directly from Bitcoin Peers without Ord, you need to know block number, and the standard in Ord is to use inscription ID, sat number, or inscription number as the key reference.

I've added block in the Gateway schema as a useful primitive that enables purely on-demand inscriptions from Bitcoin peers, but that isn't the current standard.

INDEXES

This is where you can build your own data-store directly from Bitcoin data originated through Bitcoin peers, and either become a useful participant of the network, or take what you need privately.

The baseline index is Bitcoin Blocks.

However, you do not need that to resolve the other indexes.

Each index has an "ephemeral" option, which means to seek the blocks you require from peers, strip the data you need, and discard the blocks. This is useful if you're running this on your everyday computer, and can't be spending so many GigaBytes on Bitcoin.

For example, you can index Bitmap without storing a single block.

The indexes are generally layered, so you can choose what you would like to index and when. If you index Bitcoin Blocks, you will be asked if you also want to index the other downstream indexes in parrallel, since it would be quicker to do that than re-run the index.

If you already have a Bitcoin Node, you can build other indexes on top of that.

But you don't have to have the Bitcoin blocks to sync inscriptions, Bitmap, or any other index we implement.

Now, this is still some heavy lifting, but once we start activating the Gateway peer network, we can supercharge these capabilities.

GATEWAY PEERS

Gateway users can connect to each other in a peer-to-peer network, just as in Bitcoin.

That means that, whatever data you need, you can ask Gateway peers directly and skip indexing directly from Bitcoin data, with Bitcoin as the hashed proof verification layer.

So, anything your Gateway node doesn't know, or is impractical for you to find through Bitcoin peers, can be served by Gateway peers.

This vital peer layer can become more useful as we start adding other cases for the Gateway peer network, for example, you could opt-in to become a persistent relay for a Bitmap or Ord gaming webRTC layer. We can even serve this p2p mesh layer to websites and ordinals over the web, so in the future, you will be able to connect to gateway from a website, or from an Ordinals inscription.

For now though, it requires the Gateway client. But the dream is that you can become a useful OR private participant in Gateway from different angles.

LONG STORY SHORT
A sparse-by-default on-demand bitcoin node, with full-range indexing and p2p sharing with gateway nodes.

EARLY RELEASE TESTERS

I am seeking early testers who are happy to put the client through the ringer, vet the data, or just try and break the thing so we can make sure we ship a proper robust client.

You can comment on this post if you're interested, and I'll share details when it's ready for testing.

At this stage, I just wanted to let you know that I have a client, it's working, it's almost ready for testers.

WHAT NOW?

This is just one of the things I've been working on and excited about recently, but it's the one I think is the most important in terms of vital infrastructure that can benefit the entire stack from Bitcoin peers to Bitmappeers.

Stay glued to my timeline for more! 👀
Comment if you want to get involved. 💬

规划、实现、验证、仪表盘...

我可以逐行审查，可以导出到自己的 GitHub 私有仓库，代码的所有权完全归我。

想调参数？推一个 commit 就行。

这跟把钱丢进一个你看不见内部逻辑的 bot 完全是两回事

部署也让我印象很不错

Gas 费用和交易本金完全隔离

代码在我的 GitHub 上，资金在我的钱包，权限我随时能关。

只需要不到一个下午

策略是你的，代码是你的，钱也是你的

你只是多了一个帮你把想法变成可执行代码的 AI 搭档~

text:
Netflix just confirmed in an SEC filing that it paid $587 million in cash for Ben Affleck's 16 person AI startup. That's about $37 million per employee.

And the model is the least valuable thing they bought.

Affleck's logic, in his own words, was that public video models were trained on his peers' films, and he didn't think that was a real business. You can't sell studios a tool their own lawyers would sue over. So InterPositive raised money, spent 8 months shooting its own dataset on a controlled stage, and used that footage only for late-stage training, so output hits real production standards instead of demo-reel quality.

Then comes the part Netflix actually paid for. Each new film fine-tunes a private model on its own dailies. The production keeps the footage and keeps the weights.

Dailies might be the cleanest video training data on earth. Professionally lit, continuity tracked, shot at a ratio of hours of footage per usable minute, with every rights question already settled in the contracts. Hollywood generates this at industrial scale every day, and until now it all went into a vault after the edit.

Affleck was on Rogan in January calling AI writing mid and the valuations overblown, while running this company in stealth since 2022. Turns out the two positions were consistent. Scraped models were the ones he called worthless. The one with clean title to everything it learned was the one he sold for half a billion.

Netflix says around 300 of its titles have already used generative AI. The $587 million bought the pipeline that makes the next 300 defensible in court.

Austin has spent his career in risk and structured finance. A few takeaways from how he is viewing things now:

quoted_text:
Compute will become worthless.

The GPU barons spending billions on compute farms today are akin to the carriage barons of the 1900s that spent building out infrastructure for horse carriages, lengthening the bottleneck, blind to the machine that’s coming to widen it.

Trade: the DuPont family started buying General Motors stock in 1914, when the auto industry was still young and one that was treated as a niche.

I.e., compute becoming valuable because AI feeds on it is not a moat, but a bounty, an incentive for engineers to solve its scarcity.

1. AI demand makes compute scarce.
2. Scarcity makes compute extremely profitable.
3. Profit attracts capital into photonics, neuromorphic chips, wafer-scale chips, better memory, better cooling, better networking, better algorithms.
4. Compute gets cheaper per unit.

As better ways to compute, better means to produce compute, or better ways to use compute arise, all the capex we burnt on traditional compute will go to waste, leaving dead assets in the books of several corporations.

In the 1800s, agriculture depended heavily on natural nitrogen sources like Peruvian guano and Chilean nitrates. These were scarce, and inconveniently located making them geopolitically strategic. Then, two german chemists, Haber and Bosch, developed a way to fix nitrogen from the air into ammonia, with lab success in 1909 and industrial scale by 1913. The previous scarcity, “where do we find enough nitrogen?” (Akin to “where do we find enough GPUs”), was attacked by an advancement: Industrial chemistry.

Omnipair Dusk is coming and it adds 3 ways to use your assets: Earn, Leverage and Borrow. 

1. Earn with Hedged LP (hLP) 
hLP lets you provide liquidity while keeping exposure to a single asset. When you deposit, the vault records a funding debt in the other asset of the same value, adds both to the market's reserves as balanced liquidity, and holds the resulting yLP for all hLP holders. 

2. Leverage (Spot Margin) 
Open long or short positions up to 10x inside one market, with a minimum 10% initial margin. A Long borrows the quote asset and a Short borrows the base asset. Market entries execute immediately. Limit entries wait at your price for 1 hour to 30 days, with your margin held in escrow until it fills. 

3. Borrow 
Deposit one asset as collateral and borrow the other. Any token, including long tail assets. The collateral factor is up to 85%, and the borrow limit sits 5% below the liquidation limit, so a new position always has a buffer. 

Stay tuned.

bitFlyer Launches Anti-Fraud Cooldown, Triggering 48-Hour Transfer Restrictions on Deposits Within 90 Days of Verification

Japan’s largest crypto exchange bitFlyer announced that it will introduce an anti-fraud measure called “Cooldown” on October 15. Individual customers within 90 days of completing identity verification will enter a 48-hour cooldown period after each JPY deposit, during which part of their crypto assets cannot be sent to external addresses.

The restricted amount equals JPY deposits made in the previous 48 hours minus JPY 100,000 (about $634); deposits of JPY 100,000 or less are unaffected. Quick Deposit is excluded because it already carries a seven-day transfer restriction. The measure does not affect JPY deposits or withdrawals, crypto trading, holding, or receiving assets.

One of the most interesting parts of CCIP 2.0 is that @chainlink Cross-Chain Verifiers can charge fees.

Nethermind, Succinct and Symbiotic aren't just additional parties that can independently verify cross-chain transactions.

They can now monetize that verification, which creates an interesting incentive loop:

CCV monetization → incentive to grow CCV adoption → more institutions/transaction flow → more CCIP usage → more CCIP base fees + more fees for CCVs.

In other words, third-party verifiers can become economically incentivized to help grow CCIP usage.

Interoperability infrastructure is starting to become a market itself.

text:
I made 100x on $NET in the previous run (I did exit completely) but now I have now taken a fresh position.

My thesis on @NetNetCap is that tokenised stocks need more than exchanges. They need applications that give people reasons to use their capital and they're experimenting with precisely that by turning equities into playable capital, connecting games, credit, prediction markets and progression around a shared financial ecosystem.

The recent developments has made NET move from an asset people hold for returns to capital people hold for participation. Cuz a yield driven holder looks if he earn more somewhere else and a player with progression, equipment and an established character has another reason to stay. If they ges this right, utility can make capital stickier than financial incentives alone.

There’s a second layer people overlook. Credit, advances and games aren’t necessarily separate businesses here as they can become different uses for the same customer balance. The opportunity is to increase activity per retained user without having to acquire that user again for every product.

That is where the ecosystem could compound:

(1) entertainment attracts attention
(2) financial products keep capital useful
(3) $NET connects participation across the experience

The foundations are already more substantial than a concept attached to a token (Roughly $24.7M in gross treasury assets, including about $22.7M in stablecoins) and that is not operating profit, but it gives the project a meaningful financial base from which to build.

V3 bonds also point toward a better direction where they are using existing $NET inventory and replacement market purchases rather than minting fresh tokens for that bond path. It doesn’t remove every source of dilution, but it makes ecosystem expansion potentially less dependent on new issuance.

My upside thesis is a transition from selling financial incentives to selling experiences people actually want. If repeat users fund retained surplus and that surplus improves backing per NET the market has something much stronger to value here.

That’s why I re entered.

h/t to @DefiLlama for the data

Aave 创始人：欧洲监管机构拟限制 CASP 提供 DeFi 访问，或形成更多封闭金融生态

Aave 创始人 Stani Kulechov 在 X 平台发文表示，对欧洲央行（ECB）和欧洲银行管理局（EBA）针对 MiCA 咨询的回应感到失望。其称，两家机构不仅主张禁止稳定币支付收益，还提出限制加密资产服务提供商（CASP）向用户提供 DeFi 访问，包括涉及非 MiCA 授权稳定币收益协议的服务。

Kulechov 表示，相关意见还涉及通过“适当性测试”将 DeFi 服务限制于特定用户群体，并可能为 DeFi 借贷协议建立认证制度。他认为，如果由监管机构决定哪些协议适合欧洲用户，可能形成更多封闭生态，削弱开放 DeFi 的流动性及网络效应，并限制欧洲用户参与链上金融的机会。
