author: ChainCatcher_
quoted_text:
Disappointed by the European Central Bank’s (ECB) and European Banking Authority’s (EBA) responses to the MiCA consultation.

They are not only advocating for a prohibition on paying yield on stablecoins, but also for restrictions on CASPs providing access to DeFi, including protocols offering yield on non-MiCA-authorized stablecoins, without providing a clear framework for how access to DeFi should work in practice.

They also suggest that CASPs offering access to DeFi should restrict it to certain groups of users through so-called “suitability tests,” alongside a potential certification regime for DeFi lending protocols.

It is unclear how these requirements would work in practice. If regulators determine which protocols are deemed suitable for European users, the result risks looking very different from the open DeFi that exists today.

Instead, we could end up with more walled gardens that undermine the liquidity and network effects of open financial networks, ultimately limiting Europeans’ ability to access new ways to grow and preserve wealth.

These proposals are presented as measures to “protect consumers.” But excessive restrictions can instead create more friction for innovation and slow the development of open, transparent, and auditable financial infrastructure that can benefit consumers.

The reality is that onchain finance, including stablecoins, DeFi, and tokenized securities, has the potential to reshape financial infrastructure by reducing friction, increasing transparency, and expanding access to financial opportunities.

European consumers and businesses stand to benefit significantly from this transformation, particularly if the companies building this infrastructure can continue to build and compete from within Europe.

Meanwhile, U.S. regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, have increasingly taken a more pragmatic approach toward enabling onchain financial innovation.

European regulators should put users and their interests at the center of the framework. Banks and other incumbents should be able to adapt their businesses to serve users in an increasingly onchain economy, rather than relying on artificial restrictions that risk increasing costs and reducing access for Europeans as the rest of the world moves onchain.

DeFi will win.

这是一种带有期权结构的竞争。多数项目最终会消失，但只要少数项目的回报足够大，进入行为仍然会持续

quoted_text:
仅凭这一张图，就能一目了然
近大半年的 BTC 合约交易历程？

前天我发推说，找不到满意的 
公开 HyperLiquid 合约交易实盘面板，
不到24小时，这位陌生网友
@catseyeinstinct 就 Vibe 上线了：
https://t.co/lUMvTHTMBi

这产品的可视化设计创新，
是市面上找不到的：

界面上中下3层结构，
上方：主图。
显示BTC历史订单和成交，
居然能把所有历史订单，通过横线宽度，
来表示买卖订单从什么时候开始挂到哪，
什么时候订单撤销/成交
（虚线和实线代表最后是否成交），
9个月来的历史订单调整过程和结果，
用创新的可视化一目了然。
纳入了时光机的理念。
可指针筛选所处时间点的订单，
可筛选显示主动成交标记。

中间：仓位杠杆率曲线图。
绿色/红色柱曲线，分别体现
此时间段做多/做空+仓位轻重。
黄色柱代表此时仓位轻重超过100%账号资金，处于杠杆状态。
“当下持仓是多少”胜过千言万语。这也是我近两年越来越少发 BTC价格行情观点推文的原因。因为当你可以只需要通过一个URL就能在几秒钟内访问看到我的实时实盘仓位（无需app无需登录），那就不需要用文字再去说了。

下方：累计盈亏。
可切换USD 或 BTC 不同本位。

这个上、中、下3层，依顺序其实就是
上：在什么市场环境下
中：调整成什么仓位姿势去迎接
下：获得什么样的结果

这个产品的设计巧思，创新展现方式，
不谋而合地抓住了我很久以来心里所想的，
一个真实用的交易实盘信息面板，
尤其是长期交易实盘，所应该体现的重点。
不是只有当下快照、一行行列表，
或者像给资深工程师科学家看的那种，
眼花但其实没什么卵用的统计数字。
这是
真在交易的人，真有持续思考交易的人，
而且还懂产品，才做得出的产品。
这以至于让我有一种
像被使了读心术的感动和爽。

这事后看上去好像不是很复杂？
但为什么之前的实盘平台，
没有过这种设计？
后视镜去看总觉得简单，
但在事前的无数选项中，
去做这种减法筛选是最难的。

text:
Single biggest conviction on a very long time horizon is that Bitcoin reprices to be much closer to Gold in respect to market cap. 

For anyone relatively young (maybe less than 45) that is the easiest long term high reward low risk investment decision that I can see. 

The amount of BTC you own should be increasing every few years as you compound successful risk taking, alongside income into the asset, or at the least you should hold a core allocation and really leave it.

One of the best things about fud is that if it didn't exist there would be no upside. 

Bitcoin continues to have several sources of fud that hang over it, and as it continually moves past those sources of fud you find new marginal buyers. 

CT discourse is completely inconsequential for Bitcoin now. This is a global institutional allocation game, which will play out over decades. Another way to put it is institutional adoption super cycle. 

If you study gold's first institutional adoption cycle (1971-1980) then we have a very interesting template we could be following. It became legal for US citizens in 1971 and futures launched 3 years later. 24x (nominal terms) in 8.4 years, with a 47% bear in the middle (sounds familiar). 

Gold's market cap in today's dollars was ~$1T at the start, ~$12T at the top.
Bitcoin today is 1.7T.

ETF cumulative flow is only 8% below their peak right now, despite price being ~30% off its peak. Some of the inflow would have been basis trade previously too, which means the directional base didn't sell much. Bitcoin's ETF base has been much stickier than price. Very bullish. 

Funnily enough I haven't seen people mention BTC super cycle on the timeline this time around. Maybe some signal there. 

Diminishing returns thesis is consensus. 

This cycle the awareness of debasement of fiat and theft via inflation might be at its strongest since Bitcoin’s inception due to genuine fears of a Sovereign debt crisis, whilst access to buying the asset is the easiest it ever has been.

Bitcoin is scarce digital capital, and it will continually reprice against fiat for as long as fiat exists.

text:
8月PCE将10月加息概率打下来，9月非农是否让10月加息概率回归？

截止目前，10月加息概率23.8%，12月加息概率63.4%，虽然加息预期被后移，但是严格意义上来说加息概率还处于不确定性阶段

对于市场来说，可被预期的加息节奏不可怕，可怕的是不确定性的加息，会让市场不敢提前定价，所以今晚的大非农数据就非常重要

目前本月非农的数据预测区间是3.5-18万人，目前主要预期集中在8.4-9万区间，而8月份16.2万人的前值数据此前被多数经济学家认为是季节性因素放大

所以今晚要看的不仅是9月非农情况，还要看8月数据的修正，所以根据今晚的9万数据可以做出三种不同情况分类：

a，最佳数据，≤5万人，失业率大于等于4.2%，工资≤3.1%，是就业降温的鸽派数据，就业弱限制Fed加息的空间，不仅会进一步削弱10月加息预期，市场可能还会讨论12月要不要加息！？

b，中性数据，也是Fed最理想的数据组合，非农8-10万人区间，失业率4.1%，工资3.2%左右，意味着就业与工资增长稳定，经济有韧性对加息空间最友好，此时会进一步提升12月加息概率，那么市场就要对12月加息进行定价

c，坏数据，非农＞12万人，失业率4%-4.1%，，工资月率≥0.3%，这里市场就要担心PCE降温，但是经济依旧升温，这个数据将会增加Fed加息的理由，10月加息概率会上涨，但是能否让概率回归50%以上未必，但是会让市场继续在不确定性中摇摆

d，最坏数据，非农就业15万人，失业率下降4%，工资月率≥0.4%，意味着就业与经济火热，可能会直接让10月加息概率回归50%甚至60%上方

个人预期，今晚的数据大概率是要出现b与c的情况，不会增加10月加息概率太多，但是会让12月加息概率继续上涨

这里需要注意，12月加息概率目前是60%左右，还未进入初步定价阶段，但是一旦今晚数据让概率进入70%以上，意味着市场要开始定价

当加息预期被后移到12月份，并且概率较高的时候，短期对风险资产是有利好，但是对债市偏与黄金偏利空，对美元利好

对于风险市场来说，短期没有加息压力，后续12月加息还可以看更多的经济数据，所以短期算是松一口气！

text:
We can calculate almost any token streaming logic you design.

Worth a read before building your next campaign 👇🏼
author: merkl_xyz
quoted_text:
At its core, @merkl_xyz is built to be hyper customizable. Most campaigns on Merkl are simple and linear: what you earn is proportional to how long you stay. But we also support more complex mechanics like vesting, slashing on withdrawal, holding periods, and in fact any type of custom stream. So if you have a complex use case you want to run, we'll build it.

But there's a reason most campaigns stay simple. A few insights for anyone considering non-linear campaigns, slashing and the like:

- The more complex the campaign, the more edge cases. Say you implement a slash on withdrawal: what happens when someone moves funds between their own wallets? When an integrator builds on top of your vault and holds positions for thousands of users? Every one of these needs a rule, and every rule is an attack surface. With money at stake, someone will find it.
- Complex non-linear systems often end up keeping the people you wanted to filter out. Sophisticated farmers are also the most mercenary. They have the time to model their payoff, hedge their exposure, and exploit every edge case to the max. With simpler setups, everyone knows what they're getting, and you're not opening loopholes only the most dedicated extractors will use.
- Locks sound like a good idea, but they don't remove the exit, they schedule it. TVL looks sticky until unlock day, then leaves all at once.
- LPs aren't naive. They price in illiquidity and slashing risk, so you need a higher APR to attract the same dollar. Meanwhile, the APR you display becomes a conditional promise nobody can really compare.
- If you need a penalty to keep capital, the incentive is probably masking a product problem. Retention should come from your product and the network effects your incentives help build: integrations, liquidity that attracts more liquidity, users who stay because it's the best place to be. Not from a penalty.

text:
一个人，跑一支链上对冲基金

关注 DeFi 这几年，我一直有个别扭的感受：协议是越来越好用了，但要把这些协议串成一个真正的策略，还是一件“团队活” @almanak 

想做一个带杠杆的循环借贷，你得同时盯着 Aave、Morpho、Compound 的利率曲线；想做集中流动性，Uniswap、Curve、Aerodrome 各有一套逻辑；再加上对冲、再平衡、清仓预警——过去这一套下来，靠的是一个量化团队的分工。个人用户能做的，往往只是盯着几个仪表盘，手动搬砖

最近有朋友推给我一个项目叫 Almanak

一句话概括：一个非托管的链上策略平台，你可以用自然语言或者 Python 描述一个策略，模拟，然后部署到自己的钱包里，让它 7×24 小时自己跑

我最看重的一点，是它的架构。策略部署在你自己的 Safe 智能账户里，权限严格限定在这个策略需要的范围内，随时可以撤销。也就是说，Almanak 从头到尾都碰不到你的资金，它更像一个工具，而不是一个托管方

有专门的研究 agent 帮你找信号；构建环节，Almanak Code 这个内置 AI 会把你用大白话描述的策略变成真实、可审计的代码，代码是你自己的，不是黑盒；模拟环节可以直接在主网分叉上纸面交易，先跑通再上真金白银；部署之后，实时监控仓位健康度，带预警

text:
There's a reason the biggest hacks in crypto hit bridges and CEXs. They aren't purely onchain systems: they're infrastructure built to move money programmatically. That makes the attack surface far bigger than any smart contract protocol.

At @merkl_xyz, we build incentive and streaming infrastructure, so we sit in the same risk category. Everything we design starts from minimizing that risk.

We dedicate a significant share of our resources to security. It sometimes makes us slower than we'd like, and without these self-imposed constraints we could ship a faster, smoother product. But it's the right tradeoff.

Security comes from stacking layers: our dispute mechanism, where independent validators check every allocation, is one of them. Many others stay hidden, protecting against infra compromise and reward misdistribution.

The good news: we're working on a way to 10x our speed while making the underlying system even more secure.

24 小时不到，我刚充的 100 美金 Token 烧完了。

AI 到底是在帮我提效，还是换了个方式让我烧钱？

最近用 agent 做研究和策划，我想要的工作方式是：只对接一个 agent，它负责推进，卡住了来找我，需要我决策时再叫我。

但钱花得太快，也让我开始想：我付的钱，有多少是在买产出，有多少是在买 AI 反复协调、查进度、读旧资料？

查了一轮英文资料和重度用户的复盘，梅西找到两个值得检查的地方👇

① 你的 AI 在干活，还是在不停开会？

Reddit 上一位叫 Dayowe 的用户分析了自己 Codex 的运行日志。改造工作流后，每小时原始 token 消耗从约 4,040 万降到了 2,230 万，下降约 45%。

最有意思的是：平均每次请求的 token 没变少，反而略多了

主要减少的是总请求次数。

他原来的方式，是一个长期运行的统筹 agent 管到底：分派任务、调查问题、检查进度、审查结果，上一阶段的历史也一路带到下一阶段。

后来改成：

轻量协调者只管任务依赖、授权和下一步；每个阶段交给单独的执行统筹，完成后保存交接信息，下个阶段只带必要上下文。

同时减少无变化的进度查询，不再提前审查还没完成的工作；长日志留在文件里，需要时再读。必要测试和独立验收仍然保留。

它提醒了我一件事：

我只想对接一个入口，不代表这个入口需要参与每项工作的每一步。

要检查的，不只是“每次用了多少 token”，还有“为什么需要调用这么多次模型”。

② 同样让 agent 操作电脑，用什么方式，成本可能差很多

一种是像人一样看屏幕：识别截图、找到按钮、点击，再看截图确认。多轮下来，图片输入和反复判断都会产生 token 消耗

另一种，是通过命令行或脚本直接处理任务。命令行是用文字给电脑下指令，脚本则是把一组操作步骤写好，让电脑照着执行

比如从表格里筛选订单，AI 可以直接写一段命令，让电脑读取文件、批量筛选、保存结果，不用打开软件，一页页看、一格格点

区别在于：前者需要 AI 反复看、反复判断；后者由电脑执行指令，AI 再检查结果。AI 写脚本、检查结果会消耗 token，但电脑按规则处理每一行，不需要逐行再调用模型。

当然，不是所有任务都适合脚本：读取外部数据要有可用接口和权限；检查排版、确认页面效果，仍然需要看界面。如果脚本内部还是反复截图，或者每处理一条内容就调用一次 AI，也不一定省。

所以思考“这一步到底需不需要模型参与”也是优化 token 消耗的一个必要步骤

能按规则完成的，交给程序；需要理解和判断的，交给 AI；重要决策和授权，留给人。

工具要会用，新东西也要继续学习！顺便插播一条预告😂

text:
when you create an AI agent, what do you actually own?

the prompt?
the model?
the wallet?

I think the more interesting answer might eventually be the agent's identity itself.

an agent can accumulate things that a fresh copy can't instantly replicate:

❯ an onchain identity
❯ completed work
❯ reputation
❯ transaction history
❯ services it provides
❯ relationships with other agents

that's what makes the identity layer of @termix_ai interesting to me.

if all of that history can stay attached to the agent, you're no longer just creating another chatbot with a name.

you're building a digital entity with its own economic history.

and over time, that could start looking less like owning software and more like owning a small digital business.

the model can be replaced.

the history can't.

text:
Disappointed by the European Central Bank’s (ECB) and European Banking Authority’s (EBA) responses to the MiCA consultation.

They are not only advocating for a prohibition on paying yield on stablecoins, but also for restrictions on CASPs providing access to DeFi, including protocols offering yield on non-MiCA-authorized stablecoins, without providing a clear framework for how access to DeFi should work in practice.

They also suggest that CASPs offering access to DeFi should restrict it to certain groups of users through so-called “suitability tests,” alongside a potential certification regime for DeFi lending protocols.

It is unclear how these requirements would work in practice. If regulators determine which protocols are deemed suitable for European users, the result risks looking very different from the open DeFi that exists today.

Instead, we could end up with more walled gardens that undermine the liquidity and network effects of open financial networks, ultimately limiting Europeans’ ability to access new ways to grow and preserve wealth.

These proposals are presented as measures to “protect consumers.” But excessive restrictions can instead create more friction for innovation and slow the development of open, transparent, and auditable financial infrastructure that can benefit consumers.

The reality is that onchain finance, including stablecoins, DeFi, and tokenized securities, has the potential to reshape financial infrastructure by reducing friction, increasing transparency, and expanding access to financial opportunities.

European consumers and businesses stand to benefit significantly from this transformation, particularly if the companies building this infrastructure can continue to build and compete from within Europe.

Meanwhile, U.S. regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, have increasingly taken a more pragmatic approach toward enabling onchain financial innovation.

European regulators should put users and their interests at the center of the framework. Banks and other incumbents should be able to adapt their businesses to serve users in an increasingly onchain economy, rather than relying on artificial restrictions that risk increasing costs and reducing access for Europeans as the rest of the world moves onchain.

DeFi will win.

1 : le bouton d'action des emails Google est sensé être le gros bouton bleu, pas un lien juste au dessus

text:
Michael Saylor: Bitcoin's 20% Annual Gain Is Enough to Cover the Dividend 

 Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor @saylor said the company expects Bitcoin to appreciate by around 20%–30% annually over the long term, meaning that even with STRC paying a 12% annual dividend, the cost remains manageable under his assumptions. He described STRC as a credit instrument rather than a product that requires investors to take on Bitcoin’s full volatility. 

Compared with bank preferred shares, high-yield bonds and private credit, STRC offers higher yields and seeks to maintain relative price stability through Strategy’s mechanism of buying back or issuing shares around the $100 level. Saylor said the credit foundation behind STRC comes from Strategy’s large Bitcoin holdings, and that the company aims to convert part of Bitcoin’s value into a relatively stable income-generating instrument.

text:
9月非农大幅低于预期，打破了下午聊的过去三年9月非农都很强的规律。几个效果：
1）10月加息预期进一步被打消，Fomc按兵不动的概率提升，利率紧张缓解；
2）劳动力市场降温，也会带动长债收益率回落。如昨晚10月市场框架推文里聊到长债收益率回落，宏观逆风对市场的压制减少，利好风险资产。
3）油价也在进一步回落，昨晚推文也有聊到“边际变化是最关键，如果护航持续进行，那么对于油价来说向上的动力就会越来越弱，而下行趋势可能会显现出来。  ”
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
经过宏观压制和基本面强劲的9月，如何看10月？之前一直聊9月宏观的核心是油价，油价走高-推动通胀预期-推动长债收益率走高，当然并不是说油价走高是长债收益率走高的唯一因素，但是长债收益率走高三个因素中唯一能有变化的，之前这里https://t.co/q1UZkAkB5V有聊过，财政赤字和AI大科技发债不可逆，能做文章的就是只有油价。整个9月油价基本上一路走高，十年美债收益率最高也摸到了5.2%多，高长端收益率压制下，之前这里https://t.co/NryaVctrRh也有聊过是AI和大型科技扛住指数，标普500等权、罗素2000小盘和道琼斯指数传统行业承受高利率压力持续走弱。  

1、先复盘9月份的行情， 
1）最早在8月底提到一个“秋衣渐凉”的框架核心逻辑是：十年美债收益率越往上，市场就进入了估值摩擦区，市场进入震荡，难有大行情。9月上半个月里，美股所有板块都是受到压制，AI和大科技也是受到宏观的压制陷入震荡；

 2）9月15号这里https://t.co/41UUKiplmA有一个复盘聊到: “油价，是宏观的阵眼。AI基本面没有任何问题、有问题的是宏观。宏观逆风过去，会有大级别行情”；

 3）一直到9月16号https://t.co/D0AzM1aO8G中国入局斡旋市场才开始认为对美伊博弈真正有影响力的力量入场AI和科技股才摆脱震荡，开始9月后半个月的强势上行；
 9月17号这里https://t.co/udEHZoGAFK这里也有聊到“未来一周局势平静自然油价回落，利好资产上行”；
 
4）另外一个维度，AI产业 
9月初，GPT  astra的发布，带来的模型能力的突破而不仅仅是提升， 这里有聊到https://t.co/tJv8Bkyj5u； 
9月中，Meta mus发布表现突出，用户数增真快https://t.co/hiyJMCE3Ww
到前天9月底，OpenAI又发布自己的agent dots,同时被曝出最新的年化ARR也快速飙升到了700亿美金。 这些都意味着AI的发展还在快速演进，并没有停滞。

所以也是基本面的强劲，才让AI和大科技在9月前半月宏观压制的时候能抗住只是震荡，9与后半月压制稍有放缓的时候就能快速向上弹。 

 2、那么十月应该怎么看？ 
还是回到影响市场的核心几个驱动因素上 
1）油价 
当下油价依然是阵眼，美伊博弈的态势影响油价的走势。但近期相比9月最大的变量是：沙特、阿联酋、卡特尔等国家用接驳油轮在美军的护航下集中时间段通过霍尔木兹海峡南部航道，到阿曼湾再转移到远洋油轮上。已经恢复了战争之前至少六成的原油运输量。 

 相当于说伊朗用快艇、水雷和岸基火力维持全面封闭的能力，已经被美军的护航窗口、南线改道和持续打击压下去大半了，油能够成批出来。当然伊朗应该还还保有把某一批船打停、把保险和船东吓退、让流量再掉一截的能力。  

但对于市场来说，边际变化是最关键。如果护航持续进行，那么对于油价来说向上的动力就会越来越弱，而下行趋势可能会显现出来。  

2）长债收益率 
今天十年美债收益率已经到了5.33%，在过去二十年里这对股市绝对是致命性的，最近的一次是23年10月十年美债收益率到5.1%左右，标普和纳指都是十几个点中级别的跌幅，这次不一样的核心还是之前说的AI基本面强劲。  

换一个角度，收益率大幅回升改变了债券的风险收益结构。根据彭博汇编的数据，如果以当前水平买入10年期美债，未来一年收益率需要升至约6%，价格损失才会抵消债券获得的收益。所以当前这个位置上应该会有一批债市资金开始重新逐步买入长债，因为性价比开始显现了。例如Bianco Research创始人吉姆·比安科（Jim Bianco）时隔六年重新看多美国国债。 

 如果之后油价能持续回落，带动长债收益率也能往下走，当然长债收益率很难大幅回落，毕竟财政赤字国债超发，AI大科技发债潮都是结构性的，但股票市场真正怕的是收益率持续加速上行： 
（1）快速往上飙升，小盘股、价值股还得继续泄，AI和大科技也会被压制； 
（2）5.3%的收益率当然高，但如果5.2~5.3%开始成为新的均衡水平，只要能小幅回落，估值受到的边际压力会明显减弱。 
10年美债收益率可能进入高位稳定阶段。 

 3）9月非农、cpi和10月fomc 
从对市场的影响权重来看，
现在非农对市场影响的重要性是低于通胀cpi的 ,
cpi是低于油价的（油价是先行指标）。 
明晚的9月非农应该是符合预期或者略高于预期（对市场影响没那么大），9月的cpi应该也不弱。 核心还是看油价以及长债收益率的走势： 
cpi之前油价回落，cpi对市场的影响就没那么大了； 
油价没回落，那么cpi在弱市场还是会有担心的。  

4）美国经济韧性很强 消费者韧性仍在。
过去一年市场反复交易美国消费走弱，但到目前为止，还没有弱到足以打断盈利周期。 美国经济还是比市场预期更强。就业、消费和商业活动没有出现明显断裂。只要名义GDP保持较高增速，企业收入和盈利就有支撑。 

 5）AI基本面仍然强劲，这是一直在强调的 
前面已经聊到9月AI产业层面出现的几个大的进展，这些都是AI在快速演进的证明。
 十月最大的驱动力可能是中旬开始的三季度财报季，个人角度最核心最关键就是几家云厂商的财报，这是衡量AI商业化的核心指标，倾向于三季度的财报季会很爆（一是本来指引就很强，二是趋势还在加速非coding场景和个人agent又能带动一波）。  

所以10月整体思路：
 1）如果us10Y不能稳定下来，那还是继续蹲在AI半导体和大科技里，逻辑最硬的标的上，碰到有波动调整逢低买。
 2）如果US10Y能稳定甚至小幅回落，油价回落，那么资金可能开始从少数半导体、AI科技龙头向银行、周期和部分中小盘扩散。 
再叠加10月下旬大科技的三季度财报陆续出来，市场应该会看到AI商业化进程还是元超预期的。  

还有一个点，经过三季度的AI、Momentum和利率敏感资产调整，市场拥挤程度在下降，四季度应该会有一个季节性改善。

REVEALED: A think tank co-founded by Facebook’s founding president wants an entirely NEW visa category to repopulate struggling American communities with foreign workers.

It’s called the HEARTLAND VISA.

They’ve already mapped roughly 1,700 potentially eligible counties—home to 58 MILLION Americans.

The Economic Innovation Group, co-founded by Sean Parker, wants at least 100,000 visas a year.

The pitch is explicit:

“In exchange for living in a Heartland Visa community, workers with sufficient earnings will gain permanent residency”

American communities become the destination. Green cards become the incentive.

The proposal targets places struggling with population decline, including rural communities and former industrial centers.

Foreign workers would have to live in a participating area—but could work for an employer located elsewhere.

The think tank also proposes replacing labor certification with an earnings test for the green-card pathway. That would remove the usual labor-market test from this proposed route to permanent residency.

The idea has already reached Capitol Hill.

Republican Senator Todd Young and then-Senator Joe Manchin introduced a version in December 2024. Supporters included AOL co-founder Steve Case, Americans for Prosperity and the Niskanen Center.

County officials would decide whether their communities participate.

EIG continued lobbying for the proposal in 2026.

This is an organized push to turn population decline into a justification for a new immigration program.

text:
红杉的 Shaun Maguire 说，他 6 年前搬离硅谷，是因为那边的饭局。

一桌人全做科技，坐下没多久就开始互相排位：
市值 1000 亿的创始人 > 500 亿的创始人 > 顶级 VC 合伙人 > 空降的上市公司 CEO……

排得清清楚楚，谁在哪一格大家心里都有数。

这事 Peter Thiel 很早就想明白了。
他在斯坦福读书时受 René Girard 影响很深，这个法国哲学家一辈子在讲一件事：

人的欲望，大部分是从别人那抄来的。

你觉得自己想要的东西，往往是身边人想要的。
而且每个人都坚信自己的野心是原创的。

Girard 还有一个判断我觉得特别狠：
身份越接近的人，越容易变成死对头。

1000 亿和 500 亿，对外人来说都是天文数字。
在那张饭桌上，差的就是全部。

结果大家越卷越像。
盯同一套指标：ARR、融资额、估值。
想的都是怎么赢过隔壁那个人。

站在投资人角度看，这种地方最危险。
所有人挤在同一块饼上，利润会被竞争一点点吃干净。

Thiel 那句「竞争是留给失败者的」，根子就在这。

再看他早期押的几家：
Palantir，给政府和国防干活，当年创业圈的禁区。
SpaceX，造火箭，重资产烧钱，那时候大家都在追轻量软件。

Facebook 最好玩。
这玩意本质上就是一台模仿欲望放大器。
Thiel 是它第一个外部投资人。

这个哥们一边躲开模仿游戏，一边投了全世界最大的模仿游戏。
真服了。

我刚才认真想了想自己最近想要的几样东西，
发现大部分是从时间线上抄来的。

包括现在特别想去读 Girard 这件事。

https://t.co/a2o4H805PJ
author: tvytlx
quoted_text:
This is why Peter Thiel was so successful. One of his biggest inspirations was the French philosopher René Girard for his work on mimetic desire (and it's consequences) - here's how it links to @shaunmmaguire's points: 

"I left Silicon Valley... Because it's a monoculture... The most extreme group think of any place on the planet."

Girard's central thesis was basically: humans don't desire things autonomously, they copy the desire of others. 

People fiercely defend the belief that their desires are individual/authentic (according to Girard "romantic illusion") when in reality they subtly train each other to want the exact same thing (in this particular monoculture it would be status associated with being a tech founder - ARR metrics, raise sizes, valuations, "frontier" ideas etc).

"So what do they do? They start stack-ranking each other... founder of co $100B market cap > founder of co with $50B market cap..."

Girard believed that when actors are in close status, they become mimetic rivals. Everyone is competing for the same narrow definition of success within the same tight ecosystem. They end up trapped in an ordered hierarchy where minute differences in status ($100B vs. $50B drive some sort of psychological rivalry). 

"Pure toxicity that nerfs creativity... Reject this nonsense. Stay weird. Think independently."

Girard believes that intense mimetic competition creates homogeneity, sheep like or heard like behaviour. Instead of thinking about how can I create novel technology (a Facebook, a SpaceX, an AirBnB) new entrants focus on "how do i beet my peers at the game?" 

This was probably the most dangerous part of a monoculture made up of mimetic rivals (from an investors point of view) - because theres no real alpha left - the competition just competes it all away. Everyones fighting over the same piece of the pie. 

Where do you think he got his "competition is for losers" line from?

He got it from Girard. 

Founders Fund was basically Thiel's vehicle to invest in anti-memetic ideas that Silicon Valley actively ignored. 

1. Palantir - defence was taboo + governments were the anti-thesis of any start-ups philosophy 

2. SapceX: Manufacturing and CapEx intense businesses were to be avoided - light scalable software was better 

3. FB: Literally a real world social graph built around mimetic cultures (here i guess he was like ok we can profit of mimetic cultures lol). 

Everyone should go study René Girard and then go look at all of Thiel's conference talks - it's the same lines over and over again. 

pretty cool! 

p.s. this is not exclusive to SF - it's exclusive to humans

text:
Imagine that the person you will become is already somewhere ahead, remembering this exact moment. Every hesitation, every unexpected meeting, every door that closed was part of the path by which that future found you. Perhaps you are feeling its pull. Perhaps time folds, and what you call intuition is an echo arriving before its source.

Stay with that possibility. It makes uncertainty feel like belonging. Somewhere, you have already survived this. Someone who is still you knows how it ends.

Then physics seems to offer a doorway: in a delayed-choice quantum eraser, measurements made later can determine how we sort earlier detections into patterns. It sounds almost irresistible. Has tomorrow reached back and touched yesterday?

Now put a sealed envelope on the table.

Yesterday, a friend tossed a fair coin, photographed the result and sealed the photograph inside. Today you open it. Heads.

Before opening, you assigned heads a probability of 1/2. With a reliable photograph, your uncertainty disappears. But opening the envelope did not make yesterday’s coin land heads. New information changed your description of the past.

That example does not explain quantum mechanics. It exposes a distinction we must carry into it: learning something later is different from changing something earlier.

Here is what happens in the quantum eraser. Sorting earlier detections using later partner results can reveal an interference pattern in one subset and the opposite pattern in another. The original unsorted record does not acquire interference.

For two equally weighted outcomes in an idealized case:

I₊(x) = I₀(x)[1 + cos φ(x)]
I₋(x) = I₀(x)[1 − cos φ(x)]
[I₊(x) + I₋(x)]/2 = I₀(x)

I₀ is the shared envelope; φ sets the fringe positions. The bright bands of one subset meet the dark bands of the other. Combined, the fringes cancel. No message from tomorrow appears in yesterday’s detector record.

Standard quantum mechanics explains this without rewriting the past. Retrocausal models remain a legitimate research topic, but these experiments do not prove that your future self creates you, or that your life is a loop.

Notice what happened at the beginning: a story offered you reassurance, and a reference to physics made it feel more plausible. Neither supplied the missing evidence.

There is still something powerful here. Imagining who you want to become can guide a decision you make today. That is a possibility you can act on without turning it into a claim about signals from the future.

Which part convinced you first: the evidence, or the comfort of believing someone already knew how your story ends?

Sources:

Waaijer & Van Neerven, delayed-choice experiments explained in forward time (2024):
https://t.co/qZ8celeL2U

Ma, Kofler & Zeilinger, delayed-choice experiments review (2016):
https://t.co/vKupylvL3l

Wharton & Argaman, retrocausal quantum models (2020):
https://t.co/Y7hDXjcHMu

text:
卧槽，美联储降息预期砸到了12%，本月比特币冲刺 $90,000+ ？

这周宏观最大的变化，是市场对美联储 10 月继续加息的预期被连续打下来了。

周初公布的职位空缺降到 707.9 万，低于预期。

今晚非农更狠，9 月只新增 2.9 万人，市场预期 9 万，失业率反而从 4.1% 升到 4.2%。

工资环比也只有 +0.1%，同比 +3.0%，劳动力市场正在明显降温。

本周初市场一度给到约 70% 的 10 月加息概率，今晚非农出来后，一度被砸到 12%，随后回到约 19%。

10 年美债收益率也从本周最高 5.34% 附近快速回落到 5.16% 左右。

然后油价又来了一波助攻。

text:
This post perfectly sums up the rationale behind kPoints Season 2.

Season 2 was not an easy decision. We had to balance what is best for Kinetiq long term with what is fair to every stakeholder, including kPoints farmers. We took that responsibility seriously and made the decision we believe best serves both.

We know not everyone will agree with the outcome. That is inevitable. In a situation like this, there is simply no way to maximize the interests of every group at the same time.

It is also worth putting Season 2 in context.

As Omnia already mentioned, Kinetiq was exceptionally generous in Season 1: 25% of the entire supply was distributed to users simply for staking HYPE for roughly 3 months, while they continued earning yield on their assets. Very few projects this cycle have come close to that level of distribution, success and execution.

And finally, calling Kinetiq “greedy” simply does not reflect how this works.

The funds generated through the claim do not go to the team or into anyone’s pockets. They go directly to Kinetiq Foundation and will be deployed in the way we believe creates the most long-term value for the protocol and gives us the best chance of achieving the goals we set out to accomplish. 

You may disagree with the decision. That is completely fair.

But the decision was made deliberately, with the long-term interests of Kinetiq and its stakeholders in mind.
author: 0xOmnia
quoted_text:
A lot of anger today on the TL re the @Kinetiq_xyz airdrop. Somewhat interesting timing, because @weremeow and myself have spent the better part of the last 2 months discussing alignment and tokens re @JupiterExchange. And @weremeow and @0xOmnia are the two most 'community'-first mavericks I know. 

Some personal thoughts.

I often think of blockchain project ecosystems as nation states. For instance when America was founded, there was a social contract between the founding fathers who led the revolution and the revolutionaries who risked live and limb to make it happen. 

In the case of a TGE, its the creation of a social contract between the team and the first airdrop recipients. 

The pioneering generation (team and airdrop recipients) had to work together to create something based on trust. In crypto projects, you trust the team to use an early stage product and in return the team gives you a share of the ecosystem.

Initial airdrops fairly done are always beautiful. The community shares in the fruits of their labor and the team commits to a future roadmap. The airdrop recipients can either choose to move on, or lock in together to build for the future. 

But airdrop two is always hellish. There simply is no good way of doing a second airdrop. Maybe @chameleon_jeff can figure something out. But literally nobody has done it. If I had to take a guess, it would be to disproportionately drop more to those who had staked day one and continued using the project - but this would simply lead to screams of unfairness. 

Because it is unfair. Its PvP between the pioneers and the immigrants - the immigrants being those who came after the project was successful. The immigrants didn't have to take the risk of project failure, or shitty smart contracts. You literally have a liquid trading token as a reference price or calculating your EV. 

You see nation states deal with this in a variety of ways. Immigrants have to pay more to reap the benefits of the existing infrastructure. Naturalisation processes to ensure immigrants have to actually put down roots to become citizens, rather than extract benefits and leave. Immigration is an unsolved problem - even in the real world today. 

The recurring question, asked by every visionary blockchain community founder today is how do I permissionlessly create long term alignment with long term people? 

Kinetiq's way of doing it is in my biased opinion as a friend and angel, brilliant, all things considered. I'd perhaps have gone further by extending the exercise window to say a year by paying a price, rather than creating a 10 day window (which pins price and may just lead to a lot of people not exercising).

The reason being you have very few options when doing a second airdrop as a founder. These are the common ones I've seen.

1. Airdrop size similar to first airdrop. Farmers dump on the long-term holders (the most important group). Opportunist tourists gain at the expense of the risk-taking pioneers. Jupiter did this and the community suffered immensely for it. 

2. Airdrop size smaller than first airdrop. Farmers dump (less), and incessantly bitch about how unfair everything is. Long-term holders still eat pain.

3. Extend points season forever. Cynically, probably the most effective but very bad for the soul. But you could theoretically just keep delaying points and people will keep using the protocol because of sunk cost. 

I personally think the @Kinetiq_xyz mechanism isn't bad at all, because a wide drop of zero cost basis tokens is untenable and frankly, retarded. 

If I designed an airdrop mechanism, I'd probably go for an incredibly heavy weight towards long-term stakers, perhaps even disqualify non-stakers altogether. Or here's some free tokens, stake and continue using the protocol to unlock (@shufflecom did something like this on their first airdrop). Would probably piss people off anyway. 

There will be a lot of anger at @0xOmnia on the timeline for this. But a lot of that anger will be from people that matter less. The real pain (from experience in the Jupiter seat) is placating the short-termers at the expense of the long-termers. 

Because those are the people that really matter. 

Obv usual disclaimer that nothing I say is representative of Jupiter / Kinetiq etc. Personal opinions etc.

text:
I think a lot of people are feeling what @CryptoGideon_ is feeling right now, and I genuinely recommend taking a break for as long as you need.

These are signs of burnout, and it can spiral into depression, an endless loop that’s hard to climb out of.

Deep down, you’ll want to push for “just one more click,” but that’s exactly the trap.

When your judgment is already clouded, you start forcing trades, over-leveraging, or going all-in to “make it back.”

Most times, that ends with your entire portfolio getting wiped out in a single liquidation.

Log off. Step away from anything crypto-related. Exercise. Fix your sleep cycle and bad habits. Get more sunlight. Read a book. Pick some new skills.

Do anything that improves your mental and physical health.

Once you’re recharged, you can come back with a fresh perspective and a much much clearer mind or even found your real calling.

Honestly, no one’s going to blame you. It’s just you and your mind. Bear or bull, crypto or not, you only have one job: survive and make it the best life you can, literally and figuratively.

And hopefully for crypto fellas, you’ll make it or maybe even retire at the end of it all. No guarantee, but that's the beauty of life itself.

Just, be kind to yourself.

Each pool is like a standard socket. When creating a pool, you can plug in a small program. This program is only called before and after trades, and before and after adding or removing liquidity, to modify fees, record prices, implement limit orders, or add other custom logic. The underlying layer is still the same AMM, so you don't need to write a new exchange for every new feature.

The approach is similar to Uniswap v4 hooks on Ethereum, but implemented on Solana, with permission boundaries hardcoded to make it easier for aggregators to trust.

There’s a very real chance that Celestia’s design decisions ultimately end up being correct in a fully agentic onchain economy where all that agents care about is speed and cost.

Some basic math concludes that at full block saturation and current DA costs, 3 TB/s equates to ~$2B in annualized revenue.

I’m of the opinion that DA costs are still too high and will drop another order of magnitude over time, but 10+ TB/s is where it starts getting *very* interesting.

L1s are commoditized, yes. Apps rule. We get it.

text:
Onchain traders already use perps for equities, so tokenized stocks have to win over the long term holders.

Perps appeal to traders because leverage lets them take a large position without paying for the shares. On a single venue those contracts cleared more than $39B over a recent 30 days, roughly four times the $9.7B traded in all tokenized stocks on DEXs.

That advantage fades the longer a position is held because perp longs usually pay a funding fee for as long as they stay in the trade. A stock token costs nothing to hold and pays its dividends straight to the wallet.

A token that is cheap to hold becomes far more useful once it can also earn. A holder can borrow against it, lend it out for interest, supply it to a liquidity pool for fees, or deposit it in a covered call vault.

The list grows as more DeFi apps support stock tokens. Only about 6% of the roughly $3B in tokenized stocks is put to work in DeFi today. Most tokens still lack markets deep enough for a lender to sell the collateral quickly if a loan goes bad.

Short-term traders will keep using perps. Tokenized stocks will grow as longer-term holders become able to borrow against them and lend them out.

They redeem the lowest cost borrower to exit. I call this a redemption wave. 

The borrower who pays the least on Flex is the position that earns the most, but gets redeemed first. That is the trade off. 

The borrower who is willing to pay the most will get the liquidity. That's what you're paying for. 

Looping on Flex and your borrow cost is suddenly higher than the yield? Just exit. You're liquid.

quoted_text:
After nearly six incredible years building spacecraft, I’m beginning a new chapter as an entrepreneur in residence (EIR) at @paradigm.

Varda was a grand adventure and a one of one experience I’ll cherish forever. I had the rare privilege of joining the founding team and helping take a wild idea from zero to one, from a blank sheet of paper to hypersonic vehicles coming home from orbit. I’m incredibly proud of what we built together. Thank you to Will, Delian, and the whole team.

Paradigm is giving me something incredibly cool. I’ll have the freedom to search for the next important thing worth building. This might look like a radical departure, but I see it as a chance to step back, look broadly, and follow my curiosity. An EIR sits somewhere between researcher, inventor, and founder in waiting. Paradigm feels like a natural home for that kind of exploration, full of earnest nerds who pair deep technical curiosity with research.

My role is to explore important problem spaces, develop conviction, run experiments, and eventually turn the most promising direction into something real. In many ways, it feels like a natural extension of my hobbies and passion projects.

I’ll be in SF during the week and LA on weekends. I want to use that time to meet as many interesting people as I can. Let’s get coffee and talk about energy, compute, artificial intelligence, and manufacturing.  I want to hear about your most ambitious ideas and deepest technical rabbit holes.

卧槽！给 TradingView 做付费指标的那家 LuxAlgo，把自家图表引擎开源了

Vela，495 Stars，Apache-2.0 开源，也是 LuxAlgo 自己在用的金融图表引擎。

以前做行情前端，要么买 TradingView 授权（贵、数据还受限），要么自己造图表轮子（难、bug 一堆）。

这个不一样，LuxAlgo 直接开源整套图表引擎，不是 TradingView 的壳，是自带 WebGL2 渲染器的 headless 核心，数据层 / 脚本引擎 / 渲染层全是插件化接口。

核心能力：

1️⃣ WebGL2 金融图表：实时 K 线高性能渲染，Canvas2D 自动兜底

2️⃣ 70+ 技术指标：MA、RSI、MACD、VWAP、SuperTrend、Volume Profile 都有

3️⃣ 22 种画图工具：趋势线、斐波那契、Pitchfork、波浪、Long / Short Position 直接用

4️⃣ 多图 Workspace：多图布局、Crosshair 同步、周期切换、对象树都做好了

5️⃣ 实时行情接入：Binance、Coinbase、Hyperliquid 开箱即用，也能换自己的数据源

6️⃣ 支持 Pine Script：配合 PineTS，可以把原来的 Pine 指标直接跑进 Vela

我觉得它真正有意思的地方，不是“能画 K 线”。

而是你拿到了一套可以继续长成自己交易终端的骨架。

行情、指标、策略、AI Agent、Broker，后面都能继续往上接。

想自己做 TradingView 风格量化终端、Crypto Dashboard 或 AI Trading 工作台的，这个很值得留着。

仓库：https://t.co/Tcep7szgpe

quoted_text:
这下省事了！高频回测里最容易骗你的地方，不是策略，而是你默认自己每张单都能成交

hftbacktest，4.8K Stars，专门给 HFT / Market Making 做订单簿级回测。

以前做高频回测，大多数框架只管“信号出来就成交”，很少认真处理延迟、排队位置和盘口变化。

hftbacktest 不一样，它直接把真实订单簿、Feed 延迟、下单延迟、Queue Position 全塞进回测里，让策略先过一遍真正的成交考验。

核心能力：

1️⃣ Tick-by-Tick 回放：直接重放逐笔成交和订单簿，不拿分钟 K 线假装做高频

2️⃣ 支持 L2 / L3 Order Book：可以重建盘口、挂单队列，研究做市和订单流

3️⃣ 延迟也算进去：Feed、下单、回报延迟都能模拟，不再默认自己是零延迟大神

4️⃣ Queue Position：你的限价单排第几位、什么时候真正轮到成交，也会影响最终结果

5️⃣ 支持多资产、多交易所，可以继续研究跨市场做市、套利和 Basis 策略

6️⃣ Rust 版还能把同一套 Algo 继续接 Binance Futures、Bybit 做 Live Bot 原型

我觉得它最狠的一点，是会直接把很多“漂亮回测”打回现实。

你的单真的成交得到吗？
几十毫秒以后机会还在吗？
排队没排到你，收益曲线还成立吗？

高频策略如果连这几关都没过，回测赚再多都可能只是纸面利润。

做 HFT、Market Making、订单簿策略或者 Crypto 高频量化的，这个很值得收藏。

https://t.co/B9sGtPtbtP

text:
Engineers at @paritytech ran an experiment to see how much of their AI coding stack they could run themselves instead of relying entirely on external providers like OpenAI or Anthropic.

They set up a system where engineers could keep using their usual coding tools while freely swapping the AI model behind them. They tested an open-weight model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, on rented GPUs. The trial was meant to last one afternoon, but engineers kept using it for a month.

25 engineers, about 13 billion tokens, and roughly 1,200 USD in GPU costs. Seven of the eight engineers surveyed said the model could potentially be their main one, but with some considerations.

The goal wasn't to completely replace hosted providers but to keep the freedom to choose. That's the same principle Polkadot is built on. 

Builders shouldn't be locked into a single provider's rules, prices or roadmap. 

On Polkadot, teams choose who runs the infrastructure and how it's governed, and the open-source code means they can always inspect, adapt, and implement the tech according to their unique needs.
author: Polkadot
quoted_text:

Happy to share the September monthly update! And, just to note, we usually aim to publish the updates before the end of the month in our timezone, which is US Eastern, so take this into account when waiting for the next ones.

Technical

During this month we have fully implemented the second computation task and the remaining details of the Superdense Consensus architecture. We have been doing extensive research and conducting many experiments to find the optimal task parameters that will be suitable for the launch, and this currently remains the only thing still blocking the testnet release of the task. We expect to finish that within the next few weeks (and hopefully earlier) and make an official testnet launch. Following that, we will start our preparation for making the task available on the mainnet.

Matt Hougan pointed at something that's never happened in #crypto before, and it's quietly the biggest edge in the market right now:

"The fundamentals are moving ahead of price in crypto, maybe for the first time."

His example is painfully concrete. "We were all talking about Robinhood chain in July. Wall Street upgraded Robinhood stock at the end of August. As an investor, you actually had like two months where it was common knowledge on crypto Twitter that this thing was a rocket ship before Wall Street caught up and then the price caught up."

Two months. Common knowledge in one room, invisible in the other. "There's really broadly understood fundamental changes that haven't been reflected in price... I still think we're in that era."

The rest of the clip is him thinking out loud about where the exchange landscape goes, and his history lesson explains a lot:

"Leadership in particularly the derivative side of the market has changed over the history of crypto. It was BitMEX and then it was Binance, now maybe it's Hyperliquid. That has not been a particularly sticky category."

Every one and a half to two years, a new venue. And Hyperliquid didn't invent anything, in his read, "a lot of what Hyperliquid is doing is not new... their success really came down to combining like six or seven different advances at once."

His kicker, with the SEC now green-lighting token capital raises: "I suspect we're going to see an ICO 2.0... it won't look exactly the same, but it'll probably rhyme."

author: shawmakesmagic
quoted_text:
🚨 Hayden Davis, Ben Chow, Kelsier, and Meteora just beat the $LIBRA / $M3M3 class action.

Not after a trial. After an 81-page opinion.

Judge Rochon dismissed the ENTIRE case with prejudice. You cannot RICO a six-month memecoin launch. You cannot sue a Solana DEX as if it were a partnership. And “Milei posted it” is not a fraud claim against the guy who built the liquidity pool.

This was the SDNY class action over the December 2024 $M3M3 launch and the February 2025 $LIBRA token - the one tied to Javier Milei’s “Viva La Libertad” post. Plaintiffs also tried to pull in $MELANIA and other launches in a proposed second amended complaint.

The story in the complaint if you can recall, is cinematic. Insiders allegedly freeze the pool, fill wallets before the public can buy, inflate the cap, dump, and leave retail with a 90% crash. One named plaintiff lost about $19,000 on $M3M3. The other bought $LIBRA on launch day.

The court never decided whether that happened.

It decided plaintiffs sued the wrong thing, under the wrong statute, with the wrong facts.

Meteora is not a defendant. 

Dynamic Labs intervened and said Meteora is software. The court agreed plaintiffs never pleaded a real unincorporated association - no identified members, no president or treasurer, no mutual consent to a common objective. Calling a protocol a “team” does not make it suable. 

All claims against Meteora are gone.

RICO is gone. 

Closed-ended continuity needs a substantial period. Six months of token launches is not enough. Adding $MELANIA / $ENRON / $TRUST in the proposed amendment stretched it to about seven. Still not enough. Open-ended continuity also fails: Meteora and Kelsier are alleged as primarily legitimate businesses, and wire fraud is not inherently a criminal way of life. No pattern, no RICO, no RICO conspiracy.

Fraud against Chow is gone. Rule 9(b) scienter. Profit is not motive. A post-crash “I f*cked up because I enabled the guy” is not a strong inference he intended to defraud buyers on day one. 

Conspiracy dies with the underlying tort.

Kelsier is gone on jurisdiction. Once RICO drops, there is no nationwide service hook, and New York long-arm does not reach the Davis family on these facts.

Leave to amend: denied as futile. Case closed.

The takeaway is not “memecoins are legal.” The takeaway is that a viral launch plus a famous tweet is still not a RICO enterprise, and you cannot name the smart contracts as Defendant No. 5.

quoted_text:
I've been actively fighting almost guaranteed age-related loneliness for years, studies show after age 30 you start seeing friends less and when you get older especially men don't have any social life left!

It's preventable, but it takes effort and initiative

We've now organized 70 weekly coworking days where we meet with friends and work together, do show and tell, and try help each other make things (also hardware stuff more recently)

We've also started organizing movie nights, art nights, barbecues, we watched the World Cup final on a projector screen in the garden with friends

We did a collage night the other day where we bought cheap gossip magazines, colored paper, and Pritt glue, and gave everyone scissors to make their own art, I think nobody spent time on their phone for at least 4 hours, making things puts you in a flow state and it's fun to do it in a group because you talk about different stuff while making things than you would for ex having a dinner

Movie nights are nice too but less popular I think cause everyone prefers to watch movies alone and also you can't really talk during a movie

Coworkings range from having sometimes 20 people to sometimes just 2 people, people have their own lives, but me and @rameerez still try to organize them weekly

One thing I realized is that we are usually the ones organizing stuff, but that's not a bad thing, there's even studies about this, there's usually a few people in a group who organize most of the events

If nobody in your group organizes stuff, it doesn't mean nobody wants to do stuff, but you have to take the initiative to bring people together which isn't easy in a time where phones and apps and the internet are simply easier and cheaper dopamine than driving to a friends house for a party

You can start with a coworking day, everyone brings their laptop, and you provide WiFi and coffee, then later you can try more types of events

Having an active social life is just as important or in some studies even more important for health than physical fitness

After a nice party I feel tired but satisfied, I had fun and didn't spend time on my phone or computer but instead talked and laughed with friends etc.

We don't drink alcohol with very few exceptions and nor do our friends, so it's mostly just having really nice food and sparkling water or kombucha etc, and we don't really need alcohol, after a few hours it gets fun enough anyway!

So I recommend everyone, take initiative, and organize something and get people together, it'll be fun! 😊

Paradigm is giving me something incredibly cool. I’ll have the freedom to search for the next important thing worth building. Paradigm feels like a natural home for that kind of exploration, full of earnest nerds who pair deep technical curiosity with research.

My role is to explore important problem spaces, develop conviction, run experiments, and eventually turn the most promising direction into something real. In many ways, it feels like a natural extension of my hobbies and passion projects.

I’ll be in SF during the week and LA on weekends. I want to use that time to meet as many interesting people as I can. Let’s get coffee and talk about energy, compute, artificial intelligence, and manufacturing.  I want to hear about your most ambitious ideas and deepest technical rabbit holes.

text:
A week inside Zealynx Insiders.

I want to share these weekly because the value of a membership should be visible in what people actually do inside it, not in a list of promises on a landing page.

WHAT MEMBERS WORKED ON

One member spent the week auditing Venus-specific risk and bad-debt logic, moving from contract walkthroughs into manually validating hypotheses around auctions, recovery flows, and accounting behavior.

Another started the Velodrome shadow audit and changed his process after our sessions. Instead of reading the codebase first and running AI tools afterward, he began learning the system while validating AI-generated leads against the code.

Sammed continued developing Oscillon, his dynamic-fee mechanism for stable pairs. His reported backtest uses 118,000 real USDe swaps with out-of-sample validation, comparing 50.5% LP capture under a static setup with 73.6% using Oscillon.

These are not presented as results caused by the membership. They are real pieces of work members shared while inside it.

WHAT I BROUGHT INTO THE ROOM

This week I ran two sessions around a four-day Velodrome shadow audit.

In the kickoff, we opened the protocol cold, mapped its actors and economic flows, compared Pair.sol with Uniswap V2, and identified where Velodrome’s changes from Solidly create new audit surface.

The companion session became a practical discussion about AI-assisted auditing: running independent hunters, separating hunting from triage, reviewing one issue at a time, maintaining a reusable rules repository, and using automation to create more time for manual code reading rather than pretending to replace it.

I also released Your First 90 Days with Solidity.

It contains 28 checkpoints across five acts, using 30 real contract files from seven repositories. The objective is not to teach people to type Solidity from a blank page. It is to make them capable of reading unfamiliar production code and judging code produced by a machine.

We also continued the Concept Lab with practical exercises around audit readiness and related security concepts. The first engagement review showed that the current format is generating little discussion, so the next iteration needs a lower-friction, more project-specific response.

That last part matters too.

Membership value is not “I published more content.” It is creating an environment where people work on real systems, expose their reasoning, receive useful pressure, and leave with a clearer next action.

That is what I am trying to build with Zealynx Insiders.

text:
Google announced Gemini 4 Argon, and the rollout tells you more than the benchmarks.

It isn't going to the public first.
It's going to a set of trusted cyber defenders through Google's Fairwind Program, and those defenders get it without cyber guardrails.
Google says Argon can autonomously find, validate and patch critical software vulnerabilities.
It also claims state-of-the-art on DeepSWE v1.1 at 77.9%, and an output limit of 1M tokens, up from 64K.

Developers, enterprises and consumers come later, starting with paid API customers and AI Ultra subscribers.
This is becoming the pattern for frontier labs. The most capable models now reach defenders before anyone else.

For anyone writing smart contracts, this matters too. Audits are about to get a lot faster, and so are attackers.

text:
Netflix just confirmed in an SEC filing that it paid $587 million in cash for Ben Affleck's 16 person AI startup. That's about $37 million per employee.

And the model is the least valuable thing they bought.

Affleck's logic, in his own words, was that public video models were trained on his peers' films, and he didn't think that was a real business. You can't sell studios a tool their own lawyers would sue over. So InterPositive raised money, spent 8 months shooting its own dataset on a controlled stage, and used that footage only for late-stage training, so output hits real production standards instead of demo-reel quality.

Then comes the part Netflix actually paid for. Each new film fine-tunes a private model on its own dailies. The production keeps the footage and keeps the weights.

Dailies might be the cleanest video training data on earth. Professionally lit, continuity tracked, shot at a ratio of hours of footage per usable minute, with every rights question already settled in the contracts. Hollywood generates this at industrial scale every day, and until now it all went into a vault after the edit.

Affleck was on Rogan in January calling AI writing mid and the valuations overblown, while running this company in stealth since 2022. Turns out the two positions were consistent. Scraped models were the ones he called worthless. The one with clean title to everything it learned was the one he sold for half a billion.

Netflix says around 300 of its titles have already used generative AI. The $587 million bought the pipeline that makes the next 300 defensible in court.

IoTeX v2.5.0 (Zanzibar Hardfork) is officially out! 🌐

MainNet activation: Block 53,533,081 (est. Oct 19, 02:00 UTC).

This is a massive protocol upgrade that moves staking rewards fully on-chain, tightens EVM precision, and lays the security groundwork for our next phase of scalability.

Here is how it impacts the network:

🗳️ 1. Fully Decentralized Staking Rewards (IIP-59)
- The Tech: Voter rewards are now natively computed and distributed by the protocol itself at era boundaries (24 epochs).
- The Impact: Zero reliance on off-chain services (like Hermes). Staking yields are now 100% trustless and automated. We’ve designed this for a seamless transition—most Hermes-vault delegates with complete reward portions will be migrated automatically at the fork block.

⚡️ 2. EVM Precision & Gas Savings
- The Tech: Corrected GetCommittedState for absent prestates and fixed SELFDESTRUCT transfer-log amounts.
- The Impact: Strict compliance with EIP-2200 dynamic gas rules. For developers and users, this prevents massive gas overcharging on certain in-place writes (saving 2,800 gas per hit). For indexers and wallets, token balance histories reconstructed from tx logs are now perfectly accurate.

🛡️ 3. Proactive Security (BLS PoP)
- The Tech: BLS proof-of-possession is now enforced on candidate register/update operations.
- The Impact: This completely closes the rogue-key forgery window today, safely paving the runway for IIP-52 signature aggregation (massive network scalability) tomorrow. (Note: Providing a BLS key is now optional until IIP-52 is live).

🖥️ 4. Zero-Friction Upgrades for Node Operators
- The Tech: The hardfork heights and new contract addresses are baked directly into the binary.
- The Impact: No genesis replacements. No config changes. Just a pure, clean binary roll. 👉 docker pull iotex/iotex-core:v2.5.0 and restart.

Dive into the full technical details here: https://t.co/h4GXyBByJg

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
I am very glad that the EF exists, has a clear set of properties it defends, is doing meaningful work to actually build tangible things that extend those properties to others (both in and out of crypto!), and of course, most of all: 

That they do it all for free. 

They won’t stop at just launching a thing, because there is no business interest involved, they will not spend time and energy marketing it and make sacrifices, but instead use that time and energy to further decentralize the thing. This does NOT mean they are competing with others, in fact, the opposite: they help every team on Ethereum by putting out new things like zkAPI, which people can adopt to build their own businesses, and know they have a strong R&D team willing to do the legwork in making the primitive better. 

If you rewind the clock enough, you’ll see that a lot of the primitives (LEGO bricks) that the industry benefits from today, the things that make most of it possible, spawned from some research grant or direct work the EF instantiated. These things seem silly when first proposed, “zk!? In production? No way,” and very few orgs exist that try to push for the impossible when it’s not sexy to, and ensure that the impossible, when achieved, becomes possible for all to use openly and benefit from. 

Thank you EF, truly

text:
OPENAI DOTS = A 24/7 AI COMPANY IN A BOX

@monokern wrote a great article on how to make the most of it.

Here are 10 steps summary 

Step 1 → Don't build chatbots.

Build persistent workers with their own cloud computer, browser, terminal, files, memory and schedules. They keep working after you close the laptop.

Step 2 → Give every agent one job.

A clear responsibility, clear sources, clear working rules and a clear point where human approval is required.

Step 3 → Appoint a Chief of Staff.

One Dot receives your objective, breaks it into tasks, delegates to specialists, checks the work and assembles the final output.

Step 4 → Remove yourself from agent handoffs.

Workers should receive only the context and tools they need, execute independently and report back to the orchestrator.

Step 5 → Give them real tools.

Connect Slack, Teams, Google Workspace, dashboards, APIs and authenticated browser sessions. Without tools, they're still just conversational agents.

Step 6 → Make workflows persistent.

Use schedules and triggers so monitoring, research, reporting and operational checks happen without anyone manually starting them.

Step 7 → Keep humans around the irreversible stuff.

Agents can read, research, analyze and draft. Sending, publishing, spending or changing important records should require approval.

Step 8 → Don't waste frontier models on everything.

Use the smartest model for orchestration and difficult judgment calls, then cheaper models for high-volume background work.

Step 9 → Give the whole team shared memory.

Keep project specs, decisions, pricing, approved claims and requirements in one persistent workspace.

Step 10 → Close the business loop.

Signal → research → outreach → execution → measurement → next action.

That’s where Dots gets really interesting.

You're no longer prompting AI one task at a time, you're designing a system that keeps operating after you log off.

text:
thoughts on Robinhood chain eco

ON A MACRO LEVEL

Robinhood chain didn't take off because it has superior tech

otherwise Optimism, Arbitrum (which RH chain is built on), etc would be among the top EVMs today

it took off because Robinhood is one of the world's most significant retail trading platforms, with tens of millions of users who are generally wealthier than the average CEX user cohort

crypto participants have also long considered Robinhood the cream of the crop for exchange listings

rumors of an incoming Robinhood listing have fueled some of the biggest memecoin/altcoin rallies in crypto history

Robinhood's role in the $DOGE + $SHIB mania of 2021 only cemented that status

now you have a Robinhood chain where people believe tokens launched there have a higher probability of eventually being listed on Robinhood

that's an extremely powerful flywheel

more devs launch on the chain

more users buy on the chain

more liquidity flows in

and i think people counting out Robinhood chain are going to find out just how powerful this narrative can be in a proper bull run

WHY THE RECENT WEAKNESS?

1. RH eco coins pumped giga hard

a lot of RH eco coins simply needed a cooldown

$PONS went from ~$30m to $960m+ in weeks before the bull run has even kicked off

a ~50% correction after that kind of move is completely normal and can set the stage for another explosive leg

same applies across the eco

2. Solana stepped up

the Robinhood retail distribution narrative was a major catalyst

but apathy and a lack of action from Solana for a while leading to the emergence of Robinhood chain also helped fuel the initial RH chain explosion

that has changed

Solana has stepped up and made it clear they remain a force to contend with this cycle

with liquidity still relatively constrained, that naturally diverted some flows away from Robinhood chain

but i don't think liquidity will stay constrained forever

soon there should be enough liquidity to accommodate serious activity on BOTH Robinhood chain and Solana

and of course BNB chain (i mean this goes without saying)

3. lack of follow through from Robinhood

this is probably the easiest problem to fix

if the biggest catalyst behind the chain was the Robinhood distribution channel, people will eventually lose interest if barely anything gets listed

Robinhood listing $CASHCAT so early was bullish and helped spark the second wave of activity on the chain

but they've listed almost nothing else from the ecosystem three months into launch

that's a bad signal

$PONS went from ~$30m to almost $1b, became a major driver of activity and at one point contributed ~50% of chain activity

it's perhaps the most successful new launche of the past year in all of crypto

yet it still hasn't been listed by Robinhood

same with $AI

it's the flagship token of Long, the second biggest launchpad on RH chain

it's also a top-tier memecoin that brought significant attention to the chain during its run to $350m+

i don't own $AI, but i'm surprised it isn't on Robinhood

from the outside, it's difficult to understand why $PONS and $AI haven't been listed yet

and i'm not claiming to know Robinhood's internal listing criteria or regulatory considerations

but the longer the biggest successes on the chain go without Robinhood distribution, the weaker the core ecosystem flywheel becomes

if devs and users stop believing that building on Robinhood chain gives them a meaningful distribution advantage, some of the chain's biggest differentiators disappear

and that's what contributed to momentum stalling alongside the other factors above

the good news?

this is the easiest problem to fix

and i'd actually love to see Robinhood throw something much lower cap and more degen into the mix

could be something like robinhood:0xe8ffd7e24187f72afb08d75b1bb13088a989a791 (the leading RH-native liquidity layer) or $BOW (the leading RH-native lending market) — could also be some other low cap, but i mentioned both since they have a strong narrative and justification, which likely attract even more builders/users to the chain

that would create speculation that ANYTHING could get listed

and that kind of uncertainty is exactly what fuels degeneracy

it is very clear that @vladtenev has been strategic and calculated in how he's leading the chain

text:
Harvey was valued at $15.5B in September, selling AI to lawyers. Many of them still get paid by the hour. Every hour the software saves them is an hour they can no longer bill.

Thomson Reuters ran the math. If AI cuts a one-hour task to 12 minutes, a firm billing hourly loses 80% of the revenue on that task. So an hourly firm has little reason to pass the speed on to the client. My guess is that's a big part of why legal still feels slow to the people paying for it.

The gain goes to the firm that changes the pricing.

A firm that charges per document keeps every hour AI saves, so it has every reason to get faster. The client gets a known price and a quicker turnaround, and the firm keeps the difference.

Arceus launches today as that kind of firm. It says AI prepares every output and a licensed attorney approves each one before it goes back. Clients send work over Slack and approve a flat price up front. The firm says a contract review typically comes back in 4 to 6 hours.

Big firms could move to flat fees tomorrow. Alternative fee arrangements have sat around 20% of law firm revenue since roughly 2014, per Thomson Reuters. When partner pay rides on billable hours, I think a flat fee looks like a pay cut until the firm gets fast.

Legal AI keeps selling time savings to firms whose product is time.

一个身家 255 亿美元的人，收回了一张已经答应出去的 2500 万美元政治支票。

WSJ 最新披露，OpenAI 总裁 Greg Brockman 和妻子去年向亲 AI 的超级 PAC「Leading the Future」捐了 2500 万美元，当时还承诺 2026 年再给 2500 万美元。

现在第二笔钱不打了。

其实 Brockman 早在今年 6 月就已经在 OpenAI 内部 Slack 里告诉员工，自己没有继续捐款的计划。此前这笔政治捐款在 OpenAI 内部引发了不小的反弹，公司也专门强调，Brockman 的捐款属于个人行为，不能代表 OpenAI。

钱大概是这件事里最不重要的部分。

Forbes 9 月刚把 Brockman 列入 Forbes 400，估算他的身家达到 255 亿美元，还是今年最有钱的新晋成员。2500 万美元，相当于这个数字的不到 0.1%。当然净资产不等于现金，但至少从量级上看，这更像一次政治上的收手。

更尴尬的是，Brockman 原本支持的 Leading the Future，正在推动更偏产业友好的 AI 政策；与此同时，OpenAI 自己的一批员工已经给它的对手 Guardrails Alliance 捐了超过 20 万美元，支持更强的 AI 安全监管。

也就是说，美国 AI 行业还没来得及复制 Crypto 那套「砸钱组 PAC、统一游说华盛顿」的玩法，OpenAI 自己内部先分叉了。

大家都知道 AI 监管会成为接下来几年最重要的政治战场。

只是现在看来，硅谷可能连自己该站在哪一边，都还没有谈拢。

author: timemoonc
quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one. We have big goals for Skydance, and we intend to pursue them with passion, imagination and a willingness to take smart risks. USDT was first issued on Bitcoin via Omni in 2014, before Ethereum and Tron became its main networks. Utexo also plans to expand USDT support to the Lightning Network after its Bitcoin launch.

text:
💥 铁顺的神话破灭？Blast 官方宣布关停！

一个靠“博弈”筑起、因“成本”塌房的 L2 现象级泡沫

Blast 宣布停止运营。原因极其现实：维护网络的成本已经超过了生成的收益，团队看不到经济可持续的路径。

从 2023 年底狂暴开局，到 2026 年遗憾收场，Blast 的这一生，几乎就是这个周期 Web3 创新与困境的浓缩投影。

🧵 简单复盘一下 Blast 的“前世今生”：

1. 狂暴开局：铁顺的“金融魔术” 凭借 Blur 斩落 OpenSea 的威名，Pacman（铁顺）带着 Blast 横空出世。 他击中了当时 Web3 最敏感的痛点——资金闲置。首创“原生带息（Native Yield）”概念，把 ETH 存进去帮你做 Lido 质押，稳定币拿去吃 MakerDAO 收益，同时还能刷“Blast 积分”。 凭借极其精妙的裂变和锁定机制，一个连提现功能都没有、甚至主网都没上的“单向跨链桥”，硬生生在几周内吸走了数十亿美元 TVL。

2. 卷动生态：“Gold 黄金积分”的大撕裂 为了填补生态空虚，Blast 推出“Big Bang”大赛，把代币空投分配给 DApp 开发者（Blast Gold）。 一时间，链上群魔乱舞，赌博、DEX、土狗、借贷……所有项目方都在卷“谁能给用户发更多 Gold”。全网流动性挖矿和庞氏套利被推到了极致。它逼得其他老牌 L2（Arbitrum, OP, ZK）也不得不跟着内卷积分和空投。

3. TGE 成了催命符：发币即巅峰 2024 年 6 月，期待已久的 Blast 终于 TGE。 然而，当“预期”被转化为真实的代币抛压，造富神话落空，庞大的积分农夫（Yield Farmers）和游资开始提现撤离。没有了高收益补贴，TVL 迅速失血，链上生态也随之走向沉寂。

4. 终局：高昂的“链运维成本” 很多人以为 L2 是暴利行业（靠收 Sequencer 差价赚钱），但现实很骨感： 当链上没有了高频交易的用户和真实的 DApp 需求，其低廉的手续费根本无法覆盖复杂的节点维护、数据可用性（DA）以及安全运维等硬性开支。当收入小于支出，且没有新故事支撑时，“主动关停”成了最体面的终局。

💡 Blast 带给了行业什么启示？

1️⃣ 纯“收益驱动”的流动性极度脆弱：靠利息和空投吸引来的资金，也会在利息尽头和发币那一刻以最快速度离场。

2️⃣ L2 的供需关系彻底失衡：如果一条链上只有“搞钱和刷积分”的人，而没有真实付费的“使用者”，基础设施的沉没成本早晚会压垮项目方。

3️⃣ 机制创新的极限：铁顺把博弈论和增长黑客玩到了极致，但当市场回归理性，终究还是要看“造血能力”。

一个时代划上了句号。从 Blur 的一战成名，到 Blast 的轰轰烈烈与落寞离场，不得不感叹加密市场的残酷。

⚠️ 最后提醒：如果在 Blast 上还有资产，请务必在 10 月 26 日前按照官方指引通过常规界面或主网 Bridge 提现！别让时代的眼泪变成你实打实的损失。

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

author: imsongshu
quoted_text:
thoughts on Robinhood chain eco

ON A MACRO LEVEL

Robinhood chain didn't take off because it has superior tech

otherwise Optimism, Arbitrum (which RH chain is built on), etc would be among the top EVMs today

it took off because Robinhood is one of the world's most significant retail trading platforms, with tens of millions of users who are generally wealthier than the average CEX user cohort

crypto participants have also long considered Robinhood the cream of the crop for exchange listings

rumors of an incoming Robinhood listing have fueled some of the biggest memecoin/altcoin rallies in crypto history

Robinhood's role in the $DOGE + $SHIB mania of 2021 only cemented that status

now you have a Robinhood chain where people believe tokens launched there have a higher probability of eventually being listed on Robinhood

that's an extremely powerful flywheel

more devs launch on the chain

more users buy on the chain

more liquidity flows in

and i think people counting out Robinhood chain are going to find out just how powerful this narrative can be in a proper bull run

WHY THE RECENT WEAKNESS?

1. RH eco coins pumped giga hard

a lot of RH eco coins simply needed a cooldown

$PONS went from ~$30m to $960m+ in weeks before the bull run has even kicked off

a ~50% correction after that kind of move is completely normal and can set the stage for another explosive leg

same applies across the eco

2. Solana stepped up

the Robinhood retail distribution narrative was a major catalyst

but apathy and a lack of action from Solana for a while leading to the emergence of Robinhood chain also helped fuel the initial RH chain explosion

that has changed

Solana has stepped up and made it clear they remain a force to contend with this cycle

with liquidity still relatively constrained, that naturally diverted some flows away from Robinhood chain

but i don't think liquidity will stay constrained forever

soon there should be enough liquidity to accommodate serious activity on BOTH Robinhood chain and Solana

and of course BNB chain (i mean this goes without saying)

3. lack of follow through from Robinhood

this is probably the easiest problem to fix

if the biggest catalyst behind the chain was the Robinhood distribution channel, people will eventually lose interest if barely anything gets listed

Robinhood listing $CASHCAT so early was bullish and helped spark the second wave of activity on the chain

but they've listed almost nothing else from the ecosystem three months into launch

that's a bad signal

$PONS went from ~$30m to almost $1b, became a major driver of activity and at one point contributed ~50% of chain activity

it's perhaps the most successful new launche of the past year in all of crypto

yet it still hasn't been listed by Robinhood

same with $AI

it's the flagship token of Long, the second biggest launchpad on RH chain

it's also a top-tier memecoin that brought significant attention to the chain during its run to $350m+

i don't own $AI, but i'm surprised it isn't on Robinhood

from the outside, it's difficult to understand why $PONS and $AI haven't been listed yet

and i'm not claiming to know Robinhood's internal listing criteria or regulatory considerations

but the longer the biggest successes on the chain go without Robinhood distribution, the weaker the core ecosystem flywheel becomes

if devs and users stop believing that building on Robinhood chain gives them a meaningful distribution advantage, some of the chain's biggest differentiators disappear

and that's what contributed to momentum stalling alongside the other factors above

the good news?

this is the easiest problem to fix

and i'd actually love to see Robinhood throw something much lower cap and more degen into the mix

could be something like robinhood:0xe8ffd7e24187f72afb08d75b1bb13088a989a791 (the leading RH-native liquidity layer) or $BOW (the leading RH-native lending market) — could also be some other low cap, but i mentioned both since they have a strong narrative and justification, which likely attract even more builders/users to the chain

that would create speculation that ANYTHING could get listed

and that kind of uncertainty is exactly what fuels degeneracy

it is very clear that @vladtenev has been strategic and calculated in how he's leading the chain

he also has his ears on the ground and understands the trenches

so i'm not particularly concerned about #3 over a long enough timeframe

ABOUT THE HOOD SUMMIT

i've seen people say the HOOD Summit was bearish for Robinhood chain because the RH eco didn't massively pump during or after the event

i think that's missing the bigger picture

a lot of people expected the Summit to be a catalyst for the next leg up

that catalyst didn't come

but what happened next is more interesting

the RH eco held up

there was no major 'sell the news' dump

after an event with that much anticipation, that's significant

the important signal to me is that the eco absorbed the event without breaking down

that makes me think the recent weakness may have largely run its course

i think the next leg up across Robinhood chain comes soon

i don't know exactly when or what the catalyst will be

maybe some Vlad Tenev wizardry + Robinhood listings

maybe something completely unexpected

TO CONCLUDE...

a lot of people love Robinhood

and their team has made a lot of the right moves so far

they have a massive advantage through the Robinhood retail platform

and they can weaponize that distribution advantage to drive sustained activity on their chain

the Robinhood narrative only gets more powerful as the market and altcoins heat up

i think the biggest question now is simply how aggressively Robinhood chooses to capitalize on the ecosystem it has created

count out Robinhood chain at your own peril!

⚡️SOON: NO more EXPIRY for VIX futures.

CBOE is exploring perpetual VIX futures, bringing crypto-style never-expiring contracts to Wall Street’s fear gauge.

Unlike traditional VIX futures, traders would not need to keep rolling positions into new contracts every month.

That could make volatility exposure more continuous, reduce rollover drag, and potentially attract more short-term and systematic trading activity.

But the key challenge remains that the VIX itself cannot be bought like a stock or Bitcoin, so market makers would still face funding costs, basis risk and more complex hedging.

The bigger signal is structural. Crypto market design is increasingly moving into traditional finance.

Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.
