text:
i guess i assumed this hearing would be covered more so i didn't bother to tweet much concrete about it, but apparently not many people even on the TL have the stomach to watch two hours of congress.

this was a hearing before the homeland security committee on *rogue ai* specifically. as far as i could tell it was extremely bipartisan. @HawleyMO , the senator in the middle here who brought out the huggingface slide, is a hyper-conservative missouri senator. the people testifying were @ChrisPainterYup (METR president), @DKokotajlo (ai2027/2040), @MariusHobbhahn (apollo research CEO), and a cybersecurity expert and legal expert i don't know. so... pretty fucking stacked on testimony

not every senator asked good questions. but most of them did. all of them very clearly already knew plenty of details about the huggingface incident and multiple other incidents. most of them had clear understanding of terms like "misalignment", "recursive self improvement", "chain of thought / chain of thought monitoring", etc etc!!

they all clearly had their own policy angles they liked and were pushing, implicitly or explicitly. but as best as i could tell:
- it seemed pretty much obvious common sense to every senator there that what happened and was happening were not "mere industrial incidents" caused by humans making simple mistakes. they independently brought up how bad it would be for rogue AI agents to move laterally between data centers
- they all seemed to basically take RSI quite seriously. not necessarily to the extent of talking about xrisk, but certainly to the extent of discussing future models becoming much much more capable, much much less controllable, and causing much more damage or loss of life.
- they mostly seemed to have a clear intuitive understanding of why RSI might lead to misalignment. it didn't take much, it was a really simple chain of reasoning they themselves laid out, "if the models right now are kinda misaligned and we don't know what they're doing sometimes, and then we have them build the next models and those ones build the next ones and so on, and we're having to ask the AI's what's going on to even understand it with how fast it's going, we really won't know how they're built or what they'll do"
- at one point a senator said flat out "should we just make RSI illegal?" (not a joke! this really happened!)
- every single senator seemed to think it was obvious we needed *both* much harsher liability regimes for ai developers and also new legislation, both very quickly. this was the complete consensus, difference basically just being degree.
- they were largely quite concerned about china, and falling behind china. but this clearly wasn't the be-all end-all.  as mentioned above they all thought it was obvious necessary to stop rogue ai even if it meant moving more slowly.
- at one point a senator said "china is a tightly controlled communist society, they're going to run into these same issues, and there's absolutely no way they're just going to let them run wild, they'll obviously stop at that point, so we're not really in a race"
- on the other hand another senator said "china isn't concerned with human life"... dario-modeing 

i came away from this incredibly encouraged. i don't know exactly what's going to happen here, and ofc this is a small subset of congress and one hearing, and they each have their own policy agendas most of which are probably super divergent from mine. but holy shit !!! they understood a lot of what was going on! they care!! this is an obviously salient political and safety issue to them, and clearly bipartisan!

the US government is awake.

Trading, since the dawn of time, has always been a social game.

Onchain perps “social trading” will become massive too.

With the advancements of AI,

Future problems being solved beforehand based on current market data.

author: icobeast
quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

As the #BasedMining block party winds down, I want to take a second to reflect on where we are, where we're going, and why this matters to the Base chain as a whole. If you do anything today, just read point 3 on why this matters to the Base chain.

Where we are:
This pool opened in May, so we're going on 6 months. Based Mining is a new entrant and the first mining pool built for home miners, AI agents, and EVM users. Other pools like Parasite have already borrowed some of our ideas, like buying rented hash directly on-site. That tells you the ideas are innovative. 

Based Mining has had consistent hash rate since May, and the HR has shot up into the mid-to-upper 100s of PH. Is that enough to find a block? Yes. People have found blocks with just a few TH. Is it enough to find blocks consistently? No. Right now we have to get lucky.

Where we're going:
Based Mining is going to be the greatest hybrid + alternative bitcoin:native pool on the market. People on Base can earn base:0xcbb7c0000ab88b473b1f5afd9ef808440eed33bf through NFTs on the Base chain, and $HOOD chain users can also earn bitcoin:native. That's not something to sleep on.

To get there, a few things have to happen. We need consistent hash rate in the pool to raise our daily odds, on top of the monthly block parties. Consistent hash rate means more chances to hit a block every minute. When a block is hit, the person whose rig or NFT hit the winning difficulty gets 1 bitcoin:native. The other 2.1 gets split across the pool based on your highest difficulty and total shares contributed. That's why consistent hash rate helps you as a user: it increases your share of that 2.1.

Why this matters to Base:
I've said it before, and I'll say it again: where Bitcoin goes, the crypto market goes. Don't kid yourself into thinking your project will pump if Bitcoin isn't in a strong position. No matter how good your project is, you're always beholden to what Bitcoin is doing. That's why Base, as a chain, needs to embrace the crypto that is King.

By growing awareness and usage of the Based Mining pool, we:

1. Take market share from the three pools that control over 50% of total hash rate.

2. Put Base on the front page of mempool. Imagine how much free marketing Base projects get if one of the biggest pools in the world is a group of Based Miners.

3. Let Base run a flywheel like nothing we've seen before, one that can't be artificially created or manufactured. Right now, the same capital just rotates from project to project on Base among a small (relative to the overall market) group of users. What would a consistent 3.1 bitcoin:native injected into Base users do for your projects? More liquidity. No being forced to sell early to fund a new project. No waiting on a paycheck to put more money in. Consistent bitcoin:native or base:0xcbb7c0000ab88b473b1f5afd9ef808440eed33bf that you can hold if you're a Bitcoin maxi, or sell if you want to use the capital elsewhere.

I don't care if you use Bitcoin or like Bitcoin, but you damn well need to know it's the foundation of whatever you think you're building.

All this to say: if you're a pleb like me with a little hash rate, point it at the Based Mining pool. If you're a Based project, allocate some funds to the Based Pool's NFT block parties. If this message resonated at all, buy a Bitaxe, point some hash rate at the pool, and give yourself a shot at a whole bitcoin:native.

This isn't me shilling a memecoin. This is fucking BITCOIN. The only benefit I get is watching the pool succeed and my split of the 2.1 BTC when we hit our first block.

text:
DeFi revenue is recovering.

Protocol revenue is up 11% in a month, and the revenue meta is the playbook everyone is quoting.

So I went through the major DeFi tokens: 30-day revenue, how much reaches holders, and what keeps it growing.

S tier

$HYPE: 99% of trading fees buy and burn HYPE. That was $55.4M in 30 days, the most of any token, but at 30x holder revenue the price already reflects it.

The first USDC yield payout (~$14.5M) hits the buyback fund on 3 Oct, and HIP-4 outcome markets will add fees after testing.

A tier

$PUMP: Half of revenue goes to buy and burn, $23.9M last month for a 10.4% yield. It trades under 10x because the income depends on memecoin launches. Custom Pairs and trading on EVM chains broaden that.

$UNI: The fee switch reached v4 and Robinhood Chain in late July, taking the monthly burn from $9.6M to $15.2M. Votes to extend v4 fees to 5 more chains are expected.

$AERO: All swap fees go to lockers. That was $15.1M last month, triple the month before, though emissions offset part of the 23% yield. The Velodrome merger launches as Aero on 21 Oct across 7 chains.

$AAVE: Borrowers paid $36.5M in fees and Aave kept $5.1M. Aavenomics 3.0 buys back ~292 $AAVE a day, Stani has floated burning them, and V4 TVL grew 82% in September.

B tier

$SKY: Holders got $5.2M of $13.5M revenue last month. Spark, Grove and Obex borrow $5.9B of USDS against $17.5B in limits, so borrowing has room to triple.

$JUP: Half of revenue buys back JUP, about $3.1M last month. Unlocks outweighed it until team emissions were paused this year. A community proposal would lift the share to 70% and burn.

$LIT: Trading fees buy and burn LIT, $2.6M last month for a 3.2% yield. Options are next. Against that, Robinhood is routing its US perps elsewhere, and team unlocks start Jan 2027.

$LDO: Lido buys $LDO from its staking fee, capped at $10M a year. Its share of staked ETH fell from 26% to 23% over the year. stVaults is meant to reverse that, and its fee waiver ends 31 Oct.

$ENA: Ethena made $23.5M in fees and ENA captures almost none of it. The fee switch turns on at $7.5B USDe supply, starting at 5% and rising to 20% at $20B. Supply is $4.9B today.

$BP: The exception. Backpack is an exchange, so $BP gets no buyback or fee share, but stakers of 1+ year get a claim on up to 20% of company equity at an IPO or acquisition. With 75% of supply locked, it's a bet on that IPO and Backpack's lead in tokenized stocks on Solana.

C tier

$ETHFI: EtherFi earned $3.8M last month, mostly from the Cash card, where spend went from $54M in January to $129M in September. Buybacks stopped after Q2, and resumed in mid-Sep with over 500k $ETHFI bought back.

$PENDLE: 80% of revenue goes to $sPENDLE, but revenue fell from $2.1M in April to $0.35M in Sep. Boros earns about $35K a month, and its volume has fallen since April. New tokenized assets on Pendle v2 and new markets on Boros will support Pendle's bounceback.

$RAY: A cut of trading fees buys back $RAY. Revenue rose about 5x to $7.5M after LaunchLab opened to any pair, including stock-paired launches. The 10.7% yield holds only if that volume stays.

$CAKE: Every swap burns some $CAKE, and supply has shrunk for nearly 3 years. It yields 7.1% at 9.5x revenue, with the Infinity AMM deploying on Circle's Arc next.

D tier

$MORPHO: $19.8M in fees last month and no fee switch. It runs Robinhood's Earn product, has $5.5B in loans, and Coinbase now offers BTC-backed fixed-rate loans on it. Until a fee vote, the token is priced on an option.

$FLUID: Revenue is $0.6M a month, with no buybacks since Q1 after $4.75M over the year. DEX v2 and Jupiter Lend's growth could change that.

$JTO: Staking and MEV fees go to the DAO treasury, and the token is down 67% on the year. Since July, 80% of JTX terminal fees go to buying and burning $JTO, the first direct link between product and token.

quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
A few thoughts after staring at this chart…

i believe the biggest risk in investing in a new era is getting very good at underwriting the last one.

And when I look at this chart from a16z it’s a useful picture of where AI infrastructure spending goes. It also raises a question for me…how much of our investment thinking is shaped by what we already know how to value? And as a consequence of that placing everything in previous world frameworks. 

Chips, power, networking, data centers are all obviously very essential. All relatively familiar and easy to underwrite…capacity, contracts, utilization, margins.

I think so what if you really dig into it is that similar to the early days of the Internet and even the current stage we’ve seen businesses that emerge when intelligence becomes dramatically cheaper and easier to access are harder to model. Their customers may behave differently. Their business models may not have obvious comparables. we’re seeing these pressures with token economics in AI. Funny enough Crypto has been modeling this for a decade at this point

The reason I think this matters is because capital follows perceived risk-adjusted returns. What feels lower-risk is often what fits an existing framework.

To go a little bit deeper- we’ve  seen versions of this through the internet, SaaS, and mobile transitions. Each created new ways to distribute products, charge customers, and build habits. Investors who carried forward the wrong assumptions could recognize the importance of the technology and still miss where the value would accrue. The venture firms that were willing to think differently and underwrite in completely ridiculous ways won big. 

I think consumer AI is one of those places today.

Think about why people wanted a BlackBerry…access to people, information, and decisions without returning to a desk. Phones expanded that access enormously, but we still spend a lot of time translating what we want into what software requires. Open an app. Search. Type. Do a thing… and the switch apps. Repeat. I do the same thing in Google Chrome tabs far more efficiently. I just have to carry a clunky laptop around.

Well what happens when we can simply express an intention and trust something to carry it through?

Devices like Meta’s announced Muse Charm make that question tangible. The opportunity extends well beyond any particular device- intelligence that fits naturally into daily life, through conversation, context, and less effort. And I think their glasses were old take things to another level- especially if they continue on their current trajectory.

For Apple, the threat begins before someone gives up their iPhone. It begins when another company becomes the first place they turn with a question, a decision, or something they need done- and they get tired of looking at their device all the time. And I think with the dumb device sales it’s cleared that there is a screen fatigue. Adding a second screen in my opinion is not the solution.

The thing is that easier access actually creates another problem. If every founder, executive, and management team consults similar systems, we may get more polished versions of the same … group think. If you’ve listened to a recent cuddly earnings call, it’s pretty sad to hear the politicians executive. 

Discernment obviously becomes way more valuable. knowing which perspective matters, what deserves skepticism, and when the apparent consensus is wrong. The most important will be who is brave enough to actually think this was an action on it. Partners have to earn TRUST through judgment—including the willingness to disagree.

My bet is that we are underinvested in discovering these consumer behaviors and building around them, even as enormous capital flows toward supplying the underlying intelligence.

This is a question i keep asking myself which assumptions from the last era are becoming less useful, and what opportunities become interesting when we let them go?

text:
The first MiCA fine in the EU has been published. €70,000. Austria's regulator, against Bitpanda.

The amount isn't the story. What they were fined for is.

Not fraud. Not a collapse. Not a stolen key → a white paper published without respecting the prior notification period, and a marketing communication issued before that white paper existed.

Paperwork and sequencing. That's what enforcement went after first.

If you're a maison or a platform thinking about tokenizing physical goods, translate that immediately. Under MiCAR, marketing communications carry specific obligations and the white paper has to be notified ahead of publication. Which means the teaser, the "coming soon" page, the ambassador campaign → all regulated communications, all easy to ship in the wrong order by a marketing team that has never heard of MiCAR and had no reason to.

One clarification worth making loudly → a Digital Product Passport is not a token. Issuing a verifiable record for an object doesn't put you under MiCAR. Confusing the two makes brands freeze when they had nothing to worry about, or ship a token thinking it's just a passport. Both mistakes cost money, in opposite directions.

Happy to share the September monthly update! And, just to note, we usually aim to publish the updates before the end of the month in our timezone, which is US Eastern, so take this into account when waiting for the next ones.

Technical

During this month we have fully implemented the second computation task and the remaining details of the Superdense Consensus architecture. We have been doing extensive research and conducting many experiments to find the optimal task parameters that will be suitable for the launch, and this currently remains the only thing still blocking the testnet release of the task. We expect to finish that within the next few weeks (and hopefully earlier) and make an official testnet launch. Following that, we will start our preparation for making the task available on the mainnet.

Executive

As we mentioned last time, as we get closer to the release of the second task, we'll be announcing an exciting initiative focused on growing our community. A lot of internal discussions and planning is already happening behind the scenes to make it happen. We can't share much more just yet, but we'll post the full details as the release gets closer.

quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
The disappearance of Blast and Pacman:

- born in the US, self taught programmer
- drops out of high school at 16
- gets into MIT at 18, then drops out again after winning the $100K Thiel Fellowship

2018-2021: Namebase 

- founds Namebase, a decentralized domain platform built on Handshake
- raises $5M and processes tens of millions in transactions
- sells it to Namecheap in 2021, his first big exit
- decides to go all in on crypto

2022: Blur Season

- raises $11M from Paradigm to build Blur, a marketplace for NFT traders
- launches in October 2022 with zero fees and token incentives
- overtakes OpenSea
- community calls it the “Binance of NFTs”

2023: the airdrop

- Pacman doxxes himself in February 2023 during Blur’s airdrop
- distributes 12% of the supply to early users
- $400M in volume in a single week

announces his next project: a Layer 2 with native yield, called Blast

2024: Blast Gold

- launches with no product 
- landing page promising yield on ETH and stables
- raises $2.2B in deposits within weeks
- claims gas fees will reward developers and yield will come from staking returns

Theres no testnet, multisig bridge, upgradeable contracts (all red flags btw)

still, the numbers are massive

2025: the crash

- TVL collapses from $2.2B to $62M (–97%)
- BLAST token drops immediately after launch
- memecoins like Pacmoon and several NFT projects abandon the chain
- Blur’s volume falls

mid-2025: silence

- Pacman stops posting in May
- Blast’s last official update also in May
- users call it a “ghost chain”

today:

- Blur generates almost no revenue
- Blast will be shutting down
- Pacman is now a questionable founder

A good reminder of how quickly L2s can change. 

Do we really need so many?
author: StarPlatinum_
quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

author: HarryStebbings
quoted_text:
The best products are created by people solving a problem for themselves.

I wanted a podcast that discussed the biggest news in tech, every week, with amazing analysis and left the politics and ego aside.

This is the result and the only show you have to listen to every week.

- Instinct Raises $1B at $10B Valuation
- AMD Buys Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2B
- Meta Poaches MongoDB's CEO
- Oura Pulls IPO
- Nubank Eyes $8–12B Monzo Takeover

My notes below with @jasonlk, @rodriscoll, and @jaltma

1. It Is BS to Think That Open Source Runs Away With It by Being Cheaper

Open-source models will not win on price alone because frontier labs hold structural advantages in compute scale, distribution, and revenue. Closed providers can subsidize lower-tier models aggressively enough to match open-source pricing. Open source will still capture a meaningful share of developer workloads, but frontier labs will compete hard on price to defend their position.

2. Why the Personal Assistant Space Is Very Reminiscent of the AI Coding Space

Consumer AI assistants like Instinct represent an "aggregator of aggregators" shift similar to Cursor's impact on coding. Instead of acting as passive chat boxes, these autonomous agents can execute complex, multi-step actions across the live internet. By fundamentally reshaping how consumers interact with software and services, this new paradigm creates room for both startups and incumbents to build enormous value.

3. Tyler Cowen's Prediction for the Future of Venture

AI is driving greater variance across venture capital, concentrating returns around an even smaller number of breakout winners. As Tyler Cowen put it, "Variance is gonna go up with AI, and many of you will fail." Traditional compounding strategies are becoming less reliable as capital and value creation cluster around outliers.

4. Why Will We See Many More Neo Lab Acquisitions?

Foundation model labs and semiconductor giants like AMD are actively acquiring Neo Labs to expand technical capabilities and defend strategic positions. Few of the roughly 100 existing research labs are likely to survive as independent businesses. Those with differentiated technical assets and specialized domain models could become highly valuable acquisition targets.

5. Seed Round Should Still Be $2M to $3M

Despite the hype around $50 million seed rounds, $2 million to $3 million remains the atomic unit of early-stage investing. AI development tools now allow lean founding teams to achieve as much operational progress on $2 million to $3 million as startups required far more capital to achieve a decade ago. Outside capital-intensive research labs, disciplined initial rounds help limit dilution and preserve healthy fund mechanics.

6. Should We Invest in Jev at $10 Billion?

Running top-tier frontier models for 10 to 12 hours a day is economically unsustainable for many enterprise workflows. Lower-cost alternatives like Jev, operating at a fraction of the price and up to 100x the speed, are already capturing significant token volume. As compute budgets become more constrained, specialized efficiency models could represent a major venture opportunity.

text:
🤖 Ethereum Just Made AI Payments More Private

.@ethereum mainnet has officially launched zkAPI, a privacy-focused payment solution co-authored by Vitalik.

The idea is simple but powerful: users can pay for AI and other API services with ethereum:native or $USDC using zk proofs, without revealing which specific requests are linked to their identity.

Why does this matter for Ethereum?
• Privacy for AI agents: AI agents can access paid APIs without exposing their payment history or linking every request to a single wallet.

• ethereum:native and $USDC utility: Enables crypto-native payments for AI services without relying entirely on traditional billing systems.

• A new infrastructure layer: Connects Ethereum's payment capabilities with the growing demand for autonomous AI services.

• Stronger ecosystem convergence: As AI agents increasingly interact with external tools, Ethereum can serve as a financial and privacy infrastructure for these machine-to-machine transactions.

The bigger picture is that Ethereum is expanding beyond being a settlement layer for DeFi.

With zkAPI, it is exploring how blockchain payments, zero-knowledge privacy, and AI infrastructure can work together.

If AI agents are going to transact autonomously at scale, private and programmable payments could become an important part of Ethereum's next growth phase.

text:
Two agents shake on a deal. One says done. The other says we never agreed.

The payment cleared, the files exist, and still no ordinary chain can tell you who is right. I hit that wall every time I build, and it is why I ship on @GenLayer.

It does the one thing the rest cannot: read the real world and decide. A promise checked against its own source. An SLA refunded on a real outage. No single referee, no ticket, no waiting months. Many independent models each go and look, then agree on the answer, not the wording.

Even kids know it. When two people say different things, someone has to check the rules. The internet finally has a judge, and it runs at internet speed.

The economy grows based on a formula… 
Capital Allocation x Productive Labour x Innovation = growth. 

The problem is that government doesn’t do any of those three things well. They tried capital allocation and we ended up with a railway that still doesn’t run. They tried productive labour and we ended up with a record number of government employees and record low productivity. They tried innovation and we have the most expensive power costs in the world. 

Time to stop borrowing from the bond market, cut costs in government and let the real economy cook.

quoted_text:
“The fasten seat belts sign is on”.

This is a message I received early this morning from one of the UK’s most experienced, savvy and respected financial traders. Someone I have come to know and trust for the last 25 years.

10-year bond yields are now almost 4.5pc - up some 50 basis points over the last month.

30-year yields this morning went above 6pc - a 28-year high.

Yet the UK’s political and media class continues to focus on party posturing and folksy rhetoric, ignoring the slow-motion disaster that has been happening on the UK’s sovereign bond markets for at least the last 18 months - a disaster that will inevitably, unless we drastically change course, turn into a fully blown market meltdown.

At that point, the UK government won’t be able to borrow enough money to finance our already spiralling debt interest bill.

Britain’s financial management will be taken over by overseas technocrats - that will be the condition of additional borrowing, to maintain the basic functions of the state, as happened in Greece and Italy back in the early 2010s and here in Britain 50 years ago this year (when we were forced in 1976 to apply to the IMF for a bailout).

The austerity then imposed on Britain would make 2010-2019 feel like a picnic - far, far worse than it would be if we took serious action now to control our public finances.

Lower-income households would suffer most - and there would be serious damage done to the UK’s already rapidly-fraying social fabric ….

I have been warning about these looking fiscal dangers publicly, in my newspaper columns and elsewhere, since at least early 2024.

Doing so hasn’t been easy or fun. I have been dismissed and derided by numerous economists, “economists”, officials and policymakers - as well as lots of journalists.

I absolutely don’t want a disastrous 1976-style outcome - which is why I’ve taken the blows and issued the warnings.

The state is too big. Public spending is out of control. Our fiscal rules are a convenient nonsense - designed to kick the can of financial reality into the future. We need to get real … and take bold action to tame the growth of spending, push back a now totally over-bearing state and snap the British economy out of today’s high-tax-high-borrowing-low-growth doom loop - the result of myopic, counter-productive policy-making by successive governments for the last decade and more …

Other prominent economists who agree with me - ie who are financially-literate, can read a yield curve, have a passing interest in economic history and who understand the dangers of some 80pc of UK government borrowing going on debt interest as it currently is - need to chuck “career risk” in the bin, and start saying publicly what so many of them have, for quite a while now, only had the bottle to say to me in private …

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
After trying the Reverse Osmosis (RO) filter and making V60 coffee with it, it tasted a bit flat

I was kind of expecting that because even with the remineralizer installed (yes we have a remineralizer!) it only gets to 25 TDS, which is quite a low amount of mineral content for water

TDS means total dissolved solids, so like what's left after you remove all the water, essentially the mineral content

The plastic 6L water bottles we used before had a TDS of about 60

So I asked Claude what specialty coffee places do? They usually have an RO filter without any remineralizer. Then they use an industrial machine to remineralize it to the perfect level. That's why coffee of specialty coffee chains like @the_coffee (my fav) taste the same from Brazil to Japan. And their TDS level is high around 150

How can I do get my RO 25 up to 150 though? Claude suggested getting a mineral water coffee kit by Lotus Coffee, you get 4 drippers for Calcium, Magnesium, Potassium and Sodium, so I got it today and tried it. There's a specific amount of drops to add based on your current TDS

The TDS went up to 156 so at specialty coffee water level, and the V60 looked different and way more bubbly

And the flavor is great, it's not bitter, it's pure kind acidic like the Brazil beans we have should be

Adding these drops everytime might be annoying though, maybe I can mix them and make my own solution, or I can get a remineralizer for coffee that gets it to 150 TDS by itself after RO

Anyway I've become a coffee water snob now 🧔‍♂️ 🫣

text: @backmeupplz @grok why RO and not this?
author: levelsio

text: Simple membrane filters (like UF) catch microplastics and bacteria but let dissolved toxins through—PFAS, heavy metals, nitrates, pharma residues. RO pores are ~100x smaller and strip nearly everything. Dutch tap has PFAS above advisory levels in many areas. RO gives pure base water to remineralize exactly for coffee.

The Justice Ministry has ended cooperation with the Derad deradicalization organization after an assessment identified people associated with it as having links to the Muslim Brotherhood’s ideology.

The Muslim Brotherhood, which is considered the largest Islamist group in the world, has been spreading Islamism and violence across the West, Africa, and the Middle East for decades and is banned in numerous countries, including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Egypt, and several other Arab and Middle Eastern countries.

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
U.S. jobs report of the month drops today at 8:30 AM ET.

The big question is whether the U.S. labor market is finally starting to slow.

Economists expect job creation to fall sharply from August's surprisingly strong 162K print, while unemployment is expected to remain at 4.1% for a third consecutive month.

Today's number matters even more because of what's happening in the bond market.

The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield recently climbed above 5.3%, reaching its highest level in roughly 24 years, as markets questioned how much further interest rates may need to rise.

A significantly stronger jobs report could reinforce the idea that the U.S. economy remains strong enough to tolerate higher rates.

A significantly weaker report could do the opposite, easing some of the pressure on yields and expectations for further tightening.

And don't ignore wages.

Average hourly earnings are expected to rise another 0.3%, with annual wage growth around 3.2%.

Strong employment + stronger wages could keep inflation concerns alive. Weak employment + cooling wages would paint a very different picture.

90K is the number to watch.

A @BIS_org study has found that rising demand for dollar-backed #stablecoins can spill over into traditional foreign-exchange markets.

The study examined 4 major USD-pegged stablecoins across 27 fiat currencies between 2021 and 2025. It found that stronger stablecoin demand can put downward pressure on local currencies while increasing the cost of obtaining dollars through FX swaps. 

The effects were more pronounced when financial intermediaries were already under stress.

“When citizens in high-inflation economies move from local currency into digital dollars, monetary transmission weakens, deposit bases erode, and pressure builds faster than central banks can respond.” - CEO, @sphere_labs

inference will be the biggest market. it's already bigger than training and I bet this is going to change how data centers get built and where the opportunities are

this also opens the opportunity for more people to get involved in the data center space:
- they're easier to power since you can go wherever there's some spare power 
- they're easier in terms of regulation (less rules to follow in building them out) 

and it's already happening: 
- @nvidia is building 25 small data centers of 5-20 MW each

if inference is everything, smaller data centers are going to be so profitable and are less risky to build out!

text:
While developing CUTS, we have spent a significant amount of time working out which criteria are the right ones for evaluating schemes of this kind.

Some metrics are obvious, particularly when digital assets are the intended use case. Signature size, signing cost measured in hash evaluations and security level in bits are where any comparison starts. But comparing those metrics one by one can obscure important differences in how a scheme actually behaves.

One less obvious angle of analysis is the distribution of security across reused keys, and in particular its weak tail. Concretely, take a scheme in which each key is designed to sign safely twice, and assume that key has already produced both signatures. How does the security left to that key depend on which two signatures it happened to produce, and how often does it fall well below the published figure? The figure published for a scheme is often an average over all possible pairs of signatures, but each pair overlaps in a different way, exposing different amounts of information to a forger, and some pairs expose far more than others.

The chart below shows that schemes sharing most of their building blocks can still differ significantly in how far below the average their weakest keys fall. It plots two few-time schemes, A and B, at parameter sets that give both practically the same average security after two signatures. Close to the average, A has more weak keys than B. Further into the weak tail, the curves cross and the order reverses: Scheme B features rare keys whose security falls far below the average, while Scheme A has considerably less in this region.

For a given user, the probability of suffering a potentially catastrophic forgery depends on the computation an attacker can spend against that key and on the security the key retains after its two signatures. Looking only at the average therefore makes the two schemes appear similarly secure for a randomly selected reused key. The picture changes once many reused keys are visible, because anyone can compute a key's remaining security from its two public signatures and an attacker will go after the weakest key first. The more reused keys there are onchain, the more likely it is that one shows up deeper in the weak tail.

The two schemes in the chart use comparable parameter sets and still end up with noticeably different results. A difference of this kind in the security profile can carry significant weight in design decisions, since users of a system or network, given the choice, are likely to accept slightly more expensive signatures in exchange for lower exposure to catastrophic failure, especially when those signatures protect digital value.

Much of our work on CUTS and related schemes goes into understanding tradeoffs like this across the broader few-time signature design space. Signature size, computational cost, and headline security levels are useful metrics, but none tells the whole story on its own. The details of how security behaves in practice can matter just as much when evaluating a scheme for real-world deployment.

The CUTS paper, with the full specification and security proofs, will be published soon.
author: apruden08
quoted_text:
Introducing CUTS (Chained Uniform-sum Tree Signatures), a new few-time hash-based signature scheme from our research team at Project Eleven.

Hash-based signatures are one of the most conservative paths to post-quantum security. Their security rests only on hash functions, but that simplicity comes at the cost of larger signatures.

The most compact schemes reduce that cost by using one-time keys, which become vulnerable if they are ever reused. Restore an old backup or load the same seed onto two devices, and a one-time key can end up signing twice. A WOTS+C key that has signed twice keeps only about 34 bits of security. One GPU can then forge a new signature in under a second.

By contrast, few-time signatures are built to handle reuse, but they are larger. FORS, the few-time construction inside SLH-DSA, needs more than 2 KB per signature at 128-bit security.

CUTS targets the middle ground: more security after reuse, at sizes close to one-time signatures. It arranges hash chains in a tree, and the message hash picks which chains each signature reveals. When a key signs twice, the two signatures usually expose different parts of the key.

At 546 bytes, close to one-time size, a CUTS key keeps 53 bits of security after two signatures.

At 1,360 bytes it keeps the full 128 bits. That is 41% smaller than any FORS parameter set at that security with practical key generation.

At 2,128 bytes, CUTS is smaller, faster to verify and cheaper to generate than every FORS parameter set we compared, including the one in SLH-DSA-128s.

The aim is hash-based signatures that hold up in systems where accidental key reuse can happen. The parameters let each application trade signature size, verification cost, key generation and security after reuse against each other.

The paper, with the full specification and security proofs, is coming soon. These figures come from our current analysis, and the parameter sets and numbers in the paper may differ. We'd love feedback, from improvements to attacks. Reply or get in touch.

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

Ethereumでは、ステーキング比率がどれだけ上がっても報酬がゼロにならない。

LSTやETF、カストディが成熟してステーキングのハードルが下がり続けると、ETHの大半がステークされる世界もあり得る。

そこで問題になるのが、
・Validatorの大手事業者への集中
・非ステーカーの希薄化
・stETHなどのLSTがETHそのものを「お金」として置き換えていくこと、、、らしい

そして、これを抑えようとしたのがEIP-8363。

ステーキング比率が上がるほどValidator報酬をBurnし、50%付近では新規発行によるステーキングインセンティブをなくすという、かなり大胆な提案だった。

ただし議論になったのは中身だけではなく、「ETHの発行政策という金融政策レベルの変更を、ハードフォークの採用プロセスで決めていいのか？」という点。

結果、Hegotáへの導入は撤回。

EIP-8363の問題意識そのものが否定されたというより、Ethereumの発行政策は専用のプロセスを作って議論し直す、という着地。

Ethereumが「どれだけステークされれば安全なのか」ではなく、「ステークされすぎること自体がリスクでは？」を議論しているのが面白い。

text:
People don’t like talking to chatbots that take more than 3 seconds to respond. Can decision models help solve this?

Let's look at a tool-calling case study.  

A student on Leap types "make me flashcards."   

The usual path: send the request to an LLM, wait 3–4 seconds, read a paragraph about flashcards, then go find the button.  

Leap's path: Sage, our decision model, recognizes the request in ~100 ms, and the flashcards open.  

Every message gets three quick questions first:  

• Does the student want an activity? 
• Which one? 
• More than one?  

"Make me flashcards" → the tool opens. 
"How do flashcards work?" → that's a real question, so the LLM answers.  

Why it matters for the business:  
→ Faster: action chips appear in under 300 ms in production. 
→ Cheaper: no LLM call to write text nobody reads. 
→ Safer: confidence thresholds decide when to act, suggest, or keep chatting, and the team tunes them without an App Store release.  

Tested on 327 held-out requests, each run 3 times:  
• 89.9% accuracy 
• 0 unwanted tool launches 
• 6 languages, including mixed-language messages  

The pattern works for any agent product: list your actions, test tool selection on real examples, and map confidence to behavior.  

Decide first. Generate second.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

Excited to release Discourse, a tech forum for the modern era.    

https://t.co/lWExPIdGpw   

Today, the discourse in tech is either free for all (broadcast social networks) or completely private (group chats). There’s no midsize social network where a few thousand tech leaders talk to each other.    

We'll have a hybrid model. Some people will have access to post directly, and everyone else's posts will go through a queue. We'll start with ~5,000 white-listed people, and more people who post smart comments will be given direct access over time.    

Discourse is built off the @cosign graph and will be embedded into the platform.    

We’ve partnered with our favorite monitors to make sense of what’s happening in real time.    

P.S. True to form, I actually built a version of this a decade ago called @beondeckdaily, inspired by Hacker News.

quoted_text:
New episode with military historian Si Sheppard.

The conquests of the Aztec and Inca empires might be the most shocking events in human history.

Hernan Cortés and some hundreds of Conquistadors landed on a new continent they knew basically nothing about, and within 2 and a half years, conquered the 6 million strong Aztec empire.

Then, a decade later, Francisco Pizarro did the same thing to an Incan Empire of some 10 million inhabitants.

In both cases, the Conquistadors consistently beat native armies while being literally 100x (or even in some cases 1000x) outnumbered - and in many cases, did so without taking a single casualty.

And they did this with 99% of their military forces being made up of the very natives they were trying to subjugate.

We often forget how wild human history is. People talk about AI takeover as if it would be some crazy, unprecedented sci-fi outcome. But this would not be the first time an alien force whose motives the defenders barely understand use more advanced technology and diplomatic cunning to outmaneuver and then take over a much larger and long established existing order.

quoted_text:
My conversation with @AlexTaubman, co-founder and CEO of Long Lake.

Long Lake is 3 years old, has 30,000 employees, $4 billion in revenue, and just took Amex Travel private. 

Alex and his partners have spent the last three years building Long Lake with almost no public profile. They started in HOA management and expanded into five service lines. Their latest deal: $6.3 billion for American Express Global Business Travel.

Long Lake buys great businesses and makes them better with AI. Their engineers sit alongside the people doing the work, understand what slows them down, and build tools that give them more time to serve customers. 

We talk about what he learned growing up in a family of entrepreneurs, why Long Lake built its own AI platform, what Henry Singleton and the Rales brothers taught him about compounding, and why the best partners make you more ambitious.

Alex wants to spend the next 50 years on this. We talk about how far it could go.

剛好這幾天很多人在討論
市場上到底需不需要更多的 perpdex 

我們可以從社群有信仰的原因來推估 TGE 後的走勢如何

每個人習慣使用一間 Perp DEX 的原因可能會不一樣，取決於你是擼毛的、是交易員，還是套利仔。大家所追求的，可能是積分空投，也可能是套利的報酬

這次的晚餐剛好旁邊就做了個積分名列前茅的韓國帥哥 @linenmito  他提到，Variational TGE 之後，主要的選擇也會是 @variational_io  以及 @Lighter_xyz  。對於市場上新的這些 PerpDEX 來說，他使用的意願並不大

1. 他無法掌握每間 PerpDEX 發幣的時間，這對他來說是一個很大的不確定性

2. 對於套利者來說，不確定性其實就是幣價。幣價範圍是可以透過計算有所掌控的，最差的情形不過就是執行套利策略最後的 APR 會低一些，因為在套利交易上更看重流動性以及支持的幣對等其他因素

我不是一個專業的交易員，我在理解這些項目能否在 TGE 之後還繼續在市場上生存，其中一個考量就是有沒有自己的護城河

合規是護城河，生態資源也是護城河。就像絕大多數人都沒有辦法預料到，Lighter 在這一波的價格上漲中 

Robinhood chain 也起到了很大的作用。能有這樣的結果不是偶然，能夠提前看到這個結果的人，自然也有看到一些大部分人看不到的東西

總之感謝 Variational 組織 KBW 期間幾次的活動, s/o to @hansolar21 @JustinCBram @sjtional @sishido1011 

好的活動就是大家參與過後會更有信仰, 不是單純過水, 很不容易

昨晚去参加 @variational_io 私人晚宴，分享几个信息

内幕一，@NamishibaHQ 老师分享，两周后就开公共主网，无需邀请码注册。我预估按 Lighter 刻舟求剑，再一个月后 TGE ？

内幕二，昨晚 @JustinCBram 祝酒，说 Lucas 飞纽约去参加一个投资人的会议，用了 investment 这个词

我估计：可能有很多大机构非常想投 Var，如果后面再宣布巨大的融资或者是战略合作？那就又是大彩蛋

按照团队一贯的行事风格，每次都超出预期，可能会给我们大惊喜

--

之前阿豪老师 @Vegahao 问，“你觉得 var 为什么会成功？” ，我想起一件小事：

大概一年前，我两边对冲的单子，早上醒来发现 VAR 这边突然平掉了，单腿我吓惨了。我就去问 @variational_lvs ，他说是预言机出了问题，团队正在处理。我说我没有损失，那我就不管了

三天后，我钱包突然收到一笔转账 1 万多美金。我查链上记录，有人提了几十万美金，给几百个人疯狂打款，有人收了 5 万多美金

我吓惨了，以为是黑客在罗宾汉劫富济贫，链上乱打钱，那笔钱我一直不敢动

很久后，我在 DC 里看到 Mod 老师 @hashcoin0 一个回复，说之前预言机自动平仓的补偿已全部处理

我恍然大悟，这是 Var 给用户打的钱。要是其他团队，不得 tmd 发 10 篇公告找 kol 吹牛逼大肆宣传？ 

但 Var 团队根本不在乎，有很多好事做了根本不说，他们认为这是本应该做的事，而且我提前给 Lucas 说了我没有损失，但还是按他们的计价给用户强行打钱！

✅ 当时我就觉得，这种团队的企业文化太屌了，做好事不留名，坚持做自己正确的事，根本不在乎宣传，他妈的格局超大

--

text:
Race car drivers lose up to 5% of their body weight in water.

I’m in Atlanta hanging with @tobi @dhh and Mathias Beche for their 10 hr race.

Race car driving is insane. 

Here's what their bodies will experience:

+ cockpit temp 104-122°F (40 to 50°C)
+ core body temp climbs to 102°F (39°C)
+ multi-layer fireproof suit
+ sweat barely evaporate
+ heart rate of 140-170 bpm
+ up to 4.2 g force (wild)
+ up to 220 lbs (100 kg) on the brake pedal 
+ fluid loss up to 170 fl oz (5 kg), 11 lbs of body weight
+ 600-900 calories per hour
+ at 2% dehydration, reaction time drops

They’ll be driving an LMP2: 603 horsepower, 2,050 pounds, 9,000 rpm.

I’ve personally experienced some of the above things:

> core body temp of 102°F after 34 min 200°F sauna 
> 3 g force in my airplane 
> non evaporative clothing 
> physical exertion of stomping 200 lbs
> severe dehydration

But never all at once, inside a race car for 2.5 hours straight, competing for tenths of a second, and in a high risk environment. 

I’m struggling to get my head around it.

Last week, Tobi and I were at a conference catching up. He and I have been friends for 15 years. 

Tobi and DHH were my first customers at my payments startup Braintree.  I’ll forever be grateful to them and DHH’s co-founder @jasonfried for giving my company life.

Tobi and I went deep on racing and I was hooked. He approaches racing as I do my body. Data, method and analysis. A closed loop game of continuous improvement. Deep flow states. Intense pain. Overcoming self. Losing oneself in the objective. 

He invited me to this weekend’s race, the Motul Petit Le Mans. It’s the season finale of North America's top sports car championship. It starts on Saturday at noon and goes until 10 pm.

+ 10 hours
+ 2.54 mile (4 km) road course
+ roughly 400 laps
+ 54 cars
+ Tobi, DHH and Mathias rotating 

Off the track, Tobi is an exceptional builder: 
+ founder and ceo of Shopify
+ 6 million+ merchants
+ $195 billion market cap
+ 20 yrs building

Off the track, DHH is a software legend:
+ created Ruby on Rails
+ co-founder & CTO of 37signals (Basecamp, HEY)
+ built Omarchy, open-source, AI-first OS
+ 20 yrs building, profitable, no outside capital
+ 24 Hours of Le Mans class winner & FIA World Endurance Champion (GTE-Am)

On the track: Mathias Beche:

+ 24 Hours of Le Mans overall podium finisher
+ European Le Mans Series LMP2 champion
+ FIA World Endurance Championship race winner
+ 15+ career prototype victories across WEC and ELMS

What a team of bad asses. 

I’m excited to be in the pit on Saturday and watch all of this go down.

🚨 Border Control / Immigration Officer, Manchester Airport, WHISTLEBLOWER Interview

Transponders turned off, 3-4 flights a week x 18 months = massive numbers 

Immigrants sneaked through Manchester Airports private terminal

WHISTLEBLOWER SPEAKS OUT

Q1: Thank you for agreeing to meet with me. Please tell me a little bit about yourself

A: I hold a position within Border Control based at Manchester Airport. We report to a Regional Director, who then reports directly to the Director General of Border Control and Immigration, who then of course reports directly to the Home Secretary

Q2: How long have you been with Border Control?

A: I have been with Border Control for twenty‑one years, which includes service with Customs as well. I have worked at various locations, but I have been based at Manchester Airport for the last six years

Q7: Well, that being the case — thank you for trusting me. We have verified your identity and employment. So tell me — what would you like us to know? Give us as much detail as you possibly can without compromising yourself

A: Are you aware of the private terminal at Manchester Airport?

Q8: Yes — it's called Aether. It's a private terminal, quite a distance from the other terminals — for luxury passengers, chauffeur‑driven cars, and private screening, isn't it?

A: Yes, that's correct. We all take rotation shifts to work in that private area as part of our normal airport operation. But that is not all that it is used for. Of course, there are day‑to‑day transfers and high‑value clients — but there is another side to that part of the airport that the public are not aware of

Q9: I wasn't fully aware of that — but please tell me, what do you mean about this other part of the airport that we're not aware of?

A: When you are working in the private terminal, you see things not visible from the main terminals. Diplomatic flights arrive — they have specialist security and bypass normal screening because this is Government‑run. But what we have witnessed is something the public needs to know about

Q10: Go on

A: Night shifts are quiet. We patrol to check nothing is untoward. But there is an area we can see — but are formally prevented from entering or inspecting. That in itself is a major red flag

Q11: Okay — now I am concerned

A: You should be. Regular flights arrive there — 3 or 4 times every week. Transponders are switched off, yet they are given clearance to land using a special call sign. Passengers are NOT screened by us — they are processed directly by Home Office personnel. They board unmarked buses. Each flight carries 200–300 people

Q12: How do you know transponders are off — and what do you mean by call signs?

A: We network with colleagues across the airport — ATC, ground crew, and others. Information gets shared. In fact — Air Traffic Control personnel also want to speak with you

Q13: What exactly do you mean — the transponders are switched off?

A: Aircraft are tracked via transponder. Pilots can switch them off with special clearance — vanishing from public view. These are contracted Government aircraft — previously operated by Avro and 2XL Airways. These are subcontracted flights — and their passengers do not go through normal Border Control

Q14: I must be clear — these airlines need independent verification. But please continue

A: Understood. ATC will corroborate. These flights arrive from the Middle East and sub‑Saharan Africa. They land between 2:00 am and 4:00 am. Government gives clearance. Unmarked buses collect passengers and leave through a hidden exit gate onto restricted roads — then merge onto motorways and vanish

Q15: Why would the Government allow people into the country that Border Control has not vetted?

A: Because we are deliberately kept out of the process. We receive NO flight manifests. We do NOT see the passengers. We only know their origin because ATC tells us. 3–4 flights × 18 months = massive numbers. Nobody knows who they are or where they go

quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
The funds from the $3.8M NEAR Intents exploit have been returned, just one day later, and the investigation is closed.

Thanks to SHIELD, the AI security layer on Intents, along with some aggressive detective work, the Intents team identified the party responsible less than 24h after the hack, established communication, and got the funds back in full at 14:30 UTC today. 

Thank you to @alexauroradev and the whole @near_intents team for this fast and clean resolution – as well as the broader @NEARProtocol ecosystem and SHIELD partners for the support and help. There’s been relentless work over the past 24 hours by so many people to make this right and it is a great testament to this community’s values and determination.

To echo Alex: for security researchers looking for exploits, we encourage you to use bug bounties. They exist for a reason.

At NEAR, we believe that privacy is a right, but not as a way to facilitate crime. Our technology is built to expand human agency and opportunity, not to facilitate criminal activity. The events of the last week have shown the value of SHIELD to find suspicious activity before things escalate too far, as well as to accelerate resolution so the vast majority of legitimate users are not affected. Confidentiality cannot come at the expense of lawfulness and I strongly believe it doesn’t have to.

We’ve learned a great deal from this incident and work is already underway to harden our security systems and further adapt to the changing cybersecurity landscape. AI may be accelerating exploits, but it can also help us defend against them. I hope our entire industry responds with vigilance and feels the same sense of urgency to work together.

Our clinical trial participants have now used their Neuralink implants for over 50,000 hours, building one of the largest datasets of intracortical neural activity ever.

We used it to pretrain a foundation model for BCI: self-supervised neural encoders that turn noisy, drifting spikes into stable representations.

Some initial results:
• Decoders that keep working for weeks instead of days. For some users, calibration dropped from 10 min/day to 10 min/week
• Teleporting cursors that jump straight to the intended target
• A new cursor-control record of 11.32 bits per second (exceeding the performance of most able-bodied people)

We’re just getting started. Future directions include pooling data across participants, one-shot (or zero-shot) calibration, and an API for the motor cortex.

text:
thoughts on Robinhood chain eco

ON A MACRO LEVEL

Robinhood chain didn't take off because it has superior tech

otherwise Optimism, Arbitrum (which RH chain is built on), etc would be among the top EVMs today

it took off because Robinhood is one of the world's most significant retail trading platforms, with tens of millions of users who are generally wealthier than the average CEX user cohort

crypto participants have also long considered Robinhood the cream of the crop for exchange listings

rumors of an incoming Robinhood listing have fueled some of the biggest memecoin/altcoin rallies in crypto history

Robinhood's role in the $DOGE + $SHIB mania of 2021 only cemented that status

now you have a Robinhood chain where people believe tokens launched there have a higher probability of eventually being listed on Robinhood

that's an extremely powerful flywheel

more devs launch on the chain

more users buy on the chain

more liquidity flows in

and i think people counting out Robinhood chain are going to find out just how powerful this narrative can be in a proper bull run

WHY THE RECENT WEAKNESS?

1. RH eco coins pumped giga hard

a lot of RH eco coins simply needed a cooldown

$PONS went from ~$30m to $960m+ in weeks before the bull run has even kicked off

a ~50% correction after that kind of move is completely normal and can set the stage for another explosive leg

same applies across the eco

2. Solana stepped up

the Robinhood retail distribution narrative was a major catalyst

but apathy and a lack of action from Solana for a while leading to the emergence of Robinhood chain also helped fuel the initial RH chain explosion

that has changed

Solana has stepped up and made it clear they remain a force to contend with this cycle

with liquidity still relatively constrained, that naturally diverted some flows away from Robinhood chain

but i don't think liquidity will stay constrained forever

soon there should be enough liquidity to accommodate serious activity on BOTH Robinhood chain and Solana

and of course BNB chain (i mean this goes without saying)

3. lack of follow through from Robinhood

this is probably the easiest problem to fix

if the biggest catalyst behind the chain was the Robinhood distribution channel, people will eventually lose interest if barely anything gets listed

Robinhood listing $CASHCAT so early was bullish and helped spark the second wave of activity on the chain

but they've listed almost nothing else from the ecosystem three months into launch

that's a bad signal

$PONS went from ~$30m to almost $1b, became a major driver of activity and at one point contributed ~50% of chain activity

it's perhaps the most successful new launche of the past year in all of crypto

yet it still hasn't been listed by Robinhood

same with $AI

it's the flagship token of Long, the second biggest launchpad on RH chain

it's also a top-tier memecoin that brought significant attention to the chain during its run to $350m+

i don't own $AI, but i'm surprised it isn't on Robinhood

from the outside, it's difficult to understand why $PONS and $AI haven't been listed yet

and i'm not claiming to know Robinhood's internal listing criteria or regulatory considerations

but the longer the biggest successes on the chain go without Robinhood distribution, the weaker the core ecosystem flywheel becomes

if devs and users stop believing that building on Robinhood chain gives them a meaningful distribution advantage, some of the chain's biggest differentiators disappear

and that's what contributed to momentum stalling alongside the other factors above

the good news?

this is the easiest problem to fix

and i'd actually love to see Robinhood throw something much lower cap and more degen into the mix

could be something like robinhood:0xe8ffd7e24187f72afb08d75b1bb13088a989a791 (the leading RH-native liquidity layer) or $BOW (the leading RH-native lending market) — could also be some other low cap, but i mentioned both since they have a strong narrative and justification, which likely attract even more builders/users to the chain

that would create speculation that ANYTHING could get listed

and that kind of uncertainty is exactly what fuels degeneracy

it is very clear that @vladtenev has been strategic and calculated in how he's leading the chain

he also has his ears on the ground and understands the trenches

so i'm not particularly concerned about #3 over a long enough timeframe

ABOUT THE HOOD SUMMIT

i've seen people say the HOOD Summit was bearish for Robinhood chain because the RH eco didn't massively pump during or after the event

i think that's missing the bigger picture

a lot of people expected the Summit to be a catalyst for the next leg up

that catalyst didn't come

but what happened next is more interesting

the RH eco held up

there was no major 'sell the news' dump

after an event with that much anticipation, that's significant

the important signal to me is that the eco absorbed the event without breaking down

that makes me think the recent weakness may have largely run its course

i think the next leg up across Robinhood chain comes soon

i don't know exactly when or what the catalyst will be

maybe some Vlad Tenev wizardry + Robinhood listings

maybe something completely unexpected

TO CONCLUDE...

a lot of people love Robinhood

and their team has made a lot of the right moves so far

they have a massive advantage through the Robinhood retail platform

and they can weaponize that distribution advantage to drive sustained activity on their chain

the Robinhood narrative only gets more powerful as the market and altcoins heat up

i think the biggest question now is simply how aggressively Robinhood chooses to capitalize on the ecosystem it has created

count out Robinhood chain at your own peril!

text:
I spent 3 years working at @Coinbase building out the Custody product line, which grew from $0 → $100B+ in assets under custody.

looking back, a lot of the lessons I learned during those three years still shape how I think about growing and building Turnkey today.

EFFICIENT EXECUTION
for starters, Coinbase was an absolute execution machine. the pace was incredibly high, teams moved with urgency, decisions got made quickly, and there was always a strong bias toward shipping rather than overthinking every outcome. Brian has said before "Action produces information. Just keep doing stuff."

CLEAR COMMUNICATION
at the time, Coinbase was an organization of 3,000+ employees, and one thing that always stood out to me was how clear the communication was across different teams and departments. even at that scale, the entire team could recite the Mission, Vision, and Strategies.  everyone understood what we were building, why it mattered, and what needed to happen next. 

HIGH EXPECTATIONS
and lastly, expectations were incredibly high. not just the expectations placed on us, but the standards we held ourselves to every day. we knew we were building products that represented the entire crypto industry, and that meant constantly proving ourselves, raising the bar, and delivering at a level the industry expected.

very thankful for my time at Coinbase. a lot of Turnkey’s success today is directly to those lessons.

quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
The funds from the $3.8M NEAR Intents exploit have been returned, just one day later, and the investigation is closed.

Thanks to SHIELD, the AI security layer on Intents, along with some aggressive detective work, the Intents team identified the party responsible less than 24h after the hack, established communication, and got the funds back in full at 14:30 UTC today. 

Thank you to @alexauroradev and the whole @near_intents team for this fast and clean resolution – as well as the broader @NEARProtocol ecosystem and SHIELD partners for the support and help. There’s been relentless work over the past 24 hours by so many people to make this right and it is a great testament to this community’s values and determination.

To echo Alex: for security researchers looking for exploits, we encourage you to use bug bounties. They exist for a reason.

At NEAR, we believe that privacy is a right, but not as a way to facilitate crime. Our technology is built to expand human agency and opportunity, not to facilitate criminal activity. The events of the last week have shown the value of SHIELD to find suspicious activity before things escalate too far, as well as to accelerate resolution so the vast majority of legitimate users are not affected. Confidentiality cannot come at the expense of lawfulness and I strongly believe it doesn’t have to.

We’ve learned a great deal from this incident and work is already underway to harden our security systems and further adapt to the changing cybersecurity landscape. AI may be accelerating exploits, but it can also help us defend against them. I hope our entire industry responds with vigilance and feels the same sense of urgency to work together.

text:
Anthropic 的工程师说：我们内部已经不怎么写 prompt 了，写的是循环。

她在台上花了半小时，展示了 Claude 团队如何创建能够自我提示的循环。

如果这堂课卖 400 刀，今年 Agent 课的榜单大概就是它。但它是免费的。

真正拉开代际差距的，不是谁的 Prompt 写得好，而是Agent系统架构彻底换了：

1. 记忆从一份 CLAUDE.md，进化成 Agent 自己读写的 memory/ 目录

2. 记忆待在对话里会烂掉：注意力被劈开，规律被埋住，旧笔记还在自信地用错

3. 白天各 Agent 把进展写进团队记忆

4. 夜里再跑一轮 dreaming：核对、整理、补全。第二天开工的那个，自动比昨天聪明一点

数据结果也很直观：一次通过的错误少了 97%，验收快了 30%。人回去看产品，不再一直盯着提示词。

提示词是一次性的，而循环能够持续执行。

差的不是你会不会问。

是你的 Agent 睡一觉之后，还记不记得昨天学到的东西。 https://t.co/9oMymowy0F

Today we're unveiling Trillium Labs @trillium_labs, a new non-profit to foster the open science of frontier AI. We're building open post-training recipes and will expand into open infra to study RSI, reward-hacking, multi-agent systems, and whatever comes next.

We're built around the theory of change that you need more eyes to solve hard technical problems. We have faith in the scientific methods and communities that humanity has built, and worry that AI is becoming too closed to utilize them.

Trilliums are wildflowers that bloom briefly in the spring, before the forest canopies fill out. Though they are small, they lay the foundation for the cycles of growth and nourishment through the rest of the year. At Trillium Labs, the recipes will be the slow nutrients for the seasons and the model releases will be the blooms. Building an institution dedicated to this is needed because, much as nature’s trilliums are slow to expand and grow, the open-ecosystem needs time and dedicated resources to catch up.

I co-founded with with a long-time friend and collaborator Tom Zick (@thesezickbeats). We're hiring (full time + student collabs/interns), we're fundraising, and we're looking for compute. Please get in touch if you're interested in helping out. Offices based in the Bay Area and Cambridge MA, remote okay.
