text:
OFAC just designated a terrorist financing network that moved more than $2 million to Hamas through fake charities and crypto, among other payment rails.

At the center of the fundraising network was Saleem al-Zaq (Alzaq), a battalion deputy in Hamas’ al-Qassam Brigades, who allegedly used social media to solicit donations that he claimed were for humanitarian aid in Gaza. Prosecutors allege the funds went to Hamas instead.

Al-Zaq’s network stretched from the U.S. to Gaza and beyond. In France, al-Zaq’s associates Faouzi Barika and Amel Oualid (also now sanctioned) allegedly collected donations through organizations they also claimed were charities. Two of them, Association Baraka and Ensemble C Mieux, have now been sanctioned by OFAC. 
Funds raised through the network were then aggregated in a French bank account, converted into cryptocurrency, and sent to wallets controlled by al-Zaq. 

The DOJ alleges that Louisiana brothers Abdel and Omar Adhami, along with Florida resident Raed Yousef, sent tens of thousands of dollars into the network. The network's participants allegedly used coded language and messaging apps to conceal their communications and transactions. Al-Zaq would also share crypto deposit addresses in these communications.

On-chain analysis of an address controlled by al-Zaq, which is a deposit address at a global exchange, shows a mutual counterparty moving funds into other global exchange deposit addresses that have received significant funds from numerous Hamas-related addresses targeted by Israel NBCTF seizure orders. Mutual counterparty analysis is key to providing insights on the broader networks that support terrorist financing.

The case is part of a broader pattern in Hamas-linked fundraising. U.S. authorities have repeatedly identified the use of purported charitable organizations, online and social-media campaigns, and cryptocurrency as components of Hamas's international fundraising efforts.

Recent enforcement actions also show increasing attention from U.S. authorities to the cryptocurrency infrastructure behind these campaigns.

Let’s suppose that you were able every night to dream any dream you wanted to dream, and that you could, for example, have the power within one night to dream 75 years of time, or any length of time you wanted to have.

And you would, naturally, as you began on this adventure of dreams, you would fulfill all your wishes. You would have every kind of pleasure you could conceive. And after several nights of 75 years of total pleasure each you would say “Well that was pretty great. But now let’s have a surprise, let’s have a dream which isn’t under control, where something is gonna happen to me that I don’t know what it's gonna be.”

And you would dig that and would come out of that and you would say, “Wow that was a close shave, wasn’t it?”

Then you would get more and more adventurous and you would make further- and further-out gambles what you would dream. And finally, you would dream where you are now. You would dream the dream of living the life that you are actually living today.

That would be within the infinite multiplicity of choices you would have. Of playing that you weren't God, because the whole nature of the godhead, according to this idea, is to play that he is not. So in this idea then, everybody is fundamentally the ultimate reality, not God in a politically kingly sense, but god in the sense of being the self, the deep-down basic whatever there is. And you are all that, only you are pretending you are not.

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
“Except this simply is not true”
I notice non-technical people fail to understand this point about Chinese dependency on CUDA. So here I'll explain.
You can NOT create an ecosystem by decree and subsidy. That's a real issue even in a “command economy”, and that's why China rejected H20s and is being so lukewarm even towards H200s. You need people, lots and lots of talented people, to use your chips, your servers, your frameworks, your APIs, your whole architecture, to solve cutting edge problems, give you feedback and contribute. As a rule, talented people have interesting stuff to do, and it's usually not “fixing an ngmi platform”. Superstar effects are very significant, learning curves are unforgiving. AMD is still struggling! Huawei can make good (in theory) silicon. But if the only people training on Ascends are Huawei and IFlyTek, that silicon will not get anywhere, because Huawei and IFlyTek are plainly clueless about frontier model training.
You see, everyone likes that Wenfeng's quote about lacking chips, but the core limiting factor in the “AI race” is still not compute but TALENT, both in R&D and management. Compute is the limiting factor *for DeepSeek specifically* because they are geniuses, unironically, IOI Gold level monsters. They have all the talent they need, they only lack GPUs to execute on their vision. Conversely, compute is NOT the limiting factor for titans like Meta, Microsoft and Amazon, as can be surmised from them making garbage tier models despite 1000x or greater compute advantage over DeepSeek. Most labs that whine about their hunger for compute and joke about “hnngh I want gpus go brr” despite glaring inability to match a mature V3 with vastly more than 2048 H800s are saving face. They are not bottlenecked by FLOPS, they are bottlenecked by skill issues. That's how it is in late 2025, at the end of the era of blind scaling, as announced by Ilya and the faithful. Time to update your priors.
At least two of DeepSeek engineers that I know are former NVidia interns, incidentally. What do you think they prefer to work on? 

Insofar as China has steady access to NVidia chips, this very directly and VERY DRASTICALLY slows down the development of their sovereign tech stacks because ≈100% of the cream of the crop of their talent will just go to labs that use NVidia, to work without hassle on their interesting frontier research and deliver world-class results, rather than debug CANN-ONNX with a sleepy Huawei intern. Simple as. 
They're not a Maoist society, they can't tell a proud 3500 CodeForces anime pfp autist with a top NeurIPS paper to go fuck around with CANN, he'll just leave, either to a saner lab or outright to the US. This has been going on forever, and this is what motivates Xi to impose restrictions and inconveniences on H200 procurement – he wants those who stay to have no choice but to assist domestic chipmakers. You may find this policy wrong due to a disagreement about AGI timelines and trajectory. Fine. But that is the Chinese policy. Huawei, Cambricon and others are hurt massively by NVidia. Add AMD, which seems to have finally rubbed two braincells together, and it's a full-out attack on their capability to develop an alternative to American architectures within a decade. 

I am relatively optimistic about outcomes for China in either case. They'll figure it out. My point is simply motivated by irritation about this very crude and smug misunderstanding. No bitch, locking them onto your stack has value. Do with this information what you will.

If AI can generate CUDA kernels, what does a kernel engineer do now?

The work is shifting from hand-writing every kernel toward building the systems that make AI-generated kernels useful in practice — helping agents learn new hardware, improving search and feedback, and building better ways to verify correctness. Generation is getting cheaper, but correctness is becoming a critical problem. A generated kernel can look faster on a benchmark but fail in production because of race conditions, stream interactions, output reuse, or other subtle bugs. That makes verification and deep hardware expertise more central to the job.

When I was with @Galxe, our finance team used to manage 100+ wallets across roughly 40 chains, plus bank accounts in different jurisdictions, custody providers, OTC desks and exchanges and different on-chain and fiat accounting tools.

Every one of these solved a real problem, but none of them were built to work together.

Having so many different tools for so many different use cases made it very difficult for finance to do all the patchwork themselves - they'd often have to ask engineers for help to write scripts to read all the data and reconcile everything so they could close the books.

Over the years, I've seen how much work goes on behind all those siloed systems across finance, operations and sales. Wallets weren't designed for teams. Fintechs weren't designed for on-chain businesses.

I've used pretty much all of them. The fix wasn't one more tool on top of the pile... it was about rebuilding the stack from the bottom up for the businesses running (or wanting to run) on stablecoins.

哇偶，感觉 DeepSeek Harness 正在开启 Agent 领域的 Linux 时刻，说是DeepSeek 放了个核弹级大招也不为过，所有做 AI Agent、搞代码自动化和本地工作流的铁汁都可以去下载体验啦，

为什么这么说呢，我觉得它打破了所有闭源工具把模型和界面死死绑定的垄断做法，做到了连 Agent 循环本身都能热插拔，
从双击运行的桌面端，到数百个开源插件自由组合，这篇我跟大家用大白话详细讲清楚， DeepSeek 真正想做的是下一代开源基建，

他们正式为开源 Agent 框架 DeepSeek Harness（dsh）发布了原生的 macOS 和 Windows 桌面安装包，Linux 也可以通过 npm 一行命令直接跑， 

这意味着从今天起，一个完全不被任何大厂生态绑架、零门槛双击即用的顶级开源 AI 智体底座，正式端到了所有普通用户的桌面上。

一句大变化概括这件事的本质就是： Claude Code 把 Agent 锁在闭源模型和订阅制里，而 DeepSeek 把整个 Agent 的神经中枢、工具沙箱与插件系统全部拆解开源，并用开箱即用的原生桌面端彻底砸穿了本地部署的门槛。

现在绝大多数想在本地用 AI 解决复杂工程、自动化办公的人，都在经历同一种极度痛苦的折磨：
 用闭源工具，每天面对按 token 计费的昂贵账单和随时被封号限流的窝囊气，
 转去折腾开源框架，又得在终端里配环境、搞 node 版本、修权限依赖，还没开始干活就被报错劝退， 更致命的是，市面上绝大多数 Agent 框架的底层循环是写死的，想换个模型、加个新工具就像动一场开颅手术。

我把 DeepSeek Harness 这次杀穿行业的三大核心维度给大家拆解透：

第一个，生产力底座的范式革命：
一切皆插件，连 Agent 循环本身都能热插拔 DeepSeek Harness 绝不是又一个简单的聊天外壳或套壳 IDE，它的核心哲学叫 Everything is a Plugin。 

在它的架构里没有特权核心：
 → 接入的模型是插件，DeepSeek、Kimi、Claude 或本地 Ollama 随便切；

 → 运行的环境是插件，从终端 CLI、沉浸式 TUI 到本地 Web UI 和桌面客户端自由组合；

 → 甚至连 Agent 的思考循环、任务分发与反思验证机制，都可以作为插件随时卸载、重组与热替换； 你不是在用某一家公司的工具，而是在搭积木一样定制属于你自己的专属工作机。

第二个，工程落地的降维暴击：从极客命令行直接跃迁到双击即用的桌面端 过去几个月 Harness 在开源社区狂飙突进，但很多人依然被 npm 权限和终端指令卡在门外。 

这次官方直接打包出 macOS 和 Windows 的独立桌面应用： 你不需要懂复杂的编程环境配置，下载安装包、填入 API Key、选中工作目录， 

它就能像资深架构师一样接管本地文件、自动跨文件搜索分析、运行测试、修 Bug 并生成完整的执行溯源链路， 把原本属于极客的自动化超能力，直接变成了人手一个的系统级生产力工具。

第三个，生态开放与资产主权闭环：
把工具定义权彻底还给开发者 闭源平台把用户圈在自己的围墙花园里，而 DeepSeek 选择了最彻底的开源与去中心化。 

它完美兼容 MCP（模型上下文协议）和社区数百个开源插件： 你的代码历史、本地知识库、自动化测试脚本和会话记忆全部沉淀在本地， 敏感项目绝不上传任何未授权的云端， 模型负责在远端提供算力，而真正的工具链、工作流与核心资产，从第一天起就死死攥在用户自己手里。

真实历史与数据硬核印证： 
→ 开源演进的代际规律： 从当年封闭的商业 Unix 到自由的 Linux，底层操作系统的开放最终繁衍出了整个互联网；DeepSeek Harness 正在将 Agent 的底层执行框架推向同样的 Linux 时刻； 
→ 成本与算力的解绑战报： 配合 DeepSeek 极致性价比的推理定价，跑通原本在闭源旗舰上需要几十美金的百轮复杂长任务，在本地 Harness 上只需几毛钱即可完成；
 → 社区生态的指数裂变： 从代码审查、多模态视觉桥接（ModLens）到跨项目记忆同步，GitHub 上 dsh-plugin 话题下已有数百个开源项目开箱即用。

但褪去台前的宏大光环，硬币的反面极其冷峻：
 → 自由度的代价是配置认知： 插件化赋予了极高的定制上限，但也意味着用户需要对模型特性、上下文窗口和工具调用边界有基本认知，才能组装出最顺手的流水线； 
→ 开源生态的初期兼容性博弈： 随着各家大模型接口频繁迭代，部分社区第三方插件在极端复杂边缘场景下，依然需要开发者具备一定的调试能力； 
→ 算力底座的智力分水岭： Harness 解决了执行框架和手脚问题，但任务长链条规划的上限，依然取决于你挂载的大脑模型本身的推理硬实力。

过去我们以为 Agent 竞争比的是谁的模型名字更响亮，
现在 DeepSeek 证明了，真正决定生产力未来的，是把模型变成插件、把执行权完整交还给用户的开源基础设施。

你们平时在本地跑代码和工作流，最被困扰的是环境配置太烦、闭源 API 账单太贵，还是工具生态太封闭？我的感受是以前天天在各种工具之间切来切去导上下文，现在一个完全开源可定制的本地 Harness，终于把所有的手脚给聚齐了，很爽～

The communication about this claim could’ve been way better and for that, I take full responsibility.

The allocation is now >41% claimed in a single day (fully unlocked, no vest), this tells us that even despite the thousands of pundits today, participants have been extremely receptive to the long term oriented mechanics of this program.

This was never publicly disclosed, as there’s been no point to it for over a year, but Kinetiq received a $20m term sheet at $250m ($0.25) last year prior to KNTQ genesis.

That sounds great on paper, until you realize that this would’ve essentially crushed the public economic value of the project, by creating ridiculously predatory vesting schedules that would’ve made Kinetiq (KNTQ) un-investable for years to come, which is the bane of the existence of essentially every other protocol in our singular category at the time.

This would’ve been an unacceptable outcome to us, hence swiftly declined. Proof? Ask @wassielawyer who was kind enough to personally review each term sheet.

Instead, we chose to follow through on the precedent Hyperliquid set by distributing 25% of the protocol after what was likely the shortest points program ever.

You may feel that your trust in Kinetiq and our team was misplaced, but we’ve followed through on everything we said we would, and will continue to do so - whether you’re here or not.

Regardless of how you felt about today, I (we) appreciate all of your commentary. The good, the bad, the ugly. 

The mission remains unchanged, and the vision ever more clear.

quoted_text:
Major announcement in mathematical formalization!

Finally, after 3 months of very intensive, nonstop work by several AI agents (Codex and Claude Code), we have settled a classification of ALL 15,973 semigroups of order 6. Every one of the 15,969 that has a finite basis now has it written down explicitly, and the remaining 4 are proved to have none at all.

The whole list of bases is produced for the first time in history. Until now, for most of these semigroups, mathematicians only knew that a basis exists; nobody had ever written one down. The formalization in Lean, orchestrated with a multi-agent approach, reached more than 5 MILLION lines of verified Lean code, one of the largest auto-formalization projects to date. 

It's been an amazing joint work with @JanotaMikolas and @Jan_Hula, accompanied by senior experts in semigroup theory, João Araújo and Edmond W. H. Lee.

Our paper describing this project, "Proving at Scale for Universal Algebra", has been accepted at the MATH-AI workshop, NeurIPS 2026!

When we launched this project, we were a bit pessimistic: producing proofs for 15,973 semigroups seemed out of scope for the current technology. But with a careful setup (agents communicating through a mailbox we arranged, orchestrating the effort with a custom method of bootstrapping and auto-research), it has finally come to the finish line. The last 390 semigroups took 23 more days. The very last one needed a whole structural analysis before its proof could even be written.

text:
Q3 is done, and I wanted to take a minute to appreciate what the @dynamic_xyz team actually accomplished.

When you spend every day working through the next release, customer issue, or thing that needs fixing, it’s easy to lose sight of how much has changed.

Looking back through this quarter, my reaction was pretty much: holy shit. We did a lot.

We rebuilt a huge amount of our SDK foundation: 
- SDK v5 shipped
- We removed support for v1 and v2 wallets, consolidating around WaaS V3
- Built a migration path for existing customers
- Llaunched standalone React Hooks
- Started moving React Native onto the JS SDK 

We shipped our next generation of native SDKs:
- One TypeScript spec generating native Swift, Kotlin, .NET/MAUI, and Flutter
- No webview bridge, a big change in how we build and maintain this platform (and something I’m especially proud to see come together)

We also gave customers much more control over their security:
- BYOK address screening now covers embedded and connected wallets
- Granular wallet and signer policies
- External transaction review webhooks
- A swap provider policy engine that lets us disable routing providers in seconds without a deploy
- Added Turnstile across SDKs and mobile webviews
- Shipped developer-hosted offline recovery
- Moved disaster recovery work forward that now feeds directly into some really exciting Q4 initiatives

@FireblocksHQ Flow took some big steps toward becoming a more complete payments product:
- Deposit Addresses are live with customers
- Fee Injection across EVM and SVM, giving customers a way to earn revenue through Flow
- Payment Links for payment acceptance with a shareable URL
- Flow Analytics gave teams visibility into volume, drop-off, and settlement

Lots of work on chains and gasless, working hard to scale all of this stuff as more customers came online:
- Expanded our gasless product and gasless billing across EVM and SVM
- Added support for a ton of chains
- Shipped privacy with @MidnightNtwrk 

Somehow, alongside all of that, we also:
- Launched Connections, with arguably two of the largest public companies in the world
- Shipped Business Accounts Core (more on that soon), bringing shared wallets, roles, quorum, and policies to organizations
- Shipped Agent Wallets and Agent Auth
- Added Yield through Morpho vaults in the JS SDK and Flutter.
- Rebuilt https://t.co/7caGD5OTDi into a public demo gallery people can actually explore and share

What stands out to me is how much of this work asks us to build what comes next while taking care of the customers already depending on us. Migrations, recovery, stability, testing, reviews, support… all of that takes time and care, and a release list actually captures very little of the effort.

I know what it took to get this much out the door. I also know there’s still work to do, and things we want to make better. But I didn't want to roll straight into Q4 without stopping long enough to feel proud of this quarter.

Thank you to everyone who built, reviewed, tested, debugged, supported customers, and helped each other get these things live.

I’m really proud of this team, and grateful I get to build with you.

text:
Tokenized stocks is an area where general purpose platforms have the least amount of rent seeking leverage.

Tokenized equities are much different from stablecoins because stablecoin issuers want their tokens to be integrated into various ecosystems. 

In other words, stablecoins will go where ever the activity is.

Tokenized equities are different, they are investment products. Their purpose is to draw capital to themselves rather than to integrate as a medium of exchange or collateral in a shared economy.

The above is true even from a regulatory perspective as we’ve seen with their issuance, redemption, and transferability policies.

The only platforms with any leverage in this equation will be the brokers, and as time goes by, they’ll kick back increasingly less fees to the trading infrastructure they use until they own it.

All signs point to the brokerages running their own L2s if they want some composability with existing ecosystems, or stand alone chains if they don’t.

Either way, modelling value capture based on this trend is highly flawed regardless of its expected growth.

quoted_text:
Surprised this hasn’t gotten more attention: Ethereum L1 is barely showing up in the tokenized equities boom.

Tokenized equities already account for 12% of spot DEX vol on-chain, yet Ethereum L1 has close to 0 market share.

Robinhood, Arbitrum and Base are doing the gruntwork obviously. But where does that leave the L1?

Tokenization is going to reshape  the onchain economy, and tokenized equities are going to be the  fastest-growing segment over the next 2 years. 

Ethereum needs a clear vision for what belongs on L1, what moves to L2s, and how the two fit together, from security and governance to liquidity and value accrual.

More on this in my article next week.

text:
I keep going more niche with reverse engineered web-based versions of games

👉 https://t.co/MohU4A8Zel 👈

6 months ago I tried to reverse engineer Urban Terror

Urban Terror was kind of a Counter-Strike style mod on top of the Quake 3 Arena engine, I think @Erwin_AI got me to play this during COVID

Because it runs on Quake 3's engine like RTCW and Q3 itself, I thought I could just use ioquake3 and WASM to run it on web, then add a multiplayer server and it'd just work...

But no it didn't, I got stuck 6 months ago, it was buggy and wouldn't work, I kept trying and kinda got it to load but not really play

Today I tried it again with Opus 5.5 and again, I couldn't get it to work, giving up I did a last try with Fable 5.1 on high effort and it after awhile it did figure out the issue!

"The engine's struct was 4 bytes longer than what UT's bytecode expects, everything after that point (the entity count and the entity list) was read 4 bytes off"

It rewrote the bytecode and made it work!

So now we have another game preserved, running  100% the web via WASM, with a multiplayer server tied to it, so you can play with your friends 😊

Every model that comes out makes a bit more things possible and you can just keep trying old things that didn't work before

I see lots of people mod modern games now too which looks very cool too

Following gold-medal-level performance from our AI models across five competitions in mathematics, physics, and chemistry, we asked a harder question: can AI contribute when a problem is genuinely open and without an existing solution path?

Over the past several months, mathematicians worked with Muse Spark 1.1 and Muse Spark 1.2 in Thinking Mode through the regular https://t.co/wHkMPH82ZH chat interface, with no custom research scaffold, to find solutions to such problems.

Our goal wasn't to mass-produce papers, but empower researchers. Every collaboration followed the same principles: mathematicians guided the research, a second group of mathematicians then reviewed the work, each paper marks which passages were drafted primarily by humans or AI, and each credits the prior research it builds on. Ever since I got into crypto, I've been thinking about what the most important KPI is for valuation. 

Like, what is going to be the *standard* that everyone accepts?

The KPI that is indisputable in what it reveals when comparing similar businesses. 

----

I believe we landed on it during the bear market: token buybacks. 

I know some founders will argue that this is stupid. That they need to use their revenues to grow. I get it. 

But as an investor, I always come back to this: the best crypto businesses are extremely asset-light and operationally efficient. 

- lean staff

- low capex due to leveraging L1s

- low marketing costs if managing community (the community becomes your decentralized marketing dept  which is way more powerful)

- distribution via existing L1s

- smart contracts that handle accounting & run autonomously

----

As such, the reality is that we should *not think about crypto businesses the same way we think about SaaS or other tech*

Because you should be much more* asset-light* from the jump. And you shouldn't spend 1/3 of the capital raised on Google Ads. 

----

The conclusion is that a protocol's ability to do token buybacks is the clearest signal of the following:

1. Product/market fit
2. Asset-light
3. Is scaled up (and hopefully growing on that arc)
4. Has community/distribution/low marketing spend

So, when a founder says, "We cannot do buybacks because we need to reinvest," what they are really saying is they don't have those things. 

That's ok for a business that launched recently.

It is not ok for one that has been in the market for a full cycle. 

Token buybacks give you the answer. 

----

P.S. Pump Fun has the highest buyback yield of any asset on The Watch List.

Today we're unveiling Trillium Labs @trillium_labs, a new non-profit to foster the open science of frontier AI. We're building open post-training recipes and will expand into open infra to study RSI, reward-hacking, multi-agent systems, and whatever comes next.

We're built around the theory of change that you need more eyes to solve hard technical problems. We have faith in the scientific methods and communities that humanity has built, and worry that AI is becoming too closed to utilize them.

Trilliums are wildflowers that bloom briefly in the spring, before the forest canopies fill out. Though they are small, they lay the foundation for the cycles of growth and nourishment through the rest of the year. At Trillium Labs, the recipes will be the slow nutrients for the seasons and the model releases will be the blooms. Building an institution dedicated to this is needed because, much as nature’s trilliums are slow to expand and grow, the open-ecosystem needs time and dedicated resources to catch up.

I co-founded with with a long-time friend and collaborator Tom Zick (@thesezickbeats). We're hiring (full time + student collabs/interns), we're fundraising, and we're looking for compute. text:
Coming up for air now after a very dense excellent week in Seoul at KBW, while staying on top of our response to a security event affecting part of our infrastructure. 

I can now respond to queries and speculation regarding what is impacted and what is not affected.

Based on our investigation to date, there is no indication that MetaMask wallets or customer funds in wallets have been affected. Your Secret Recovery Phrase, your keys, and the assets in your wallet were not part of this incident because they CANNOT be. You custody and control your own keys. That is how self custody works. You are fully in control of your own money in MetaMask.

Like many providers in our industry, we constantly face attempted attacks from a range of threat actors and periodically encounter security issues. Our approach follows established best practice: we do not publicly discuss the details of an open incident, but we disclose promptly to partners and relevant stakeholders once an issue is sufficiently understood. In this case, we shared the relevant details with partners, agreed and implemented a response strategy together, and then disclosed publicly.

As a precaution, we and our partners rotated validator keys. That step is operationally inconvenient which is regrettable as validators must exit the staking queue and then re-enter the queue to restake, which takes time. 

The validator staking architecture of Ethereum separates the key that proposes and attests from the key that can withdraw the stake. In accordance with the Ethereum principle of self-custody, we do not hold withdrawal keys for our clients. Because of that separation, an issue in the validator infrastructure CANNOT result in the improper movement of the underlying ETH. Rotating those keys was how we reduced residual operational risk.

Self-custody and user control are a central design principle guiding how we build -- in MetaMask, in staking and validation, and across Ethereum more broadly. Self custody plus rigorous decentralization represents a paradigm shift in security. Increasingly, the world is waking up to the benefits of this sounder architecture.

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
Chamath: 3 Things Every Company Needs in the Age of Super Intelligence

1) End-to-End Traceability

2) Policy-to-Risk Mapping

3) Auditable Evidence

@Chamath:

“There's really three things that you're going to need in an age of super intelligence so that boards are protected, CEOs have visibility, and all of the other compliance infrastructure and governance infrastructure of a company like D&O Insurance and all these other things are kept in place, which is end-to-end traceability, right?

Which is to say, when you deploy super intelligence, you need to know what's going on. You need to map it to the policies so that you understand what the risks are. All companies have standard operating procedures, but you need to know exactly when you're deploying super intelligence, how that builds on top of your standard operating procedure, so you need to map policies to risk.

And then the third is you need to have auditable evidence, which is your way of showing all of your downstream ecosystem, ‘Here's what I've done.’

So if anybody taps you on the shoulder, whether it's a lawyer, whether it's an auditor, whether it's a regulator, whether it's in a lawsuit, whether it's a customer, ‘Hey, how did this happen?’ You can present something. So these are, like, very practical, sane things, and you have this solution where the alternative was to hit the pause on trillions of dollars of GDP so that we could sort this out in a multinational body.

The alternative was crazy, so I think what happened was historic and important.”

text:
Dot, Muse, Grok Bot, and Hermes are all EXCELLENT agents

They all have their own strengths and weaknesses, so you need to know which to use for each task

Here is each agent, and when you should be using them:

GROK BOT- best agent for heavy knowledge work

Strengths: Because you can create many different agents with many different contexts, skills, and memories, you are able to get a wide plethora of work done really really well

Weaknesses: Grok 4.7 is a great model, but not frontier. Also not much usage on cheaper plans.

Who it's for: People who have a diverse set of responsibilities and tasks they need to get done

META MUSE: best agent for getting personal tasks done online

Strengths: Lightning fast, free, and by far the best agent at navigating the internet. Can just 'figure it out' for getting tasks done in browsers

Weaknesses: Not great at coding. Model is lightning quick, but not the smartest or most creative. Weaker at knowledge work because of this.

Who it's for: The best 'personal assistant' agent. Booking reservations, finding flights, filling out forms, unsubscribing from websites. The more 'normie' type use cases. Also it's free. So anyone on a budget.

HERMES: Open source, fully customizable, do anything assitant

Strengths: Fully open source and customizable. Anything you want to change in the agent, you can just change it. Use any model or subscription. Does almost anything you ask without many guardrails. Also a smaller decentralized team supporting it, so it's always great to support the rebels

Weaknesses: No mobile app. Because it's open source and fully customizable, it's not always the most reliable if you tinker too much

Who it's for: tinkerers who want full control over their agent. Also great for the local model community and people with their own home AI labs. My Hermes maintains all my networks and equipment for me better than any other agent

DOT: Your ultimate AI agent project manager

Strengths: The smartest model in the best harness. You get Astra capabilities with best in class ChatGPT tools like Voice, Spaces, and Codex. Can manage all your Codex threads for you and see your projects to completion. Also has ALL of your ChatGPT memories out of the box, so no onboarding needed

Weaknesses: Feels rushed. Lots of rough edges at the moment. Slowest agent. Has trouble with computer and browser use more than you'd like. Tokens in the Dot chat are free, but can heavily burn tokens when managing Codex threads.

Who it's for: Builders who do a lot of coding. ChatGPT power users. Anyone who has long running tasks they'd like an agent to project manage for you

If you put the right agents on the right tasks, you'll have super powers. I use all 4 of these every single day, and switching between them is a breeze

They're all also EXCELLENT agents, so if you can only use one, using any of them is good enough. You can choose literally any of these 4 as daily drivers and you'll be way more productive than the average person

Just make sure you're USING them, and not just reading about them.

on launch day, a dev had Opus 5.5 one-shot a remake of Lander, the classic Acorn Archimedes 3D game by Elite creator David Braben. he saved the exact prompt and reference images, then ran them again 9 days later.

what he says got worse:

* rendering → props now snag and glitch as the camera moves
* physics → the ship no longer breaks apart on crash
* the menu → the intro controls screen is gone
* bullets → spawn at the back of the craft and clip through things
* camera → no more camera toggles

his setup:

→ same prompt, same reference images, a fresh workspace
→ Opus on Extra High effort both times
→ he says the gap is too big to blame on randomness

text:
CCIP 2.0 makes interoperability a lot less one-size-fits-all.

An asset issuer can use @Chainlink's standard CCIP security model AND add additional verification from:

• its own infrastructure
• another institution
• third-party CCVs

The important word is add. I emphasize this word because that's a common misconception I've seen thrown around the timeline.

A bank doesn't have to choose between Chainlink's security model and its own internal requirements. It can layer its requirements on top.

That's probably a much more realistic path to institutional interoperability than asking every institution to accept exactly the same security model.

我的油管第11期：《中美历史恩怨合订本——十大美好瞬间和十大交恶时刻》。

历史每天都很正确，就是不能看合订本。郭德纲老师说，凡事就怕同行衬托。别看宴会上你侬我侬唱你问，我爱你，有多深……你爱我有多深，得看合同签几分。

历史就这么诡异，当年要是乒乓球运动员科恩没上错大巴，老毛晚上安眠药剂量再大一点，基辛格表演肚子疼没成功……中美指不准啥时候才能建交，老百姓指不准啥时候才能看上电视、冰箱。

1979年大年初一，邓小平在飞往美国的专机上说：回头看这几十年，凡是和美国搞好关系的国家，都富起来了。

在肯尼迪中心，200名美国孩子用中文合唱《我爱北京天安门》……你看，美国早就让孩子唱中文歌接待中国元首了。邓小平竟然还跑上台去亲吻孩子，用洋范儿动作争取西方世界的接纳。你很难把这温馨一幕跟十年后下令广场开枪的屠夫联想起来。

卡特说“送10万人来！”邓小平马上给美国送去一大批留学生，其中就有王沪宁……

邓小平戴上女骑手献上的白色牛仔帽，向全场挥帽致意。临别时他对卡特说：“我们不怕美国的制度，美国也不必怕我们。”

但对美国制度骨子里的恐惧很快暴露，四年后中美交恶，因为19岁的网球女子运动员——胡娜出逃，寻求政治庇护。坊间狗血传说，邓小平怒斥里根，其中一条是拐骗了我的干女儿。

中美价值观迥异，现实需求却是刚需。里根放宽对华技术出口，承诺执行“一个中国”政策，中国再次掀起赴美浪潮。这一年，一位年轻的中国县委书记随农业考察团来到小城马斯卡廷。他衣着整洁、每次准时，很有好奇心，住进了当地一户农民家。他，就是习近平……

老布什在长城饭店举行答谢宴会，邀请了中国异见知识分子方励之夫妇，但方励之夫妇在路上被警察堵住了。“六四”发生，枪声和坦克履带声打碎了幻想……老布什带头全面制裁中国，中美关系再次降到冰点。

中美就像一场虐恋。克林顿称：只要中国经济发展了，民主就水到渠成。1997年，正式邀请江泽民访美，在夏威夷，老江愉快地弹起夏威夷吉他……蜜月又回来了。中美总是规律性的一会儿蜜月，一会儿交恶。

1998年6月，克林顿访华，在人民大会堂的全球记者会上，在中央电视台全程直播中，全国人民都看见了——克林顿公开表示：“六四事件中使用武力、造成人命损失是错误的”，他还力挺达赖……而江泽民竟然在央视全程直播中，跟美国总统碰撞六四、西藏、台湾这些极敏感的话题，这是中国元首史上唯一一次。

惊喜不惊喜，意外不意外。所以，当看到小白们因为这次会谈上唱了中国歌就激动不已，我这老登真想拍着您的肩膀说：年轻人，图漾图森破……

两天后，克林顿去北大与学生辩论自由和人权问题，央视竟然播出画面。克林顿引用胡适的话说：个人争取自由，也是在为国家争取自由。北大中文系女生马楠反驳……几年后她移民美国，嫁给美国人。

经历过那个时代的我，也被这段历史给惊呆了，中国元首竟然跟美国总统在央视直播辩论六四、西藏，人权。美国总统竟可以窜访北大……回首往事，恍若隔世。就请问：您怀不怀念那个时代，而那个时代，正是中美之间最好的时代。

结论是：一定要和美国搞好关系，和美国关系好的时候，就是中国最开放的时代。

🇪🇺NEW: Stablecoin giant Circle is PUSHING BACK on Europe's crypto rules.

The $74B USDC issuer says ONLY 3 of the world's 25 biggest stablecoins are regulated under MiCA, keeping the largest ones outside Europe's regulatory reach.

It wants the EU to replace the requirement that issuers hold 30% to 60% of reserves in bank deposits with a more flexible liquidity rule, siding with the European Central Bank.

Circle also wants to scrap limits that it says would force large issuers to spread reserves across dozens of banks.

The EU is expected to overhaul MiCA in 2027.

寓言般的画面是：马斯克，黄仁勋，库克，苏姿丰和她老公，与美国总统、中国元首坐一张桌吃饭。你能想像马云、马化腾、雷军、潘石屹跟习近平坐在一张桌上吃饭？

要啥自行车？让你活着就是皇恩浩荡。当年马云挥斥方遒跟马斯克对谈。五年后，马云消失，马斯克成了世界首富，马斯克问：马云在哪儿……

马斯克公开骂川普，还当世界首富，还是川普座上宾……任志强写了一封内部信，就判了十八年，生死不明……

据说一批中国企业家到了华盛顿，没等到通知，稍息、立正，就地解散，从“随行商界代表团”变成“自由行”，跟旅游团大妈打卡去了。而川普用空军一号拉着一群商人到北京吃国宴，又拉着他们在白宫吃国宴，中国商人跟元首一张桌吃饭？

这还叫社会主义吗，红旗还要不要打？美国商人跟总统吃饭时，中国商人正想着补税和外逃，想着从香港还是越南走更安全，后备厢够不够大，女朋友能不能装下……

制度DNA差异。商业立国，谁本事大谁上桌。领导立国，让谁上桌才能上桌，鱼头冲谁，霍金见着领导，渐冻症也得好了，站起来“我先干了，领导您随意”。

中国经济能不能好起来，你的生活能不能好起来，取决于中美关系能不能好起来。

text:
Ben Affleck (Hollywood star & Artists Equity CEO) talks about how he fine-tunes open video models by unfreezing weights and trained only the last cinematic layer so a film crew can hit real production standards.

for context, Ben Affleck founded InterPositive in 2022, a 16-person AI shop for film post and Netflix bought it in March 2026 for $587 mn in cash.

He needed that model because public video models were trained on his peers' films, and he did not think that was a real business. So InterPositive raised money, shot its own dataset for 8 months on a controlled stage, and used it only as late-stage training. 

Each new film then trains a private model on its own dailies, so the production keeps the footage and the learning. That is the product Netflix paid $587 million for.

----

quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

A little over 1 day into this, it’s vital to set the record straight:

The communication about this claim could’ve been way better and for that, I take full responsibility.

The allocation is now >41% claimed in a single day (fully unlocked, no vest), this tells us that even despite the thousands of pundits today, participants have been extremely receptive to the long term oriented mechanics of this program.

This was never publicly disclosed, as there’s been no point to it for over a year, but Kinetiq received a $20m term sheet at $250m ($0.25) last year prior to KNTQ genesis.

That sounds great on paper, until you realize that this would’ve essentially crushed the public economic value of the project, by creating ridiculously predatory vesting schedules that would’ve made Kinetiq (KNTQ) un-investable for years to come, which is the bane of the existence of essentially every other protocol in our singular category at the time.

This would’ve been an unacceptable outcome to us, hence swiftly declined. Proof? Ask @wassielawyer who was kind enough to personally review each term sheet.

Instead, we chose to follow through on the precedent Hyperliquid set by distributing 25% of the protocol after what was likely the shortest points program ever.

You may feel that your trust in Kinetiq and our team was misplaced, but we’ve followed through on everything we said we would, and will continue to do so - whether you’re here or not.

Regardless of how you felt about today, I (we) appreciate all of your commentary. The good, the bad, the ugly. 

The mission remains unchanged, and the vision ever more clear.

text:
🚨 O que eu fiz na situação da solana:dog1viwbb2vWDpER5FrJ4YFG6gq6XuyFohUe9TXN65u / @bitget esta semana — e um passo a passo para quem passar por algo parecido:

Após o incidente de segurança da Bitget, os saques foram suspensos.

No dia 25 de setembro, enquanto os saques ainda estavam indisponíveis, a Bitget anunciou que o par solana:dog1viwbb2vWDpER5FrJ4YFG6gq6XuyFohUe9TXN65u/USDT seria deslistado.

Ter fundos em uma CEX com os saques suspensos e, ao mesmo tempo, receber um anúncio de deslistagem obviamente não é uma situação confortável.

SEM PÂNICO. Foi isso que fizemos:

1️⃣ Verifiquei tudo por fontes oficiais
Conferi o anúncio da deslistagem, a suspensão dos saques e todas as atualizações posteriores diretamente na Bitget, em vez de confiar em posts ou rumores.
2️⃣ Abri tickets no suporte imediatamente
Perguntei especificamente sobre a solana:dog1viwbb2vWDpER5FrJ4YFG6gq6XuyFohUe9TXN65u em BTCRUNES, se os saques seriam reabertos e se os usuários teriam tempo suficiente para retirar seus fundos.

3️⃣ Guardei registro de tudo
Screenshots, e-mails, números dos tickets, respostas do suporte e anúncios oficiais foram todos salvos.
4️⃣ NÃO vendi em pânico
Alguns dias depois, a Bitget adiou a deslistagem da solana:dog1viwbb2vWDpER5FrJ4YFG6gq6XuyFohUe9TXN65u, manteve o trading spot ativo e confirmou que os saques seriam reabertos gradualmente.

5️⃣ Preparei a saída antes mesmo de os saques reabrirem
Verifiquei que a @krakenfx aceitava depósitos de solana:dog1viwbb2vWDpER5FrJ4YFG6gq6XuyFohUe9TXN65u via BTCRUNES e deixei preparado o endereço de depósito correto.
6️⃣ Quando os saques reabriram hoje, NÃO enviei tudo de uma vez
Primeiro, fiz um pequeno saque de teste da Bitget → Kraken.

Esperei a Bitget processar, localizei a transação no Bitcoin, aguardei as confirmações e só então confirmei que a solana:dog1viwbb2vWDpER5FrJ4YFG6gq6XuyFohUe9TXN65u realmente tinha chegado à minha conta na Kraken.
7️⃣ Só depois que toda a rota foi comprovada, retirei o restante
Essa transação também foi confirmada com sucesso e agora toda a minha solana:dog1viwbb2vWDpER5FrJ4YFG6gq6XuyFohUe9TXN65u está fora da @bitget e recebida na @krakenfx.

A maior lição é:
Quando alguma coisa dá errado em uma CEX, não deixe o medo tomar as decisões por você.

Verifique → documente → comunique-se → prepare-se → teste → confirme on-chain → só então execute.
Espero que essa experiência ajude outro holder a lidar com uma situação parecida com mais segurança.

🚨 What I did in the $DOG / @bitget situation this week & a playbook for anyone who faces sth similar:

Followin Bitget’s security incident, withdrawals were suspended
On Sept 25, while withdrawals were still unavailable, Bitget announced that $DOG/USDT would be delisted

Havin funds on a CEX while withdrawals r suspended & receivin a delistin announcement is obviously not a comfortable situation

NO panic, it’s what we did:

1️⃣ Verified everything through official sources
I checked the delistin announcement, withdrawal suspension & every subsequent update directly from Bitget rather than relyin on posts or rumors

2️⃣ Opened support tickets immediately
I specifically asked about $DOG on BTCRUNES, whether withdrawals would reopen & whether users would have enough time to withdraw

3️⃣ Kept records of everything
Screenshots, emails, ticket numbers, support responses & official announcements were saved

4️⃣ I did NOT panic sell
A few days later Bitget postponed the $DOG delistin, kept spot tradin active & confirmed that withdrawals would gradually reopen

5️⃣ Prepared the exit before withdrawals reopened
I verified that @krakenfx accepted $DOG deposits through BTCRUNES & prepared the correct deposit address

6️⃣ When withdrawals reopened today, I did NOT send everything
First, I sent a small test withdrawal from Bitget → Kraken

I waited for Bitget to process it, found the transaction on Bitcoin, waited for confirmations & then confirmed that the $DOG actually arrived in my Kraken account

7️⃣ Only after the entire route was proven did I withdraw the rest

That transaction also confirmed successfully & all my $DOG is now out of @bitget & received at @krakenfx 

The biggest lesson:

When things go wrong with a CEX, don’t let fear make the decisions

Verify → document → communicate → prepare → test → confirm on chain → then execute

Hopefully this experience helps another holder handle a similar situation safely

a16z 刚刚领投 Conway Research，创始人 Sigil Wen 只有 22 岁。因为有不少核心圈的钱，特地翻了下他的经历，感觉甚至投他可能和做什么都没关系。

他在多伦多长大，来自移民家庭，自学工程，没有走常规的大学路线。

17 岁，他从多伦多跑到旧金山，一度睡在 WeWork。按他自己的回忆，David Holz 给他看了正在训练的图像模型，把他拉进一个只有 20 人的 Discord。那个群后来变成了 Midjourney。

也是在这一年，Naval 带他参加了一场活动，他在那里认识了 a16z 的 Chris Dixon。

18 岁，他在一个 AI 创业者合租房住了 11 个月。按他本人和 a16z 的记载，Karpathy 也住在那里，周末一起做项目的人里，有参与开发 DALL·E、Whisper、GPT-3 和 Stable Diffusion 的研究员和工程师。Anthropic 联创 Ben Mann 还邀请他测试一个 Slack 机器人，后来成了 Claude。

在合租房生活期间，一个邮件应用的漏洞泄漏了他的私人邮件。这件事后来成了他做本地个人 AI 的动机之一。

19 岁，Naval 邀请他加入 Spearhead，成为当时最年轻的成员。这个项目给创业者一只 200 万美元的基金，让他们去投其他创业者。他披露的早期投资包括 Etched、Friend、Kerna Labs，还帮 Friend 招过核心技术工程师。

也是 19 岁，他把 GPT-2 的蒸馏版跑到了 Apple Watch 上。不是调用云端 API，而是模型真的在手表本地运行。

这一阶段，他也在跟 Naval 做 Airchat，开发 AI 功能、设计邀请机制、招聘工程团队。在这段合作中，他招来了大部分工程团队，还参与把 Whisper 搬到 iPhone 上。Naval 和 Airchat 也支持了他的 O-1 签证申请。

20 岁时，他已经办下 O-1，开始把自己花九个月申请签证的经历拍成教程，获得了几十万次观看。那件印着“Alien of Extraordinary Ability”的卫衣，也是他做的。他的 EB-1A 绿卡申请也在 20 岁获批。

找他帮忙的人越来越多。他先帮朋友，再组织申请人和已经获批的人交流，逐渐把这件事做成了一家公司。

21 岁，他已经在经营 Extraordinary，专门帮创业者和工程师申请 O-1、EB-1A 等签证和移民类别。他也以这家公司的创始人身份，入选了 Thiel Fellowship。

22 岁，他写《Web 4.0》，探索让 AI 自己赚钱、支付算力、参与经济活动，并通过 Conway Research 做模型、推理引擎和个人 AI 产品。

此时，帮人办签证也已经成了一门生意。按他自述，Extraordinary 做到了七位数美元营收并实现盈利，披露的服务对象包括 Cognition、Lovable、Ramp、a16z、Founders Fund 等。他把 CEO 的位置交给团队，自己转任执行董事长。

现在，Conway Research 推出了 Underdog，主打在用户自己的 Mac 上运行个人 AI。a16z 宣布领投。

a16z 的投资公告花了很大篇幅写他怎么帮人招聘、做产品、帮其他创业者融资，以及这些年对本地 AI 的尝试。他们既认同这个方向，也已经认识、观察了这个创始人好几年。

text:
When a technology project fails, the first mistake is often to argue about breach before protecting the system and the evidence.

Missed milestones, unstable releases, scope changes, acceptance disputes and unpaid invoices rarely form one simple problem. A rushed termination can make the facts harder to recover and create a second failure during migration.

A disciplined first response should:

1. Stabilise operations. Protect repositories, administrator credentials, cloud access, data, documentation and key personnel. Freeze avoidable changes and define an interim operating protocol.

2. Preserve the complete record. Keep the contract and notices, but also repository history, issue trackers, test results, release notes, incident reports and project communications. Preserve metadata.

3. Build a neutral chronology. Connect each milestone to the promised deliverable, agreed date, dependencies, changes, test outcome and the parties’ responses. Treat disputed facts as disputed.

4. Obtain focused technical input. Establish what was delivered, which defects are reproducible and what repair, completion or migration would require. Technical findings do not by themselves decide contractual responsibility.

5. Choose the process that fits the problem. Negotiation, mediation, expert determination and arbitration solve different kinds of disputes. Urgency, value, complexity and the remedy required should determine the route.

The same discipline applies across AI, digital platforms, crypto and blockchain, IP and licensing, startup and investor relationships, technology finance, service providers, users and enterprise customers.

Practical guide from A-Resolve:
https://t.co/fyE19nDcyT

General information only; not legal advice.

text:
30 年河东，30 年河西，这是人生。

一年河东，一年河西，这是币圈。

两年前爆火的 Blast，正式宣布关停。

记得2024 年主网上线时，Blast 桥上资金一度超过 23 亿美元。原生收益、Points、邀请制、空投预期，再叠加 Blur 创始人 Pacman 的光环，钱像疯了一样往里冲。

那时候甚至链都还没正式上线，用户就愿意先把 ETH 存进去锁几个月等积分。

两年后，Blast 宣布关停，L2赚的钱已经养不起这条链了。

高峰时期 Blast 单月手续费收入还有三百多万美元，到了 2026 年 9 月，整个月链上收入只剩大约 1800 美元。DeFi TVL 也从 22 亿美元级别掉到约 3200 万美元，跌了接近 99%。

积分停了、空投发了，刷分的人撤了，真正留下来用链的人根本撑不起一条 L2。

简单回顾一下 Blast 这三年：

2023 年 11 月，Blast 官宣。主网还没上线就开放存款，只能进不能出，靠 Points、邀请码和空投预期，几天吸进去约 3 亿美元。

Paradigm 当时甚至公开批评这种先锁钱再上线的玩法。

2024 年 2 月，主网上线，桥上资金超过 23 亿美元。

3 月 Munchables 内鬼一度卷走 6250 万美元，最后资金追回。

6 月 BLAST 正式空投，第一期发掉 17% 代币。也是从这里开始，资金慢慢撤退。

2024 年下半年到 2025 年，积分挖矿热度消失，用户、交易量、手续费、TVL 一路往下掉。曾经靠空投预期撑起来的繁荣，最终没能变成真实使用需求。

2026 年 10 月 2 日，Blast 宣布关停。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

quoted_text:
🚨 Polymarket Perps Volume Inflation

In under a day, two Polymarket accounts traded $206 MILLION… with each other, then got paid ~800K pUSD.

Extremely easy to find in public data because:

- Same funder.
- Trades 1 millisecond apart.
- Money comes from Polymarket's own fee wallet.

ALL THE INFO is from public on-chain data; link at the end. 
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📅 MAY 28: TWO ACCOUNTS, ONE FUNDER

One unknown wallet funds two brand-new Polymarket Perps accounts with 100,000 pUSD each.

🅰️ Account A, funded at 15:39 UTC
🅱️ Account B, funded 12:23 UTC

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Less than an hour after A is funded:

🕐 16:21:10.925: A sells B 22.336 OIL @ $88.823
🕐 16:21:10.926: A buys it right back. 

Same size. Same price.

⏱ - 1 millisecond apart
📍- Both accounts end up exactly where they started
📈 - Volume created: $3,967.90

It happened in 36 sequences, totaling $825,040.91 in trades that went… nowhere 🔁

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

From May 28 to 08:00 UTC on May 29:

🔄 64,816 trades between A and B
💵 $206,048,005.51 in volume

That's over 1,000x their combined starting money, all traded against each other.

What did it cost them? 🧾

Fees: 41,209.60 pUSD
Maker rebates back: 10,302.40 pUSD
➡️ Net: 30,907.20 pUSD

Remember that number. Then the payments start 👇

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💸 FOLLOW THE MONEY

So who paid them? Let's trace it back.

On June 5, money moves through four wallets in one day:

🏦 Polymarket's fee wallet (where exchange trading fees are collected)
⬇️ sends 979K
🎁 Polymarket's rebate wallet (pays rewards to traders)
⬇️ sends 757K
👛 A middle wallet that refills other wallets
⬇️ sends 700K
📤 The wallet that pays Perps traders
📅 The next day, that last wallet starts paying… A and B.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🎯 JUNE 6: GUESS WHO GETS PAID

The payout wallet credits… Account A and Account B.

71,027.97 pUSD in two payments.

And it keeps going:
📆 9 dates
🔁 17 credits
💰 698,844.64 pUSD by August 4

Every time, the upstream transfers come first. Then the pair gets credited.

🫥 Why nobody spotted it: the money flows into the Perps custody contract, which credits A and B internally.
❌ Wallet token-transfer tabs show nothing
✅ Custody deposit records name A and B as recipients
What the records don't name is the reason for the payments.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
From Aug 7 to Sep 25, the pair also receives 98,298.54 pUSD across 8 distributions as liquidity rewards.

Nothing unusual there. It just means these rewards alone more than cover the 30.9K pUSD the pair paid in fees.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Polymarket's Perps own rules say rewards are for real maker participation, order-book depth, and uptime. They also exclude trades between accounts in the same known rewards entity from maker-share calculations.

A and B had the same funder and traded against each other 64,816 times.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
📊 THE SCOREBOARD
💸 Net fees on their mutual trades (May 28–29): 30,907.20 pUSD
💰 Credited to them (Jun 6 to Sep 25): 797,143.18 pUSD
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

❓ TWO QUESTIONS HERE

1️⃣ What were the 698,844.64 pUSD in payments to A and B for?
2️⃣ How does your reward system treat accounts with shared funding that trade against each other?
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

author: hooeem
quoted_text:
I use Claude. GPT. Grok. Gemini. Hermes. Grokbot. Even Dot now.

they’re all useful for different things.

however, the annoying thing I find is that I get really comfortable with a model, then something new drops in the OpenAI eco that I want to try, but the last 3 months I’ve mostly been using Claude? 

FUCK. I’m back to square one.

well the way to fix this is with a harness.

What’s a harness? a harness is everything you build around your model which makes them become replaceable.

You do this by giving it context, memory, instructions, skills, tools, workflows so whenever you go from Claude to GPT, or GPT to Gemini, or Gemini to Grok you’re giving everything your brain (model) needs.

here’s how I’d make one:

1. download Obsidian

Create a vault called MY-AI.
This is the folder every AI will eventually work from.

2. create PROFILE. md

Tell it who you are, your goals, interests, preferences + how you like to work.
Only include information that actually helps an AI work with you.

3. create AGENTS. md

This is your rulebook.
Add how you want AI to research, reason, write + behave.
Tell it to read PROFILE. md, CURRENT. md + check /Skills before starting a task.

4. create CURRENT .md

Keep your current projects, priorities + open questions here.
Keep it short and update it often.

5. create /Skills

Every prompt/process you repeatedly use becomes a skill:
crypto-research. md
challenge-thesis. md
Write the steps once. Improve them over time. Reuse them everywhere.

6. create /Memory

Save important:
> research
> decisions
> lessons
> outcomes
Your agents can now learn from what you’ve already done instead of starting from zero.

7: create /Projects

Give every important project its own folder + a short README.md explaining the goal, status + next steps.

8: connect it

Open the MY-AI folder in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor etc.
They now work from the same context, rules, skills + memory.

9: back it up

Put MY-AI in a private Git repo.
Now your entire harness is portable + version controlled.

OKAY OKAY OKAY.

I’ll create a prompt for you so that you can make your own harness easily. Give me a bit of time and I’ll quote retweet this post with it.

quoted_text:
Hi, I’m Vibhor, Product Lead for Ecosystem at @OpenAI. I am going to use this space to share what we are doing to further the Ecosystem for our customers, and partners. DevDay feels like a good time to start.

One of the best parts of DevDay was the deep collaboration with partners: @Adobe, @Atlassian, @Canva, @Figma, @Instacart, @MagicPathAI, @Shopify, Superpower, and @tldraw.

While I went in excited I left with even more conviction in what we’re building together for our shared customers. It was also incredible to meet AI native partners and hear how our platform is empowering them build a sustainable business on ChatGPT 🎉

A conversation is often just the beginning of a task. You describe an idea, work through it, and eventually want something you can use: an edited image, a working prototype, a diagram you can keep refining. Getting there takes great tools and the people who know how to build them. Our ambition is to make those capabilities feel like a natural part of working with ChatGPT.

At DevDay, we shared several steps in that direction.

1. Plugin Extensions help our partners bring interactive experiences to ChatGPT. Adobe is a good example. You can ask for an image edit, then adjust the details with hands-on controls. With tldraw, you and the agent can work on a shared canvas. MagicPath brings interactive prototypes into the conversation, with room to edit them yourself.

These examples make the idea much more tangible:
- Adobe: https://t.co/6Enl2SDC7e
- tldraw: https://t.co/ogQLrZ09Lx
- MagicPath: https://t.co/0DEOfjniMQ
- Figma: https://t.co/MUh78VqCVp
- Shopify: https://t.co/OJUcqYma3V

2. A useful plugin can package skills, an MCP server, or both. That gives builders different ways to contribute: reusable workflow knowledge, access to live information, or actions that help someone finish a task. We introduced Plugin Creator and improvements to submissions, including automated checks and clearer feedback. Sites can also host supported plugins. There’s still work to do to make building and maintaining a plugin consistently straightforward.

3. We also announced improvements to plugin discovery, ranking and recommendations, in the directory and in conversations. This matters for both sides of the ecosystem. Users need to find something useful when they need it. Developers need a way for their work to reach those users. The goal is to make suggestions genuinely helpful, with good judgment about when they add value and when they get in the way.

4. MCP Events lets users ask ChatGPT to watch for supported events, such as a new message or a document comment, and respond when they arrive. It opens up another way for developers to make their tools useful beyond a single exchange.

5. ChatGPT Sites can now host MCP servers including plugin extensions! Create an MCP server with extensions, deploy the MCP server to Sites, turn the MCP server into a plugin, and install the plugin across platforms.

There’s still plenty to do, especially around reliability, discovery and the developer experience. Thank you to the teams and partners doing this work with us. The future feels bright, and we’re just getting started. Onward!

author: _0xKenny
quoted_text:
I reverse-engineered every buyable bottom on SPY. 

Here is what actually flagged them.

Instead of debating which indicator predicts bottoms, I worked backwards. I took 2 years of SPY daily data (501 trading days), found every pivot low that bounced 5% or more within 10 days (7 of them) and every pivot high that dropped 5% or more (3 of them), then measured what 13 technical studies were printing at each exact turning point versus ordinary days.

The winner surprised me.

Bollinger %B under 0.15 caught 86% of the buyable bottoms.

6 out of 7 bottoms printed %B below 0.15 at the pivot close. Zero of the tops did. Only 7% of ordinary days did. Quick refresher: %B measures where price sits inside the Bollinger Bands. 1.0 is the upper band, 0 is the lower band, below 0 means price closed under the lower band.

How the studies ranked (median at bottoms vs ordinary days):

•  MACD histogram: -2.80 vs +0.42 (catches everything, but noisy, 43% false positives)
•  Bollinger %B: 0.11 vs 0.67 (the clean trigger)
•  Stochastic %K: 16 vs 83
•  Stochastic %D: 21 vs 83
•  RSI(14): 39.6 vs 55.3

The RSI surprise: median RSI at real bottoms was 39.6, not 30. The classic "buy when RSI goes under 30" rule caught only 29% of actual bottoms. Waiting for deep oversold meant missing most of the bounces.

Three rules worth forward-testing:
1.  %B under 0.15 alone: 86% of bottoms, 7% false positive rate. Best single filter in the study.
2.  %B under 0.15 AND price under the 50-day average: keeps most bottoms, trims the noise further.
3.  RSI under 35 AND %B under 0.15: only caught 29% of bottoms, but zero false flags anywhere. Rare, high conviction when it fires.
Recent flags for reference: 
Jul 29 2026 (%B -0.16, then +6.1%), 
Jun 26 2026 (%B 0.14, then +5.0%), 
Mar 30 2026 (%B -0.02, then +7.6%).

The honest part, because small samples lie: 7 bottoms is thin, the window was mostly bull market, and tops had no clean signal at all. In September the flag tripped 4 times without a full 5% bounce following, so treat %B under 0.15 as "conditions are washed out," not "bottom confirmed." 

I am setting up automations to flag for these triggers live. When the next %B washout flags it will auto post in my slack. Was only able to pull for a couple years but would like to see a larger sample set

quoted_text:
Nightshades (@MeebitCompany & @ClutchMarkets) 
turns Uniswap v4 liquidity pools into the game board for an onchain faction war. Players choose between four factions by holding and trading their tokens and NFTs. During each Night, a random onchain result selects which factions survive and which are struck, along with the severity of the damage.

Before that result is generated, the hook closes public trading. This prevents anyone from seeing the outcome and trading ahead of its execution, while still allowing the protocol vault to carry out the game’s actions onchain.

Liquidity is removed from the struck factions and their tokens are sold. The released ETH, sale proceeds, and Night Booster Fund are then used to buy tokens from the surviving factions and strengthen their liquidity. Every action is visible through the pools and contract events.

At Sunrise, the hook reopens trading with a temporary anti-snipe tax that starts high and falls to zero over one hour. Using Uniswap v4’s beforeSwap and afterSwap return deltas, the hook adjusts buy inputs and sell outputs during settlement. Part of the tax funds the next Night, and part is reserved for faction liquidity.

The hook is not an accessory to the game. It is the game engine. It controls when the market can trade, enforces fair execution, settles the economic consequences of each result, and feeds activity from one Night into the next.

author: francescoswiss
quoted_text:
Coming up for air now after a very dense excellent week in Seoul at KBW, while staying on top of our response to a security event affecting part of our infrastructure. 

I can now respond to queries and speculation regarding what is impacted and what is not affected.

Based on our investigation to date, there is no indication that MetaMask wallets or customer funds in wallets have been affected. Your Secret Recovery Phrase, your keys, and the assets in your wallet were not part of this incident because they CANNOT be. You custody and control your own keys. That is how self custody works. You are fully in control of your own money in MetaMask.

Like many providers in our industry, we constantly face attempted attacks from a range of threat actors and periodically encounter security issues. Our approach follows established best practice: we do not publicly discuss the details of an open incident, but we disclose promptly to partners and relevant stakeholders once an issue is sufficiently understood. In this case, we shared the relevant details with partners, agreed and implemented a response strategy together, and then disclosed publicly.

As a precaution, we and our partners rotated validator keys. That step is operationally inconvenient which is regrettable as validators must exit the staking queue and then re-enter the queue to restake, which takes time. 

The validator staking architecture of Ethereum separates the key that proposes and attests from the key that can withdraw the stake. In accordance with the Ethereum principle of self-custody, we do not hold withdrawal keys for our clients. Because of that separation, an issue in the validator infrastructure CANNOT result in the improper movement of the underlying ETH. Rotating those keys was how we reduced residual operational risk.

Self-custody and user control are a central design principle guiding how we build -- in MetaMask, in staking and validation, and across Ethereum more broadly. Self custody plus rigorous decentralization represents a paradigm shift in security. Increasingly, the world is waking up to the benefits of this sounder architecture.

quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
Coming up for air now after a very dense excellent week in Seoul at KBW, while staying on top of our response to a security event affecting part of our infrastructure. 

I can now respond to queries and speculation regarding what is impacted and what is not affected.

Based on our investigation to date, there is no indication that MetaMask wallets or customer funds in wallets have been affected. Your Secret Recovery Phrase, your keys, and the assets in your wallet were not part of this incident because they CANNOT be. You custody and control your own keys. That is how self custody works. You are fully in control of your own money in MetaMask.

Like many providers in our industry, we constantly face attempted attacks from a range of threat actors and periodically encounter security issues. Our approach follows established best practice: we do not publicly discuss the details of an open incident, but we disclose promptly to partners and relevant stakeholders once an issue is sufficiently understood. In this case, we shared the relevant details with partners, agreed and implemented a response strategy together, and then disclosed publicly.

As a precaution, we and our partners rotated validator keys. That step is operationally inconvenient which is regrettable as validators must exit the staking queue and then re-enter the queue to restake, which takes time. 

The validator staking architecture of Ethereum separates the key that proposes and attests from the key that can withdraw the stake. In accordance with the Ethereum principle of self-custody, we do not hold withdrawal keys for our clients. Because of that separation, an issue in the validator infrastructure CANNOT result in the improper movement of the underlying ETH. Rotating those keys was how we reduced residual operational risk.

Self-custody and user control are a central design principle guiding how we build -- in MetaMask, in staking and validation, and across Ethereum more broadly. Self custody plus rigorous decentralization represents a paradigm shift in security. Increasingly, the world is waking up to the benefits of this sounder architecture.

text:
Karpathy大神又给我们播撒智慧了，放下手中的活，把这段仔细读读，以后让llm写文章就要求 ASD-STE100方式吧，以下是全文：

“
我们将花更多时间去理解语言模型的输出。以下是几点想法与技巧：

写作。 我实践中较为有效的一种做法是：请 LLM 用 ASD-STE100 解释某事。这是一种受控语言规范，最初为航空航天维修文档而制定。LLM 对此语言相当熟悉，它在清晰文风上施加了严格约束，我往往觉得这样的文本更易读。有时我会稍作放宽，例如要求“达到 ASD-STE100 的 80%”，因为该规范相当严苛。但还有更好的方式：

图表 / 图像。 与其写成文字，不如请 LLM 生成图表。这类形式往往更容易处理、解析和理解。但还有更好的方式：

网页。 要求以 “HTML” 形式输出，即可得到美观、可交互的网页。LLM 在前端方面已相当擅长，能够制作出色的体验与动画等。但还有更好的方式：

讲解视频。 我最为看好的输出形式，是针对任意主题生成完全定制、专属的讲解视频。可以尝试类似这样的提示：“制作一段 3b1b 风格的 X 主题讲解视频。使用我的 ElevenLabs API 密钥进行语音旁白。”（后者需要 API 密钥，也可请 LLM 为你寻找使用本地算力的合适免费替代方案。）这实际上已经开始奏效了。

总结：

随着 LLM 变得更强，它们将越来越多地自主完成具体工作，而我们的工作会更多地上升到更高抽象层，转向监督与理解。
幸运的是，LLM 在这方面也能提供帮助：随着智能与代码日益充裕，你可以要求生成大型、定制、用后即弃的软件产物（例如网页应用、讲解视频），而这类产物在以往并不值得专门制作。在这一方向上推进边界，结果往往会出乎意料。”
author: Zen_with_AI
quoted_text:
We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

In summary:
- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.
- Luckily, LLMs can help here too because as intelligence and code are increasingly abundant, you can ask for large, custom, discardable software artifacts (e.g. web apps, video explainers) that would have never made sense to create before. Push the boundaries here and you'll be surprised.
