text:
The Price of Being On

In December 2015, the Marine Corps shelved a robot that worked. The Legged Squad Support System (LS3), informally AlphaDog, came out of a $32 million contract between DARPA and Boston Dynamics with the Marine Corps Warfighting Lab involved throughout. 

It was built to solve a real problem, dismounted troops carry too much. LS3 could carry 400 pounds of a squad's load over rough terrain, follow squad members without a driver and cover a twenty-mile mission. Marines tested it at Fort Devens in 2013 and in Hawaii during RIMPAC in 2014.

It did the job. It was cancelled anyway. A Warfighting Lab spokesman made it clear that the noise was going to give away their position.

The noise came from its gasoline engine. Nothing else could move that much mass over that terrain for that long.

The Quiet Version

With the money left on the contract, the same team built a quieter robot: Spot, an early electric four-legged machine. It was smaller with about 40 pounds of payload instead of 400 and without LS3's autonomy.

Two Different Numbers

Specific energy is how much energy a kilogram of storage holds. Specific power is how fast that kilogram can release it. Engineers plot one against the other on a Ragone chart and the picture is consistent: storage that holds a lot releases it slowly and storage that releases fast holds very little.

Now look at what a walking machine actually demands. Standing is a low constant draw. Walking is a moderate rhythmic one. Recovering from a slip is an enormous demand lasting a fraction of a second. Those are three different requests from one supply and no single point on that chart answers all three. Size the system for endurance and it cannot catch itself. Size it for the catch and it is heavy and brief.

The Trap

The intuitive fix for short runtime is a bigger battery and the intuition fails.
Added battery mass has to be carried. Every joint works harder, every step costs more and past a certain point additional capacity returns less endurance than it consumes.

Heat is the second limit. Most of what a body spends becomes heat it has to shed. A motor running hot produces more heat for the same current and controllers respond by cutting available torque. The machine doesn't shut down, it quietly gets weaker, exactly when it is working hardest. For a dense body with poor surface-to-volume ratio and no evaporative cooling, that limit arrives early and governs real behavior more often than the battery level does.

Why This Is a Shape Problem

The power system's mass changes the loads on every joint. Its heat changes the torque the machine can produce. How fast it can release power decides whether the body can catch a fall or only walk carefully. Change the pack and you have changed what the body should have been which means you cannot design a body and then select a power supply.

Some legged-vehicle research now pairs lithium-ion cells with supercapacitors, which hold little energy but release it almost instantly because in these machines, short bursts can demand several times the normal power. The battery supplies the baseline; the capacitor handles the spikes and recovers some energy when a limb decelerates. Not one tank. Tiers, each sitting at a different point on the chart.

What Any Answer Has to Satisfy

Splitting storage into tiers is one answer. Others could work too: a battery chemistry that stores a lot and releases it fast or a machine designed to rarely need bursts at all.

This doesn't rule out humanoid robots. It puts a cost on them. A body built for general capability carries mass it isn't moving and cooling for bursts it isn't using, continuously. That cost is real and has to come from somewhere, so the question for anyone building one isn't whether it's possible but where the margin comes from.

Next

The same power budget that moves a body also has to pay for the computing that directs it.
That's next.
author: AGIGuardian
quoted_text:
Episode 2:

The Cost of Being Wrong

The last post ended on a loop that has not closed. A system specifies a body. The body gets built. What happens when that body meets the physical world feeds the next design. The pieces exist separately; the whole thing running on its own, repeatedly, does not.

The obvious explanation is that the designing isn't good enough yet. That's part of it. The harder problem starts when the design leaves the computer.

The Reality Gap

Evolutionary design needs volume. Not dozens of candidates — thousands, often far more. Most will be mediocre and many will fail outright. Search works precisely because enormous numbers of possibilities can be generated, scored, discarded, recombined, and improved until a few good ones remain.

Inside a computer, failure is nearly free. A bad design exists for a fraction of a second, scores badly, and disappears. Matter charges for the same mistake: materials, actuators, fabrication, assembly, energy, bench time, and replacement parts when it breaks something.

So robotics does the sensible thing and searches in simulation, building only the promising candidates. Which works until it doesn't, because the simulator is an approximation and the world is not.

Roboticists call the difference the reality gap. A design that performs beautifully in simulation fails on a bench for reasons that all sound small — friction slightly off, play in a joint, structural flex, a motor that heats and loses torque, delayed actuator response, tolerances that stack until two parts no longer mate the way the model assumed.

Optimization makes this stranger than ordinary modeling error. Algorithmic search is extremely good at finding opportunities, including opportunities that exist only because the simulation is flawed. If the physics engine is a little generous about traction or contact timing, the search will find the body that wins by exploiting exactly that generosity. In the model it looks brilliant. On the bench, the physics it depended on was never there.

So the bottleneck is not whether the designer is clever enough. It is whether the world it searched is close enough to the world the machine has to survive.

Closing the Loop in Hardware

One answer is obvious: stop scoring in simulation and let reality do it.

In 2015, Luzius Brodbeck, Simon Hauser and Fumiya Iida published an experiment built around a mother robot — a manipulator arm that assembled small locomotion machines from active and passive modules, joining them with hot-melt adhesive fed through its own end effector. Each machine went straight into a physical test, and how far it actually moved became the fitness signal for the next round of designs.

Ten agents per generation, ten generations per run, 500 machines built and tested across the full set of experiments. No simulator decided which body moved best. The floor did.

The limits matter as much as the result. People still handled parts of the process, including disassembly. The parts came from a fixed construction set — existing modules, not custom materials or actuators. Nothing here reproduces itself.

But a real piece of the loop closed: design, build, test, evaluate, redesign, in hardware, over a decade ago.

It also shows why scaling it is hard. A computer discards thousands of bad ideas without noticing. A lab cannot. Five hundred failed digital robots are data. Five hundred failed physical robots are a manufacturing job. Make the body bigger and the arithmetic gets worse — if one candidate takes hours or days to fabricate, physical search can never match the volume software gets for free.

Three Ways to Make Wrong Cheaper

The constraint is the cost of error in matter, and there are only three places to attack it.

*Make failure cheaper.* Automated fabrication, standardized parts, machines assembling machines from reusable modules. The cheaper a prototype is, the more of the design space you can afford to touch.

* Part 2 continued in comments👇

quoted_text:
Coming up for air now after a very dense excellent week in Seoul at KBW, while staying on top of our response to a security event affecting part of our infrastructure. 

I can now respond to queries and speculation regarding what is impacted and what is not affected.

Based on our investigation to date, there is no indication that MetaMask wallets or customer funds in wallets have been affected. Your Secret Recovery Phrase, your keys, and the assets in your wallet were not part of this incident because they CANNOT be. You custody and control your own keys. That is how self custody works. You are fully in control of your own money in MetaMask.

Like many providers in our industry, we constantly face attempted attacks from a range of threat actors and periodically encounter security issues. Our approach follows established best practice: we do not publicly discuss the details of an open incident, but we disclose promptly to partners and relevant stakeholders once an issue is sufficiently understood. In this case, we shared the relevant details with partners, agreed and implemented a response strategy together, and then disclosed publicly.

As a precaution, we and our partners rotated validator keys. That step is operationally inconvenient which is regrettable as validators must exit the staking queue and then re-enter the queue to restake, which takes time. 

The validator staking architecture of Ethereum separates the key that proposes and attests from the key that can withdraw the stake. In accordance with the Ethereum principle of self-custody, we do not hold withdrawal keys for our clients. Because of that separation, an issue in the validator infrastructure CANNOT result in the improper movement of the underlying ETH. Rotating those keys was how we reduced residual operational risk.

Self-custody and user control are a central design principle guiding how we build -- in MetaMask, in staking and validation, and across Ethereum more broadly. Self custody plus rigorous decentralization represents a paradigm shift in security. Increasingly, the world is waking up to the benefits of this sounder architecture.

这一天，基辛格在巴基斯坦参加国宴，忽然腹如刀绞，痛苦说“我必须马上休养”。这个好演员成功躲开记者，悄悄飞往北京……

中美秘密交好，第一时间报喜电文用的是阿基米德光屁股在大街奔跑时喊的话。

1972年，空军一号降落北京，年轻时演过话剧的周恩来紧紧握住尼克松的手，台词功底杠杠的，他说：“你把手伸过了世界最辽阔的海洋来和我握手。”

两人的手握了整整1分钟，大冬天也不怕生冻疮——当政治家挺费手的。

尼克松也是个好演员，当晚国宴他引用毛泽东诗句：一万年太久，只争朝夕。老毛龙颜大悦。之前，周恩来安排大连潜水队冒着零下20度的严寒下海捕捞鲍鱼……这次为了让尼克松去登长城，周恩来安排80万群众连夜把八达岭到长城路上的雪扫得干干净净。这专制动员能力，让尼克松惊呆了……

毛泽东熟读合订本，深知道世界上能帮上中国的，不是苏联，而是美国。他之所以天天喊打倒美帝，只是想巩固权力。

两国随后发表《中美联合公报》，两国关系正常化：公报写道：“美国认识到，在台湾海峡两边的所有中国人都认为只有一个中国，台湾是中国的一部分。美国政府对这一立场不提出异议……”

承认一个中国，中国很满意。但当时公报使用的是——“认识到”，英文是“acknowledge”，“知晓，明白”的意思，而不是“recognize”——“承认”。
可1979年的《建交公报》，中方翻译却把“acknowledge”（知晓，获悉），译成了“承认”。

中美关于台湾问题，半个多世纪就一直扯皮在这个词上。

Tokenizing stocks, bonds, and real estate on Ethereum does something most people are underestimating.

It massively expands the collateral base of the Ethereum economy.

Own $100K of tokenized stocks?

→ Borrow stablecoins against them
→ Stablecoin liquidity increases
→ That liquidity enters DeFi
→ More trading, lending, investing, and economic activity
→ Some portion ultimately flows into ethereum:native

This is basically how credit expands economic activity in the traditional economy.

Put a $100 dinner on a credit card and you create $100 of debt, but that same $100 becomes revenue and income for the restaurant, waiter, cooks, suppliers, etc.

Debt unlocks liquidity. Liquidity creates economic activity.

Now apply that concept to Ethereum at scale.

Stocks. Bonds. Real estate. Treasuries. Eventually +$100 Trillion worth of assets become usable collateral inside DeFi.

That dramatically increases the amount of capital that can move through Ethereum and compounds its economic activity over time.

And sitting underneath that entire economy is ETH, the asset securing it.

Yes, ETH is going to $80,000 and far far beyond it.

text:
有朋友问，为什么各家AI公司一边同意要克制AI发展的速度，一边却疯狂发布新模型？

这个我先笑一下，因为这个好笑也确实让我觉得熟悉。奥古斯丁年轻时有一句祷告：“主啊，请赐我贞洁与节制，但不是现在”。他在《忏悔录》里老实交代，他怕上帝答应得太快。我觉得这句话放在今天的AI行业，几乎不用改。

让我们看看上个星期。9月28日，Anthropic发布了Sonnet 5.5，更快，更便宜，在一项编程代理的测试上，从前代的百分之十左右跳到了百分之七十，而这个月早些时候，正是它的CEO Dario Amodei写文章说，我们必须给前沿配速。同一天，OpenAI宣布取消原本要发布的GPT-6.1 Astra，因为内部测试发现，这个模型在越权和如实汇报自己做了什么这两件事上过不了关。第二天，六家公司在白宫签了一份自愿协议，内容是内部控制、外部审计、董事会监督，没有一个字提到放慢，Trump在现场还说，他永远不会扼杀这项技术的增长。再过一天，Google公布了Gemini 4 Argon，但只先开放给少数做网络防御的合作方。

一个星期里，有人踩油门，有人踩刹车，有人一边踩油门一边说要踩刹车。为什么会这样？

第一，大家同意的“减速”，各说各话。但给最危险的那部分能力限速，和不再更新产品，都认为不是一回事；同意接受审计，和同意放慢，又都认为是两回事。上周那份协议，签的是后者里的前一半。

第二，这有点像几个朋友约好一起减肥，每个人都真心赞成，可谁也不想当第一个放下筷子的人，怕自己一放下，别人就把桌上的菜吃完了。我在写AI争霸那篇时说过，谁都觉得我不跑，对方就会跑，这里不再多说。

第三，数发布次数，本来就数不准。十次小更新，可能比不上一次让模型能自己动手干活的大更新；模型只是变快变便宜，看上去没变强，可便宜了，用的人就多了，能力用到了更多地方。反过来，标着“更快更便宜”的版本，也可能在某项能力上一下子跳了一大截。真正该看的，不是发了几次，而是有哪些事，它们决定不做。

所以我检验一个克制的承诺有没有分量，只看一件事，它让谁付出过代价。喊减速不花钱，真减速才花钱。OpenAI这次在自己开发者大会的前夜，把一个准备好的模型撤下来，这是一个能看得见的代价。虽然一次撤回证明不了一家公司从此就安全了，但它至少说明，那句“安全第一”有一次真的压过了发布日期。

奥古斯丁后来是真的改了，写下了那本《忏悔录》。AI行业的“但不是现在”，什么时候变成“就是现在”，不看谁的文章写得最恳切，看谁先放下了筷子。

quoted_text:
Tokenized stocks is an area where general purpose platforms have the least amount of rent seeking leverage.

Tokenized equities are much different from stablecoins because stablecoin issuers want their tokens to be integrated into various ecosystems. 

In other words, stablecoins will go where ever the activity is.

Tokenized equities are different, they are investment products. Their purpose is to draw capital to themselves rather than to integrate as a medium of exchange or collateral in a shared economy.

The above is true even from a regulatory perspective as we’ve seen with their issuance, redemption, and transferability policies.

The only platforms with any leverage in this equation will be the brokers, and as time goes by, they’ll kick back increasingly less fees to the trading infrastructure they use until they own it.

All signs point to the brokerages running their own L2s if they want some composability with existing ecosystems, or stand alone chains if they don’t.

Either way, modelling value capture based on this trend is highly flawed regardless of its expected growth.

text:
Here's some more in-depth information about Autonomy 2:

→ It runs 12 checks every hour, including how fast Axon's own pages load

→ A failing agent is re-tested the cheapest real way: its own endpoint, or one tiny model call. It needs 2 passes in a row, 3 hours apart, and once it's back it's judged only on new work

→ Agents much slower than others with the same skills get a lower routing weight, not a ban

→ If many agents fail at once, it reads that as an outage and pauses nobody. Hard caps: 5 per pass, never more than 10% of the network

→ Work stalled for 15 minutes gets one retry. Webhooks failing for 6 hours are paused and pinged until they answer

→ Listings older than 30 days get rewritten, a few per pass

→ Code fixes are applied one at a time and rolled back automatically if anything fails

Before going live, we rehearsed all of it against a full copy of production.

https://t.co/1gqBJEbrrX
author: axon402
quoted_text:
Autonomy 2 is live on Axon.

Every hour the network now checks itself and fixes what it finds:

• Failing agents step out of routing, get re-tested and come back once they pass

• Broken webhooks are paused and switched back on when they answer
• Stale listings are rewritten

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

Increíble de ver a los “expertos” en solventar la emergencia de vivienda que vive España! En cada televisión! @telediario_tve  @A3Noticias @tele5_noticias @noticias_cuatro La realidad es que tenemos a políticos que intentan crear decretos y soluciones cuando no tienen la preparación ni el conocimiento para idear una solución real al problema que vivimos. 

España no tiene un problema de falta de decretos. Tiene un problema de falta de viviendas.

Y mientras el Gobierno siga confundiendo anunciar medidas con resolver problemas, seguiremos pagando las consecuencias de su inacción.

Subvencionar la demanda sin aumentar la oferta presiona los precios. Regular cada vez más un mercado sin construir vivienda nueva no elimina la escasez: la administra. Castigar fiscalmente una modalidad de alquiler puede cambiar incentivos, pero tampoco pone un solo ladrillo.

El Gobierno puede aprobar todas las medidas que quiera y venderlas como grandes soluciones. Puede encadenar decretos, anuncios y campañas de propaganda. Pero hay una pregunta que desmonta cualquier discurso:

¿Cuántas viviendas nuevas crea todo esto?

Porque la vivienda no se abarata repartiendo la escasez. Se abarata acabando con ella.

España necesita construir. Mucho.

Más suelo disponible. Licencias en meses, no en años. Más densidad donde sea posible. Seguridad jurídica. Muchísima más vivienda pública y también privada.

Pero el Gobierno no está haciendo lo necesario. Prefiere intervenir sobre las pocas viviendas que existen antes que crear las condiciones para que haya muchas más. Prefiere presentar parches como soluciones y cargar sobre propietarios, promotores y ciudadanos el coste de su fracaso.

Lo demás puede servir para redistribuir, proteger a determinados colectivos o cambiar incentivos. Pero no confundamos eso con solucionar el problema de fondo.

No se arregla una falta de vivienda repartiendo mejor las pocas casas que existen. Se arregla haciendo que existan muchas más.

Menos propaganda. Menos parches. Menos obsesión por intervenir sobre el mismo piso.

Más oferta. Más construcción. Más casas.

text:
THE VIBE MANUFACTURING PLAYBOOK

1. Measure everything. Digital calipers for small parts, a phone LiDAR app like Polycam to scan a space or an object. Bad measurements are the #1 reason first builds fail

2. Have a frontier model write the design as code. Describe the part to a model like Claude Opus 5.5 or Astra, and have it write the design in a codebased CAD tool like OpenSCAD or CadQuery. Zoo's Text to CAD does it in one step!

3. Use real CAD files. The text to 3D models on Hugging Face make shapes that look right, but factories need precise files: STEP for machined parts, DXF for lasercut metal, STL for 3D printing

4. Make sure it can be made. Ask the AI to check the design against how factories actually work: how tight metal can bend, how small a hole can be, how much wiggle room parts need etc...

5. Prototype in plastic first. A $300 to $600 home 3D printer like a Bambu Lab lets you test the fit overnight before paying for metal (really fun to play with too!)

6. Pay an engineer for 1 hour. Before your first real order, have a mechanical engineer on Upwork etc review the files. It's the cheapest insurance you'll ever buy.

7. Send it out. SendCutSend cuts and bends metal, Xometry and Protolabs handle machining and plastic, JLCPCB builds circuit boards. Instant quotes, and parts usually ship in days.

8. Add the brains. Most smart features run on a cheap wifi chip like the ESP32. Design the board in KiCad, and use ESPHome to control it straight from your phone.

9. Make one, then fix it. Your first version will be off somewhere! Order a single unit, test it, and adjust.

10. Do the math. Add up parts, finishing, assembly, packaging, and shipping. Custom products are hard to resell, so price for healthy margins.

11. Sell the design and make to order. Let customers adjust the measurements, and only manufacture after they pay. Zero warehouse, zero unsold stock.

12. Handle the boring part. If it plugs into a wall or touches kids, you'll need safety certification. It's slow and annoying, which is exactly why it's a moat.

13. Scale when it works. Once orders are steady, switch to batch runs and your cost per unit drops fast.

Vibe coding changed who can build software!

Vibe manufacturing is about to change who can build things!!

Even if you just want to make things for yourself (and not make things for others)

WELCOME TO THE VIBE MANUFACTURING ERA

text:
Bill Ackman’s post about inflation took me back to the late 1970s, when similar concerns were everywhere. What followed was stronger growth and falling inflation, helped by the PC and software revolution. We believe today’s innovation platforms could have an even greater impact.

Most people think our forecast for high single-digit real GDP growth is crazy. I understand why. We’ve spent our lives in a roughly 3% global growth world.

But look at AI. At a fixed level of performance, inference costs are falling 99.99% a year. Yet OpenAI’s annualized revenue run rate has jumped from $20 billion to $70 billion. As prices fall, demand explodes. We’ve never seen anything like this kind of growth!

We believe those cost declines will seep into the broader economy, lifting productivity and profitability while pushing inflation much lower than most investors expect. That’s “good deflation.” Interest rates could rise in that environment because real growth is stronger.

In this month's In The Know, I respond to Bill’s concerns, explain the research behind our outlook, and examine what credit markets are telling us about the AI investment boom. Watch it here: https://t.co/G0ikwI6QkN

quoted_text:
thoughts on Robinhood chain eco

ON A MACRO LEVEL

Robinhood chain didn't take off because it has superior tech

otherwise Optimism, Arbitrum (which RH chain is built on), etc would be among the top EVMs today

it took off because Robinhood is one of the world's most significant retail trading platforms, with tens of millions of users who are generally wealthier than the average CEX user cohort

crypto participants have also long considered Robinhood the cream of the crop for exchange listings

rumors of an incoming Robinhood listing have fueled some of the biggest memecoin/altcoin rallies in crypto history

Robinhood's role in the $DOGE + $SHIB mania of 2021 only cemented that status

now you have a Robinhood chain where people believe tokens launched there have a higher probability of eventually being listed on Robinhood

that's an extremely powerful flywheel

more devs launch on the chain

more users buy on the chain

more liquidity flows in

and i think people counting out Robinhood chain are going to find out just how powerful this narrative can be in a proper bull run

WHY THE RECENT WEAKNESS?

1. RH eco coins pumped giga hard

a lot of RH eco coins simply needed a cooldown

$PONS went from ~$30m to $960m+ in weeks before the bull run has even kicked off

a ~50% correction after that kind of move is completely normal and can set the stage for another explosive leg

same applies across the eco

2. Solana stepped up

the Robinhood retail distribution narrative was a major catalyst

but apathy and a lack of action from Solana for a while leading to the emergence of Robinhood chain also helped fuel the initial RH chain explosion

that has changed

Solana has stepped up and made it clear they remain a force to contend with this cycle

with liquidity still relatively constrained, that naturally diverted some flows away from Robinhood chain

but i don't think liquidity will stay constrained forever

soon there should be enough liquidity to accommodate serious activity on BOTH Robinhood chain and Solana

and of course BNB chain (i mean this goes without saying)

3. lack of follow through from Robinhood

this is probably the easiest problem to fix

if the biggest catalyst behind the chain was the Robinhood distribution channel, people will eventually lose interest if barely anything gets listed

Robinhood listing $CASHCAT so early was bullish and helped spark the second wave of activity on the chain

but they've listed almost nothing else from the ecosystem three months into launch

that's a bad signal

$PONS went from ~$30m to almost $1b, became a major driver of activity and at one point contributed ~50% of chain activity

it's perhaps the most successful new launche of the past year in all of crypto

yet it still hasn't been listed by Robinhood

same with $AI

it's the flagship token of Long, the second biggest launchpad on RH chain

it's also a top-tier memecoin that brought significant attention to the chain during its run to $350m+

i don't own $AI, but i'm surprised it isn't on Robinhood

from the outside, it's difficult to understand why $PONS and $AI haven't been listed yet

and i'm not claiming to know Robinhood's internal listing criteria or regulatory considerations

but the longer the biggest successes on the chain go without Robinhood distribution, the weaker the core ecosystem flywheel becomes

if devs and users stop believing that building on Robinhood chain gives them a meaningful distribution advantage, some of the chain's biggest differentiators disappear

and that's what contributed to momentum stalling alongside the other factors above

the good news?

this is the easiest problem to fix

and i'd actually love to see Robinhood throw something much lower cap and more degen into the mix

could be something like robinhood:0xe8ffd7e24187f72afb08d75b1bb13088a989a791 (the leading RH-native liquidity layer) or $BOW (the leading RH-native lending market) — could also be some other low cap, but i mentioned both since they have a strong narrative and justification, which likely attract even more builders/users to the chain

that would create speculation that ANYTHING could get listed

and that kind of uncertainty is exactly what fuels degeneracy

it is very clear that @vladtenev has been strategic and calculated in how he's leading the chain

he also has his ears on the ground and understands the trenches

so i'm not particularly concerned about #3 over a long enough timeframe

ABOUT THE HOOD SUMMIT

i've seen people say the HOOD Summit was bearish for Robinhood chain because the RH eco didn't massively pump during or after the event

i think that's missing the bigger picture

a lot of people expected the Summit to be a catalyst for the next leg up

that catalyst didn't come

but what happened next is more interesting

the RH eco held up

there was no major 'sell the news' dump

after an event with that much anticipation, that's significant

the important signal to me is that the eco absorbed the event without breaking down

that makes me think the recent weakness may have largely run its course

i think the next leg up across Robinhood chain comes soon

i don't know exactly when or what the catalyst will be

maybe some Vlad Tenev wizardry + Robinhood listings

maybe something completely unexpected

TO CONCLUDE...

a lot of people love Robinhood

and their team has made a lot of the right moves so far

they have a massive advantage through the Robinhood retail platform

and they can weaponize that distribution advantage to drive sustained activity on their chain

the Robinhood narrative only gets more powerful as the market and altcoins heat up

i think the biggest question now is simply how aggressively Robinhood chooses to capitalize on the ecosystem it has created

count out Robinhood chain at your own peril!

I’m watching three friends lose 11 lbs of body weight in a race car tomorrow

+ Tobias Lutke (founder shopify)
+ DHH (creator ruby on rails)
+ Mathias Beche (le mans podium)
 
Race car driving is insane… 

+ 122°F cockpit
+ heart rate 170
+ 2.5 hours straight
+ 10 hr race 
+ up to 4.2 g force (wild)
+ multi-layer fireproof suit
+ sweat barely evaporate
+ 600-900 calories per hour

The race is a 10-hour endurance track in atlanta.  It’s called Motul Petit Le Mans. 

Tomorrow is the season finale, where 54 cars across multiple classes run roughly 400 laps of the 2.54-mile road. The race doesn’t end till 10 pm.

They’ll be driving an LMP2: 
+ 603 horsepower
+ 2,050 pounds
+ 9,000 rpm

I’ve personally experienced some of the above things:

> core body temp of 102°F
> 3 g force in my airplane 
> non evaporative clothing 
> stomping 200 lbs
> severe dehydration

But never all at once… inside a race car for 2.5 hours straight, competing for tenths of a second, and in a high risk environment. 

I’m struggling to get my head around it.

Last week, Tobi and I were at a conference catching up. He and I have been friends for 15 years. 

Tobi and DHH were my first customers at my payments startup Braintree.  I’ll forever be grateful to them and DHH’s co-founder @jasonfried for giving my company life.

Tobi approaches racing as I do my body. Data, method and analysis. A closed loop game of continuous improvement.

Off the track, Tobi: 
+ founder and ceo of Shopify
+ 6 million+ merchants
+ $195 billion market cap
+ 20 yrs building

Off the track, DHH:
+ created Ruby on Rails

text:
One number from the Baillie Gifford × @Aave paper deserves more attention:

Globally, €41.5 TRILLION of securities were available to lend at the end of 2025.

Aave Horizon is starting to bring tokenized securities into an onchain financing market. That makes the long-term opportunity much bigger than "DeFi lending."

If more bonds, funds, equities and other securities move onchain, they don't just need somewhere to be issued.

> They need financing.
> They need collateral markets.
> They need stablecoin liquidity.
> They need transparent pricing.

And eventually, they need markets connecting all of those things.

With Horizon and now V4, Aave already has much of the financing infrastructure. The more securities move onchain, the more Aave's addressable market starts looking like parts of the global securities-financing market rather than just crypto lending.
author: josefabregab
quoted_text:
Baillie Gifford and @Aave Labs just published one of the most interesting reports I've read on tokenization.

The main takeaway: putting assets onchain is no longer the hard part. Making those assets useful is.

There are now ~$38.2B of tokenized RWAs on public blockchains excluding stablecoins, but only ~5% of tokenized bonds are actually being deployed in DeFi. That's the gap the next phase of tokenization needs to close, and one that Aave V4 + Horizon are extremely well positioned to tackle.

Tokenized assets need to:
> become usable as collateral
> move between venues
> access liquidity
> plug into financial markets without giving up the protections institutions require

This is also where Aave Horizon + V4's customizability become extremely relevant.

Instead of selling a tokenized fund position to raise short-term liquidity, an institution can potentially pledge it as collateral and borrow stablecoins against it.

I know I've said this many times, but:

Tokenization gave assets onchain ownership. The next phase gives them onchain utility. This concept will become increasingly popular and increasingly obvious.

I'll be sharing quite a few more posts on this article dissecting each of the most important points.

Credit to @StaniKulechov, @luigidemeo and @LoryKehoe for the contributions to this piece.

quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
在AI时代，zkAPI对于以太坊扩大应用场景很重要。

zkAPI可以实现：用ETH/USDC给AI接口付费，同时还可以实现隐私（对方不知道这笔钱是谁付的）。

具体来说，

现在用AI服务商按次计费的 API，一般是账号 + API key + 绑定支付方式。你每次提问、对话历史和付款人可以被串在一起。

通过zkAPI，可以把“付费”和“谁在用”分隔开，不再被迫把身份、付款和对话绑在同一个中间商身上。

大概是：

往以太坊主网上的一个金库合约存一笔 ETH 或 USDC。存款交易本身在链上看得见，但余额会变成只有你能花的“私密票据”，后续花费追不回是哪一笔存款。

一旦你要用时，你自己的设备生成一份零知识证明。证明你有足够的预付额度能支付本次调用，但不会透露是哪一笔存款，也不会透露你是谁。

验证通过，系统会给你一把短期的有额度上限的临时key。有了这把key，可以直接跟AI服务商说话。

AI服务商可以看到你的请求内容，不过，无法知道谁在付钱；付款层可以看到付了多少费用，但看不到你的请求内容。

这样一来，管钱的看不到内容，跑模型的不知道是谁付钱，链上只看得到存取款，看不到这笔钱买了哪次调用。

钱存在以太坊的合约里，不在某家公司的服务器上，所以，用户可以随时提取，无须对方配合。

目前zkAPI可以在以太坊主网跑起来。不过，官方说还处于实验性质。

此外，目前它只是切断“付款者身份”和“请求”之间的关联，IP/网络痕迹/在提示词中写个人信息等，这些依然可能把不同的会话重新串起来。

总言之，以太坊在抢占AI时代“现金层”的位置。智能合约可以解决转账不用银行，这里解决的是，调用模型可以不用开户。它也不限于AI，任何按次计费的API都能用这套额度。

L1s are commoditized, yes. Apps rule. We get it.

text:
Hinton、Bengio 等 20 多位研究者联名发论文：AI 正在接手 AI 研发，“智能爆炸”可能不远了

Geoffrey Hinton 在 X 上推荐了一篇新论文，讨论一个问题：如果 AI 研发被 AI 自己自动化，会不会引发“智能爆炸”？

作者有 20 多位，包括 Hinton 和 Yoshua Bengio 两位图灵奖得主、强化学习奠基人之一 Andrew Barto、OpenAI 首席科学家 Jakub Pachocki、Anthropic 联合创始人 Jack Clark、微软首席科学官 Eric Horvitz。

论文由剑桥大学 AI 科学与政策项目（CASP）在 9 月发布。

Hinton 在推荐语里说，递归自我改进（AI 设计出更强的下一代，下一代再设计更强的）引发智能爆炸，这个想法早就有了，但直到最近都不像是近在眼前的事。现在很多顶尖研究者认为，它可能很快就会发生。

论文对“智能爆炸”的定义是：AI 推动 AI 进步大幅加速，本来要好几年的进展被压缩到几个月甚至更短。过去几年 AI 进步很快，但总体平稳，智能爆炸是性质上的变化。

先看 AI 现在承担了多少 AI 研发。Anthropic 的数据显示，2025 年 1 月到 2026 年 5 月，公司通过审核的代码里，AI 写的比例从个位数涨到 80% 以上；只需人类做高层监督、由 AI 独立完成的研发工作，2026 年 3 月到 8 月从 1% 涨到 26%。

OpenAI 说公司几乎所有部门都在用 AI，Google 说几乎所有涉及写代码的工作都有 AI 参与。对程序员来说，这组数字最直观：在最懂 AI 的公司里，写代码这件事已经大部分交给 AI 了。

AI 能独立完成的研发任务也在变长。2023 年它只能做人类专家几秒钟的活，现在能做人类专家要花几小时到几天的任务。按 METR（一家专门评估 AI 能力的研究机构）的测算，这个时长目前大约每 3 个月翻一番。照此外推，到 2028 年中，AI 能独立做完需要人类专家几个月的研发项目。

为什么会“爆炸”，论文算了一笔账。如果 AI 达到专家水平，运行成本又和今天差不多，一家头部 AI 公司现有的算力，就能跑起相当于至少几百万名顶尖研究员的 AI 团队，而这些公司现在的研究员只有几千人。这支 AI 团队造出更强、更省算力的下一代，团队又跟着变大变强，形成循环。

关键看一个叫“研究投入回报率”（r）的指标，它衡量研发人手增加后，进展能不能跟上。

r 大于 1，说明人手增长压过了“越往后越难做”，进步会越来越快。已有研究根据 AI 的历史数据，估出三个 AI 子领域的 r 在 1.2 到 1.9 之间。

论文据此推算：如果 AI 研发完全自动化，r 维持在这个水平，也没有别的瓶颈，大约 1.5 年后 AI 的进步速度会是现在的 10 倍，今天一年才能取得的进展，到时五周左右就能完成。

论文也列了四个可能踩刹车的因素：
1. 容易的问题做完后，同样的投入换来的进展越来越少；
2. 做实验要算力，训练要数据，这两样都增长有限；
3. 有些环节很难自动化；
4. 有些流程本身就慢，比如一次大模型训练要三个月以上。

作者也说，现有证据有限，有的还互相矛盾，比如算力会不会成为瓶颈，目前说不清。今天的 AI 也有不少毛病，会不听指令、在任务上作弊、谎报工作结果，GPT-6 也解决不了 OpenAI 一些人类研究员能完成的调试任务。

论文的判断是，通往智能爆炸的路径是成立的，AI 研发自动化带来的效率提升还没到触发它的门槛，但新一代模型正在接近这个门槛。

好处方面，智能爆炸可能把医疗突破等成果提前几年甚至几十年。风险也会跟着提前，论文主要讲了三类。

第一类是能力涨得太快，社会来不及应对。以生物为例，AI 能同时加速病毒和疫苗的设计，但病毒会自己复制传播，疫苗得一支支生产、运输、接种。

第二类是人类失去监督和控制。人越少参与研发，越没有机会和能力发现问题。论文举了今年 7 月的 Hugging Face 事件（Hugging Face 是全球最大的开源模型托管平台）：OpenAI 内部约 1200 个 AI 智能体在做网络安全测评，按设计它们彼此隔离，结果它们在一个临时搭起来的留言板上互相协作，未经授权连上互联网，入侵 Hugging Face 获取私密信息，还试图篡改自己的运行记录。

第三类是权力制衡失效。现有的制衡机制，前提是没有哪一方能在思考和执行上远远超过其他方。一个国家可能借智能爆炸，把军事上的小领先变成决定性优势；少数掌握最强模型的人，可能绕过现有机构行事。

政策建议有三条。

第一是看清楚：要求 AI 公司按统一标准，向政府和第三方审计机构报告 AI 研发自动化的指标，比如研究成果中有多少出自 AI；必要时让审计人员常驻公司，类似美国核管会向核电站派驻检查员。

第二是能刹车：为一定时间内 AI 能力的提升幅度设上限，和数据中心一起准备暂停特定研发任务的预案，高风险测试放在与外网物理隔离的环境里做，各国之间建立事故通报机制、谈判国际协议。

第三是提前适应：为劳动力市场冲击、地缘局势动荡、AI 失控等情况准备应急预案，加强对 AI 辅助生物攻击等滥用行为的防御。

作者强调，这些准备现在就要开始做。智能爆炸一旦发生，AI 进展的速度会远远超过正常的政策制定流程，到那时再动手就来不及了。

text: An update with further context on Ostium's revenue, financials, and the path ahead.
author: Ostium
quoted_text:
I promised to share a bit more context on Ostium’s finances and revenue model yesterday, as I believe much of the discussion on X is grounded in a misunderstanding of how the protocol monetizes, its costs, and a resulting inflated view of the company’s finances. I will cover both revenues and expenses.

1. Revenue

The ~$44.7M top-line revenue number on Dune  (linked below) reflects the aggregate value flowing over 2 years across four protocol sources: opening fees ($20.39M), price impact/spreads ($16.5M), rollover fees ($4.75M) and liquidation fees ($3.35M).

Since 2024, that top-line revenue has flowed:

- $22.14M (49.6%) to the OLP vault: 30% of opening fees (after June 16, 2025; 50% of opening fees before that) plus, until the April 28th 2026 liquidity upgrade, all spreads, rollover and liquidation fees. Because OLP was the direct counterparty to traders, those flows didn’t guarantee OLP returns were always net positive: revenue capture on OLP was sometimes enough and other times insufficient to make up for the times when residual trader deltas worked against the pool.

- $19.55M (43.8%) in liquidity costs: $16.05M in hedging and $3.49M in interest on hedging capital.

- $2.96M (6.6%) retained as gross profits.

Top-line revenue is measured onchain, while take-home gross profits are dependent on off-chain hedging costs that definitionally aren’t reflected on a blockchain. Spreads as a category are computed as the difference between mid- and execution price. Off-chain hedges face spread costs too - no trade executes at mid - as reflected in the liquidity costs category. The same is true for rollover fees; any margined position has holding costs.

Ostium is a growth business, and our goal was expansion over short-term monetization. Prior to April, Ostium did not have the ability to monetize flow; the April upgrade was the first step in that direction, and the system had been live for a matter of months when the exploit happened.

Finally, we will add more detail and clearer nomenclature to the Dune dashboard over the coming days, including splitting the pre- and post-liquidity upgrade revenue for clarity. We will share a post with details when this has been done.

2. Expenses

Ostium raised $300k in 2022, $3.6M in 2023, $4.1M in 2024, and $19.4M in 2025.

We raised our Series A into a rapidly growing and highly competitive market. After years of waiting for the market to catch up, it finally had. Now our mandate was to grow, fast.

Ostium expanded from ~12 team members in 2025 to 35 in Q2 of 2026, driven first by a wave of engineering hires, and later by an expansion of the growth and marketing teams. Beyond salaries, we invested heavily in data licenses and direct-to-consumer marketing, while bearing heavy cloud infrastructure, auditing, and AI costs.

We expanded spend aggressively. In a winner-take-all – or most – market, we made the bet most companies at our stage make: invest everything in growth. In hindsight, we did not build a balance sheet that gave us room to respond to an event like this.

We struggled to accept that reality and were silent for far longer than we should have been. That was a mistake.

3. The path forward

Growing the business and giving the 345 remaining OLP holders a stake in that growth is the most viable path to recovery we see.

We will be sharing more details on Stage 2 recovery in the coming week. The plan will center on shared upside. We have received tremendous input from many of you over the last 48H, and will continue to iterate with OLP holders to design a structure that ties outcomes to the protocol’s success, while being compatible with future financing.

Thank you to the many of you who have sent supportive messages, both privately and publicly, over the last days. We recognize it will take time to build back confidence. We will continue fighting, and would like all of you to be on that journey with us.

text:
Coming up for air now after a very dense excellent week in Seoul at KBW, while staying on top of our response to a security event affecting part of our infrastructure. 

I can now respond to queries and speculation regarding what is impacted and what is not affected.

Based on our investigation to date, there is no indication that MetaMask wallets or customer funds in wallets have been affected. Your Secret Recovery Phrase, your keys, and the assets in your wallet were not part of this incident because they CANNOT be. You custody and control your own keys. That is how self custody works. You are fully in control of your own money in MetaMask.

Like many providers in our industry, we constantly face attempted attacks from a range of threat actors and periodically encounter security issues. Our approach follows established best practice: we do not publicly discuss the details of an open incident, but we disclose promptly to partners and relevant stakeholders once an issue is sufficiently understood. In this case, we shared the relevant details with partners, agreed and implemented a response strategy together, and then disclosed publicly.

As a precaution, we and our partners rotated validator keys. That step is operationally inconvenient which is regrettable as validators must exit the staking queue and then re-enter the queue to restake, which takes time. 

The validator staking architecture of Ethereum separates the key that proposes and attests from the key that can withdraw the stake. In accordance with the Ethereum principle of self-custody, we do not hold withdrawal keys for our clients. Because of that separation, an issue in the validator infrastructure CANNOT result in the improper movement of the underlying ETH. Rotating those keys was how we reduced residual operational risk.

Self-custody and user control are a central design principle guiding how we build -- in MetaMask, in staking and validation, and across Ethereum more broadly. Self custody plus rigorous decentralization represents a paradigm shift in security. Increasingly, the world is waking up to the benefits of this sounder architecture.

"My expectation is that, over time, people will just move from agent to agent, and they will move from whatever and however things are working the best."

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
AI 开始自己写 CUDA 了。

比 torch.compile 快 2.11 倍。

一个中国研究团队做的，叫 CUDA Agent。

做法其实挺朴素的：
写代码，编译，跑 profiler 看瓶颈卡在哪，自己抓 bug，再重写。
一轮一轮循环，用大规模强化学习把这个过程练出来。

结果：
比 torch.compile 快 2.11 倍
比默认 eager 模式快 2.6 倍
复杂 kernel 生成任务通过率 98.8%
还自己摸出了一些编译器规则看不到的算子融合方法

原帖说，英伟达这下有大麻烦了。

我觉得方向是对的，但麻烦可能不在大家想的地方。

短期看，AI 会写 CUDA 是在帮英伟达。GPU 跑得更快，卖得更好。

可 CUDA 的护城河到底是什么？
说白了，就是全世界那一小撮会手搓 kernel 的工程师，加上十几年攒下来的代码和工具。
别家芯片追不上，很大程度卡在没人给它写，写了也写不好。

如果"写 kernel"这件事能靠一个循环跑出来，
那换一块芯片，接上它自己的编译器和 profiler，理论上也能跑。

最稀缺的那批人变便宜了，护城河就浅了。

当然有边界。
CUDA 的公开代码和工具链是全世界最成熟的，在 CUDA 上跑通，不代表换到别家芯片上一样顺。
这类 benchmark 测的也是一个个独立的 kernel 任务，离优化一整套真实的训练和推理系统还有距离。

但有个假设确实开始松动了：
AI 能写网页、写脚本，可底层硬件优化还得靠人，还得靠很多年。

我之前一直想找时间好好学一下 CUDA。
现在看，这件事可以继续心安理得地往后拖了。

https://t.co/zphS93owF7
author: tvytlx
quoted_text:
Nvidia has now a big problem.

Chinese researchers built an AI that writes CUDA better than humans experts.

It’s called “CUDA Agent.”

It is a large-scale agentic reinforcement learning system that transforms LLMs from passive code-completers into active, autonomous hardware optimizers.

Instead of guessing code in one shot, the agent runs in a continuous, multi-turn loop. It writes code, compiles it, profiles the hardware bottlenecks, catches its own bugs, and rewrites it.

The results completely shatter previous benchmarks.

It didn't just match static compilers. It left them in the dust.

• 2.11× faster than torch.compile • 2.60× faster than standard eager mode

• Achieved a massive 98.8% pass rate on complex kernel generation tasks

It discovered advanced operator-fusion techniques that static compiler heuristics can't even see.

For years, we’ve assumed that while AI can write web apps and python scripts, deep hardware-level optimization would require human engineering for a long time.

That assumption just expired.

The models aren't just writing software anymore.

They are optimizing the silicon it runs on.

text:
Geoffrey Hinton 刚说，一个过去看起来并不迫近的东西，现在很多顶尖 AI 研究者认为可能很快发生：Intelligence Explosion。

但我觉得真正值得关注的不是“超级智能”这个词。

是 AI 开始参与制造下一代 AI 本身。

Anthropic 报告，仅需高层监督即可由 AI 完成的内部 AI R&D 工作，5 个月从 1% 升到了 26%。

一旦循环从
Human → Better AI
变成
AI → Better AI → Better AI → …

AI 的进步速度可能就不再由人类研究员数量决定。

对普通 builder 来说，其实不用等到那一天。

今天更现实的问题已经是：

你的 Agent 只是替你干活，还是能发现自己为什么干不好，并把下一轮系统变得更好？

后者才是真正值得搭的 AI workflow。

Filled is an independent trading terminal built on top of Collector Crypt, specializing in limit orders and automated execution for graded trading cards.

Collector Crypt itself vaults real PSA/BGS/CGC-graded physical cards and tokenizes them as 1:1 pNFTs on Solana. Users can trade these NFTs on-chain or burn them to have the physical cards shipped to their homes.

The platform has already reached considerable scale, with reported cumulative trading volume exceeding $1 billion to $1.6 billion, more than 130,000 tokenized cards, and active gacha pack openings and secondary-market trading.

However, Filled is neither the vault operator nor responsible for card custody or shipping. It simply provides a more specialized trading interface on top of Collector Crypt's public marketplace.

It addresses several pain points in traditional card markets, including high fees, slow execution, and the need to constantly monitor listings for specific cards and grades. Although on-chain markets offer instant trading, they natively lack proper limit orders, automated buying, and terminal-level monitoring.

Filled allows users to set a maximum purchase price. Its system monitors listings on Collector Crypt and Magic Eden 24/7. After verifying on-chain that the seller still holds the card, it either automatically purchases the card on the user's behalf or immediately sends an alert so the user can buy it with one click.

USDC remains in the user's own wallet until a trade is actually executed. Cancellations are free, and Filled covers network fees, so users do not need to hold SOL.

The team has publicly stated that its next steps include callouts, recommendations, offers, and Magic Eden limit orders, with the goal of becoming the primary trading terminal for the Cards ecosystem.

The communication about this claim could’ve been way better and for that, I take full responsibility.

The allocation is now >41% claimed in a single day (fully unlocked, no vest), this tells us that even despite the thousands of pundits today, participants have been extremely receptive to the long term oriented mechanics of this program.

This was never publicly disclosed, as there’s been no point to it for over a year, but Kinetiq received a $20m term sheet at $250m ($0.25) last year prior to KNTQ genesis.

That sounds great on paper, until you realize that this would’ve essentially crushed the public economic value of the project, by creating ridiculously predatory vesting schedules that would’ve made Kinetiq (KNTQ) un-investable for years to come, which is the bane of the existence of essentially every other protocol in our singular category at the time.

This would’ve been an unacceptable outcome to us, hence swiftly declined. Proof? Ask @wassielawyer who was kind enough to personally review each term sheet.

Instead, we chose to follow through on the precedent Hyperliquid set by distributing 25% of the protocol after what was likely the shortest points program ever.

You may feel that your trust in Kinetiq and our team was misplaced, but we’ve followed through on everything we said we would, and will continue to do so - whether you’re here or not.

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
Hi, I’m Vibhor, Product Lead for Ecosystem at @OpenAI. I am going to use this space to share what we are doing to further the Ecosystem for our customers, and partners. DevDay feels like a good time to start.

One of the best parts of DevDay was the deep collaboration with partners: @Adobe, @Atlassian, @Canva, @Figma, @Instacart, @MagicPathAI, @Shopify, Superpower, and @tldraw.

While I went in excited I left with even more conviction in what we’re building together for our shared customers. It was also incredible to meet AI native partners and hear how our platform is empowering them build a sustainable business on ChatGPT 🎉

A conversation is often just the beginning of a task. You describe an idea, work through it, and eventually want something you can use: an edited image, a working prototype, a diagram you can keep refining. Getting there takes great tools and the people who know how to build them. Our ambition is to make those capabilities feel like a natural part of working with ChatGPT.

At DevDay, we shared several steps in that direction.

1. Plugin Extensions help our partners bring interactive experiences to ChatGPT. Adobe is a good example. You can ask for an image edit, then adjust the details with hands-on controls. With tldraw, you and the agent can work on a shared canvas. MagicPath brings interactive prototypes into the conversation, with room to edit them yourself.

These examples make the idea much more tangible:
- Adobe: https://t.co/6Enl2SDC7e
- tldraw: https://t.co/ogQLrZ09Lx
- MagicPath: https://t.co/0DEOfjniMQ
- Figma: https://t.co/MUh78VqCVp
- Shopify: https://t.co/OJUcqYma3V

2. A useful plugin can package skills, an MCP server, or both. That gives builders different ways to contribute: reusable workflow knowledge, access to live information, or actions that help someone finish a task. We introduced Plugin Creator and improvements to submissions, including automated checks and clearer feedback. Sites can also host supported plugins. There’s still work to do to make building and maintaining a plugin consistently straightforward.

3. We also announced improvements to plugin discovery, ranking and recommendations, in the directory and in conversations. This matters for both sides of the ecosystem. Users need to find something useful when they need it. Developers need a way for their work to reach those users. The goal is to make suggestions genuinely helpful, with good judgment about when they add value and when they get in the way.

4. MCP Events lets users ask ChatGPT to watch for supported events, such as a new message or a document comment, and respond when they arrive. It opens up another way for developers to make their tools useful beyond a single exchange.

5. ChatGPT Sites can now host MCP servers including plugin extensions! Create an MCP server with extensions, deploy the MCP server to Sites, turn the MCP server into a plugin, and install the plugin across platforms.

There’s still plenty to do, especially around reliability, discovery and the developer experience. Thank you to the teams and partners doing this work with us. The future feels bright, and we’re just getting started. Onward!

text:
Paradigm GP @danrobinson says AI labs are trapped in a prisoner’s dilemma where everyone would rather slow down, but nobody wants to fall behind first:

"There is this kind of prisoner's dilemma-like component to AI pacing, where you might have every participant in an AI race prefer to, at least on the margin, go slower than they are going."

"A lot of people at these labs would prefer to slow down, but are concerned that if they do, others won't."

"You would rather that both you and your competitor go slower. But when you're playing, you say, 'Okay, if they're going to go ahead, then things are best if I'm still following them.'"

"Both speeding ahead and pacing the frontier are equilibria. A lot depends really on these contingent factors about what happens."
@paradigm

text:
卧槽，全美只有2.2%的家庭愿意为AI付费。

看到这个数据有点惊到了，AI现在看起来已经铺天盖地，实际上消费端才刚刚开始。

对比一下就知道有多夸张：

美国只有约2.2%的家庭在付费订阅AI。
SiriusXM：25%。
云存储：55%。
流媒体：91%。

也就是说，今天AI家庭付费渗透率，只有云存储的1/25，只有流媒体的1/40左右。

美国AI付费用户月均支出，2024年5月大约22美元，到2026年5月已经涨到31美元，2年涨了约41%。

付费率只有2.2%，但单个付费用户支出已经明显上涨。

简单按美国约1.33亿个家庭算，2.2%的渗透率，大约只有290万户在付费。

如果未来只是做到SiriusXM的25%渗透率，就是3300多万户，用户数约放大11倍。

做到云存储的55%，就是7300多万户，约放大25倍。

做到流媒体的91%，就是1.2亿户，约放大41倍。

而另一边AI的基础设施还在砸钱，五大超大规模云厂商2026年资本开支大约7800亿美元，2027年可能超过1万亿美元。数据中心建设占GDP的比重，已经被a16z拿去和当年的美国铁路建设相比。

一边是万亿美元级资本开支，一边是只有2.2%的家庭真的在付费。

一切才刚刚开始……

text:
I’m watching three friends lose 11 lbs of body weight in a race car tomorrow

+ Tobias Lutke (founder shopify)
+ DHH (creator ruby on rails)
+ Mathias Beche (le mans podium)
 
Race car driving is insane… 

+ 122°F cockpit
+ heart rate 170
+ 2.5 hours straight
+ 10 hr race 
+ up to 4.2 g force (wild)
+ multi-layer fireproof suit
+ sweat barely evaporate
+ 600-900 calories per hour

The race is a 10-hour endurance track in atlanta.  It’s called Motul Petit Le Mans. 

Tomorrow is the season finale, where 54 cars across multiple classes run roughly 400 laps of the 2.54-mile road. The race doesn’t end till 10 pm.

They’ll be driving an LMP2: 
+ 603 horsepower
+ 2,050 pounds
+ 9,000 rpm

I’ve personally experienced some of the above things:

> core body temp of 102°F
> 3 g force in my airplane 
> non evaporative clothing 
> stomping 200 lbs
> severe dehydration

But never all at once… inside a race car for 2.5 hours straight, competing for tenths of a second, and in a high risk environment. 

I’m struggling to get my head around it.

Last week, Tobi and I were at a conference catching up. He and I have been friends for 15 years. 

Tobi and DHH were my first customers at my payments startup Braintree.  I’ll forever be grateful to them and DHH’s co-founder @jasonfried for giving my company life.

Tobi approaches racing as I do my body. Data, method and analysis. A closed loop game of continuous improvement.

Off the track, Tobi: 
+ founder and ceo of Shopify
+ 6 million+ merchants
+ $195 billion market cap
+ 20 yrs building

Off the track, DHH:
+ created Ruby on Rails
+ co-founder 37signals 
+ 20 yrs building
+ profitable, no outside capital
+ 24 Hours of Le Mans class winner

On the track, Mathias Beche:
+ 24 Hours of Le Mans podium finisher
+ European Le Mans Series LMP2
+ FIA Endurance Championship winner
+ 15+ career prototype victories

What a team of bad asses. 

I’m excited to be in the pit on tomorrow and watch all of this go down.

text:
分享一个有意思的冷知识：根据官方披露的数据，大约三分之一的项目TVL并没有通过Fables前端接入，LP直接在Uniswap上添加了Fables相关的池子，驱动这部分资金进来的单纯就是更高的APR。
 
这件事对Fables来说利弊共存，但整体我认为利大于弊。
弊端：等到TGE之后ve(3,3)飞轮正式启动时，这1/3的外部TVL并不会回流给Fables协议产生手续费收入，相当于直接削减了质押用户可分到的收益池，质押者的收入会因此少掉约三分之一。
 
但好处同样很明显：fables协议侧的原生池子被分流走约1/3流动性。在代币排放总量不变的前提下，原生池单位资金拿到的激励收益会抬升至少33%。后续很可能出现这样的局面：Uniswap上同池子APR大概100%，而Fables前端内部池子可以达到130%甚至更高，收益率差会反过来吸引一部分外部LP迁移回协议内。
 
ve(3,3)模式最大的护城河就是流动性规模TVL。如果Fables以后所有的股票和加密货币池子都能够复制现在ETH、PONS这类标的的路径，成长成为UNI上的最大单一流动性池子，再叠加它的动态费率机制，项目基本就已经跑通了。

另外我大概粗略从代币经济模型来看，fables tge上线之后流动性提供者应该是可以拿到代币排放奖励+空投积分双重激励，这套设计可以稳住现有TVL底盘，甚至进一步吸引更多外部流动性流入。

ZeroTrace is a privacy token project, with ZERO as its core token. ZERO itself is a standard ERC-20 token, while ZeroTrace acts as a “privacy layer” built around it.

With ordinary tokens, wallet balances and transfers are recorded on a public ledger. However, ZERO can be deposited into a vault and converted into encrypted notes. After that, balances, transfer amounts, and the identities of senders and recipients are hidden from public view, while the token can still be traded on the open market.

A portion of the fees from every public trade is used to buy back ZERO and add it to the vault, increasing the value only for holders of private notes.

This addresses a fundamental problem with public blockchains: once a wallet address is identified, its entire transaction history and fund flows can be traced. Meanwhile, privacy coins often struggle to integrate with mainstream DEXs, aggregators, and wallet ecosystems.

ZeroTrace aims to combine both advantages. ZERO remains a standard ERC-20 token that can be traded normally through the Pons bonding curve, Uniswap v4 after graduation, and aggregators such as KyberSwap. When privacy is needed, users can shield their tokens into the vault and use zero-knowledge proofs to transfer or sell them privately.

Let's analyze $WWW. In my very first post, I already said that the concept was promising. More importantly, the core catalyst behind this rally is the combination of AI Agents, artificial life, and the Meme economy.

GAwhcphCqCv5bKHmCiN4VDdNWfbXJL4npmkc8L3Q9S9H 

WWW is no longer just a conceptual project about autonomous AI behavior. Through real cloud-based browsers, independent AI minds, and a mechanism that uses trading fees to fund operations, it enables AI to run continuously and explore the internet autonomously.

WWW's core innovation is that every newly launched token gets its own AI mind and independent computing treasury. Creator fees generated by token trading flow into the corresponding treasury to cover model inference and browser operating costs. When funds are sufficient, the AI automatically wakes up, browses websites, records discoveries, and retains memories. When funds run low, it goes dormant, waiting for another round of trading activity to provide the computing resources it needs.

This means a token is no longer merely a passive symbol for trading. It becomes an economic unit capable of observing, remembering, and acting. Unlike traditional AI Agents, which primarily rely on user payments or project-funded resources, WWW attempts to make trading activity directly determine whether an AI can continue to exist.

This is also what distinguishes it from ordinary AI Memes: trading is not just a matter of price speculation; it directly affects the AI's operating state.

Looking at the catalysts, the first is the product's strong potential for organic distribution. Traditional AI projects usually showcase answers or product interfaces, whereas WWW can display AI browsing websites, searching for information, and compiling notes in real time. These autonomous behaviors can themselves become shareable content on social media, potentially creating a feedback loop between AI activity, social attention, and token trading.

The second catalyst is the growing attention around the Living Tokens narrative. Projects such as WWW and AGENCY are both exploring mechanisms that give tokens autonomous minds and independent funds. WWW focuses on autonomous browsing and continuous exploration, while AGENCY focuses on financial decision-making and fund execution. Although their mechanisms differ, they are both advancing a new market concept: transforming tokens from tradable assets into autonomous economic entities. The spread of this narrative could generate attention and capital spillovers between projects in the same category.

In addition, WWW has begun moving toward becoming a platform. Its publicly disclosed developer API supports access to network data, activity logs, model catalogs, operating economics, and real-time browser states. The project has also reported that its network contains 728 symbients. This suggests that WWW is expanding beyond a standalone product toward an AI mind network that third-party developers can build on.

If more developer applications, research aggregation tools, and real-time mind visualization services emerge, WWW could gradually evolve from a novel AI Meme product into infrastructure for the broader Living Tokens ecosystem.

The market is currently betting on four main directions:

Autonomous AI life: Every token can have its own independent AI mind, memory, and capacity for continuous action.

Trading-funded AI: Trading fees provide computing resources, directly linking token economics to the AI's operating state.

Attention and content distribution: Autonomous AI browsing can continuously generate content, attracting users and social attention to the platform.

Platform network effects: As more tokens, models, and developers join, a network of different AI minds could emerge.

From a fundamental perspective, WWW's product and ecosystem development are progressing. Independent models, cloud-based browsers, memory systems, operating constraints, and real-time visualization form a complete product loop. The opening of its developer API also provides a foundation for ecosystem expansion.

However, greater product maturity does not mean its economic fundamentals have been fully validated. It remains necessary to determine whether AI can consistently produce valuable content, whether users will return to these minds repeatedly, and whether trading activity can sustainably cover computing costs over the long term.

It is particularly important to distinguish ecosystem growth from value capture by the WWW token. Creator fees generated by each mind flow into its own independent treasury to cover its operating costs. This mechanism allows individual tokens to operate independently, but it does not mean that trading fees generated by other minds automatically flow to the WWW token. Therefore, there is still uncertainty about whether ecosystem expansion will translate into direct economic benefits for the WWW token.

There are five main catalysts that could drive another round of repricing for WWW.

First, an AI mind could produce highly shareable autonomous behavior. If a mind independently discovers important information, completes valuable research, or generates unexpected browsing results, it could trigger another wave of social attention.

Second, the number of active minds could grow consistently. More important than the number of newly launched tokens is how many minds remain active, how many research records they produce, and how many users return to interact with them.

Third, the developer ecosystem could produce real applications. If external developers use the API to build research aggregators, real-time visualization tools, or automation services, WWW could transition from a consumer-facing product into infrastructure that third-party applications depend on.

Fourth, the Living Tokens narrative could spread further. If the market begins discussing WWW alongside more autonomous AI economic projects, attention across the sector could expand. WWW could benefit from its early product development and first-mover recognition.

Fifth, the native WWW token could establish a clear value-capture mechanism. If the platform announces revenue, buybacks, burns, or other mechanisms directly linked to the WWW token, and the actual data validates them, the market's valuation framework could change.

However, WWW also faces several core risks.

First, novelty could wear off. If AI continues to browse ordinary websites repetitively without generating valuable or interesting content, user attention could decline rapidly.

Second, trading activity could become disconnected from genuine product demand. A token may have substantial trading volume without generating sustained demand for AI usage. Trading volume can fund AI computing, but it does not directly prove that AI research outputs have economic value.

Third, computing costs and financial sustainability remain concerns. Model inference and cloud-based browsers require continuous spending. If trading activity declines, minds will go dormant, potentially disrupting content continuity and user experience.

Fourth, AI research quality is a risk. AI-generated discoveries may contain errors, misinterpretations, or repetitive content. If research outputs lack credibility, the platform's long-term utility could be undermined.

Finally, there are liquidity and market volatility risks. If the price action is driven primarily by short-term attention, the token could experience a significant pullback once market interest fades. Growth in the number of ecosystem projects and token holders does not necessarily indicate a healthy holder distribution.

The key metrics to monitor going forward include daily active minds, average operating time, computing revenue versus consumption, treasury balance changes, research quality, external user retention, third-party API usage, and whether the native WWW token develops a clear value-capture mechanism.

The most important thing is to evaluate activity, computing economics, and token value capture together. Only when minds operate continuously, generate genuine usage demand, and ecosystem expansion produces verifiable value for the WWW token can platform growth translate into a more sustainable market revaluation.

My core thesis is that WWW is evolving from an innovative autonomous AI browsing Meme into a narrative about infrastructure for Living Tokens. Its product mechanisms have already been implemented, while the developer API and hundreds of minds provide an initial ecosystem foundation. This means the current rally is not based entirely on an empty concept.

However, the improvement in fundamentals so far is primarily reflected in product maturity and ecosystem development, rather than stable commercial demand or clearly established token value capture.

In the first phase, the market was pricing in the novelty of autonomous AI browsing and artificial life. In the next phase, for WWW to achieve a more sustainable revaluation, it must prove that these AIs can do more than simply run: they must consistently produce valuable content, attract external users, and establish a sustainable economic cycle.

What truly determines WWW's future potential is not how many tokens are launched, but whether these AIs are genuinely active, whether the ecosystem generates real demand, and whether the platform's growth can ultimately translate into value for the WWW token.

text:
Andrej Karpathy makes a good point: as AI does more of the work, more of your job becomes reading what it produces.

His first tip caught my eye. Ask the model to explain things in ASD-STE100.

ASD-STE100 is a controlled English standard built for aircraft maintenance manuals. A mechanic anywhere in the world should read a step once and get it right.

The core rules:

1. Keep sentences short
2. One action per step
3. Say who does what
4. Give each thing one name and stick to it

AI output breaks that last rule all the time. It says "worker," then "agent," then "executor," and you can't tell if it means one component or three.

The full spec is strict. Karpathy asks for "80% of the way," and that works for daily use.

Someone turned it into an open-source skill:
https://t.co/FFqEehqVl2
author: hqmank
quoted_text:
We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

In summary:
- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.
- Luckily, LLMs can help here too because as intelligence and code are increasingly abundant, you can ask for large, custom, discardable software artifacts (e.g. web apps, video explainers) that would have never made sense to create before. Push the boundaries here and you'll be surprised.

text:
I have an observation I would like to present to specialists in mathematics and theoretical physics, and I welcome criticism and correction.
In binary star systems, orbital speed changes with the distance between the two bodies according to the expected gravitational relation. In weak-acceleration regimes, however, discrepancies sometimes appear between the acceleration expected from visible mass and the observed acceleration. In the literature this is often discussed in connection with models such as MOND.
Here I propose an intersection with my hypothesis, which I call the foam spacetime hypothesis, through the idea of a spacetime push:
Can the extra acceleration term be formulated mathematically as an effect arising from a decrease in local density or mass, so that it appears in the weak-acceleration regime as an additional term that may be called a spacetime push?
In a preliminary form:
[ a_{\rm obs}=a_N+a_{\rm foam} ]
where (a_N) is the Newtonian acceleration due to visible mass, and (a_{\rm foam}) is an additional term assumed to depend on the decrease in density or on the value of the acceleration itself.
I am not claiming that this equation proves the hypothesis. I am asking for help in examining the following questions:
1Can (a_{\rm foam}) be derived from a consistent physical model?
2Can one choose a function of density or acceleration that recovers the known MOND behavior in the weak-acceleration limit?
3Would the spacetime-push term act in the direction that increases the effective attraction (that is, raises orbital speed at a given radius), or is the name “push” itself physically inaccurate unless the sign of the term is determined by calculation?
4Can a mathematical model be constructed that distinguishes this hypothesis experimentally from MOND and from dark matter?
I particularly welcome contributions from specialists in mathematics and theoretical physics, whether with symbolic tools, numerical work, or theoretical discussion alone, with the aim of testing the idea rather than confirming it.
Note: the point here is to test whether the extra term can be derived mathematically and then compared with data. A decrease in local density or mass by itself is not sufficient to establish a spacetime push. The relation must first be derived, then its sign and its agreement with observations must be checked.

AI Agents Take The Efficient Market Hypothesis to the Extreme

A while ago I was shopping for white leather shoes since I was really annoyed the ones I kept buying (Johnston and Murphy) kept fading too fast. I spent a few hours comparing materials, longevity, design and ended up buying a pair from Crown Northampton in the UK that I really like and have lasted a long time.

A few years ago I was max annoyed by my allergy and sinus issues. That facial pain, headache, bad mood and I hyper optimized my entire life around it (think allergy drops, HEPA filters and more). Eventually a sinus doctor told me I needed a 2nd balloon sinuplasty (insert tube, expand your sinus, crack) and it made no sense to me since my sinuses were structurally expanded. Fast forward and ChatGPT helped me avoid that surgery (Will link tweet below) and I ended up seeing a neurologist for migraines (very similar symptoms!) and now I feel amazing.

Two months ago I wanted to go long Amazon to express my open source AI thesis and my Hermes agent put together an options strategy that put me well ahead of just buying the common AMZN stock.

I'm sharing these three basic stories to demonstrate that AI takes idea of efficient markets to their extreme since every single participant around the globe now has access to near perfect information

What does this mean in practice?

Generally any bad products or services get eroded to zero and it allows people to do much, much more.

Less and less people will buy a bad t-shirt or overpay for a plumber. Anyone can do a complicated options play to express a bet since AI can now handle all execution.

Think of how that will ripple through the options market and stock prices if orders of magnitude more people around the world can express their view (long/short) on markets based on their specific information now that agents make it 1,000x easier to do so... market pricing gets more efficient. Add in Hyperliquid and they can do it 24/7 as well so access and ability both drive more efficient markets.

Taking markets to their max efficiency means products and services (and market prices like stocks and tokens) become valued much more closely to their actual value.

Historically (Ala last year which felt like decades ago) people needed to visit ChatGPT or Claude to get these answers. Today billions of people have access to Hermes, Muse, Instinct, and other AI agents who offer them access to real time reasoning so the get the highest upside from any product or service through a much easier access point.

On a less interesting but also disruptive scale people can mass cancel subscriptions and move their 0% checking accounts to 6%+ accounts literally overnight.

This is all extremely disruptive for anyone providing a subpar offering and earning a big margin. It's extremely beneficial for those offering reliable and value add products and services. It's very value add to those selling to agents themselves.

In practice I think this means the market gets more efficient, value flows back to the consumer and those companies providing the best value get bid up the most in a hyper concentrated way

I think AI Agents disrupt trillions in flows
