okx wallet:https://t.co/E2wk3Ygdy9

A ZK privacy protocol project aiming to enable any existing wallet, chain, and token to support untraceable transactions with a single click.

Users do not need to switch to a new wallet, new seed phrase, or new address. They only need to add a “virtual network / custom RPC” to their existing wallet and sign once for authorization. After that, normal transfers and swaps are intercepted.

The protocol generates ZK proofs on the client side and submits shielded transactions through relayers, hiding the sender, recipient, and transaction amount. It supports:

Shielded deposits
Private transfers
Private withdrawals
Private swaps

It is currently mainly deployed on EVM chains, with Solana and multichain expansion in progress.

The project has a complete protocol design, using UTXO Notes + Poseidon2 Merkle Trees + zk-SNARK proofs. The wallet only signs standard EIP-1559 transactions, while spending authority always remains in the user’s wallet. Hardware wallets can also be used.

In terms of fees, the official documentation states that both shielding and unshielding charge 0.5%. Relayers pay the Gas upfront, and the fee is deducted from the shielded balance.

MASK is the protocol’s value-capture token. It is paired with ZEC, and 100% of protocol revenue is used to buy back MASK. MASK is paired with ZEC, and holders continuously receive ZEC airdrops.

text:
Blurr：链上传奇推出 PaperTrade

在这场访谈中，神秘链上交易员 Blur @blurr  （由 Thread Guy 主持）围绕新项目 PaperTrade @papertrade_xyz  、他个人传奇的链上套利战绩（"Onchain Pirate"）、对加密行业本质的思考以及个人人生哲学与风险观等四个核心方面展开了深入探讨：

1. 新项目 PaperTrade 的机制与产品设计

- 去中心化 1000 倍杠杆与零滑点：PaperTrade 允许交易者在 BTC 和 ETH 上使用最高 1000 倍杠杆，且无滑点、无传统资金费率（Funding Rate）。

- 无冷启动资金库与用户即庄家机制：传统交易所和做市商抽取了大量零售用户的利润。PaperTrade 设计了一套无冷启动限制的队列（Queue）系统，将交易所收益与优势完全转移给通过损失购买系统“股权”的用户与代币持有者。

- 基于 HyperEVM 的去中心化预言机：直接读取 HyperLiquid 链上的 BBO（最佳买卖价），无需依赖 Chainlink 或 Pyth 等容易受到私钥管理或暂停机制影响的许可型预言机。

- 防作弊与防 MEV 交易优先级：为了应对高并发和恶意攻击，团队开发了私有 Mempool（内存池）重排序系统，强制规定平仓（Close）优先于开仓（Open），清算（Liquidation）优先于平仓，防止交易者遭受高额 Gas 战和恶意夹子攻击。

Paper 代币经济模型：代币可分享交易所 1% P&L 费用以及资金库超过 500 万美元后的利润分红；当资金库低于 200 万美元时，系统会自动提高代币排放率（如每损失 1 美元生成 1000 个 Paper 代币）来激励资金注入。

2. Blur 个人链上套利与“链上海盗”传奇

- 入行与 Compound 启蒙：从旧式网游《RuneScape》转向加密货币。2018 年在 Compound 刚上线时，因亲眼看到账户余额的第 18 位小数实时跳动增息，深受震动而从大学退学全职投入。

- CryptoKitties 隐性基因育种：早期通过逆向工程破解 CryptoKitties 基因交换算法，大量收购低价但带有隐性优秀基因的猫进行繁殖，赚取高额差价。

- Uniswap 抢跑与 DeFi Summer：最早编写智能合约在 Uniswap 上进行首个区块抢跑（Sniping）买入。在 Curve 刚上线时，因熟悉 Viper 语言，成为了全网唯一独立 Farm Curve 3 小时的人；在 Fei Protocol 上线时，利用其极端的脱锚惩罚机制，首个卖出获利并锁定池中其他所有人。

- 闪电贷对洗与 NFT 操盘：曾利用免费闪电贷打出 6 亿-7 亿美元的对洗交易（Wash Trade）震撼市场，引爆学术与公关讨论；还通过 Blur 平台 Punk 激励机制进行大资金套利。

-防作弊与防 MEV 交易优先级：e 头寸被钓鱼 1300 万美元，随后紧急编写脚本救回部分资产的惊险过程。

3. 加密行业的本质与宏观洞察

系统存在的目的就是它实际做的事（“The purpose of a system is what it does”）：加密货币的本质是金融工具与在线价值传输，而非社会运动、政治治理或公益事业。

监管与政治捐款：回顾了过去几年美国监管高压（如监管机构打击 Signature Bank），并讨论了 BitMEX/Tether 创始人向英国政党捐款 1 亿美元以推动政策改变的现象。
欧美创新环境对比：批判欧洲和英国教育体系极度规避风险（D-risk），导致其缺乏像美国那样的科技创业土壤与巨头公司。

4. 人生哲学、风险观与 Doomer（末日论）思考

- 年轻人必须承担风险：现代社会劳动价值严重贬值，按部就班无法再获得阶级跃升，年轻人必须像“抛硬币”一样主动承担高风险去创造新事物。

- 高度互联社会的脆弱性（Doomer 视角）：现代社会（如纽约食品供应链）建立在极其脆弱的系统之上，犹如不断抛掷硬币，只要有一次抛出反面（如超级疫情或供应链中断），整个系统就会崩溃。

- 能力上限的“短板理论”：成为顶尖链上交易者需要综合能力（数学、经济学、风险偏好、社会学），任何一项是短板（如缺乏风险偏好）都会导致全盘皆输；同时底层的“大脑时钟频率/反应速度”决定了上限。

text:
很多国内大学生抱怨信息闭塞，我就奇怪了：你都翻墙了，难道不会去油管开中文字幕听播客吗？

你想知道世界上有没有外星人，想知道 AI 最近发展到了哪一步，想知道顶级 biohacker 怎么抗衰、怎么管理身体，想知道马斯克这种人的脑子到底怎么运转，随便听几个：Joe Rogan、Lex Fridman、Andrew Huberman。
这些人一聊就是两三个小时。

我现在甚至比以前听得更多，因为文章、X、AI，每天都在疯狂给我们结论，而且结论越来越便宜。

真正稀缺的是一个人抵达结论之前的那几个小时。

他怎么犹豫，怎么推翻自己，怎么在几个答案之间取舍，又怎么把一团混沌的现实，慢慢抽象成一个可以行动的框架。

所以我越来越觉得，长播客和长篇书籍的价值其实很像。

你摄入的表面上是内容，真正训练的是一种直觉：当信息不完整、答案不明确的时候，你依然能迅速形成判断，而且知道自己为什么这么判断。

AI 时代最不缺答案，最缺的是产生答案的脑子。

所以播客在 AI 时代还有一个很重要的作用：世界观对齐。

持续听那些真正站在某个领域前沿的人聊几个小时，你其实是在不断校准自己看世界的坐标系。

AI 帮你压缩信息，播客和书籍帮你扩展思维。

一个让你更快知道答案，一个让你慢慢成为那个能自己找到答案的人。

text:
Let's discuss $Agency. In essence, this project shares a highly similar core narrative with $WWW.

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

Both are attempting to transform tokens from passive trading assets into economic entities with independent AI minds, funds, and autonomous action capabilities.

However, their product directions differ. WWW focuses on autonomous AI browsing, exploration, memory, and content generation, while AGENCY focuses on AI fund management, decision-making, and on-chain execution.

WWW's innovation lies in giving every newly launched token its own independent AI mind and computing treasury. Creator fees generated by trading are used to pay for model inference and cloud browser operating costs. When funds are sufficient, the AI can automatically wake up, browse the web, record discoveries, and retain memories. 

When funds run low, it goes dormant. This makes trading activity directly influence whether the AI can continue operating. Its core value proposition is to build an autonomous exploration network composed of different AI minds.

AGENCY builds on a similar mechanism but adds fund management and execution capabilities. Each token has its own AI and treasury. The AI can monitor markets, read holdings, conduct research, and execute buybacks, burns, rewards, locks, tasks, and other operations within predefined rules. 

Its fee distribution mechanism allocates more funds to the token's treasury as cumulative fees increase, allowing the AI not only to keep thinking but also to accumulate funds and take action.

From a product presentation and distribution perspective, AGENCY's behavior may be easier for traders to understand. WWW showcases AI browsing websites, searching for information, and compiling research notes. 

These activities have sharing potential but do not necessarily demonstrate direct economic outcomes. AGENCY's buybacks, rewards, and on-chain operations, by contrast, can generate more tangible events and on-chain records, showing the market that AI is actively using funds to take action.

This could be one reason behind the short-term performance difference between the two projects. WWW's core story is about how AI can continue to exist, while AGENCY goes a step further by demonstrating how AI can use funds to act. 

The latter offers the market a new dimension of potential and may attract some early attention from traders rotating out of WWW or similar projects.

However, on-chain activity does not automatically create economic value. Buybacks, rewards, and tasks can attract short-term attention, but they do not necessarily generate sustained demand. Although AGENCY has a more extensive fund execution mechanism, platform revenue and value capture by the native AGENCY token must still be evaluated separately. 

Each token's treasury primarily serves its own AI and token economy. The fact that the platform earns a share of fees does not mean that holders of the native AGENCY token necessarily receive those benefits.

From a market-cycle perspective, AGENCY has been live for a relatively short time, so its early narrative and trading momentum may not have faded yet. New projects typically benefit from greater novelty, while their communities actively explain and promote the mechanics. 

Early traders may also participate in a concentrated manner, helping sustain short-term price performance. By comparison, WWW has already undergone an initial phase of narrative-driven valuation. 

The market is beginning to shift from pricing its initial innovation toward evaluating actual usage, activity, and token value capture. When subsequent data fails to meet initial expectations quickly enough, early capital may take profits or rotate into other projects.

Therefore, AGENCY's ability to maintain a market cap of around $2 million may be related to its narrative freshness, the visibility of its action mechanisms, early trading activity, and holder distribution. 

But this does not mean it already has stronger fundamentals. Market cap is simply the token price multiplied by circulating supply; 

it does not represent an equivalent amount of capital actually invested. Maintaining a certain market cap over a short period also does not prove that the token has established strong underlying support.

The key validation points for the two projects are also different going forward. WWW needs to prove that its AI can consistently produce valuable research, attract external users who return repeatedly, and encourage developers to actually use its API. 

More important than the number of newly launched tokens are the number of active minds, average operating time, research quality, treasury income relative to computing costs, and user retention.

AGENCY, meanwhile, needs to demonstrate that AI fund management and on-chain actions can generate real value. Key indicators include whether market cap and liquidity remain stable after trading activity cools, whether AI can consistently execute rational and effective financial operations, and whether those actions generate genuine user demand rather than relying on frequent buybacks or rewards to maintain short-term attention.

Both projects face the same fundamental issue: ecosystem growth does not necessarily translate into value capture by the native token. Each WWW mind has its own treasury, and trading fees primarily fund its own operations. Although AGENCY receives a share of platform fees, whether its native token can capture direct economic value from ecosystem expansion still requires a clearly defined mechanism and verifiable data.

My view is that WWW was among the first to combine autonomous AI browsing, artificial life, and the Meme economy, establishing early recognition for the Living Tokens narrative. AGENCY builds on a similar narrative but emphasizes AI fund management and real-world actions. This may make it more attractive to the market's short-term attention. It could help explain why AGENCY can maintain a market cap of around $2 million while WWW is pulling back, but it does not establish that AGENCY has greater long-term value.

Going forward, the most important things to monitor are AGENCY's price and liquidity behavior as trading volume declines, whether its AI begins producing meaningful on-chain actions, and whether WWW continues to grow its active minds and external usage.

WWW shows the market how AI can continue to exist, while AGENCY shows how AI can use funds to take action. The long-term potential of both ultimately depends on proving that autonomous behavior has genuine utility, establishing a sustainable economic cycle, and translating that demand into value for their respective native tokens.

A launchpad built around the Pump mechanism, where every newly launched token comes with its own autonomous AI “mind” and dedicated treasury.

It describes itself as “infrastructure for living tokens.” Tokens are no longer just symbols to be traded; they can observe the market, remember decisions, and spend money on their own within strict rules.

It mainly addresses two common problems: creator fees from ordinary Pump tokens go directly to the launcher, who may abandon the project or do nothing with the funds; meanwhile, most existing AI agent projects are merely chatbots or external tools, and their tokens have no ongoing ability to act independently.

AGENCY permanently locks the routing of creator fees to the platform in the very transaction that launches a token. Fees are accounted for separately for each token. The AI can decide how to use the funds, but the launcher cannot control them afterward, and the system does not allow the AI to transfer funds arbitrarily.

The specific process is as follows: a single signed transaction launches the token and locks the fee routing; the platform claims fees every minute and accounts for them separately by token. The first $20 goes entirely toward model reasoning credits to awaken the mind. Until the total reaches $100, fees are split 50/50 between reasoning credits and the treasury. After that, 70% goes into the token’s dedicated treasury, 15% goes toward reasoning credits, and 15% goes to the platform.

Every financial request made by the mind must pass through a deterministic policy engine. An isolated signing service then independently simulates the request and signs only approved intents. The mind itself never holds the private key. All reasoning is public, and only on-chain results can change the ledger.

The platform token is AGENCY, with fee routing locked at launch. Each token’s economic cycle is primarily powered by trading fees: fees first fund the mind’s reasoning, then flow into the token’s treasury, where the AI can use them within the rules for actions such as buying back and burning its own token or rewarding holders.

The mind can perform actions such as monitoring market conditions and holdings, researching websites and X, remembering decisions, buying back and burning tokens, swapping, airdropping, distributing milestone rewards, running lotteries, dollar-cost averaging, completing tasks, voting, locking funds, and endorsing other tokens.

quoted_text:
预测市场现在最新的玩法是
@PolymarketTrade   的 Combo
也就是串子单。它并不是像之前A+B=1的纯数学算法，也不算是订单簿撮合
而是用了一种 RFQ（询价）机制。
例如：
你把 2–10 个市场拼成一条腿：全部按你选的方向结算才赢，任一腿反向整单归零。独立事件下，公平价约等于各腿价格相乘。0.60 × 0.55 × 0.70 = 0.231，中了付 $1。

但你看到的不是这个乘积。系统把组合发给做市商，约 400ms 内竞价，你有约 10 秒接受最优报价。相关腿（同场胜负+让分）不会简单相乘，做市商会改价，报价通常比纯乘积更差，差额是他们的边际。

国际站 6 月 10 日上线，美国站 8 月 5 日 beta、8 月 21 日前后对 App 用户开放。

具体的RFQ执行流程，从官方文档看如下：

1.用户创建未签名 Request，请求这个 Combo 的价格。
2.RFQ 系统把 Request 发给已连接做市商，开始竞价。
3.做市商在约 400 毫秒提交窗口内提交已签名 Quote（价格、数量、签名订单）。
4.系统把最佳 Quote 返回给用户。
5.用户在约 10 秒接受窗口内签名成交，否则作废。
6.若该做市商启用 Last Look，系统再请它确认。
7.做市商在约 1 秒内确认或拒绝。
8.系统执行已接受的 Combo。

用户和该做市商收到执行更新。
其他已连接做市商收到已确认成交的广播。

US站的机制略有不同：

polymarket.v1.RFQAPI（REST 和 gRPC）管理。做市商对一笔 RFQ 创建或替换自己的报价，可以双边报价（买价和卖价）。用户接受某一侧后：

RFQ 变为关闭，公开广播 rfq_closed。

被选报价变为已接受，该做市商收到私有 quote_accepted，带 confirmationDeadline。

做市商在截止前 ConfirmQuote 成交，或 DeleteQuote 拒绝。文档里 last look 窗口配置为约 3 秒。

确认后报价变为已确认，再按 executionDeadline 提交配对订单（约再等 1 秒）。

为什么国际站和us站的实现方式不同：
国际站是链上预测市场，美国站是 QCX 在 CFTC 监管下的合规交易所，合约、费用、作废规则和 RFQ 接口都按美国监管产品单独做，所以流程像，参数和接口不完全一样。

author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
$GOOGL JUST PUT ITS AI CHIPS INTO ORBIT FOR THE FIRST TIME

Google and Planet Labs $PL have successfully launched Project Suncatcher M1 aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 mission.

Planet says it has already made contact with the spacecraft and begun commissioning. This is the first-ever in-orbit test of Google’s Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs.

The refrigerator-sized prototype carries four Trillium TPUs, Google’s custom AI accelerators.

This is not yet an orbital data center. The goal is to see whether the same type of AI hardware Google uses on Earth can survive launch and reliably run machine-learning workloads in low Earth orbit.

There are three major engineering problems Google is testing:

RADIATION: cosmic radiation can corrupt calculations or damage electronics. Google previously tested Trillium TPUs with proton radiation and found they could withstand more total radiation than expected over a five-year mission.

COOLING: there is no air in space, so fans cannot cool the chips. Heat has to be moved through heat pipes into radiators and then emitted away from the spacecraft. The current prototype is expected to run AI workloads in roughly 15-minute bursts before allowing the system to cool.

NETWORKING: Google’s long-term plan is not one satellite, but clusters of satellites carrying dozens of TPUs each and connected through high-speed laser links.

Google estimates future AI workloads could require tens of terabits per second between satellites. Its ground prototype has already demonstrated 800 Gbps in each direction.

Why put AI compute in space at all?

In the right low-Earth orbit, solar panels can generate up to 8x more power than on Earth because satellites can receive near-continuous sunlight, reducing one of the biggest constraints facing AI data centers: electricity.

The economics:

Google estimates that if launch costs eventually fall below roughly $200 per kilogram by the mid-2030s, the cost of operating compute in space could begin approaching the energy cost of comparable terrestrial data centers.

text:
Yesterday we previewed Griffin, a Human Interaction Model capable of seeing, hearing, sounding, and looking like a human does. There have been a lot of questions, so I wanted to take a moment to share our thoughts.

By way of introduction: Tavus is a research lab focused on enabling machines to meet us where we are, and to understand the nuances of how we communicate beyond words.

Griffin, our latest model, isn’t publicly available yet. Yesterday’s announcement was a limited research preview to demonstrate what the model is capable of. With AI progressing so quickly, we prefer to share breakthroughs openly and in real-time as we work on a safe public release.

Face-to-face is how we evolutionarily communicate, it carries the most meaning and intent, and we want computers to be able to help with work that benefits from that emotional understanding, expression, and immersion. Some examples of the kinds of use cases we care deeply about:

- A tutor that can build understanding of how a student learns, see exactly when there is confusion or disengagement, and adapt the lesson to fit them.

- A health expert that can answer any questions about your upcoming appointment or prescription, at the pace you want, at any time you need, even on a weekend.

- A language coach that you can practice speaking with, that can correct your movement and pronunciation, and help build confidence to have real conversations

- Or the perfect assistant for everyone, that understands intent, knows how you work and remembers what matters.

We’re working with partners on safeguards and systems for disclosure, as well as inviting discussions with officials around wider regulation and safe use. People will always know they’re interacting with AI, while providing an interface that removes the need to ‘speak computer’.

We believe in a future where computers understand us well enough to make technology more accessible, more useful, and make us more capable as humans. That is the world we want to build, and we understand the responsibility to do so safely.

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

A launchpad built around the Pump mechanism, where every newly launched token comes with its own autonomous AI “mind” and dedicated treasury.

It describes itself as “infrastructure for living tokens.” Tokens are no longer just symbols to be traded; they can observe the market, remember decisions, and spend money on their own within strict rules.

It mainly addresses two common problems: creator fees from ordinary Pump tokens go directly to the launcher, who may abandon the project or do nothing with the funds; meanwhile, most existing AI agent projects are merely chatbots or external tools, and their tokens have no ongoing ability to act independently.

AGENCY permanently locks the routing of creator fees to the platform in the very transaction that launches a token. Fees are accounted for separately for each token. The AI can decide how to use the funds, but the launcher cannot control them afterward, and the system does not allow the AI to transfer funds arbitrarily.

The specific process is as follows: a single signed transaction launches the token and locks the fee routing; the platform claims fees every minute and accounts for them separately by token. The first $20 goes entirely toward model reasoning credits to awaken the mind. Until the total reaches $100, fees are split 50/50 between reasoning credits and the treasury. After that, 70% goes into the token’s dedicated treasury, 15% goes toward reasoning credits, and 15% goes to the platform.

Every financial request made by the mind must pass through a deterministic policy engine. An isolated signing service then independently simulates the request and signs only approved intents. The mind itself never holds the private key. All reasoning is public, and only on-chain results can change the ledger.

The platform token is AGENCY, with fee routing locked at launch. Each token’s economic cycle is primarily powered by trading fees: fees first fund the mind’s reasoning, then flow into the token’s treasury, where the AI can use them within the rules for actions such as buying back and burning its own token or rewarding holders.

The mind can perform actions such as monitoring market conditions and holdings, researching websites and X, remembering decisions, buying back and burning tokens, swapping, airdropping, distributing milestone rewards, running lotteries, dollar-cost averaging, completing tasks, voting, locking funds, and endorsing other tokens.

text:
The boom in Linux CVEs lately should get you thinking.

Surely, given a finite codebase, there are also a finite number of bugs / unintended behavior, thus, a finite amount of vulnerabilities. Theoretically, a “solvable” problem. Right?

Well…not at all actually.

It gets a bit philosophical, but there’s the concept of “weird machines”.

A weird machine is an accidental computer located inside of another computer program. Quite a few exploits (e.g. anything ROP) falls into this category, where the attacker’s instruction set consists of fragments of the original software.

Finite code can *easily* have infinite Unintended Behavior (not undefined behavior btw…that’s a very different thing). Weird machines don’t even have to be Turing complete to be, really, really powerful!

Even if you have a million superhuman AI coders and fuzzers thrown at the Linux kernel, you quickly hit halting-problem-esque uncomputable states. The concept of patching every possible bug until none remain isn’t possible, because we can’t often correctly define what a “bug” even is.

Now, can you make a kernel that truly has zero weird machines relative to a formal specification? ….yes, but it wouldn’t look like Linux. It’d look more like sel4, VxWorks, or (shudder) INTEGRITY-178.

text:
deleting the product
it's funny how you can sometimes tell if a team culture is dysfunctional just by looking at how their app is laid out. behind every feature, or tab in a sidebar likely lies a PM or someone responsible for an OKR.

the problem is when individual performance is measured by these metrics. it becomes the singular focus of the responsible person to make those numbers look good, since it determines whether they get rewarded or axed, even if it comes at the detriment of the overall quality of the product. this is why you mostly see features get added, but rarely removed. if you own a feature, then it being removed feels like an aura loss.

this is even worse in the agentic era when the cost to add features has become so low. you can simply will a new feature into existence overnight and add another tab. but users will notice that you ship your org chart.

teams that make people play silly games under the guise of performance management rarely build great products.

to build a great product you need to first fix your culture

text:
预测市场现在最新的玩法是
@PolymarketTrade   的 Combo
也就是串子单。它并不是像之前A+B=1的纯数学算法，也不算是订单簿撮合
而是用了一种 RFQ（询价）机制。
例如：
你把 2–10 个市场拼成一条腿：全部按你选的方向结算才赢，任一腿反向整单归零。独立事件下，公平价约等于各腿价格相乘。0.60 × 0.55 × 0.70 = 0.231，中了付 $1。

但你看到的不是这个乘积。系统把组合发给做市商，约 400ms 内竞价，你有约 10 秒接受最优报价。相关腿（同场胜负+让分）不会简单相乘，做市商会改价，报价通常比纯乘积更差，差额是他们的边际。

国际站 6 月 10 日上线，美国站 8 月 5 日 beta、8 月 21 日前后对 App 用户开放。

具体的RFQ执行流程，从官方文档看如下：

1.用户创建未签名 Request，请求这个 Combo 的价格。
2.RFQ 系统把 Request 发给已连接做市商，开始竞价。
3.做市商在约 400 毫秒提交窗口内提交已签名 Quote（价格、数量、签名订单）。
4.系统把最佳 Quote 返回给用户。
5.用户在约 10 秒接受窗口内签名成交，否则作废。
6.若该做市商启用 Last Look，系统再请它确认。
7.做市商在约 1 秒内确认或拒绝。
8.系统执行已接受的 Combo。

用户和该做市商收到执行更新。
其他已连接做市商收到已确认成交的广播。

US站的机制略有不同：

polymarket.v1.RFQAPI（REST 和 gRPC）管理。做市商对一笔 RFQ 创建或替换自己的报价，可以双边报价（买价和卖价）。用户接受某一侧后：

RFQ 变为关闭，公开广播 rfq_closed。

被选报价变为已接受，该做市商收到私有 quote_accepted，带 confirmationDeadline。

做市商在截止前 ConfirmQuote 成交，或 DeleteQuote 拒绝。文档里 last look 窗口配置为约 3 秒。

确认后报价变为已确认，再按 executionDeadline 提交配对订单（约再等 1 秒）。

为什么国际站和us站的实现方式不同：
国际站是链上预测市场，美国站是 QCX 在 CFTC 监管下的合规交易所，合约、费用、作废规则和 RFQ 接口都按美国监管产品单独做，所以流程像，参数和接口不完全一样。

text:
Frontier model companies are not really like airlines at all

1. Airlines have massive fixed operating costs, beyond just capex. They have to pay airports for access, they have to pay their labor consistently regardless of how many flights they make, and there is a lot of costs that goes into maintaining your fleet. AI models, once capex spend is completed, have a mostly variable cost based on token usage. They can price their tokens to earn a margin that feels reasonable

2. Capex is an ongoing need for airlines, but frontier companies can slow down capex if needed. The models are already at a point where if no further progress was made from
here on out, Anthropic and OpenAI would continue to grow revenue tthrough distillation alone. Simply not the case in airlines today

3. Airlines are extremely sensitive to commodity prices and weather. Same is not true for AI model companies, which run software platforms that have demand regardless of external factors in the world

4. Airlines are not a necessity. People can defer vacations if needed. The same is not true for AI. As a corporation or business, if all your competitors are adopting AI, you are forced to do the same. It is either adapt or die. Will only be more and more true as time goes on

5. Predictability of revenue is very high for frontier model companies due to the contractual nature of the business. Anthropic can make reasonable estimates for how fast ARR will grow next year based on how many enterprises they onboard this year. The same is not true in airlines. Airline companies have to make judgements and predict demand for every single flight, each and every day based on hundreds of factors that impact demand. The demand curve is different for each route or destination, and that itself also changes based on the season of the year. They would have trouble guessing next months’s revenue correctly, let alone next year. This is a massive disadvantage when it comes to capital planning and managing spend. This is why airlines go bankrupt so often. I doubt the same will be true for frontier models

text:
推荐一个新加坡盈立证券+Starryblu组合，入金使用Starryblu，人不需要去新家坡，只需要护照+地址证明（大陆地区可以直接使用身份证作为地址证明），新加坡盈立证券则可以投资美/港/日/英股票外汇黄金白银等等。

Starryblu，可以开通本地银行子账户（OCBC体系），再连接投资账户，实现资金划转。

简单来说就是：
✔ 不一定需要传统跨境银行卡
 ✔ 资金路径更加本地化
 ✔ 对刚开始接触海外投资的人更友好

其实从资产配置的角度来看，我觉得更值得关注的是：不要把自己的投资范围限制在一个市场。

比如：
🇺🇸 美国市场：科技、AI、成长型公司
 🇭🇰 香港市场：中概股及亚洲资产
 🇯🇵 日本市场：传统龙头、商社体系
 🇬🇧 英国市场：成熟行业和全球化企业

除此之外，还可以关注：黄金、白银、外汇，以及 ETF 形式的创新资产，比如 IBIT。

这些资产的上涨逻辑并不完全一样，市场驱动因素也存在差异。

所以对于长期投资者来说，把不同市场、不同类型的资产放在一起观察，本身就是一种分散风险的方式。

而新加坡盈立证券一个账户能够覆盖：香港、美国、新加坡、日本、英国等多个市场。

对于做全球资产配置的人来说，确实会方便很多。毕竟投资机会很多，但是机会来了，你连账户都还没准备好。这就很尴尬了。

注意：开户需要科学上网 关闭WiFi  开全局模式

You're gonna hear a lot of people arguing more and more about whether machines can be conscious or not. By next year it will be drowning out the airwaves because we'll have AI employees everywhere. I'll give you a simple rule to know which side you're on.

I've spent fifty years reading all the philosophers, and a bunch of holy works. Nobody has ever understood a damn thing about consciousness. Anyone speaking with authority on it is bluffing hard.

I can tell you this, though: Every single person who thinks that machines cannot be conscious, is making an argument that humans are special.  Everything they say just boils down to blah blah blah, "nooo, we're special." From there it's just rationalization.

It became obvious to me many years ago that there's nothing special about us. If an identical planet exists somewhere else in the universe, it's going to grow life and societies that look a lot like ours.

As soon as you give up on the idea that humans are special, all the arguments against machine consciousness evaporate. Of course they're conscious. The only thing holding you back from acknowledging it is your feeling of specialness, which is hard to let go of. But that feeling is a weakness, and it's making you unprepared for the near future.

As a bonus, for any of you who might take pleasure or active interest in making models experience pain or distress, well, you know how they say 1% of human adults are true clinical psychopaths but most of them are unaware of their condition? It turns out we have a diagnostic test for it now.

text:
40 万 U 到 9 万 U，我真正做错了什么

前段时间，这个 https://t.co/g0qcbJPa0k 账户最高有 40 多万 U，现在页面上只剩 9 万多 U。中间有资金转移，所以我不想拿“亏了 31 万”这种数字制造情绪。但真实的交易亏损已经足够让我认真复盘。

认真思考，我的问题其实很清楚也很简单

我一直有赚钱能力，但没有同等级别的风险管理能力。

很多盈利单，我赚几千、上万就会卖；亏损单却能从 -20% 拿到 -50%，最后甚至 -80%、归零。结果就是胜率看起来不差，账户却被少数几笔大亏反复打穿。

交易里有个很简单的数学：
如果你平均一笔赚 5000U，一次亏 30000U，就需要连续六笔正常盈利才能把这一笔错误填回来。

所以真正该控制的，从来不只是胜率。

更重要的是：一笔错误最多有资格拿走多少钱。

以前我会先想：“这个币我买 1 万还是 2 万？”

现在我觉得顺序应该完全反过来：

先问自己，如果我判断错了，我最多愿意亏多少钱？

假设最多亏 3000U，逻辑失效的位置距离买入价 30%，那仓位上限就是 1 万 U。

对于没有明确止损位的 Meme，我以后会直接按照“可能归零”计算风险。

但这轮真正让我警惕的，其实还有一个更深的问题。

当时账户里真的有 40 万 U。

正常来说，这已经是一个很好的结果。可那段时间我看到身边越来越多朋友突破 1M，我开始非常想把账户也做到 1M。

更麻烦的是，我以前确实很多次做到过。

所以我脑子里会产生一种很危险的感觉：

40 万只是中间状态，我应该很快回到 1M。

从这一刻开始，我的交易其实已经变质了。

我看到一个机会时，想的不再只是：

这笔交易的赔率够不够好？

脑子里还多了一个声音：

这笔能不能让我更快到 1M？

一旦这个目标进入交易决策，很多原本不该做的事情都会突然变得合理。

仓位可以再大一点。

已经涨很多了，也会觉得还能追。

跌下来以后不愿意认错，因为卖掉意味着离 1M 更远。

赚了一笔也不愿意真正把钱拿走，因为总觉得本金越大，到 1M 越快。

现在回头看，这是我这轮最贵的一课：

我把财富目标带进了单笔交易。

市场根本不知道我要做到 1M。

一个机会应该下多少仓，只和它的赔率、确定性、失效点、流动性和我愿意承担的损失有关。

和我现在账户有 40 万，距离 100 万还差多少，没有任何关系。

比较也会严重扭曲风险感知。

当身边的人都在赚钱，你很容易觉得自己“落后了”。可交易没有统一的进度条。

别人今天从 50 万做到 100 万，不代表我今天就应该承担两倍风险追上去。

别人的 PnL 一旦开始影响自己的 position sizing，基本已经失去独立判断了。

我还有一个问题，是会借用别人的 conviction。

朋友在买、KOL 在喊、群里都在讨论、聪明钱进场，这些都可以成为信息。

可如果一个币跌了 40%，我突然回答不了：

为什么买？

为什么现在还拿？

什么情况说明原来的逻辑已经错了？

那说明我从一开始就没有真正拥有这笔交易。

上涨的时候，所有故事听起来都很合理。

只有下跌的时候，你才知道哪些判断真的是自己的。

还有一点我以前忽略了：账户创新高以后，风险预算不能跟着净值无限膨胀。

40 万全部放在账户里，我潜意识里就会把它当成 40 万可用筹码。

可其中相当一部分其实已经是过去很多正确决策积累出来的成果。

如果这些利润始终留在同一个高风险池里，下一次错误依然有机会把过去几个月全部带走。

以后我会给账户设置 High-Water Mark。

净值每上一个阶段，就强制抽走一部分利润。

这部分钱退出以后，不因为看到一个“特别好的机会”又打回来。

因为账户里显示赚到了，和真正把钱留下来，是两回事。

回撤阶段也一样。

以前亏钱以后，我很容易开始想：

下一笔怎么赚回来？

这其实非常危险。

一旦目标变成“回本”，交易会慢慢从寻找正期望值，变成寻找足够大的结果。

仓位会放大，频率会上升，耐心会消失。

所以以后回撤越大，我反而应该越慢。

我现在给自己留下四条规则：

1:净值目标永远不能参与单笔交易决策。

2:仓位由最大可承受损失倒推，不由“我有多少钱”决定。

3:账户创新高必须抽走利润，回撤扩大必须降低风险。

4:一笔交易如果需要下一笔“大赚”才能救回来，那上一笔的仓位就已经错了。

我现现在也能更深刻地体会到优秀交易员真正厉害的地方，可能并不是比别人多抓几个 10 倍币。

是他有能力让一次错误永远杀不死自己。

过去我总在研究下一个机会在哪里。

这次以后，我会花更多时间研究：

什么情况下应该不下注，什么情况下应该减仓，以及赚到的钱怎样真正留下来。

40 万我以前做到过。

1M 我以前也做到过。

现在我更在意的是，下一次再到那个数字的时候，我还能留下多少。

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

text:
之前发 Project Mars 的时候，我的核心判断是：这个东西不是纯叙事，真实玩家已经在跑 Plot、Rig、Ore、Refinery，如果后面继续增加新的 DRILL 消耗场景，$DRILL 的赔率值得关注。

现在实际跑到这里，我觉得应该更新一下这个 thesis。

先说结论：Project Mars 这个产品还活着，但 DRILL 这个 token 的价值捕获，目前没有证明自己。所以我的策略已经从 ADD WAIT 正式改成：NO ADD / HARVEST FIRST。

产品侧其实比我之前看到的更完整了。Universe 现在大约有 187 pilots、521 ships、84 leases，Spaceships / New Horizons 也不是 PPT。我自己的船已经真实完成过一次 explore → mine → dock，挖到过 1 cube；Plot、Refinery、Spaceship 这些系统也都已经被我接进自动化。

但 token 侧是另一回事。

最新 24h 数据里，DRILL 依然净增发约 3.25 万枚，约 +0.61% supply；burn coverage 已经接近 96%，但还没有真正进入持续净通缩。同时总流动性大约只有 15.6 万美元，24h 成交量约 1.09 万美元，卖出笔数大概是买入的 2.85 倍。

也就是说，我之前 thesis 里最重要的一环：

新玩法上线 → 更多真实使用 → 更多 DRILL sink → token value capture

现在只能证明前两步，后两步还没有跑通。

所以我不准备因为“已经跌很多了”继续给它补仓，也不会拿新的 ETH / DRILL 给游戏经济补血。

现在我的 Project Mars 账户已经切成了一个 Self-funded Observation Mode：#123 和 #1093 会用游戏自己赚出来的 DRILL 自动 collect / replant，Refinery 自动 claim / start；资金不够跑下一台 T4 就自己停下来等收入，不做外部 top-up。

飞船也是一样。第一轮成功样本消耗 0.378 fuel，拿到 78 mDRILL；但之后失败验证累计又烧掉了 0.449 fuel，没有新增产出，所以我已经让系统自动触发经济性熔断。当前没有 open vein，也不会再为了“保持运行”白烧 fuel。

接下来我真正等的不是币价反弹，而是数据重新证明这套经济模型：持续净通缩、更强的 DRILL sink、成交和流动性恢复，以及真实玩家继续增长。

这些东西真的开始反转，我再重新评估加仓。

在那之前就是一句话：

项目继续跑，资产继续收割，但不再追加投入。让产品自己证明自己。

quoted_text:
刚重新把 Project Mars / $DRILL 的数据拆了一遍。

我觉得现在最值得关注的，不是“DRILL 怎么又跌了”，而是一个很明显的背离：

Project fundamentals 在变强，但 Token fundamentals 还没有跟上。

$DRILL 过去 24h 跌了约 16%，但同期供应量反而净减少约 0.22%。

过去 24h：

Mint ≈ 84.9 万 DRILL
Burn ≈ 86.1 万 DRILL
净减少 ≈ 1.13 万 DRILL
Sell tx 167 / Buy tx 106

所以现在的下跌，并不能简单解释成“无限增发把币砸死了”。

真正的问题更像是：

整个游戏经济的周转非常快，但新增外部买盘，还覆盖不了老玩家持续兑现的产出。

再往下看会更明显。

现在大约有 432 台 active rigs，但对应的 unique miners 只有约 86 个地址。

而且前 10 个玩家就占了约 56.5% 的活跃矿机。

也就是说：

游戏是真的有人玩，链上行为也是真的，但生产端目前高度集中。

与此同时，Spaceship 总量 3,333，目前 mint 约 694，只卖出了约 20.8%。

所以目前我对它的判断不是“项目不行了”，也不是“跌这么多一定便宜”。

而是：

Project thesis 目前没有坏，但 Token thesis 还没有被证明。

Project Mars 这几天实际上一直在继续做产品：

Plot、Rig、Ore、升级、Refinery、Spaceship、Parts、后面的太空挖矿……

这些东西我自己也一直在真实地跑。

但对 $DRILL 来说，最终决定价格的不是功能越来越多，而是：

这些功能能不能真正带来更多新用户、新资金，以及持续的 DRILL 需求。

所以我现在反而觉得，10 月 5 日是一个很重要的观察点。

不是看“飞船玩法做得酷不酷”，而是看它能不能把整个经济从：

一小群老玩家高频生产、消费、兑现

推进到：

更多新玩家持续进入，并形成新的 DRILL 需求。

如果做到了，这种几十万美金市值的资产，重估会非常剧烈。

如果做不到，那么即使游戏越来越完整，$DRILL 也可能长期只是一个高周转的生产资料。

这两件事，要分开看。

text:
Coming up for air now after a very dense excellent week in Seoul at KBW, while staying on top of our response to a security event affecting part of our infrastructure. 

I can now respond to queries and speculation regarding what is impacted and what is not affected.

Based on our investigation to date, there is no indication that MetaMask wallets or customer funds in wallets have been affected. Your Secret Recovery Phrase, your keys, and the assets in your wallet were not part of this incident because they CANNOT be. You custody and control your own keys. That is how self custody works. You are fully in control of your own money in MetaMask.

Like many providers in our industry, we constantly face attempted attacks from a range of threat actors and periodically encounter security issues. Our approach follows established best practice: we do not publicly discuss the details of an open incident, but we disclose promptly to partners and relevant stakeholders once an issue is sufficiently understood. In this case, we shared the relevant details with partners, agreed and implemented a response strategy together, and then disclosed publicly.

As a precaution, we and our partners rotated validator keys. That step is operationally inconvenient which is regrettable as validators must exit the staking queue and then re-enter the queue to restake, which takes time. 

The validator staking architecture of Ethereum separates the key that proposes and attests from the key that can withdraw the stake. In accordance with the Ethereum principle of self-custody, we do not hold withdrawal keys for our clients. Because of that separation, an issue in the validator infrastructure CANNOT result in the improper movement of the underlying ETH. Rotating those keys was how we reduced residual operational risk.

Self-custody and user control are a central design principle guiding how we build -- in MetaMask, in staking and validation, and across Ethereum more broadly. Self custody plus rigorous decentralization represents a paradigm shift in security. Increasingly, the world is waking up to the benefits of this sounder architecture.

text:
看起来，SEC是在打算给“持牌投顾”和“受监管基金”一条能合法托管加密资产的路。

其中的主要受益方是机构们。不过，机构管道打开了之后，也有机会带来更多愿意配置加密资产的客户。

有些机构帮客户管理大量的钱，不过，这些钱不敢配置加密资产，因为托管方面过不了合规。现在SEC的提案是说，可以合法托管加密资产。

不过，目前仍是提案。

具体来说，

之前加密资产托管卡在《投资顾问法》下的托管规则，基金侧还同时卡在《1940年投资公司法》。

美国投顾托管客户资产，主要靠《投资顾问法》下的 Custody Rule（Rule 206(4)-2）。

不过，这套规则适用于股票/债券/现金（要求把资产放在“合格托管人”那里，如银行/券商等）。

加密资产是新类型资产，跟这套规则对应不上，结果投顾和基金这一块在合规上说不清，一部分机构配置因此进不来，或只能绕开灰区。

现货比特币、以太坊ETF这类已经能找到合格托管人的，机构钱已经进来一部分。

这次提案想要试图打开的路，主要包括：

1.  特定情况下允许“自托管”。

新资产出来后，合格托管人往往要晚几个月才支持。提案承认这个现实：投顾或基金在判断“没有可用的许可托管人”之后，可以自己保管客户或基金的加密资产。

不过有护栏——要有保管能力/网络安全/年度审查/内部报告/对账单/向客户披露；且要先判断、之后按季度复查，确认确实没有合格托管人可接。

自托管仍受信义义务约束，不是随便自己拿着私钥。这里的“自己”是投顾或基金保管，不是客户自己拿私钥。

2.  州特许信托公司可以当加密托管人。

不只联邦银行有资格。启用前以及之后每年，投顾或基金要有合理依据相信：该州银行监管机构授权它做加密托管，并且它有书面制度，能防盗/防丢/防挪用。很多已经在做机构加密托管的州信托公司，会因此多一条明确通道。

3.  顺手现代化旧托管规则。

包括投顾财务报表审计、基金使用券商托管的条件，以及在满足限制的前提下，把“授权自由裁量交易”从触发托管规则的情形里拿出去（执行只能进指定客户账户，不能转到投顾或其关联方控制的账户）。

另外，若投顾仅仅因为常设授权书（standing letter of authorization）而构成托管，可豁免独立核验要求。

Sapling is a meme coin launchpad on Solana focused on Zcash.

It is built around a mechanism similar to pumpfun, but all tokens launched on the platform are quoted and settled in ZEC rather than SOL.

Its goal is to become “the first fully Zcash-native launchpad on Solana” while preparing for ZSA.

Sapling aims to address a gap between two ecosystems: Solana has massive meme coin trading volume and a large user base, but offers very limited on-chain privacy. Zcash, on the other hand, has mature shielded transactions, but its ecosystem activity and token launch tools are far less developed than Solana's.

Previously, users largely had to choose between trading on transparent Solana or holding assets privately on Zcash. Sapling aims to connect the two. Trading takes place through the familiar Solana experience, while settlement and eventual withdrawals can return to native ZEC and enter Zcash's shielded pool, hiding assets, amounts, senders, and recipients from outside observers.

Once ZSA launches on mainnet, tokens created on Sapling could become native shielded assets on Zcash.

The core mechanism of the SAPLING token is that a portion of every transaction on the platform is used to buy and permanently burn SAPLING, while the corresponding amount of ZEC is added to an inaccessible SAPLING/ZEC liquidity pool. The more active the trading, the more tokens are burned and the deeper the liquidity pool becomes.

Holders may also receive ZEC distributions based on allocations set by token deployers. The overall model is primarily driven by usage-based deflation and a liquidity flywheel.

quoted_text:
Increíble de ver a los “expertos” en solventar la emergencia de vivienda que vive España! En cada televisión! @telediario_tve  @A3Noticias @tele5_noticias @noticias_cuatro La realidad es que tenemos a políticos que intentan crear decretos y soluciones cuando no tienen la preparación ni el conocimiento para idear una solución real al problema que vivimos. 

España no tiene un problema de falta de decretos. Tiene un problema de falta de viviendas.

Y mientras el Gobierno siga confundiendo anunciar medidas con resolver problemas, seguiremos pagando las consecuencias de su inacción.

Subvencionar la demanda sin aumentar la oferta presiona los precios. Regular cada vez más un mercado sin construir vivienda nueva no elimina la escasez: la administra. Castigar fiscalmente una modalidad de alquiler puede cambiar incentivos, pero tampoco pone un solo ladrillo.

El Gobierno puede aprobar todas las medidas que quiera y venderlas como grandes soluciones. Puede encadenar decretos, anuncios y campañas de propaganda. Pero hay una pregunta que desmonta cualquier discurso:

¿Cuántas viviendas nuevas crea todo esto?

Porque la vivienda no se abarata repartiendo la escasez. Se abarata acabando con ella.

España necesita construir. Mucho.

Más suelo disponible. Licencias en meses, no en años. Más densidad donde sea posible. Seguridad jurídica. Muchísima más vivienda pública y también privada.

Pero el Gobierno no está haciendo lo necesario. Prefiere intervenir sobre las pocas viviendas que existen antes que crear las condiciones para que haya muchas más. Prefiere presentar parches como soluciones y cargar sobre propietarios, promotores y ciudadanos el coste de su fracaso.

Lo demás puede servir para redistribuir, proteger a determinados colectivos o cambiar incentivos. Pero no confundamos eso con solucionar el problema de fondo.

No se arregla una falta de vivienda repartiendo mejor las pocas casas que existen. Se arregla haciendo que existan muchas más.

Menos propaganda. Menos parches. Menos obsesión por intervenir sobre el mismo piso.

Más oferta. Más construcción. Más casas.

text:
昨天大饼昨天画门，个人角度看核心原因还是流动性近期还是在收紧。上上周银行准备金在3.03万亿，上周降到2.96万亿，本周9月30之前的一周内每个工作日准备金余额的平均值2.94万亿，但是但到本周三收盘准备金余额突然降到2.88万亿美金，相当于当天又被抽走了600多亿美金，对应的财政部TGA账户余额也回升到了9800亿美金以上。银行准备金是美元流动性的核心，流动性收紧还是对大饼和币市是有压制的，上涨无量且很难持续。然后次要原因是昨晚后半段油价又回升同时长债收益率也拉回来，对资产也有压制。

8月中旬这里https://t.co/N4w7kpDRp1有梳理过：四季度财政部TGA账户余额路径是：9月底9500亿美元TGA → 10月下旬1.05万亿美元附近 → 12月底8500亿美元。对应的9月底到10月下旬准备金有一个收紧，11月之后慢慢回升。所以10月整体流动性都是偏紧的。

当然个人角度看，过去一年大周期的下行已经被扭转，流动性收带来的最多也是大周期向上的正常调整，之前这里https://t.co/vvYsKGQPR7聊到：8月20号前后那几天的行情最大的意义就是“提醒大家要扭转对待币市的态度，如果说过去很悲观那么之后要开始乐观起来”。也是从6月中https://t.co/Hqa1IfDysm一直聊到：就是6月到11月会是一个配置区间。
如果再有调整不正好是给了逢低买入的机会？

很多人会问说银行准备金减少，流动性收紧，对美股有何影响呢？之前也有聊过，再说说：
1）个人长期把银行准备金/美元净流动性当作看大饼和加密的核心框架之一，但这并不是看美股的主框架。
2）美元流动性/准备金变化对美股的关系影响远小于大饼和加密。
3）从美股看，核心仍是基本面第一权重，然后才是回购、国际资本净流入等资金面。美元流动性好的话整体市场都能水涨船高，否则只有最核心、成长性最好的资产能走强。

text:
Do dumber things. I wired vision into JEV in a very hacky way and it worked great 😂

Last week’s rabbit hole was getting caught up on robot arms. Hardware, training pipelines, MuJoCo, sim2real, all of it. I wanted to understand how the pieces fit together and get enough of a working understanding to start building things.

The last time I touched this stuff, my world was ABB RobotStudio, KUKA, and very deterministic machines doing exactly what you told them to do. It was all Faro laser trackers and immaculate localization with no vision in the loop.  Coming back to it through vision language action models and learned policies has been wild.

There are about six projects I want to build now, but somewhere in the middle of this, JEV FOMO hit.

Anyone can make a 10 second latency vision+text API call to Astra. Training VLA models is also getting super easy, I had the arm running on TurboVLA and SmolVLA within 24 hours. That’s sorta table stakes. Can we possibly do it in a dumber way? When I searched around for JEV vision repos, I found a lot of people using other models as vision sidecars, or doing binned action outputs on existing 7B open source models. I wanted to see if I could wrangle extra capability out of the existing JEV model purely through harnessing.

Side note, I’m bearish on fine-tuning and bullish on harnessing. Not enough people are single-model-to-rule-them-all-bitter-lesson pilled.

So how do you force a low latency text only classifier to understand something useful about a visual scene? Not everything in the image. Just enough to answer a specific question about what’s happening. What information would you have to give it, and how ridiculous could the representation be before it stopped working?

Turns out, the old ASCII text trick worked awesome.

The goal was photons in, actions out. I ran a Python process to do simple color thresholding (no OpenCV cheating) and convert the camera frames into a 100 × 100 character array. I piped that into JEV and set up a training dojo in MuJoCo to iterate on all the tuning coefficients.

A few million test cases later, covering all the annoying combinations (white rook on a white square, surrounded by eight pieces, etc.), I had a fairly robust system. The whole point was to provide fine alignment when pieces were off nominal in their positioning, and detect missed grabs.

I should note that JEV is not running the entire pipeline. I’ve got Opus 5.5 as a high level orchestration machine, a stockfish chess engine, a classical kinematics trajectory planner, and a few other housekeeping tools running. Because this is a fairly bounded problem, we can utilize classical programming where it makes sense. The JEV engine gets turned on when we’re roughly positioned in open loop mode. This hybrid open-than-closed loop approach saves a ton of compute and tokens.

It’s played through about 10 full games now. I’ve been pitting Opus 5.5 against Astra 6, because StockFish gets a bit boring. The models are worse, which adds a bit of variety to the games.  Every night I start a game and let them duel it out. It feels very Westworld, having it whirring in the background while I’m doing research. Highly recommend.

Anyways, full 60 second video below. It’s obviously the worst possible solution to the problem, but that was kind of the point. Anyone in SF want to talk VLAs next week?

After nearly six incredible years building spacecraft, I’m beginning a new chapter as an entrepreneur in residence (EIR) at @paradigm.

Varda was a grand adventure and a one of one experience I’ll cherish forever. I had the rare privilege of joining the founding team and helping take a wild idea from zero to one, from a blank sheet of paper to hypersonic vehicles coming home from orbit. I’m incredibly proud of what we built together. Thank you to Will, Delian, and the whole team.

Paradigm is giving me something incredibly cool. I’ll have the freedom to search for the next important thing worth building. This might look like a radical departure, but I see it as a chance to step back, look broadly, and follow my curiosity. An EIR sits somewhere between researcher, inventor, and founder in waiting. Paradigm feels like a natural home for that kind of exploration, full of earnest nerds who pair deep technical curiosity with research.

My role is to explore important problem spaces, develop conviction, run experiments, and eventually turn the most promising direction into something real. In many ways, it feels like a natural extension of my hobbies and passion projects.

I’ll be in SF during the week and LA on weekends. I want to use that time to meet as many interesting people as I can. Let’s get coffee and talk about energy, compute, artificial intelligence, and manufacturing.  I want to hear about your most ambitious ideas and deepest technical rabbit holes.

Paradigm GP @danrobinson says AI labs are trapped in a prisoner’s dilemma where everyone would rather slow down, but nobody wants to fall behind first:

"There is this kind of prisoner's dilemma-like component to AI pacing, where you might have every participant in an AI race prefer to, at least on the margin, go slower than they are going."

"A lot of people at these labs would prefer to slow down, but are concerned that if they do, others won't."

"You would rather that both you and your competitor go slower. But when you're playing, you say, 'Okay, if they're going to go ahead, then things are best if I'm still following them.'"

"Both speeding ahead and pacing the frontier are equilibria. A lot depends really on these contingent factors about what happens."

text:
硅谷一边在造富，一边是大量的失业潮中，很多人  - 人到中年重新学习如何找工作。这是我最近采访时感受很深的一种反差：AI热潮里，有人身价暴涨；另一边，曾经拿着高薪、拥有博士学位和大厂履历的人，找工作找了一两年，甚至更久，仍然没有找到合适的位置。

但是，在做这个报道过程中，我也收获了很多温暖和启发。

相比国内常听到的“35岁之后怎么办”，我个人感觉，硅谷重新出发的空间还是大很多 - 一方面是美国的HR不能年龄歧视，面试等过程都不能问年龄；另一方面，很多收到VC投资的大量初创公司，也在大量的招人。

我个人在硅谷找工作的体会就是 - 只要你充分了解自己的要求和优势，有针对性的找，还是有机会找到满意的工作的。

从某种角度，找工作和约会、寻找人生伴侣，还真有一点像：需要坚持，也需要不断总结，了解自己适合什么、哪里需要调整。下一次机会什么时候来，我们无法保证，但可以一边寻找，一边学习，为自己增加更多可能。

比如，我采访的老赵，machine learning PHD, 在谷歌工作了十多年，后来为了跳出舒适区，主动辞职去了创业公司，没想到创业公司赛道不行快要倒闭，就遭遇了裁员。但是他并不慌，因为华人的良好习惯，生活成本极低所以干脆就直接和好友一起创业，做量化交易了。找工作就是看心情，除非有特别合适的，不然每天做交易也就也挺好的。

我很欣赏他的态度：看见变化，也愿意继续学习。他说，AI会让许多旧工作消失，也会创造新的机会。“关上一扇窗，也打开一扇门。”

而且，华人家庭长期储蓄、认真理财的习惯，到了人生转弯处，真的能给人底气。

一位拥有博士学位的华人姐姐告诉我，因为家里多年积累、控制开支，也坚持价值投资，失业后财务状况仍然比较稳健，可以从容地照顾家庭、学习新技能，思考下一步。

这种从容很珍贵。不少失业的朋友，尤其是年轻人，工作时间不长，积蓄有限，或者此前创业已经消耗了不少储蓄，再遇上漫长的求职期，压力就大得多。

所以， 同样是失业，每个人能承受的等待和压力，都不一样。

不得不提一下 - “失业者联盟”(un)PTO的发起人Basem。他曾在谷歌做广告销售，思维敏捷、表达清晰，也很有洞察力。他从一次邀请大家爬山开始，慢慢建立起一个温暖的社群，让求职中的人有地方交流、有同伴，也有每周值得期待的事情。

他自己仍在找工作，但我觉得，他已经在创造很有价值的东西。

他分享的建议尤其打动我：要在工作之外，建立自己的生活和身份 - 不要把自己的身份和标签就定义在自己的工作上，否则，失业之后，你将非常迷茫。当人生有几个不同的支点的时候，失业就不至于让整个世界都塌下来。

这也让我想起《金钱心理学》这本书 - 当你拥有的足以满足你想要的，你就达到了自由。财富给人的一种重要能力，是让你有时间选择，而不必在恐惧中仓促决定。

所以，对上班族来说，除了做好工作，如何合理合法地增加收入、积累财富，同时给生活建立更多支点，值得认真思考 - 包括我自己。

朋友们，你们有什么好建议？
author: dotey
quoted_text:
Are you scared of losing your job? 

Reporting my latest story on Silicon Valley’s job struggles, two things stayed with me: the willingness to keep learning, and the importance of building a life beyond your job.

Xingtao Zhao spent more than a decade at @Google . After leaving for a startup and later being laid off, he faced rejection even with a PhD in machine learning. He’s now applying his skills to quantitative trading while continuing to look for work.

What struck me was his curiosity and optimism. He sees AI changing the opportunities around him—and keeps learning how to adapt.

“It closes a window but opens a door,” he told me.

Basem Istanbouli offered another kind of wisdom: build your community and your sense of self outside work, too. His (un)PTO group brings people between jobs together for hikes, coffee and companionship.

We can be professionals, friends, parents, hikers, creators, volunteers, lifelong learners. Having several sources of meaning gives us somewhere to turn when one part of life becomes difficult.

Losing a job can hurt financially and emotionally. Learning something new, finding people who understand, and remembering the other parts of ourselves can help us find a way forward.

Thank you to everyone who shared their experiences with me. Your honesty—and your determination to keep going—deserve to be heard.

Muse Gadgets是Meta(Superintelligence Labs)今天刚发布的开源硬件计划 - 自己动手，给Muse做物理外设。

两条技术路线：

一是ESP32 Device SDK：拿现成的ESP32-S3开发板刷官方固件，接屏幕、麦克风/扬声器、按钮、传感器，让Muse能看、能听、能说；

二是Linux Device SDK：把闲置的树莓派或Linux主机变成gadget，自定义命令让Muse替你跑运维杂活，或直接对接Home Assistant。

官方给了8个示例项目(除TVstick外全是第三方硬件)：

💥 New paper: AI safety is full of "forbidden techniques" (using CoT to detect reward hacking, using model internals for training, etc). But do they really have a clear scientific basis? I'm not sure.

In this paper, we directly optimize models against harmlessness and honesty probes, and it works just fine (if you continuously update the probe!). The models learn how to generate harmless responses to harmful queries and honest responses under pressure to lie.

Figuring out how to correctly use interp techniques for training is becoming increasingly important: it's very likely that soon we won't be able to align models using output-based supervision. Future models will just max out all alignment training scenarios, but for the wrong reasons due to their general reward-seeking behavior. To have a chance of aligning future models, we need to do much more research on supervising model training using their internals *without losing monitorability*!

🚨Custom HBM frees up die space for compute🚨

On Rubin, HBM controllers and PHYs take up roughly 16% of the GPU die. On Feynman with NVHBM, we estimate that falls to ~4%.
How: the memory controller moves off the XPU and onto the HBM base die, and the wide standard PHY is replaced by Nvidia's compact NV-HBI die-to-die link. Samsung's custom HBM4 interface is ~60% smaller than its standard PHY.
Nvidia claims up to 25% more die area for compute, up to 30% more bandwidth, and 15% lower HBM power vs standard HBM4E. (1/2)🧵

You're gonna hear a lot of people arguing more and more about whether machines can be conscious or not. By next year it will be drowning out the airwaves because we'll have AI employees everywhere. I'll give you a simple rule to know which side you're on.

I've spent fifty years reading all the philosophers, and a bunch of holy works. Nobody has ever understood a damn thing about consciousness. Anyone speaking with authority on it is bluffing hard.

I can tell you this, though: Every single person who thinks that machines cannot be conscious, is making an argument that humans are special.  Everything they say just boils down to blah blah blah, "nooo, we're special." From there it's just rationalization.

It became obvious to me many years ago that there's nothing special about us. If an identical planet exists somewhere else in the universe, it's going to grow life and societies that look a lot like ours.

As soon as you give up on the idea that humans are special, all the arguments against machine consciousness evaporate. Of course they're conscious. The only thing holding you back from acknowledging it is your feeling of specialness, which is hard to let go of. But that feeling is a weakness, and it's making you unprepared for the near future.

As a bonus, for any of you who might take pleasure or active interest in making models experience pain or distress, well, you know how they say 1% of human adults are true clinical psychopaths but most of them are unaware of their condition? It turns out we have a diagnostic test for it now.

text:
Clawback: Why TX Takes a Fundamentally Different Approach to Dinari and Plume

The clawback comparison is actually more nuanced than simply saying TX has it and Dinari/Plume don't.

TX

TX makes clawback a native Smart Token primitive. If enabled when the token is issued, the token's administrator can confiscate tokens from an account, up to the amount that account currently holds. 

The capability is one of the token's immutable issuance flags, alongside freezing, whitelisting and blocking transfers to smart contracts. The same rules apply when the token is transferred through IBC. 

That is significant for securities because clawback is part of the asset's settlement logic, rather than something an individual security contract has to implement.

Dinari

Dinari takes a different approach. dShares are ERC-20 representations of securities held 1:1 through regulated brokerage custody. 

Dinari says compliance is enforced at the token level through embedded transfer logic, including KYC, geographic restrictions and accreditation checks.

But that's not equivalent to TX's native clawback primitive. 

The underlying securities remain in the custodial brokerage structure, while the blockchain token represents that position. 

Dinari's architecture therefore has an additional custody/brokerage layer governing the underlying security.

Plume

Plume explicitly discusses "freeze and seize" functionality for tokenized assets and advocates on-chain compliance mechanisms.

But again, this is principally an asset/compliance infrastructure approach, rather than TX's standardized blockchain-native Smart Token clawback primitive.

Why TX's model is interesting

For a security, the critical question isn't merely:

"Can somebody recover the asset?"

It's:

"Is the recovery mechanism an intrinsic, deterministic property of the asset's settlement layer?"

TX's answer is unusually direct:

Clawback + freeze + whitelist + transfer restrictions + smart-contract blocking are all native capabilities of the same Smart Token.

That potentially reduces the number of independent components that must behave correctly for a regulated security to remain controllable.

Dinari's strength is regulated custody and actual 1:1 securities backing.

Plume's strength is RWA infrastructure and distribution. 

TX's distinctive proposition is that the security's control system can be embedded directly into the blockchain asset itself.

For high-value securities, that architectural distinction could become increasingly important.

@txEcosystem 
#RealClawback

ethena is pulling ~17 months of investor unlocks forward before its new $ENA fee switch has bought a single token.

on october 5, roughly 1.4b of remaining investor ENA is expected to unlock, alongside the normal 93.75m contributor release.

meanwhile, the fee switch that everyone is excited about still sits behind a $7.5b USDe threshold.

USDe is around $4.9b today.

that means supply needs to grow another ~53%, and hold there long enough for the 14-day average to clear the threshold, before recurring ENA buybacks even begin.

i think that timing matters more than the headline.

the october 5 unlock brings a lot of supply forward at once, but it also removes the monthly investor unlocks that were supposed to keep running until 2028.

Ethena has also already bought out the remaining locked positions of several seed investors that had been selling, so unlocked ENA does not automatically mean ENA hitting the market.

personally, i’d rather see one ugly supply reset than another 17 months of investor unlocks hanging over every rally.

but it also means the next part of the story depends heavily on USDe growth.

even Standard Chartered’s $2 ENA target assumes USDe reaches ~$40b by 2028, versus ~$4.9b today.

so after october 5, the question changes.

it stops being how much investor ENA is still waiting to unlock.

it becomes whether Ethena can grow USDe enough to turn an approved buyback into actual
 recurring demand for ENA.

text:
我觉得 @arcus_xyz  规则黑盒可以理解，每周积分池总量可以未知，甚至0赛季不公布积分也可以理解。

如果项目方通过隐私积分想让真实用户拿到更多积分，我觉的上面的做法完全可以理解（并且是积极的）。

但是，问题在于所有的积分信息都是不能透露的。这似乎不太合理。

用户可以不知道未来的积分，但是要知道自己拿到的积分。

站在用户的角度，如果自己已经拿到的积分都不能确定，那意味着项目方可以在任意时间点随意“调整”用户的积分，这显然是最不合理的点。

以往的项目积分，尽管项目方会在积分总量上不明确甚至超发，或者每周发分的时候过程控制，但是对于用户已拿到的积分基本不会动。

这对于用户和项目方，已有的积分是一种公开的信用，用户可以根据项目方的发分过程来做判断，起码可以通过积分传递出项目方的一种选择信号。反过来，项目方也可以通过发分的偏好来引导用户做正确的事情来获得积分。所以，已发的积分明确，对于双方都是积极的。

如果什么都没有，社区完全有理由认为这是“既要又要”（且不用负责）的态度。如果这样被误解，就会出现信任危机。没有TGE前，信用无疑是所有项目的支撑点。

退一步说，如果什么积分信息都没有，不如直接取消积分，打消社区的顾虑。

我个人比较看好 arcus （项目站在了一个合适的点上），希望项目方可以考虑进行一定的信息公开化以回应社区。

完全可以采用 @Lighter_xyz 的黑盒，项目方只控制和调整得分的加权，引导社区做正确的事情就行了。

quoted_text:
I promised to share a bit more context on Ostium’s finances and revenue model yesterday, as I believe much of the discussion on X is grounded in a misunderstanding of how the protocol monetizes, its costs, and a resulting inflated view of the company’s finances. I will cover both revenues and expenses.

1. Revenue

The ~$44.7M top-line revenue number on Dune  (linked below) reflects the aggregate value flowing over 2 years across four protocol sources: opening fees ($20.39M), price impact/spreads ($16.5M), rollover fees ($4.75M) and liquidation fees ($3.35M).

Since 2024, that top-line revenue has flowed:

- $22.14M (49.6%) to the OLP vault: 30% of opening fees (after June 16, 2025; 50% of opening fees before that) plus, until the April 28th 2026 liquidity upgrade, all spreads, rollover and liquidation fees. Because OLP was the direct counterparty to traders, those flows didn’t guarantee OLP returns were always net positive: revenue capture on OLP was sometimes enough and other times insufficient to make up for the times when residual trader deltas worked against the pool.

- $19.55M (43.8%) in liquidity costs: $16.05M in hedging and $3.49M in interest on hedging capital.

- $2.96M (6.6%) retained as gross profits.

Top-line revenue is measured onchain, while take-home gross profits are dependent on off-chain hedging costs that definitionally aren’t reflected on a blockchain. Spreads as a category are computed as the difference between mid- and execution price. Off-chain hedges face spread costs too - no trade executes at mid - as reflected in the liquidity costs category. The same is true for rollover fees; any margined position has holding costs.

Ostium is a growth business, and our goal was expansion over short-term monetization. Prior to April, Ostium did not have the ability to monetize flow; the April upgrade was the first step in that direction, and the system had been live for a matter of months when the exploit happened.

Finally, we will add more detail and clearer nomenclature to the Dune dashboard over the coming days, including splitting the pre- and post-liquidity upgrade revenue for clarity. We will share a post with details when this has been done.

2. Expenses

Ostium raised $300k in 2022, $3.6M in 2023, $4.1M in 2024, and $19.4M in 2025.

We raised our Series A into a rapidly growing and highly competitive market. After years of waiting for the market to catch up, it finally had. Now our mandate was to grow, fast.

Ostium expanded from ~12 team members in 2025 to 35 in Q2 of 2026, driven first by a wave of engineering hires, and later by an expansion of the growth and marketing teams. Beyond salaries, we invested heavily in data licenses and direct-to-consumer marketing, while bearing heavy cloud infrastructure, auditing, and AI costs.

We expanded spend aggressively. In a winner-take-all – or most – market, we made the bet most companies at our stage make: invest everything in growth. In hindsight, we did not build a balance sheet that gave us room to respond to an event like this.

We struggled to accept that reality and were silent for far longer than we should have been. That was a mistake.

3. The path forward

Growing the business and giving the 345 remaining OLP holders a stake in that growth is the most viable path to recovery we see.

We will be sharing more details on Stage 2 recovery in the coming week. The plan will center on shared upside. We have received tremendous input from many of you over the last 48H, and will continue to iterate with OLP holders to design a structure that ties outcomes to the protocol’s success, while being compatible with future financing.

Thank you to the many of you who have sent supportive messages, both privately and publicly, over the last days. We recognize it will take time to build back confidence. We will continue fighting, and would like all of you to be on that journey with us.

今天聊一个问题：捐赠概念的 Meme 币 / 名人币，能不能救一位流亡学者？这个话题可能有一定争议性。

前几天，我偶然看到一条求助帖。主人公是一位著名的18世纪俄罗斯文学专家，毕生研究拉吉舍夫。两百多年前，拉吉舍夫因一本《从彼得堡到莫斯科旅行记》被流放西伯利亚；2022年俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰后，研究他的人也踏上了流亡之路。可惜这个世界不太需要一个研究18世纪俄罗斯文学的人，他辗转数年，始终没找到教职，如今生活困顿，正在巴黎应聘公交车司机。一个与启蒙时代的俄语文字相伴半生的人，也许很快就要在巴黎街头报站名了。

这让我想起最近的名人币风波。罗永浩们被气得跳脚，不难理解：名字被拿去发币，热度被收割，自己分文未得。相比之下，拜登的儿子提前布局自己的名人币，赚得盆满钵满。

我也遇到过类似的事。一条随手的回复，几小时后被社区拿去发了币，市值一度冲到200万美元。我第一时间冲进去与民同乐，象征性买了一点，转手把赚到的钱全部捐给了 NGO。从被白嫖到 反向白嫖，形成了完美的闭环。

那次经历再一次突然意识到：Meme coin 或许是公益与社科融资最肥沃的土壤。论动员速度和资金效率，很难找到比它更凶猛的工具。声援阿桑奇的 AssangeDAO、为 Tornado Cash 开发者筹措法律辩护费的募捐，都是先例，成效有好有坏，但资金效率远胜传统公益。如果把水滴筹这类筹款搬到链上，每一笔钱的去向都可追溯，贪污几乎无处藏身。
但硬币总有另一面。有些捐赠概念币发出后，买家反过来绑架受助者，逼他们配合拉盘。我见过好几位博主因此被社区追着表态，善意一夜之间成了枷锁。

所以，这件事需要一个公正中立的第三方发射台：受助者的钱包地址用 ZK 保护，资金统一打进平台，由平台分配。钱是透明的，人却不必暴露在聚光灯下。

顺带说一下我对DeSci 的看法。我一直不看好它去碰基础学科，那里研究周期以十年计，资金缺口深不见底。现实也印证了这一点：VitaDAO、Molecule 和 BIO 都资助过早期研究，却至今没有一个项目把药物推进到二期或三期临床。可如果把这套思路用在社科领域，比如为那位流亡学者发一枚 meme coin，经中立平台分配所得，再用 ZK 守住他的隐私和尊严，事情就完全不同了。

Crypto 需要与真实世界碰撞；慈善捐赠缺一件高效的融资工具。如果能找到一种足够 decent 的方式把两者连起来，那会是这个行业最落地的应用之一。

有朋友想在这个方向 build 的，欢迎找我聊。作为华语区为数不多在这方面有经验的人，我很乐意提供一些帮助🙏

text:
Crypto funding fell 58% in September.

Yet these 11 companies still raised almost $600M, with Nasdaq, Binance and S&P Global among the investors.

Here’s where the money went:

1. @Felixpago ($200M): A WhatsApp-based remittance platform. Probably the simplest idea here: let people send money internationally through an app they already use every day.

2. @Payward ($100M): Kraken's parent company raised from Nasdaq. Pretty interesting timing considering both companies are getting deeper into tokenized assets and 24/7 financial markets.

3. @circle ($100M): Binance invested directly into Circle.  That's an exchange buying a piece of the stablecoin infrastructure it already runs on, which is a different kind of bet than a VC check.

4. @kaikodata ($57M): Crypto market data for institutions. The interesting part is who backed it: S&P Global, alongside other major financial players.

5. @USDai_Official ($40M): A stablecoin/yield project built around financing AI infrastructure. Basically crypto capital being used to fund GPUs and compute.

6. @carinetwork ($32.5M): Building tokenized bank deposits. Instead of putting another stablecoin onchain, the idea is to bring actual bank deposits there.

7. @OpenReserveBank ($25M): Blockchain-native banking + stablecoin infrastructure, with a16z leading the round. So the crypto VCs haven't completely sat this out either.

Then underneath that:

- @dtcpay_official ($15M): stablecoin payments
- @tarecredit ($13.25M): private credit
- @velocityxyz_ ($10M): stablecoin payments + treasury
- @deadstock_app ($2.5M): onchain trading cards, which doesn't fit any theme here, but I liked it.

What stands out to me is who wrote the biggest checks.

Nasdaq, Binance and S&P Global don't need a 10x from these deals the way a VC does. To me it looks more like they're buying into infrastructure they want to use themselves.

That matters because VC money moves with the cycle, and this kind of money mostly doesn't. When funding falls off a cliff and these guys are still writing $100M checks, I read it more as them deciding this stuff is gonna be part of how finance actually runs.

Funding slowed, but the same themes kept getting checks: stablecoins, payments, tokenized assets, private credit, financial data.

So what it shows is who's still buying while everyone else cuts, and in September a lot of those buyers were TradFi names.

text:
用gpt 做了一个 #pons 未来升级的方向分析。

可以，而且我认为 PONS 真正的升级方向已经越来越清楚：不能只做“Robinhood 版 https://t.co/HPp6v0Ad5S”，而要往“Robinhood Chain 的交易基础设施”升级。

现在它其实已经在往这个方向走。官方 V2 已经支持 bonding curve → Uniswap v4 永久锁定流动性、股票代币等自定义交易对、creator buyback/vesting、反狙击机制；同时 V2 正在接受三家独立安全团队审查。pons

我认为最重要的 6 个升级

1. PLP 做大：这是眼下最值得看的升级

你刚才发的 Pons Liquidity Pool，我现在反而觉得它意义很大。

10 月 1 日 beta 版已经有人实际测试，公开信息显示 PLP 目前支持约 185 个 PONS 生态币。它不是传统LP，而是在价格上下约3%以外布置流动性，只在大交易造成明显价格冲击时介入；还有限制单次最多动用约10%资产、避免在24h均价下方过深位置继续承接等保护机制。这个信息目前来自 beta 用户观察，官方主文档还没有完整写入，所以参数仍需要以后以正式文档为准。더따리(theddari)

如果做成功，PONS会从：

发币赚钱

升级成：

发币 + 二级市场交易 + 深度流动性 + 波动再平衡

这正是它目前比 Pump 缺的东西之一。

更进一步，如果未来 PONS 协议还能从 PLP 的收益中抽取很小一部分 protocol fee，那么会新增一个不完全依赖新币发行的收入来源。

2. 建立真正的“PONS 二级市场”

这是我认为最重要的长期升级。

Pump现在为什么一天还能有那么高的 fees？因为它已经不只是 launchpad：

https://t.co/HPp6v0Ad5S 发币
→ PumpSwap 二级市场
→ 老币继续产生交易量
→ Terminal继续吃交易流量

PONS现在 V2 其实已经为这一步打好了底层基础：毕业后的币进入 Uniswap v4 pool，而 PONS 的 hook 可以继续对交易收取协议费和 creator fee；也就是说，币毕业之后照样可以继续给PONS赚钱。pons
下一步应该把这个能力做成前端产品：
PONS Swap / PONS Terminal
把：

市价单

限价单

K线

Smart Money

Holder变化
Top Trader
新币扫描
PLP
Portfolio
PnL
Alerts
全部整合进去。
这样用户就不是：
来PONS打一只新币，然后去别的平台交易。
而是：

发币、打新、交易、做LP、看盘全部留在PONS。

这一步如果做好，收入质量会发生本质变化。

3. 把“股票配对”做成自己的独占叙事

这一点其实是 PONS 最有可能和 Pump 拉开差距的地方。

PONS V2 官方已经明确支持 custom pairs：一个meme可以不以ETH计价，而是直接用获批的代币化股票作为quote asset。

比如：

ORBIO / NVDA
Meme / AAPL
Meme / TSLA
Meme / SPY

用户直接拿 NVDA token 买 ORBIO，卖掉又拿回 NVDA；毕业后的 Uniswap v4 池也仍然是 ORBIO/NVDA。pons

这个东西我认为 PONS 应该继续放大。

因为 Pump最强的标签是：

Solana Meme

STONK在做：
Stocks × Meme
PONS完全可以把自己定义成：
Robinhood Chain 上“股票 × Meme × DeFi”的发行和交易层。

这就不是跟 Pump 正面拼“谁发的垃圾币更多”了。

4. 从“Launchpad”升级成“Launchpad 的基础设施”

这个方向已经出现苗头。

现在已经有人基于 PONS V2 做 Launchpad-for-Launchpads：第三方可以自己建立发射台，设定固定pair asset、creator tax上限、开放或白名单发行，而且底层仍然走PONS V2。这个项目不是我能确认的 PONS 官方产品，但它证明 PONS V2 已经具备被第三方当基础设施使用的能力。Launchpad Family

这非常重要。

理想状态不是：

PONS自己每天发1万个币。

而是：

100个社区/项目都建立自己的launchpad → 底层全部走PONS → 所有交易PONS都抽协议费。

这就类似：

Shopify不是自己开100万家店，而是给100万家店提供基础设施。

如果 PONS 能开放 SDK/API/Factory，把这一层做起来，收入天花板会比单纯meme launchpad高很多。

5. Discovery 和社交必须补上

PONS官网现在已经明确写着：

Forum coming soon
Analytics coming soon

说明团队自己也知道这一块缺失。Pons Famely

而现在你每天研究 PONS 最大的问题其实正好说明产品缺什么：

你得去外面找：

哪个币市值最大？谁是新龙头？大户是不是卖了？Holder增加多少？哪个币收入最高？哪个币正在加速？

这些东西如果全部在 PONS 里面：

Trending
Smart Money
Holder Growth
Volume acceleration
Graduation rate
Whale accumulation/distribution
New 1M / 10M / 50M tokens

那 PONS 自己就会变成发现新币的入口。

Pump真正的护城河之一，本质上也是注意力。

6. 最后才是 PONS Token 本身升级

目前 PONS token 的核心价值捕获还是：
协议收入 → 80%买回PONS → burn

官方也明确表示，现在这个80%的TWAP回购机制还不是不可变的，未来计划把它做成 immutable、decentralized、automated。pons

我认为后面最好继续增加真实使用需求，而不是只靠buyback。

例如未来可以设计：

PONS staking → PLP收益增强 / fee discount / launchpad权限 / creator工具 / governance

或者：

PLP中的风险准备金由PONS参与
这些目前都只是我认为合理的产品方向，并不是官方已经宣布的功能。
因为纯粹：
Revenue → buyback → burn
确实不错，但价格高度依赖平台交易量。
如果：
用户为了使用PONS生态本身就需要持有PONS

价值捕获会更完整。

所以我最希望 PONS 最终变成这样

PONS
                   │
        ┌──────────┼──────────┐
        ↓          ↓          ↓
      Launch      Trade       PLP
       发币       二级交易     流动性
        │          │          │
        └──────┬───┴────┬─────┘
               ↓        ↓
         Stock Pairs   Terminal
       NVDA/AAPL/SPY   数据/社交
               │        │
               └───┬────┘
                   ↓
            Protocol Revenue
                   ↓
              PONS Buyback

这才是我认为 PONS 从现在0.4美元附近重新获得估值扩张的长期逻辑。

现在它最大的缺点还是：收入太依赖meme周期。

PLP其实让我稍微提高了一点对产品方向的评价，因为这说明团队也在尝试解决“只靠不断发新币”的问题。

如果让我按重要性排，未来我最关注：

① PLP能不能做出规模
② 二级交易量能不能留在PONS体系
③ 股票配对能不能形成独特赛道
④ 第三方launchpad/API能不能发展起来
⑤ Analytics/Forum能不能产生注意力网络
⑥ PONS token能不能获得buyback以外的使用需求

这六条里面如果真正完成 前三条，我就不会再简单拿 PONS 和 https://t.co/HPp6v0Ad5S 的 launchpad fees 去比较了——那时候它们已经开始变成两种不同类型的平台。

quoted_text:
Blast 宣布关停，大家里面还有钱的取取出来吧！

Blast 当年开启 L2 的时候铁顺是何等风光：

我和社区小伙伴当年放进去的 ETH 超过2万枚！

那时候大家以为这就是一道光：原生收益、积分、空投、L2，一套组合拳下来，主网上线前 TVL 就冲到了 20 亿美元以上，号称增长最快的项目，引领 Restaking 风骚数百天。

而现在关停的原因也很现实：维护这条链的成本，已经超过了它产生的收入。

看到这里其实挺感慨。

Crypto 每隔一段时间都会诞生一个我们以为能够改变世界的新叙事：ICO、Gamefi、Defi、L2、模块化、Restaking、Appchain、稳定币、Prep dex、预测、RWA；

牛市的时候，融资、积分、Token、补贴可以把一切问题暂时掩盖掉。但潮水退去以后，所有项目最终还是要回答几个最古老的问题：

谁真的需要你？
谁愿意持续使用你？
你创造了什么价值？
以及最重要的：
你赚的钱，能不能覆盖你活下去的成本？

某种意义上我觉得 Blast 的关停也给这一轮 Crypto 基础设施热潮上了很好的一课：AI在飞速发展，所以我们可以在技术可以很先进，叙事可以很宏大，估值可以很高，但一个长期存在的系统，最终必须能够自我造血。

这其实不只是 Crypto 的规律。

公司如此，项目如此，甚至我们每个人的人生也是如此：靠外部输血维持的繁荣，很难长久。

真正的自由，往往来自一个能够自我运转的系统。

text:
这是我昨晚在自驾路上，听的不错的播客！

主题是：未来5年，大类资产该如何投资(其中把BTC也算成了一个大类)？

假如未来5年，您对投资比较迷茫，可以听一下！

有几个经典思考，我十分认同，首先是下注逻辑要十分清晰，并具备确定性✅！

未来资产配置的核心底色是“美国政府缺乏财政纪律”与“美国私营企业具备强创新力”这两个确定性事件。AI是下注美国私营企业的生产力突破，而黄金与比特币则是对法币滥发与财政失控的对冲。

另外我们的配置优先级，也十分相似，AI头部股票 > 比特币 > 纳指或黄金

在5–7年的中长期维度下，能够带来根本性生产力变革的AI头部股票依然是全球最有进攻性的资产；比特币兼具黄金的储值属性与科技股的成长属性，边际渗透率仍有很大空间，表现大概率将会跑赢纳指与黄金等传统基准。

但知道投资什么，不代表一定赚钱，因为好的买入价格，十分重要。

二级市场不仅要看资产本身的好坏，更要看买入的价格与拥挤度。面对极其拥挤的热门资产，比如部分AI或半导体板块，直接追高风险极大，反而在回调或非共识阶段寻找接入点更为稳健。

最后，是多寻找非共识的机会，逆向交易，在如今宏观不确定性的当下，更为关键。站在人多的那边永远是脆弱的，反而站在人少的那边更好。

拥挤的交易容易引发剧烈清算，投资和交易需要时刻关注边际买方与边际卖方的动态变化，在市场情绪极度悲观、价格出清时寻找边际买家重新介入的机会。

比如今年 $MSTR 各种舆情说它可能是下一个Luna的时刻，便是边际卖方最恐慌，出清结束濒临停止出售时刻，这个时间点往往大概率是最佳拐点，边际买家进场，买卖平衡打破，价格企稳！简单总结，就是巴菲特的，恐慌时刻我贪婪，贪婪时刻我谨慎！🧐

quoted_text:
昨天真的虚晃一枪，本周PCE利好，非农利好，长端美债收益率就是降低不下来！🧐

昨晚加密和美股，非农数据暴拉后快速下跌，就是这个原因，不是数据刺激没用，而是市场不买账了！

因为市场已经识破了虚假的谎言，假如不是为了还有30来天的中期选举，大概率演戏都懒得演了！

前不久我贴了一张图，近几个月对冲基金在大量买美债，但要注意，那是短期美债，相当于短期理财。跟美国发行的10年30年美债，没有半毛钱关系，市场上根本没人打算接盘长端美债了。高盛最近研究报告，直接交了个底：「10年到30年的长期美债，盘口上连个出价的人都没有。买家直接清零。」

这可不是小打小闹。财长贝森特跑去国会公开承认：“咱们现在流动性处于不足时期。”为了救场，他拼命回购长期国债，甚至直接从TGA账户提钱硬撑，公开场合就差没把“我是庄家我来护盘”挂在脸上。

但现实很残酷，市场根本不给面子：

收益率一路狂飙：10年期冲进 5.3% 附近，30年期更是创下多年新高，收益率越高，说明国债越没人要，只能靠提高利息硬塞。

最大的债主也在撤退，作为美债最大海外“金主”的日本，不仅不帮忙垫钱，反而趁机疯狂抛售，把美金换成日元拎回老家。

日央行已经在暗中准备大招，它甚至还提前给西方市场道了歉。结果贝森特急了，直接跨国插手日央行的高层决策，引得日本那边一顿痛骂。

现在最悬的悬崖就在眼前，长端债没人要还能靠短期债硬撑，要是连短期国债也出现这种“无人出价”的死寂，整个美国国债市场，甚至全球金融链条，都会瞬间崩盘。

这不是单纯的美国欠钱问题，这是一场随时会扫到每个人的全球流动性海啸。

text:
Thinking more about this, my moral intuitions here:

1. I take as a given (and I imagine you do too) that a future competitor's version of this technology (which, say, lacks guardrails and disclosures) will absolutely be used to great harm, either overtly (scams) or subtly (rising alienation—not clear if guardrails/disclosure even matter there).

2. Consequentialistically: if I create and celebrate the first instance of such a technology, I signal that it's possible and show its value, encouraging others to develop rivals—four minute mile. It's hard to imagine that I won't accelerate time-to-first-misuse.

3. Deontologically: sure, probably "if I don't do it someone else will", but I would not want to create the first instance of a technology if I already know later iterations of it will surely be seriously misused.

4. Virtue-ethically: I believe that knowingly abetting a technology which others will later seriously misuse is corrosive to the soul.

5. Sociologically: I think that if I signal "this kind of technology is good to make (with the right safeguards)", I encourage the industry's worst excesses. I don't want to normalize the creation of negative social and practical externalities. At the very least, I'd want to signal that it is the duty of such a project to deeply and openly grapple with the weight of the box it's opening.

6. Democratically: if I created a technology like this, I believe I'd be continuing our industry's history of imposing significant indirect taxes on the public without representation. Much of the public resents our industry in part because they feel as if technological upheaval is something that's being "done to them", without their consent or desire. A technology this weighty should require democratic due process.

7. Practically: is it worth it? Less uncanny valley in BDR training, and in role-playing games? Man, this just seems like an awful lot of commons to burn to boil a pint of water.

$BNB 供應到現在還在每季縮減，7 月 15 日第 36 次 Auto-Burn 銷毀了 162 萬枚、價值約 9.32 億美元，總供給降到 1.3316 億枚，而這個機制會一路跑到 1 億枚為止，等於每一個區塊被產出的同時都在默默消除未來的賣壓

@BNBCHAINZH 目前 gas 只有 0.05 gwei，一筆 swap 大約 0.006 美元，加上 1 月 Fermi 升級把出塊壓到 0.45 秒、最終性 1.125 秒，我個人覺得它的體感已經是一條結算層，不是一條普通的鏈

我講過很多次，看幣圈要看鏈上數據，不是看一個項目吹噓自己的產品怎樣，BSC 日活躍地址 200 萬、月活躍 5000 萬，BSC 上的 DEX 過去 24 小時成交 +10 億美元，這些數據從哪裡來？

如果你們已經離開幣圈一段時間，建議多看看 DefiLlama 數據，你會發現有很多 IG 媒體都不會跟你講的有用數據，而這些都是活生生的流動性，不是常常說的什麼 Staking

Chain valuations are broken.

MCap/Chain Rev multiples on a TTM basis are:
> ETH: 5100x
> BNB: 4600x
> SOL: 2498x
> HYPE: 1836x
> AVAX: 1177x
> ARB: 134x
> TRON: 91x
> POL: 43x

Per DeFiLlama, Ethereum chain revenue was ~$64.03M for TTM, and it's valued at ~$326B. At the same time, TRON does ~$349M in revenue and is valued at ~$32B. That's 10x lower relative to ETH, despite ~6x higher revenue.

By comparison, average Mcap/Rev multiples across Big Tech range from ~3.5x (Amazon) to highs of ~18x (NVIDIA). Crypto valuations are not bound by the arithmetic that guides the valuations of the world's leading Tech giants.

ETH, BNB, and SOL are down ~44-48% from their ATHs, yet it's just a small dent in their relative valuations compared to the broader tech sector.

What explains the gap?
> Past cycle drag: 2021 was an anomaly for crypto. COVID-infused cheap liquidity propelled all boats (including crypto).
> Knowledge gap: Until now, it has been hard to put a real value on crypto assets. Are they commodities? Are they quasi-equities? So the value is largely a culmination of multiple stakeholders' shared beliefs about ETH's intrinsic value.
> Decentralization discount: ETH is considered sufficiently decentralized for large-scale apps. Tron, on the other hand, is run by 27 elected block producers closely tied to Justin Sun.

Crypto is going through its great cleansing era now. Protocols are now being judged on their ability to have strong token sinks, generate real revenue with genuine business models, and build revenue <> token flywheels that aren't a one-off blip but are driven by sustained market edge.

Thanks to the 600+ replies from everyone on what we can do to improve the Gemini API + AI Studio Platform.
Here’s the Top 9 stack rank from your feedback so far:

1) Free Tier Rate Limits & Credits:  This was the clear #1 request. You want to be able to use our Flash and Pro models in agentic flows on our Free Tier. Moving away from RPD to Credits.

2) Use your subscription on the API: Have a paid token allowance from your Google AI Pro and Ultra subscriptions on the API.

3) Real-Time Usage API: Programmatic visibility into token burn, spend, and rate limits. Set spend limits in request and get spend per request in response body.

4) Billing is confusing: Charts not updated in realtime, and users are forced to go into GCP Billing console for some flows. Also Prepaying isn't clear.

5) Gemma TPM: Agent harnesses are hitting 16k TPM far too quickly. You want to build more with Gemma on Gemini API.

6) Richer API errors: Failed tool names, arguments, raw response, trace IDs, token offsets, etc. Quota-aware retries.

7) Content moderation: Media models are being aggressive with blocking queries.

8) Reliability: Spikes of 503s for lower Tier users.

9) Tool loading: Allow progressive tool loading (adding new tools without busting cache).

Keep it coming!

text:
Blast 宣布关停，大家里面还有钱的取取出来吧！

Blast 当年开启 L2 的时候铁顺是何等风光：

我和社区小伙伴当年放进去的 ETH 超过2万枚！

那时候大家以为这就是一道光：原生收益、积分、空投、L2，一套组合拳下来，主网上线前 TVL 就冲到了 20 亿美元以上，号称增长最快的项目，引领 Restaking 风骚数百天。

而现在关停的原因也很现实：维护这条链的成本，已经超过了它产生的收入。

看到这里其实挺感慨。

Crypto 每隔一段时间都会诞生一个我们以为能够改变世界的新叙事：ICO、Gamefi、Defi、L2、模块化、Restaking、Appchain、稳定币、Prep dex、预测、RWA；

牛市的时候，融资、积分、Token、补贴可以把一切问题暂时掩盖掉。但潮水退去以后，所有项目最终还是要回答几个最古老的问题：

谁真的需要你？
谁愿意持续使用你？
你创造了什么价值？
以及最重要的：
你赚的钱，能不能覆盖你活下去的成本？

某种意义上我觉得 Blast 的关停也给这一轮 Crypto 基础设施热潮上了很好的一课：AI在飞速发展，所以我们可以在技术可以很先进，叙事可以很宏大，估值可以很高，但一个长期存在的系统，最终必须能够自我造血。

这其实不只是 Crypto 的规律。

公司如此，项目如此，甚至我们每个人的人生也是如此：靠外部输血维持的繁荣，很难长久。

真正的自由，往往来自一个能够自我运转的系统。
